2)	the name of the court examining the case, the composition of the court, the court session secretary, the advocate and the prosecutor participating in the case;

3)	that the course of the court session is recorded with technical means;

4)	the time of opening the court session;

5)	the name of the case;

6)	information about the arrival of the parties to the case, witnesses, experts and interpreters;

7)	information that the procedural rights and obligations have been explained to the parties to the case;

8)	information that witnesses, experts and interpreters have been warned of criminal liability;

9)	information about the examination of material and written evidence;

10)	court orders and decisions that have not been adopted in the form of separate procedural documents;

11)	information about the court's withdrawal to adopt a decision or render a judgment;

12)	information about the pronouncement of a judgment or a decision adopted in the form of a separate procedural document;

13)	information about the explanation of the content of the judgment or decision, the procedure and time limit for appeal;

14)	information about when the parties to the case may familiarise themselves with the court session protocol, the sound recording and the text of the judgment;

15)	the time of closing the court session;

16)	the time of signing the court session protocol.

(2)	A notation is made in the court session protocol about the plaintiff's withdrawal from the claim, as well as about the defendant having acknowledged the claim and the parties to the case having acknowledged legal facts.

(3)	The court session protocol is signed by the presiding judge of the court session and the court session secretary.

(4)	The protocol of individual procedural actions performed outside the court session must comply with the requirements of this Section.
(In the wording of the law of 19.12.2013. with amendments made by the laws of 14.12.2017. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 63. Section. Writing the Protocol

(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 64. Section. Notes on the Protocol

(Deleted by the law of 19.12.2013., which enters into force on 04.01.2014.)

8.	Chapter Procedural Sanctions

### 65. Section. Types of Procedural Sanctions

In the cases specified in this law, the court may apply the following procedural sanctions:

1)	warning;

2)	removal from the courtroom;

3)	fine;

4)	compulsory bringing to court.

### 66. Section. Warning

The presiding judge of the court session issues a warning to a person who disturbs order during the trial of a case, and a notation thereof is made in the court session protocol.

### 67. Section. Removal from the Courtroom

If the parties to the case, witnesses, experts or interpreters repeatedly disturb order during the trial of a case, they may be removed from the courtroom by a court decision, but other persons present may be removed by an order of the presiding judge of the court session also without prior warning.

### 68. Section. Fine

(1)	The court imposes a fine in the cases and amounts specified in this law. If the court imposes a fine in a court session, the decision is entered in the court session protocol.

(2)	The court decision on the imposition of a fine is sent to the person on whom the fine has been imposed.

(3)	A person on whom a fine has been imposed may, within 10 days of the issuance of the court decision, request the court that imposed it to release this person from the fine or reduce its amount. This application is examined in a court session, having previously notified the person on whom the fine has been imposed of the session. The non-appearance of this person is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(4)	Fines imposed on officials are collected from their personal funds.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 19.12.2013. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 69. Section. Compulsory Bringing

(1)	In the cases specified in this law, the court may adopt a decision on the compulsory bringing of a person to court.

(2)	This decision is executed by the police institution indicated by the court.

### 70. Section. Administrative and Criminal Liability of Parties to the Case and Other Persons

Parties to the case and other persons who, by their action or inaction, obstruct the work of the court, in addition to the procedural sanctions provided for by law, may be held administratively or criminally liable in the cases specified by law.

Part Two Parties to the Case

9.	Chapter Civil Procedural Legal Capacity and Active Legal Capacity

### 71. pants. Civil Procedural Legal Capacity

(1)	Civil procedural legal capacity is the capacity to be vested with civil procedural rights and obligations.  

(2)	Civil procedural legal capacity is recognised equally for all natural and legal persons.

### 72. pants. Civil Procedural Active Capacity

(1)	The capacity to exercise civil procedural rights and fulfil obligations (civil procedural active capacity) belongs to adult natural persons insofar as it has not been restricted by a court, and to legal persons.  

(2)	For natural persons aged from 15 to 18 years, cases in court are conducted by their legal representatives. For adult natural persons whose active capacity has been restricted by a court, cases in court are conducted by their representatives or — in cases provided by law — by representatives together with these persons. In cases conducted by the representatives of the aforementioned persons, the court also invites these persons themselves to participate.  

(3)	For natural persons who have not reached 15 years of age, cases in court are conducted by their legal representatives.  

(4)	In cases provided by law, minors are entitled to independently exercise their civil procedural rights and fulfil obligations. In such cases, at the court's discretion, the legal representatives of these persons may be invited to provide them with assistance in conducting the case.  

(5)	Adult natural persons whose active capacity has been restricted by a court nevertheless have full civil procedural active capacity in cases examining restrictions on their actions and freedom, as well as disputes between such person and their guardian. In such cases, the court invites a prosecutor and a representative of the orphan's court.  
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 73. pants. Concept of Participant in a Case

(1)	Participants in a case are the parties, third persons, representatives of the parties and third persons, the prosecutor and those state or local government institutions and persons to whom the law has granted the right to defend in court the rights of other persons and legally protected interests, institutions which are invited to give opinions in cases provided by law, as well as the representatives of these persons.  

(2)	A participant in a case may be a person who has civil procedural legal capacity and active capacity. State and local government institutions to whom the law has granted the right to defend in court the rights of other persons and legally protected interests may be participants in a case regardless of whether they are legal persons.  
(With amendments made by the law of 07.04.2004, which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

73.1 pants. Bad Faith Use of Rights and Obligations or Contempt of Court

(1)	If a participant in a case uses their rights in bad faith or fulfils their obligations in bad faith, including provides the court with deliberately false information about facts and circumstances of the case or deliberately by action or inaction delays the examination of the case or matter, the judge issues a warning to the participant in the case or imposes a fine of up to 800 euros.  

(2)	For contempt of court — any conduct that demonstrates blatant disregard of the rules existing in a court session or in court — the court may impose a fine of up to 1000 euros on a participant in a case.  

(3)	For the submission of a deliberately false application, statement of claim or complaint, excluding ancillary complaints, appeals or cassation complaints, with the intention of achieving an unlawful objective or obstructing the protection of rights or legitimate interests, the court may impose a fine of up to 1200 euros on a party.  

(4)	The court imposes the fine referred to in paragraph three of this Article by a decision by which the case is decided on the merits or by which the application, claim or complaint is left without examination, or the proceedings are terminated. A person on whom a fine has been imposed may express objections to the imposition of the fine by submitting an appeal, cassation complaint or ancillary complaint, if the decision is appealable to a higher court instance. The imposition of a fine is not separately appealable from the decision by which it was imposed, when appealing the decision.  
(In the wording of the law of 23.04.2015 with amendments made by the law of 25.10.2018, which enters into force on 28.11.2018.)

73.	2 pants. Restriction of Rights of Participants in a Case to Protect State Secrets

The court by a reasoned decision in the interests of protecting state secrets may restrict the rights of participants in a case who do not have the appropriate special authorisation for access to state secrets to familiarise themselves with the volume in which state secret objects are compiled, insofar as it does not affect the establishment of objective truth.  
(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

10.	nodaļa Parties

### 74. pants. Parties, Their Rights and Obligations

(1)	In civil proceedings, any natural or legal person may be parties — the plaintiff and the defendant.  

(2)	Parties have the following civil procedural rights:

1)	to familiarise themselves with the case materials and make copies thereof;  

2)	to participate in a court session;  

3)	to file challenges;  

4)	to submit evidence;  

5)	to participate in the examination of evidence;  

6)	to file petitions;  

7)	to give oral and written explanations to the court;  

8)	to express their arguments and considerations;  

9)	to raise objections to the petitions, arguments and considerations of other participants in the case;  

10)	to appeal court judgments and decisions;  

11)	to receive the judgment, decisions and other documents in the case or copies thereof, as well as to exercise other procedural rights granted to them by this law.  

(3)	The plaintiff is additionally entitled to:

1)	renounce the claim in full or in part;  

2)	reduce the amount of the claim;  

3)	amend in writing the basis or subject matter of the claim or increase the amount of the claim before the examination of the case on the merits has commenced (Article 163 of this law).  

(4)	The defendant is entitled to acknowledge the claim in full or in part, raise objections to the claim or file a counterclaim.  

(5)	The parties may agree on the use of mediation, as well as conclude a settlement or agree on the referral of the case for examination to an arbitral tribunal.  

(6)	Parties must exercise their rights and fulfil their obligations in good faith.  

(7)	Parties have the obligation to:

1)	appear at the court's invitation;  

2)	notify in writing in a timely manner of the reasons why they cannot appear at a court session, submitting evidence thereof;  

21) ensure the assistance of an interpreter if they do not speak the language of the proceedings, except in cases provided in this law, including ensuring the assistance of an interpreter also for experts or witnesses summoned at the request of the parties, if the expert or witness does not speak the language of the proceedings;  

3)	fulfil other procedural obligations imposed on them in accordance with this law.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011, 22.05.2014, 04.02.2016 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 75. pants. Procedural Joinder

(1)	A claim may be brought by several plaintiffs against one defendant, one plaintiff against several defendants or several plaintiffs against several defendants.  

(2)	Each co-plaintiff and co-defendant acts independently in relation to the other party and other co-participants.  

(3)	Co-participants may entrust the conduct of the case to one of them or to one common representative.

### 76. pants. Plaintiff in Cases Initiated at the Initiative of Other Persons

A person in whose interests a case has been initiated at the application of a prosecutor, as well as of a state or local government institution or person to whom the law has granted the right to defend in court the rights of other persons and legally protected interests, participates in the case as plaintiff.

### 77. Section. Succession of Procedural Rights of a Party

(1)	If one of the parties in a case withdraws (death of a natural person, a legal person ceases to exist, assignment of a claim, transfer of debt and other circumstances), the court shall allow this party to be replaced by its successor in rights.

(11)	An application for succession of procedural rights shall be examined in written proceedings, except in cases where the court considers it necessary to examine the application in a court session.

(12)	Before adopting a decision on succession of procedural rights, the court shall verify in the Court Information System whether the party that has assigned the claim is registered in the Register of Applicants and Debtors of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund. If it is established that the party is a maintenance debtor, the court shall adopt a decision rejecting the application for succession of the party's procedural rights.

(2)	Succession of rights is possible at any stage of the proceedings.

(21) An appeal may be filed against the court's decision.

(3)	All actions performed in the proceedings until the moment of entry of the successor in rights shall be equally binding on the successor in rights as they were on the person whose rights have been succeeded.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011., 22.06.2017. and 05.10.2023., which enter into force on 02.11.2023. Part 1.2 enters into force on 01.12.2023. See transitional provision 182.)

11.	Chapter Third Parties

### 78. Section. Participation of Third Parties in Civil Proceedings

(1)	A third party in civil proceedings may be a natural or legal person whose rights or obligations towards one of the parties may be affected by the judgment in the case.

(2)	The provisions on procedural legal capacity and capacity to act of parties shall apply to third parties, they shall have the procedural rights and obligations of parties with the exceptions set out in Section 80 of this Law.

(3)	Third parties may enter the case before the examination of the case on the merits has been completed in the court of first instance. They may also be invited to participate in the case at the request of the parties or the prosecutor.

### 79. Section. Third Parties with Independent Claims

(1)	Third parties who assert independent claims regarding the subject matter of the dispute may enter the case by submitting a statement of claim.

(2)	Third parties with independent claims shall have the rights and obligations of a claimant.

### 80. Section. Third Parties without Independent Claims

(1)	Third parties who do not assert independent claims regarding the subject matter of the dispute may enter the case on the side of the claimant or the defendant if the judgment in the case may affect the rights or obligations of these persons towards one of the parties.

(2)	Third parties who do not assert independent claims shall have the procedural rights and obligations of a party, except for the rights to amend the basis or subject matter of the claim, to increase or reduce the amount of the claim, to withdraw from the claim, to acknowledge the claim or to conclude a settlement, as well as to request enforcement of the court judgment.

(3)	Applications for inviting third parties and applications of third parties for entering the case on the side of the claimant or the defendant shall indicate the grounds on the basis of which the third parties are to be invited or allowed to participate in the case.

### 81. Section

Court Decision on Inviting or Allowing a Third Party to Participate in a Case

A third party shall be invited or allowed to participate in a case in accordance with a court decision. A decision granting or rejecting a request for inviting a third party or for entry into a case shall not be subject to appeal. The decision shall be sent to the third party to the official electronic address or by registered mail.
(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012. with amendments made by the laws of 23.11.2016. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

12.	Chapter Representatives

### 82. Section. Right to Representation in Civil Proceedings

(1)	Natural persons may conduct their cases in court themselves or through authorised representatives.

(2)	Cases of legal persons in court shall be conducted by their officials acting within the powers granted by law, statutes or regulations, or by other authorised representatives of legal persons.

(3)	Cases of state or local government institutions which have been granted by law the right to defend the rights of other persons or interests protected by law shall be conducted in court by the head of the institution or a representative authorised by him or her.

(4)	The participation of the participants in the case referred to in paragraphs one, two and three of this Section in civil proceedings shall not deprive them of the right to invite an advocate to their case for the provision of legal assistance. In this case, the scope of the advocate's powers shall be determined by Section 86 of this Law, he or she shall not provide explanations on the substance of the case.

(5)	(Deleted by the law of 12.02.2004.)

(6)	(Deleted from 01.01.2019. by the law of 14.12.2017. See Transitional Provision 132.)

(7)	(Deleted from 01.01.2019. by the law of 14.12.2017. See Transitional Provision 132.)
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 31.10.2002., the judgment of the Constitutional Court of 27.06.2003., the laws of 12.02.2004., 19.12.2013. and 14.12.2017., which enter into force on 15.01.2018.)

82.	1 Section. Exceptions to General Provisions on the Right to Representation

(1)	Natural persons and legal persons shall conduct cases themselves or through an advocate in the court of first instance and the court of appeal:

1)	in cases within the jurisdiction of the Economic Court;

2)	in cases arising from the law of obligations if the claim amount exceeds 150 000 euros;

3)	in cases concerning the protection of trade secrets against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure (Chapter 30.8).

(11) Cases concerning the protection of trade secrets against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure (Chapter 30.8) may also be conducted through a professional patent attorney.

(2)	In the cases referred to in paragraph one of this Section, a case shall be conducted by a legal person itself if it is conducted by its officials acting within the powers granted by law, statutes or regulations, as well as by persons who are in employment or civil service relations with the respective legal person and are authorised thereto in the manner prescribed by this Law. If a legal person is a parent or subsidiary company of a group, the officials referred to in this paragraph, as well as persons who are in employment relations with the respective legal person, may also conduct cases of the parent or subsidiary company.

(3)	Cases of natural persons in the court of cassation shall be conducted by themselves or through an advocate.

(4)	Cases of legal persons in the court of cassation shall be conducted by their officials acting within the powers granted by law, statutes or regulations, or they shall be conducted through an advocate.

(5)	Cases of natural and legal persons concerning infringements and protection of industrial property rights and cases referred to in point 3 of paragraph one of this Section in the court of cassation may also be conducted through a professional patent attorney.
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the laws of 28.02.2019., 01.10.2020., 21.01.2021. and 25.03.2021., which enter into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 83. Section. Person Who May Be an Authorised Representative in Civil Proceedings

Any natural person may be an authorised representative in civil proceedings, observing the restrictions set out in Section 82.1 and Section 84 of this Law.
(In the wording of the law of 12.02.2004. with amendments made by the laws of 19.12.2013. and 14.12.2017., which enter into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment to the Section replacing the number and words "sixth and seventh paragraphs of Section 82" with the number and word "Section 82.1" enters into force on 01.01.2019. See transitional provision 132.)

### 84. pants. Persons who cannot be representatives in civil proceedings

(1)	The following persons cannot be representatives in civil proceedings:

1)	a person who has not reached the age of majority;  

2)	a person for whom guardianship has been established;  

3)	a person who has been deprived by court judgment of the right to conduct cases of other persons;  

4)	a person who is in a relationship of kinship up to the third degree or affinity up to the second degree with the judge who is to hear the case;  

5)	a person who has provided legal assistance to the other party to the dispute in this or another related case;  

6)	a mediator who has participated in mediation in this or another related case.  

(2)	Upon establishing the circumstances referred to in paragraph one of this Section, the court shall not admit such person to the hearing of the case.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 22.05.2014, which enter into force on 18.06.2014.)

### 85. pants. Formalisation of representation

(1)	Representation of natural persons shall be formalised by a notarially certified power of attorney. The represented person may express the authorisation of the representative orally in court, and an entry thereof shall be made in the court session record.  

(2)	Representation of legal persons shall be formalised by a written power of attorney or documents certifying the rights of an official to represent the legal person without special authorisation.  

(3)	The authorisation of an advocate to provide legal assistance shall be certified by a warrant. If an advocate appears as an authorised representative of a party, this authorisation shall be certified by a written power of attorney.  

(31)	The authorisation of a provider of state-ensured legal aid to provide legal assistance shall be certified by an assignment issued by the responsible state institution for the provision of legal aid.  

(32)	Representation by a professional patent attorney shall be formalised by a written power of attorney and a document certifying the status of the patent attorney.  

(4)	Parents, adoptive parents, guardians and curators shall present to the court documents certifying their rights.  

(5)	If the authorised representative is one of the procedural participants on behalf of other participants, the represented person may express his or her authorisation orally in court, and an entry thereof shall be made in the court session record.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001, 12.02.2004, 17.02.2005, 10.12.2015 and 11.11.2021, which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 86. pants. Scope of powers of representatives

(1)	A representative has the right to perform all procedural acts on behalf of the represented person, except those for which special authorisation is required. If a natural person conducts a case through an authorised representative, court notifications and documents shall be sent only to the representative. If the authorised representative of a natural person whose declared place of residence or indicated address is outside Latvia does not indicate an e-mail address or does not notify of the registration of his or her participation in the online system, court notifications and documents may be sent only to the represented person.  

(2)	Full or partial withdrawal from a claim, amendment of the subject matter of a claim, filing of a counterclaim, full or partial acknowledgment of a claim, conclusion of a settlement, referral of a case to arbitration, appeal of court judgments in the procedure of appeal or cassation, submission of writs of execution for enforcement, receipt of adjudged property or money, termination of enforcement proceedings must be specifically indicated in the power of attorney issued by the represented person.  

(3)	All procedural acts performed by a representative in accordance with the power of attorney issued to him or her shall be binding on the represented person.  

(With amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003 and 01.06.2017, which enters into force on 01.07.2017.)

### 87. pants. Early termination of representation

(1)	The represented person may at any time revoke the authorisation given to the representative, immediately notifying the court thereof in writing. An oral notification of the revocation of authorisation may be given at a court session, and an entry thereof shall be made in the court session record.  

(2)	A representative has the right to refuse to conduct a case, notifying the represented person and the court thereof in writing in due time.  
(With amendments made by the law of 23.11.2016, which enters into force on 01.01.2017.)

13.	nodaļa Institutions and persons who
participate in proceedings in accordance with law
(Chapter title in the wording of the law of 07.04.2004, which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

### 88. pants

Participation of state or local government institutions and individual persons in proceedings, defending the rights of other persons

(1)	In cases provided for by law, international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia or European Union legal acts, state or local government institutions and persons may submit an application to a court to defend the rights and legally protected interests of other persons.  

(2)	The institutions and persons referred to in this Section may familiarise themselves with the case materials, file challenges, give explanations, submit evidence, participate in the examination of evidence, submit requests, appeal court judgments and decisions.  

(3)	The withdrawal by the said institutions and persons from an application they have submitted in accordance with paragraph one of this Section shall not deprive the person for whose interests the application was submitted of the right to request that the court hear the case on the merits.  
(With amendments made by the law of 09.06.2011, which enters into force on 18.06.2011.)

### 89. pants. Participation of institutions in proceedings to give an opinion

(1)	In cases provided for by law, the court shall invite institutions to participate in proceedings so that they give an opinion in the case within their competence and defend the rights and legally protected interests of persons.  

(2)	The invited institutions have the right to familiarise themselves with the case materials, participate in the examination of evidence, submit requests and give an opinion.  
(In the wording of the law of 07.04.2004, which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

14.	nodaļa Prosecutor

### 90. pants. Participation of a prosecutor in civil proceedings

(1)	A prosecutor has the right to participate in the hearing of a case if he or she has brought a claim, submitted an application or his or her participation is mandatory.  

(2)	A prosecutor has the right to bring a claim or submit an application to a court if:

1)	it is necessary for the protection of state or local government rights and interests provided for by law;  

2)	the rights or legitimate interests of minors, persons under guardianship, persons with disabilities, prisoners or other such persons who have limited possibilities to defend their rights have been violated;  

3)	a violation of law has been established during a prosecutor's inspection.  

(3)	The participation of a prosecutor in the hearing of a case is mandatory if it is provided for by law or the court has deemed it necessary.  

(4)	A prosecutor who participates in the hearing of a case has the right to familiarise himself or herself with the case materials, file challenges, submit evidence, participate in the examination of evidence, submit requests, give an opinion on issues that have arisen in the course of the trial and on the merits of the case as a whole, submit a protest against a court judgment or decision, receive a judgment, decision or other document in the case or a copy thereof, as well as perform other procedural acts provided for by law.  

(5)	If a prosecutor is a party to a case, he or she has the right to submit a protest against a court judgment or decision in all cases where other parties to the case have the right to appeal a judgment or decision.  

(6)	The withdrawal by a prosecutor from a claim or application he or she has submitted to a court shall not deprive the person for whose interests the prosecutor submitted the claim or application of the right to request that the court hear the case on the merits.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 91. Section. Recusal or Challenge of a Prosecutor

(1) A prosecutor may not give an opinion in a case if he or she has previously been a judge, party, third person, representative, witness, expert, interpreter or court session secretary in the examination of that case, as well as in the cases specified in Clauses 2,
3 and 4 of the first part of Section 19 of this Law.

(2) In the presence of the aforementioned circumstances, the prosecutor must recuse himself or herself before the commencement of the trial.

(3) If the prosecutor has not recused himself or herself, the participants in the case are entitled to file a challenge to the prosecutor on the grounds specified in this Section.

(4) A challenge to a prosecutor is filed and the court decides it in the procedure laid down in Sections 20 and 21 of this Law.

Part Three Evidence

Chapter 15
General Provisions on Evidence

### 92. Section. Evidence

Evidence is information on the basis of which the court determines the existence or non-existence of facts that are relevant to the adjudication of the case.
(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 93. Section. Duty to Prove and Submit Evidence

(1) Each party must prove the facts on which it bases its claims or objections. The plaintiff must prove the validity of his or her claims. The defendant must prove the validity of his or her objections.

(2) Evidence is submitted by the parties and other participants in the case. If it is not possible for the parties or other participants in the case to submit evidence, the court shall request it at their reasoned request.

(21) If the parties submit evidence or the court requests evidence that contains a state secret object, the court

shall request from the competent authority that has classified the information as a state secret object an opinion on the right of the participant in the case to become acquainted with it.

(3) Evidence shall be submitted to the court no later than 14 days before the court session, unless the judge has set a different time limit for the submission of evidence. The second sentence of the fourth part of Section 48 of this Law does not apply to this time limit.

(31) During the trial of a case, evidence may be submitted at the reasoned request of a party or other participants in the case if it does not delay the trial of the case or the court has recognised the reasons for failure to submit evidence in a timely manner as justified, or the evidence concerns facts that became known during the trial of the case.

(32) If a participant in a case submits evidence after the expiry of the time limit and the court does not recognise the reasons for failure to submit it in a timely manner as justified, it shall impose a fine of up to 750 euros on the participant in the case.

(33) A court decision to refuse to accept evidence is not subject to appeal, but objections to it may be expressed in an appeal or cassation complaint.

(4) If the court finds that no evidence has been submitted for any of the facts on which the party's claims or objections are based, it shall notify the parties thereof and, if necessary, set a time limit for the submission of evidence.
(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002, with amendments made by the Laws of 19.06.2003, 07.09.2006, 29.11.2012, 12.09.2013 and
11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 94. Section. Relevance of Evidence

The court shall accept only evidence that is relevant to the case.

### 95. Section. Admissibility of Evidence

(1) The court shall admit only the means of proof provided for by law.

(2) Facts which, in accordance with law, can be proved only by specific means of proof may not be proved by any other means of proof.

### 96. Section. Grounds for Exemption from Proof

(1) If the court recognises a fact as generally known, it need not be proved.

(2) Facts established by a judgment that has entered into legal force in one civil case need not be proved again when trying other civil cases in which the same parties participate.

(3) A court judgment in a criminal case that has entered into legal force, a prosecutor's order for punishment, as well as a decision to terminate criminal proceedings on non-rehabilitating grounds, is binding on the court examining a case concerning the civil liability of the person in respect of whom the relevant decision was adopted, only on the question of whether the criminal act or omission occurred or was committed or permitted by the same person.

(4) Facts which, in accordance with law, are considered to be established need not be proved. Such presumptions may be challenged in the general procedure.

(5) A party need not prove facts which the other party has not challenged in the procedure laid down in this Law.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002 and 05.02.2009, which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

### 97. Section. Evaluation of Evidence

(1) The court shall evaluate evidence according to its inner conviction, which is based on evidence comprehensively, fully and objectively examined at the court session, guided by legal consciousness based on the laws of logic, scientific findings and observations gained in life.

(2) No evidence has a predetermined force that would bind the court.

(3) The court must indicate in the judgment why it gave preference to one piece of evidence over another and recognised some facts as proved and others as not proved.

Chapter 16 Securing of Evidence

### 98. Section. Admissibility of Securing Evidence

(1) If a person has grounds to believe that the submission of evidence necessary for him or her may later be impossible or difficult, he or she may request that this evidence be secured.

(2) Applications for securing evidence may be submitted at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before filing a claim in court.

(3) Evidence before the initiation of a case in court shall be secured by the district (city) court in which the claim is to be filed. Evidence after the initiation of a case in court shall be secured by the court examining the case.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 14.12.2006 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 99. Section. Application for Securing Evidence

The application for securing evidence shall indicate:

1) the applicant's name, surname, the case for the examination of which it is necessary to secure evidence, or its possible participants;

2) the evidence that needs to be secured;

3) the facts for the proof of which this evidence is necessary;

4) the reasons for which the applicant requests the securing of evidence.

### 100. pants

Procedure for deciding an application for preservation of evidence before filing a claim

(1) The court or judge shall decide on an application for preservation of evidence within 10 days from the date of its receipt.

(2) If the application for preservation of evidence is decided by the court, the applicant and possible parties to the case shall be summoned to the court hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the submitted application.

(3) By decision of a judge, evidence may be preserved without summoning possible parties to the case only in urgent cases, including urgent cases of intellectual property rights infringement or possible infringement, or in cases where it is not possible to determine who will be the parties to the case.

(4) If a decision on preservation of evidence has been adopted without the presence of the possible defendant or other party to the case, he or she shall be notified of this decision no later than the moment of execution of the said decision.

(5) The examination of witnesses, as well as on-site inspection and expert examination, shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of this law.

(6) When granting an application for preservation of evidence before filing a claim, the judge shall set a time limit for submission of the statement of claim, not exceeding 30 days.

(7) When granting an application for preservation of evidence before filing a claim, the judge may require that the possible plaintiff, by depositing a specified sum of money into the bailiff's deposit account or by providing an equivalent guarantee, secure coverage of the losses that the defendant may incur in connection with the preservation of evidence.

(8) The minutes of the court hearing and the materials collected in preserving the evidence shall be kept until they are requested by the court examining the case.

(9) A secondary complaint may be filed against the judge's decision to refuse to accept an application for preservation of evidence or the decision referred to in paragraph three of this Section. If a decision on preservation of evidence has been adopted without the presence of a party to the case, the time limit for filing a secondary complaint shall be counted from the date of issue or dispatch of the decision.
(As worded by the Law of 14.12.2006 with amendments made by the Law of 20.12.2010, which enters into force on 01.01.2011.)

### 101. pants

Procedure for examining an application for preservation of evidence after initiation of a case in court

(1) An application for preservation of evidence shall be examined at a court hearing in accordance with the relevant provisions of this law.

(2) The submitter of the application and other parties to the case shall be notified of the time and place of the hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examining the application for preservation of evidence.

### 102. pants. Court commissions

(1) If it is not possible for the court examining the case to collect evidence located in another city or district, the court or judge shall commission the relevant court to perform specific procedural actions.

(2) The decision on a court commission shall briefly set out the substance of the case being examined and indicate the circumstances to be clarified and the evidence to be collected by the court executing the commission. This decision shall be binding on the court to which it is addressed, and it must be executed within 15 days.
(With amendments made by the Law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 103. pants. Procedure for executing court commissions

(1) Court commissions shall be executed at a court hearing in the procedure established by this law. The parties to the case shall be notified of the time and place of the hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the execution of the commission.

(2) The minutes and other case materials collected in executing the commission shall be sent to the court examining the case within three days.

103.1 pants. Termination of preservation of evidence

If a decision on preservation of evidence has been adopted before filing a claim and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the judge shall, upon receipt of an application from the possible plaintiff or defendant, adopt a decision to cancel the preservation of evidence.
(As worded by the Law of 14.12.2006, which enters into force on 01.03.2007.)

103. 2 pants. Compensation for losses caused by preservation of evidence

The defendant shall be entitled to claim compensation for losses incurred in connection with the preservation of evidence if the preservation of evidence has been cancelled in the case provided for in Section 103.1 of this law, if the claim filed against him or her has been dismissed, left without examination, or the proceedings have been terminated in the cases provided for in points 2 and 4 of Section 223 of this law.
(As worded by the Law of 14.12.2006, which enters into force on 01.03.2007.)

17. nodaļa Means of proof

### 104. pants. Explanations of parties and third persons

(1) Explanations of parties and third persons that contain information about facts on which their claims or objections are based shall be recognised as evidence if they are confirmed by other evidence examined and evaluated at the court hearing.

(2) If one party acknowledges facts on which the other party bases its claims or objections, the court may recognise such

facts as proven if it has no doubt that the acknowledgement has not occurred under the influence of fraud, violence, threats or mistake, or in order to conceal the truth.

### 105. pants. Witness testimony

(1) A witness is a person who has knowledge of facts relating to the case and who has been summoned to the court hearing by the court.

(2) A party to the case, when requesting that a witness be examined, must indicate what circumstances relevant to the case the witness can confirm.

(3) No person summoned to court as a witness shall have the right to refuse to give testimony, except in the cases provided for in Sections 106 and 107 of this law.

(4) A witness may be examined only about facts to be clarified in this case.

(5) Witness testimony based on information whose source is not known or on information provided by other persons, if these persons have not been examined, cannot be evidence.

### 106. pants. Persons who cannot be witnesses

The following may not be summoned and examined as witnesses:

1) clergy — about circumstances that have become known to them while hearing confession, and persons who, by virtue of their office or profession, do not have the right to disclose information entrusted to them — about such information;

2) minors — about circumstances that testify against their parents, grandparents, brothers and sisters;

3) persons who, due to their physical or mental deficiencies, are unable to correctly perceive circumstances that are relevant to the case;

4) children up to seven years of age;

5) persons who have participated in mediation in this or another related case.
(With amendments made by the Law of 22.05.2014, which enters into force on 18.06.2014.)

### 107. pants. Persons who may refuse to testify

(1) The following may refuse the duty to testify:

1) relatives of the parties in the direct line and in the collateral line in the first and second degree, the spouse and first-degree in-laws, as well as family members of the parties;

2) guardians and trustees of the parties, as well as persons who are under the guardianship or trusteeship of the parties;

3) persons who are in litigation with one of the parties in another case.

(2) The court must explain to the said persons their right to refuse to testify.

### 108. pants. Duties of a witness

(1) A person summoned as a witness must appear in court and give truthful testimony about circumstances known to him or her. A witness may also be examined using videoconference in court at the witness's location or in a place specially equipped for this purpose.

(2) A witness must answer questions from the court and the parties to the case.

(3) The court may examine a witness at his or her location if he or she cannot appear following the court summons due to illness, age, disability or other justifiable reason.

(With amendments made by the Law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

### 109. pants. Liability of a witness

(1) For refusal to testify for reasons that the court has recognised as unjustifiable, and for deliberately giving false testimony, a witness shall be liable in accordance with the Criminal Law.

(2) If a witness fails to appear following a court or judge summons without justifiable reason, the court may impose a fine of up to 60 euros on him or her or have him or her brought to court by force.
(With amendments made by the Law of 12.09.2013, which enters into force on 01.01.2014.)

### 110. Article. Written Evidence

Written evidence is information about facts that are significant to the case, and this information is recorded in documents, other writings, as well as in relevant recording systems (audio, video tapes, computer diskettes, etc.) by means of letters, numbers and other written signs or technical means.

### 111. Article. Procedure for Submitting Written Evidence

(1)	When submitting written evidence to the court or requesting that it be requested, the parties to the case must indicate what circumstances significant to the case this evidence may confirm.

(2)	Written evidence shall be submitted in the original or in the form of a copy certified in the prescribed manner. If a part of a written document or other writing is sufficient to clarify the facts that are significant to the case, an extract thereof may be submitted to the court.

(3)	Original documents, as well as written evidence certified in the prescribed manner, shall be submitted if laws or international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia provide that specific facts may be proved only with original documents or copies certified in the prescribed manner.

(4)	If written evidence has been submitted to the court in the form of a copy, the court, upon a reasoned request of the parties to the case or on its own initiative, shall be entitled to request that the original be submitted or produced if it is necessary to clarify the circumstances of the case.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 112. Article. Procedure for Requesting Written Evidence

(1)	The court or judge, upon a reasoned request of a party to the case, shall be entitled to request written evidence from state and local government institutions, other natural and legal persons.

(2)	A party to the case who requests the court to request written evidence must describe this evidence and give reasons why he or she believes that it is in the possession of the said person.

(3)	State and local government institutions, other natural and legal persons who are unable to submit the requested written evidence or to submit it within the time limit set by the court or judge must notify the court thereof in writing, indicating the reasons.

(4)	If a party refuses to submit the requested written evidence to the court, without denying that this evidence is in its possession, the court may recognise as proven those facts for the confirmation of which the opposing party has referred to this written evidence.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 113. Article. Return of Written Evidence in the Case

The court shall return the originals of written evidence to the submitter after converting them into electronic form and attaching them to the case materials. If it is not possible to convert the originals of written evidence into electronic form, the court shall return them to the submitter after the court judgment has entered into legal force.

(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 114. Article. Inspection of Written Evidence at Its Place of Storage

If the submission of written evidence to the court is impossible or difficult due to their number, volume or other reasons, the court may carry out an inspection and examination of the written evidence at their place of storage.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 115. Article. Material Evidence

Material evidence is physical objects which, by their properties, characteristics or very existence, may be useful in clarifying facts that are significant to the case.

### 116. Article. Submission and Requesting of Material Evidence

(1)	A party to the case who submits material evidence to the court or requests that it be requested must indicate what circumstances significant to the case this evidence may confirm.

(2)	A party to the case who requests the court to request material evidence must describe this evidence and give reasons why he or she believes that it is in the possession of the said person.

(3)	The court or judge, upon a reasoned request of a party to the case, shall be entitled to request material evidence from state and local government institutions, other natural and legal persons.

(4)	State and local government institutions, other natural and legal persons who cannot submit the requested material evidence or cannot submit it within the time limit set by the court or judge must notify the court thereof in writing, indicating the reasons.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 117. Article. Inspection of Material Evidence at Its Place of Storage

If the submission of material evidence to the court is impossible or difficult due to their number, volume or other reasons, the court may carry out an inspection and examination of the material evidence at their place of storage or instruct a bailiff to do so.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 118. Article. Storage of Material Evidence

(1)	Material evidence shall be attached to the case or stored in the court's material evidence repository.

(2)	Objects that cannot be brought to court shall be stored at their location. They shall be described and, if necessary, photographed or filmed. The descriptions and images shall be attached to the case.

(3)	The court shall inspect perishable material evidence immediately, notifying the parties to the case thereof. After the inspection, this material evidence shall be returned to the persons from whom it was received.

### 119. Article. Return of Material Evidence

(1)	Material evidence shall be returned to the persons from whom it was received or transferred to the persons to whom the court has recognised rights to these objects after the court judgment has entered into legal force.

(2)	Material evidence which, by law or court judgment, may not be returned to the parties to the case or to the persons from whom it was received, shall be transferred by the court to the relevant state institutions.

(3)	In individual cases, material evidence may be returned before the judgment has entered into legal force if this does not prejudice the examination of the case.

### 120. Article. Liability for Failure to Submit Written and Material Evidence

If the court has not been notified that it is not possible to submit the requested written or material evidence, or if it has not been submitted for reasons which the court has recognised as unjustified, the court may impose a fine of up to 40 euros on the guilty person. Payment of the fine does not release this person from the obligation to submit the evidence requested by the court.
(With amendments made by the law of 12.09.2013, which enters into force on 01.01.2014.)

### 121. Article. Expert Examination

(1)	The court shall order an expert examination in the case upon a party's request in cases where special knowledge in science, technology, art or another field is necessary to clarify facts significant to the case. If necessary, the court shall order several expert examinations.

(2)	The expert examination shall be carried out by persons specified in the Law on Forensic Experts. The expert shall be chosen by the parties by mutual agreement, but if such agreement is not reached within the time limit set by the court, the expert shall be chosen by the court. If necessary, several experts may be chosen.

(3)	The parties to the case shall have the right to submit to the court questions on which, in their opinion, the expert should give an opinion. The court shall determine the questions on which an expert opinion is necessary. The court must give reasons for rejecting questions posed by the parties to the case.

(4)	The court decision on ordering an expert examination shall indicate on what questions an expert opinion is necessary and who is instructed to carry out the expert examination.

(5)	The expert examination shall be carried out in court or outside the court if carrying it out in court is not possible or is difficult.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 122. Section. Duties and Rights of an Expert

(1) A person appointed as an expert must appear upon summons by the court. An expert may also be examined using videoconference in court at the expert's location or at a specially equipped place for this purpose.

(2) If a summoned expert does not appear at a court hearing for reasons which the court has found to be unjustified, the court may impose a fine of up to 60 euros on him or her.

(3) An expert has the right to familiarise himself or herself with the case materials, to ask questions of the parties and witnesses, and also to request the court to obtain additional materials.

(4) An expert gives an objective opinion in his or her own name and is personally responsible for it.

(5) An expert may refuse to give an opinion if the materials provided to him or her for examination are insufficient or if the questions posed exceed the limits of his or her special knowledge. In such cases, the expert notifies the court in writing that it is not possible to give an opinion.

(6) For refusal without justified reason to perform his or her duties or for knowingly giving a false opinion, an expert is liable in accordance with the Criminal Law.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 12.09.2013, which enter into force on 01.01.2014.)

### 123. Section. Removal or Challenge of an Expert

(1) An expert may not participate in the examination of a case if he or she has previously been a judge, a party to the case in the examination of this case, or in the cases provided for in points 2, 3 and 4 of the first part of Section 19 of this Law.

(2) An expert may not participate in the examination of a case also if:

1) he or she is or has been dependent on a party or another participant in the case by official position or otherwise;

2) one of the parties in the case at hand has been connected with the performance of this expert's professional duties before the initiation of the case in court;

3) it is established that he or she is not competent.

(3) Where the said circumstances exist, the expert must remove himself or herself before the commencement of the trial of the case.

(4) If the expert has not removed himself or herself, the parties have the right to file a challenge against him or her on the grounds referred to in this Section.

(5) A challenge to an expert is filed and the court decides it in the procedure laid down in Sections 20 and 21 of this Law.

### 124. Section. Expert Opinion

(1) An expert opinion must be reasoned and substantiated.

(2) The opinion is expressed in writing and submitted to the court. An expert opinion must contain a precise description of the research carried out, the conclusions drawn as a result thereof, and reasoned answers to the questions posed by the court. If an expert, in carrying out an examination, establishes circumstances which are relevant to the case and about which questions have not been posed to him or her, he or she has the right to indicate these circumstances in his or her opinion.

(3) If several experts are appointed, they have the right to consult among themselves. If the experts reach a common opinion, it is signed by all the experts. If the opinions of the experts differ, each expert writes a separate opinion.

### 125. Section. Evaluation of an Expert Opinion

(1) The court evaluates an expert opinion in accordance with the provisions of Section 97 of this Law.

(2) If an expert opinion is not sufficiently clear or is incomplete, the court may order a supplementary examination, assigning its performance to the same expert.

(3) If an expert opinion is not substantiated, and also in the case where the opinions of several experts are contradictory, the court may order a repeated examination, assigning its performance to another expert or experts.

### 126. Section. Opinion of an Institution

The court evaluates the opinion of an institution invited in the procedure laid down in Section 89 of this Law as evidence. The court's non-adherence to the opinion must be reasoned in the decision adopted in the case.
(In the wording of the law of 07.04.2004, which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

Part B
Proceedings in a Court of First Instance

Fourth Division Claim Proceedings

Chapter 18 Filing of a Claim

### 127. Section. Persons Who May File a Claim in Court

(1) Persons who have civil procedural capacity have the right to file a claim in court to defend their infringed or contested civil rights.

(2) On behalf of minors, a claim is filed by the legal representatives of these persons, but in the cases provided for in the fourth part of Section 72 of this Law, the claim may be filed by the minor himself or herself. On behalf of persons under guardianship, a claim is filed by the representatives of these persons together with the person under guardianship or by themselves alone in place of the respective person if so determined by the court, except for the case provided for in the fifth part of Section 72.

(3) A prosecutor, state or local government institutions or persons who have been granted rights by law to defend in court the rights of other persons or interests protected by law may file a claim to defend the infringed or contested civil rights of these persons.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 128. Section. Statement of Claim

(1)	A claim is brought by submitting a written statement of claim to the court.  

(2)	The statement of claim shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court to which the application is submitted;  

11)	the claimant's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, or, if there is none, — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant consents to electronic communication with the court, an email address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included;  

12)	the defendant's, third party's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, or, if there is none, — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. The defendant's personal identity number or registration number shall be indicated if it is known;  

13)	the claimant's representative's (if the claim is brought by a representative) first name, surname, personal identity number and address for communication with the court; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant's representative, whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia, consents to electronic communication with the court, an email address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included. If the claimant's representative's address is outside Latvia, an email address shall additionally be indicated or notification of registration of their participation in the online system shall be provided;  

2)	(deleted by the law of 29.11.2012.);  

21) the name of the credit institution and account number to which payment of the amount to be recovered or reimbursement of litigation costs is to be made;  

3)	the subject matter of the claim;  

4)	the amount of the claim, if the claim is assessable in monetary terms, as well as the calculation of the amount to be recovered or contested;  

5)	the circumstances on which the claimant bases their claim, and the evidence confirming them;  

51) information on the use of mediation for dispute resolution before applying to the court;  

6)	the law on which the claim is based;  

7)	the claimant's demands;  

8)	a list of documents attached to the statement of claim;  

9)	the time of preparation of the statement of claim and other information if it is necessary for the examination of the case. The claimant may indicate their telephone number if they consent to communication with the court using the telephone.  

(3)	The statement of claim shall be signed by the claimant or their representative, or the claimant together with the representative if so determined by the court, except in the case provided for in the fifth paragraph of Section 72 of this law. If the claim is brought on behalf of the claimant by their representative, a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to bring the claim shall be attached to the statement of claim.  

(4)	A statement of claim in a case concerning maintenance in cases provided for in European Union legal acts and international agreements, using the forms specified in the relevant legal acts, may be submitted or forwarded through the intermediary of the Latvian central authorities designated to ensure cooperation.  

(5)	In the statement of claim in cases concerning debt recovery, claims for payments for management activities in a multi-apartment residential building (management costs), claims for payments for services necessary for the maintenance of the building (utility services) and claims for payments to the apartment owners' community reserve fund (reserves) shall be indicated separately.  

(6)	In the statement of claim in cases concerning the non-existence of marriage or divorce, in claims for personal injury, in claims for recovery of maintenance, in claims for division of the parties' common dwelling in which they live in one household, or for determination of the procedure for use of the dwelling in which the parties live in one household, and in cases arising from custody and contact rights, if a decision on temporary protection against violence has been adopted before bringing the claim, the court that adopted the decision on temporary protection against violence and the date of adoption of the decision shall be indicated.  

(7)	If the claim is related to a state secret object, then information containing a state secret shall not be indicated in the statement of claim. Information containing a state secret shall be indicated in a separate document.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 09.06.2011., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012., 22.05.2014., 29.10.2015., 23.11.2016.,
01.06.2017., 22.06.2017., 21.01.2021., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 129. Section. Documents to be Attached to the Statement of Claim

(1)	(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.)

(2)	Documents confirming the following shall be attached to the statement of claim:

1)	payment of state duty and other court costs in the procedure and amount prescribed by law, except in cases where the statement of claim has been submitted and payment made in the online system;  

2)	compliance with the procedure for prior out-of-court examination of the case, if such is prescribed by law;  

3)	the circumstances on which the claim is based.  

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.)

(4)	In cases provided for by law, a certified translation in the prescribed manner shall be attached to the statement of claim and the documents attached thereto, if the documents are intended for issuance to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law. A translation need not be attached by a person who is exempt from payment of court costs.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 130. Section. Submission of the Statement of Claim to the Court

(1)	The statement of claim shall be submitted to the court of first instance in accordance with the rules on jurisdiction.  

(2)	(Deleted by the law of 23.04.2015.)

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 23.04.2015.)

(4)	An unsigned statement of claim shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.  
(With amendments made by the law of 23.04.2015., which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

### 131. Section

Resolution of the Question of Acceptance of the Statement of Claim and Initiation of Civil Proceedings

(1)	After receipt of the statement of claim by the court, the judge shall, within ten days, but after receipt of the application referred to in Section 644.7 or 644.17 of this law no later than the next day, adopt a decision:

1)	on acceptance of the statement of claim and initiation of the case;  

2)	on refusal to accept the statement of claim;  

3)	on leaving the statement of claim without progress.  

(2)	If examination of the case in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council or Regulation (EC) No 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council is not possible, the judge shall, in the cases provided for in the said legal acts, adopt one of the decisions provided for in the first paragraph of this Section regarding the progress of the statement of claim.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 04.08.2011. and 25.10.2018., which enters into force on 28.11.2018.)

### 132. Section. Grounds for Refusal to Accept a Statement of Claim

(1) The judge shall refuse to accept a statement of claim if:

1) the dispute is not subject to the court;

2) the claim has been brought by a person who does not have the right to bring a claim;

3) the parties have agreed in the manner prescribed by law to submit the dispute for consideration to an arbitral tribunal, except in cases where a statement of claim has been submitted to the court for recognition of the arbitration agreement as invalid;

31) the parties have agreed in the manner prescribed by law to resolve the dispute using mediation, and no evidence has been submitted that the proposal to resolve the dispute using mediation has been rejected or that a mediation agreement has not been concluded, or that mediation has been terminated without reaching an agreement in the manner prescribed by the Mediation Law;

4) proceedings are pending in the same or another court concerning a dispute between the same parties, on the same subject matter and on the same grounds;

5) in a dispute between the same parties, on the same subject matter and on the same grounds, a court judgment that has entered into legal force or a decision to terminate proceedings due to the claimant's withdrawal from the claim or approval of a settlement between the parties exists;

6) the case does not fall within the jurisdiction of this court;

7) the claimant has not complied with the procedure for prior out-of-court examination of the case established for the relevant category of cases or has not taken the measures prescribed by law to settle the dispute with the defendant before bringing the claim;

8) the statement of claim has been submitted by a person who does not have civil procedural capacity;

9) the power of attorney or other document attached to the statement of claim does not show authorisation for the representative to bring such a claim;

10) no power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to bring a claim is attached to the statement of claim.

(2) The judge shall adopt a reasoned decision on the refusal to accept the statement of claim. The decision together with the submitted statement of claim shall be issued to the claimant.

(3) The decision may be appealed in the manner prescribed by this Law, except for a decision on refusal to accept a statement of claim on the grounds of point 10 of paragraph one of this Section.

(4) The judge's refusal to accept a statement of claim on the grounds of points 6 to 10 of paragraph one of this Section shall not be an obstacle to the submission of the same application to the court once the deficiencies have been remedied.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 29.11.2012., 22.05.2014., 23.04.2015. and 28.05.2015., which enter into force on 02.07.2015.)

### 133. Section. Leaving a Statement of Claim Without Progress

(1) The judge shall leave a statement of claim without progress if:

1) the statement of claim does not contain all the particulars specified in paragraph two, four or five of Section 128 of this Law;

2) the documents specified in Section 129 of this Law are not attached to the statement of claim;

3) the statement of claim in a simplified procedure case is not drawn up in accordance with the requirements of Section 250.20 of this Law.

(2) The judge shall adopt a reasoned decision on leaving the statement of claim without progress, send it to the claimant and set a time limit for remedying the deficiencies. This time limit may not be shorter than 20 days, counting from the date of sending the decision. The judge's decision may be appealed in the manner prescribed by this Law. The appeal period shall be counted from the day the decision is issued to the claimant.

(3) If the claimant remedies the deficiencies within the specified time limit, the statement of claim shall be deemed to have been submitted on the day it was first submitted to the court.

(4) If the claimant does not remedy the deficiencies within the specified time limit, the statement of claim shall be deemed not to have been submitted and shall be returned to the claimant.

(5) The return of the statement of claim to the claimant shall not be an obstacle to its repeated submission to the court, observing the general procedure for submission of statements of claim prescribed by this Law.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 23.04.2015., 14.12.2017. and 21.01.2021., which
enter into force on 01.03.2021.)

### 134. Section. Joinder of Claims and Civil Cases

(1) The claimant is entitled to join several interrelated claims in one statement of claim.

(2) If several similar cases in which the same parties participate are pending in court proceedings, or cases in which one claimant brings a claim against several defendants or several claimants against the same defendant, the court is entitled to join these cases in one proceeding if such joinder will facilitate faster and more correct examination of the cases.
(With amendments made by the Law of 08.09.2011., which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

### 135. Section. Separation of Claims and Civil Cases

(1) The judge may instruct the claimant to separate one claim or several claims from the joined claims into a separate claim if it considers separate examination of the claims expedient.

(2) The court examining the case may, by decision, separate one claim or several claims from the joined claims into a separate case if their examination in one proceeding has become difficult or impossible.

### 136. Section. Bringing a Counterclaim

(1) The defendant is entitled, until the examination of the case on the merits is completed, to bring a counterclaim against the claimant in the court of first instance.

(2) A counterclaim shall be brought in accordance with the general rules for bringing a claim.

(3) The court or judge shall accept a counterclaim if:

1) mutual set-off is possible between the original claim and the counterclaim;

2) satisfaction of the counterclaim wholly or partially excludes satisfaction of the original claim;

3) the counterclaim and the original claim are interrelated and their joint examination will facilitate faster and more correct adjudication of the case.

(4) The counterclaim shall be examined together with the original claim.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 19.06.2003. and 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

Chapter 19
Security for a Claim and Interim Protection
(Chapter title in the wording of the Law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 137. Section

Grounds for Security for a Claim and Interim Protection and Content of the Application

(1) Security for a claim may be applied in claims of a proprietary nature if there is reason to believe that the execution of the court judgment in the case could become difficult or impossible.

(2) Interim protection may be applied in claims of a proprietary or non-proprietary nature if there is reason to believe that the claimant's rights are being infringed or could be infringed before the moment the decision enters into force, and if the application of interim protection is necessary to prevent possible substantial harm. Interim protection shall also be applied in cases where, before the moment the decision enters into force, it is necessary to establish a temporary regulation of disputed relations, if this is necessary for the claimant to prevent possible substantial harm.

(3) The court or judge may, upon a reasoned application by the claimant, adopt a decision on the application of security for a claim or interim protection. Security for a claim and interim protection may also be applied simultaneously.

(4) The application shall indicate:

1) the name of the court to which the application is submitted;

2) the claimant's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant consents to electronic communication with the court, the e-mail address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included;

3) the respondent's, third party's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. The respondent's personal identity number or registration number shall be indicated if it is known;

4) the claimant's representative's (if the claim is brought by a representative) first name, surname, personal identity number and address for communication with the court; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant's representative, whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia, consents to electronic communication with the court, the e-mail address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included. If the claimant's representative's address is outside Latvia, the e-mail address shall additionally be indicated or notification of registration of their participation in the online system shall be provided;

5) the subject matter of the claim;

6) in claims of a proprietary nature — the amount of the claim;

7) the security for the claim or interim protection measure that the claimant requests to be applied;

8) the circumstances by which the claimant substantiates the necessity of security for the claim or interim protection.

(5) Evidence confirming the circumstances by which the necessity of security for the claim or interim protection is substantiated shall be attached to the application.

(6) It is permissible to examine the question of security for a claim or interim protection at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before bringing the claim to court.
(In the wording of the Law of 25.03.2021 with amendments made by the Law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 138. Section Measures for Security for a Claim

(1) Measures for security for a claim are:

1) seizure of movable property and cash belonging to the respondent;

2) entry of a prohibition note in the relevant movable property register or other public register;

3) entry of a security for claim note in the Land Register or ship register;

4) arrest of a ship;

5) prohibition on the respondent to perform certain actions or obligation on the respondent to perform certain actions within a specified time limit;

6) seizure of payments due from third parties, including funds in credit institutions and other financial institutions;

7) suspension of enforcement actions (including prohibition on the bailiff to transfer money or property to the judgment creditor or debtor or suspension of the sale of property).

(2) When securing a claim by entry of a prohibition note in the relevant movable property register or other public register, the decision shall indicate what type of prohibition is to be entered.

(3) If the subject matter of the claim is the right of ownership to movable property or immovable property or the claim is directed towards the execution of registration of a right, security for the claim shall be made by seizing the disputed movable property or by entering a prohibition note in the Land Register in the relevant immovable property section.

(4) If the subject matter of the claim is a right in rem to immovable property, security for the claim shall be made by entering an encumbrance note in the Land Register in the relevant immovable property section.

(5) If the subject matter of the claim is a monetary claim, its security with immovable property shall be made by entering a pledge right note in the Land Register in the relevant immovable property section, indicating the amount of the claim to be secured.

(6) Arrest of a ship shall be applied only in maritime claims.

(7) Suspension of the sale of property is not permissible in cases where the claim is brought for recovery of money.

(71) Seizure of payments due from third parties, including funds in credit institutions and other financial institutions, is not permissible in claims where the claim is compensation to be determined at the court's discretion.

(8) When granting an application for security for a claim, the decision shall indicate the amount up to which the security extends, but it may not be greater than the amount of the claim.

(9) It is permissible to apply several measures for security for a claim simultaneously, observing the provisions of paragraph eight of this Section.
(In the wording of the Law of 07.09.2006 with amendments made by the Laws of 05.02.2009, 04.08.2011, 11.09.2014 and 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

138.1 Section Interim Protection Measures

(1) Interim protection measures are:

1) seizure of movable property belonging to the respondent;
