(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006. and 08.12.2016., which enters into force on 04.01.2017. Amendments to the Section in connection with the European Account Preservation Order enter into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision point 121)

### 208. Section. Sending of a Judgment to the Parties to the Case

(1) A judgment shall be sent to a party to the case who has not participated in the court hearing no later than within three days after the announcement of the judgment.

(2) (Deleted as of 01.03.2018. by the law of 14.12.2017. See transitional provision point 137)

(3) If, in the cases referred to in the first paragraph of this Section, a judgment is to be sent to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this Law and, in cases provided for in this Law, a translation is to be attached to the judgment, the court shall send the judgment together with the translation immediately after the preparation of the translation.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

22.1 Chapter Default Judgment

## (Chapter 31

Edition of law 10.2002, which enters into force 01.01.2003.)

208.1 Article. Judgment by default

(1) A judgment by default is a judgment made by a first instance court in a case where the defendant has not provided an explanation regarding the claim and has not appeared following the court's summons, without notifying the reason for non-appearance.

(2) The court makes a judgment by default based on the plaintiff's explanations and the materials in the case, if the court considers them sufficient for resolving the dispute.

(3) A judgment by default cannot be made in cases:

1) which cannot be terminated by settlement;

2) where the defendant's declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is not in the Republic of Latvia;

3) where the defendant is summoned to court by publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis";

4) where there are several defendants and at least one participates in the proceedings.

(4) The provisions on judgment by default do not apply to special proceedings.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force 01.12.2021.)

208.2 Article. Form and content of judgment by default

(1) The court makes and compiles a judgment by default in the procedure specified in Articles 189-198 of this law, observing the specificities established in this Article.

(2) The fact that the judgment is by default is indicated in its title.

(3) The descriptive part of a judgment by default indicates the plaintiff's claims, the essence of the plaintiff's explanation, the procedural basis for making this judgment, except in cases where the descriptive part of the judgment by default is made in accordance with the requirements of Article 194, paragraph 1, point 2 and paragraph 2 of this law.

(4) In the operative part of a judgment by default, in addition to that mentioned in Article 193, paragraph 6 of this law, the court indicates that the plaintiff is entitled to appeal the judgment by way of appeal, but the defendant within 20 days from the date of sending the judgment by default is entitled to submit to the court that made the judgment by default an application for restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force 01.12.2021.)

208.3 Article. Sending of judgment by default to the defendant

A judgment by default is sent to the defendant to the official electronic address or by registered mail.
(Edition of law 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

208.4 Article. Appeal of judgment by default

(1) The plaintiff is entitled to appeal a judgment by default by way of appeal.

(2) The defendant is not entitled to appeal a judgment by default by way of appeal.

208.5 Article. Restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case

(1) The defendant is entitled within 20 days from the date of sending the judgment by default to submit to the court that made the judgment by default an application for restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case.

(2) The application indicates:

1) the name of the court that made the judgment by default;

2) the defendant's name, surname, personal code, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the defendant agrees to electronic communication with the court, also indicates the email address and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also includes an indication of registration;

21) the name of the credit institution and account number to which litigation costs are to be reimbursed;

3) the date of making the judgment by default and its essence;

4) the reasons why the defendant did not take part in the case;

5) the defendant's objections to the claim and judgment, the basis for the objections;

6) evidence confirming the objections and their basis, the law on which they are based;

7) requests for acceptance of evidence or its procurement;

8) a request to restore proceedings in the case and re-examine the case.

(3) The following documents are attached to the application confirming:

1) payment of state fee and other court costs in the procedure and amount established by law, except in cases where the application is submitted and payment is made in the online system;

2) the basis for the objections.

(4) Evidence confirming the circumstances on which the application is based is attached to the application.

(5) An unsigned application is considered not submitted and is sent back to the submitter.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 23.04.2015., 23.11.2016., 22.06.2017. and 11.11.2021., which
enter into force 01.12.2021.)

208.6 Article. Leaving application without movement

(1) The judge leaves the application without movement if:

1) the application does not contain all the requisites established in Article 208.5, paragraph 2 of this law;

2) the documents established in Article 208.5, paragraphs 3 and 4 of this law are not attached to the application.

(2) The judge adopts a reasoned decision on leaving the application without movement, which is sent to the defendant, and sets a time limit, not shorter than 20 days, for remedying deficiencies. The time limit is counted from the date of issuance of the decision. The judge's decision is appealable in the procedure established in this law. The appeal time limit is counted from the date of issuance of the decision.

(3) If the defendant has not remedied the deficiencies within the time limit set by the judge, the application is considered not submitted and is returned to the defendant. The decision on returning the application is not appealable.

(4) If the application is returned to the defendant, he or she does not have the right to repeatedly submit an application to the court.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force 01.12.2021.)

208.7 Article. Actions of the judge after acceptance of the application

(1) Having found that the application complies with the requirements of Article 208.5 of this law, the judge notifies the plaintiff and third parties about the application and sends them the application. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the claim may also be sent to the plaintiff and third parties.

(2) The judge examines the application within seven days after its receipt and adopts one of the following decisions:

1) on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case, if it finds that the examination of the case without the defendant's participation and verification of the evidence submitted by him or her has led or could have led to incorrect adjudication of the case;

2) on rejection of the application, if it finds that there is no basis specified in point 1 of paragraph 2 of this Article for re-examination of the case.

(3) In the decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case, the judge sets the day and time of the court session and the persons to be summoned and called to court.

(4) If a decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case has been adopted and the plaintiff has submitted an appeal against the judgment by default, the appeal is returned to the plaintiff.

(5) An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against a decision rejecting the application. A decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case is not appealable.
(With amendments made by the laws of 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enter into force 07.07.2022.)

208.8 Article. Entry into legal force of judgment by default

(1) A judgment by default enters into legal force if an appeal has not been submitted within the time limit established by law and an application for restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case has not been submitted.

(2) If an application for restoration of proceedings has been rejected and an appeal against the court judgment has not been submitted, the judgment by default enters into force after the time limit for appealing the judge's decision has expired.

(3) If the judge's decision on rejection of the application has been appealed and the appellate court has left it unchanged, the judgment by default enters into force from the moment of pronouncement of the appellate court's decision.

208.9 Article. Re-examination of the case

If a decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case has been adopted, the judgment by default does not enter into force and the case is re-examined in full in the procedure provided for in Chapter 21 of this law. The restriction established by law on a judge's participation in re-examination of a case does not apply to this case.

23. Chapter
Postponement of examination of the case

### 209. pants. Court's Duty to Postpone Examination of a Case

The court shall postpone the examination of a case:

1) if one of the parties to the case does not appear at the court hearing and has not been notified of the time and place of the court hearing;

2) if one of the parties to the case who has been notified of the time and place of the court hearing does not appear at the court hearing for a reason which the court recognises as justified;

3) if the defendant has not been served with the statement of claim and therefore requests postponement of the examination of the case;

4) if it is necessary to summon as a party to the case a person whose rights or legally protected interests may be affected by the court judgment;

5) in the case provided for in Section 240 of this Law;

6) if the defendant does not appear at the court hearing, to whom in accordance with the first paragraph of Section 56.2 of this Law a notice of the time and place of the court hearing has been sent and confirmation of delivery of documents has been received (second paragraph of Section 56.2), but the defendant has not received the notice in due time;

7) if the defendant does not appear at the court hearing, to whom in accordance with the first paragraph of Section 56.2 of this Law a notice of the time and place of the court hearing or the statement of claim has been sent, and no confirmation of delivery of documents (second paragraph of Section 56.2) or non-delivery of documents has been received;

8) if the consent of the parties to mediation has been received.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 22.05.2014. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 210. pants. Court's Right to Postpone Examination of a Case

(1) The court may postpone the examination of a case:

1) if the plaintiff, who has been notified of the time and place of the court hearing, does not appear at the court hearing for an unknown reason;

2) if the defendant, who has been notified of the time and place of the court hearing, does not appear at the court hearing for an unknown reason;

3) if it considers that it is not possible to examine the case because a party to the case whose participation in the examination of the case is mandatory according to law has not appeared, as well as a witness, expert or court-provided interpreter;

4) at the request of a party to the case, in order to give him or her the opportunity to submit additional evidence;

5) if a person is unable to participate in the court hearing using videoconference for technical or other reasons beyond the court's control;

6) if an interpreter does not appear at the court hearing for a reason which the court recognises as justified.

(2) For the reason specified in point 1 or 2 of the first paragraph of this Section, the court may postpone the examination of the case no more than once.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011. and 04.02.2016., which enter into force on 29.02.2016. The amendment concerning interpreters made in point 3 of the first paragraph and the amendment supplementing the first paragraph with point 6 enter into force on 31.07.2016. See transitional provision point 114)

### 211. pants. Decision on Postponement of Examination of a Case

(1) The decision on postponement of the examination of a case shall be recorded in the minutes of the court hearing.

(2) When postponing the examination of a case, the court shall indicate all procedural actions to be performed before the next court hearing, as well as set the date of the next court hearing. If the court postpones the examination of a case in the case provided for in point 7 of Section 209 of this Law, the next court hearing shall be set only after the conditions referred to in point 2 of Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council or in the second paragraph of Article 15 of the 1965 Hague Convention have been complied with or, if the legal acts referred to in this Section are not applicable, equivalent measures have been taken.

(21) When postponing the examination of a case in the case referred to in point 8 of Section 209 of this Law, the court shall, in the decision on postponement of the examination of the case, set a time limit for the use of mediation, which shall not exceed six months, and the obligation of the parties to submit to the court evidence of the result of mediation no later than seven days after the termination of mediation. The court's decision on postponement of the examination of a case for the use of mediation shall not be subject to appeal.

(3) The court shall notify the date of the next court hearing to persons who have appeared at the court hearing. Persons present shall not be summoned or called to the court hearing again.

(4) A decision on postponement of the examination of a case shall not be subject to appeal, except for a decision in which the date of the next court hearing has not been set.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011., 22.05.2014., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which
enter into force on 07.07.2022.)

### 212. pants. Examination of Witnesses When Postponing Examination of a Case

(1) If all parties to the case are present at the court hearing, the court, when postponing the examination of the case, may examine witnesses who have appeared.

(2) If necessary, examined witnesses may be summoned to the next court hearing.

### 213. pants. Resumption of Examination of a Case

(Deleted by the law of 07.09.2006., which enters into force on 11.10.2006.)

24. nodaļa Suspension of Proceedings in a Civil Case

### 214. pants. Court's Duty to Suspend Proceedings

The court shall suspend proceedings if:

1) a natural person has died or a legal person which is a party or third party with independent claims in the case has ceased to exist, and if the disputed legal relationship allows succession of rights;

2) the court has imposed on a party or third party such a restriction of legal capacity which does not allow it to independently exercise civil procedural rights and obligations;

3) a party or third party is completely unable to participate in the examination of the case due to serious illness, age or disability;

4) it adopts a decision on submission of an application to the Constitutional Court or the Constitutional Court has instituted a case in connection with a constitutional complaint submitted by a party or third party;

41) it adopts a decision on referring a question to the Court of Justice of the European Union for a preliminary ruling;

5) the examination of the case is not possible until another case has been decided, which is to be examined in civil proceedings, criminal proceedings, administrative proceedings or administrative offence proceedings;

6) (deleted by the law of 08.09.2011.);

7) the Competition Council is examining a case concerning an infringement of competition law which is related to a claim for damages;

8) the Consumer Rights Protection Centre is examining a case concerning an infringement of consumer rights which is related to a collective action by consumers.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 07.04.2004., 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012.,
19.10.2017., 11.11.2021. and 14.09.2023., which enter into force on 15.10.2023.)

### 215. pants. Court's Right to Suspend Proceedings

The court, at the initiative of a party to the case or on its own initiative, may suspend proceedings if:

1) a party or third party with independent claims is outside the borders of Latvia in connection with a long-term business trip or performance of state duties;

2) a search for the defendant has been announced;

3) a party or third party with independent claims is unable to participate in the examination of the case due to illness;

4) the court orders an expert examination;

5) there is a mutual agreement between the parties on suspension of proceedings and the third party with independent claims does not object to it;

6) in claims of a proprietary nature, insolvency proceedings of a legal person or insolvency proceedings of a natural person have been declared for the defendant.
(With amendments made by the law of 18.04.2013., which enters into force on 22.05.2013.)

### 216. Section. Terms for Suspension of Proceedings

Proceedings are suspended:

1) in the cases provided for in paragraph 1 of Section 214 of this Law — until the determination of a successor in title or the appointment of a legal representative;

2) in the cases provided for in paragraph 2 of Section 214 of this Law — until the appointment of a legal representative;

3) in the cases provided for in paragraph 3 of Section 214 of this Law — until the time limit set by the court for formalising representation;

4) in the cases provided for in paragraphs 4, 4.1 and 5 of Section 214 of this Law — until a decision of the Constitutional Court or the Court of Justice of the European Union or a decision in civil proceedings, criminal proceedings, administrative proceedings or administrative offence proceedings enters into legal force;

5) in the cases provided for in paragraphs 1 to 4 of Section 215 of this Law — until the circumstances mentioned in those paragraphs have ceased to exist;

6) in the cases provided for in paragraph 5 of Section 215 of this Law — until the time limit set in the court decision;

7) (deleted by the Law of 08.09.2011);

8) in the cases provided for in paragraph 6 of Section 215 of this Law — until the termination of the legal person's insolvency proceedings or the natural person's insolvency proceedings;

9) in the case provided for in paragraph 7 of Section 214 of this Law — until the competition authority has adopted a decision or otherwise terminated the examination of the case;

10) in the case provided for in paragraph 8 of Section 214 of this Law — until the Consumer Rights Protection Centre has adopted a decision or otherwise terminated the examination of the case.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 20.06.2001, 07.04.2004, 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 18.04.2013, 19.10.2017,
11.11.2021 and 14.09.2023, which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

### 217. Section. Decision on Suspension of Proceedings

(1) The court shall adopt a reasoned decision on the suspension of proceedings, which shall be drawn up in the form of a separate procedural document.

(2) The decision shall indicate the circumstances until the occurrence or cessation of which the proceedings are suspended, or the time limit for which the proceedings are suspended.

(3) An appeal may be lodged against the court's decision to suspend proceedings.

### 218. Section. Resumption of Proceedings

(1) The court shall resume proceedings by decision on its own initiative or at the request of the parties to the case.

(2) If legal person's insolvency proceedings or natural person's insolvency proceedings have been declared against the defendant in claims of a proprietary nature, the court shall resume the suspended proceedings:

1) at the request of the creditor, if the insolvency administrator has adopted a decision not to recognise or to partially recognise the creditor's claim on the grounds that there is a dispute over rights;

2) if, when examining an appeal against a decision of the insolvency administrator, it has been established that there is a dispute over rights, and a request to resume proceedings has been made within the time limit set by the court.
(With amendments made by the Law of 18.04.2013, which enters into force on 22.05.2013.)

25. Chapter
Leaving a Claim Without Examination

### 219. Section. Court's Duty to Leave a Claim Without Examination

(1) The court shall leave a claim without examination if:

1) the claimant has not complied with the procedure for prior out-of-court examination of the case established for the relevant category of cases or has not taken the measures provided for by law to settle his or her dispute with the defendant before bringing the claim;

2) the statement of claim has been submitted by a person who does not have civil procedural capacity;

3) the claim has been brought in the name of the claimant by a person who is not authorised to do so in the manner prescribed by law;

4) a dispute in the claim case between the same parties, on the same subject matter and on the same grounds is being examined by the same or another court;

5) in accordance with international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia and European Union legal norms, the case does not fall within the jurisdiction of a Latvian court;

6) the parties have agreed in the manner prescribed by law to resolve the dispute using mediation, except for an employee's claim arising from employment legal relations, and no evidence has been submitted that the proposal to resolve the dispute using mediation has been rejected or that a mediation agreement has not been concluded, or that mediation has ended without reaching an agreement.

(2) The court shall leave the claim without examination in the part for which a European payment order is not issued in the case provided for in Article 10(2) of European Parliament and Council Regulation No 1896/2006.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 05.02.2009, 29.11.2012 and 22.05.2014, which enters into force on 18.06.2014.)

### 220. Section. Court's Right to Leave a Claim Without Examination

The court may leave a claim without examination if:

1) the claimant or his or her representative repeatedly fails to appear in court and has not requested that the case be examined in his or her absence;

2) a person who is one of the parties to the case has died and within one year from the suspension of proceedings no succession case for this person has been initiated.
(In the wording of the Law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 221. Section. Decision on Leaving a Claim Without Examination

(1) The court shall adopt a reasoned decision on leaving a claim without examination in the form of a separate procedural document.

(2) An appeal may be lodged against the court's decision to leave a claim without examination.

### 222. Section. Consequences of Leaving a Claim Without Examination

If a claim has been left without examination, the claimant is entitled to submit a statement of claim to the court again, observing the procedure prescribed by law.

26. Chapter Termination of Proceedings

### 223. Section. Grounds for Termination of Proceedings

The court shall terminate proceedings in a case if:

1) the examination of the case is not subject to the court;

2) the claim has been brought by a person who does not have the right to bring a claim;

3) a court judgment that has entered into legal force has been delivered in a dispute between the same parties, on the same subject matter and on the same grounds, or a court decision terminating proceedings has been adopted;

4) the claimant has withdrawn the claim;

5) the parties have concluded a settlement and the court has approved it;

6) the parties have agreed in the manner prescribed by law to refer the dispute for examination to an arbitral tribunal;

7) the natural person who is one of the parties to the case has died and the disputed legal relationship does not allow succession of rights;

8) the legal person who is one of the parties to the case has ceased to exist and there is no successor in title;

9) natural person's insolvency proceedings have been terminated and in accordance with Section 164 of the Insolvency Law the natural person has been released from the relevant obligations;

10) the debtor's insolvency administrator has submitted a request in a claim for the exclusion of that debtor from another company, which has been brought in accordance with Sections 136.1 and 195 of the Commercial Law.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 18.04.2013 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. Paragraph 10 in the part on termination of proceedings in a case if the debtor's insolvency administrator has submitted a request in a claim for the exclusion of that debtor from another company, which has been brought in accordance with Section 136.1 of the Commercial Law, enters into force on 01.07.2023. See transitional provision paragraph 180)

### 224. Section. Decision on Termination of Proceedings

(1) Proceedings shall be terminated by a reasoned court decision, which shall be adopted in the form of a separate procedural document.

(2) An appeal may be lodged against the court's decision to terminate proceedings.

### 225. Section. Consequences of Termination of Proceedings

If proceedings have been terminated, repeated recourse to the court in a dispute between the same parties, on the same subject matter and on the same grounds is not permitted.

27. Chapter Settlement

### 226. Section. Agreement on Settlement

(1) A settlement is permitted at any stage of the proceedings.

(2) A settlement is permitted in any civil dispute, except in the cases provided for in this Law.

(3) A settlement is not permitted:

1) in disputes related to amendments to civil status registers;

2) in disputes related to the proprietary rights of persons under guardianship or curatorship;

3) in disputes concerning immovable property if among the participants there are persons whose rights to acquire immovable property in ownership or possession are restricted in the manner prescribed by law;

4) if the terms of the settlement infringe the rights or legally protected interests of other persons.

### 227. Section. Conclusion of a settlement

(1) The parties conclude the settlement in writing and submit it to the court.

(2) The settlement shall indicate:

1) the claimant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; if the claimant is a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;

2) the defendant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address (addresses) indicated in the declaration and place of residence, if they are known, but if the defendant is a legal person — its name,

registration number and legal address;

3) the subject matter of the dispute;

4) the obligations of each party that it voluntarily undertakes to perform.

(3) The court may approve the settlement without the presence of a party at a court hearing or in written proceedings if the settlement has been made before a notary in the form of a notarial deed and contains a statement by the parties that they are aware of the procedural consequences of approving the settlement.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015. and 04.02.2016., which enter into force on 29.02.2016.)

### 228. Section. Court decision on approval of settlement

(1) Upon receiving the parties' settlement, the court shall ascertain whether the parties have voluntarily agreed to the settlement, whether it complies with the requirements of Sections 226 and 227 of this law and whether the parties are aware of the procedural consequences of approving the settlement.

(2) If the court finds that the settlement complies with the requirements of this law, it shall adopt a decision approving the settlement and terminating the proceedings in the case.

(3) A settlement approved by a court decision shall be enforceable in accordance with the rules for enforcement of court judgments.

28. Chapter Court decision

### 229. Section. Adoption of a decision

(1) A court ruling by which a case is not decided on the merits shall be adopted in the form of a decision.

(2) A decision shall be drawn up in the form of a separate procedural document or recorded in the minutes of the court hearing and announced after its adoption. In cases provided for in this law, a decision may be drawn up in the form of a resolution. In such a case, only the time and place of adoption of the decision, the name and composition of the court, as well as the ruling of the court or judge shall be indicated.

(3) In the form of a separate procedural document, a court decision shall be drawn up in cases provided for in this law.

(4) A decision may be adopted regarding a judge's procedural action outside a court hearing, which shall be drawn up in the form of a separate procedural document.
(With amendments made by the laws of 15.03.2012., 29.10.2015. and 25.10.2018., which enter into force on 28.11.2018.)

### 230. Section. Form and content of a decision

(1) A decision shall consist of an introductory part, a descriptive part, a reasoning part and an operative part.

(2) The introductory part shall indicate the time and place of adoption of the decision, the name and composition of the court, the parties to the case and the subject matter of the dispute.

(3) The descriptive part shall indicate the issues on which the decision has been adopted.

(4) The reasoning part shall indicate the established facts, the evidence on which the conclusions and arguments of the court or judge are based, as well as the normative acts by which the court has been guided.

(5) The operative part shall indicate the ruling of the court or judge and the procedure and time limits for appealing the decision.

(6) In decisions that are necessary for a bailiff, additional information shall be provided about the parties to the case [natural person
— claimant or applicant — name, surname, personal identity number (if known) and declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; natural person — defendant — name, surname, personal identity number (if known), declared place of residence, additional address (addresses) indicated in the declaration and place of residence, if known; legal person — name, legal address and registration number].

(In the wording of the law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

230.1 Section. Abbreviated decision

(1) The court shall draw up an abbreviated decision:

1) on granting an application for undisputed enforcement of obligations;

2) on granting or partially granting an application for enforcement of obligations in warning procedure
— with respect to the granted part;

3) on approving a settlement concluded by the parties.

(2) An abbreviated decision shall be drawn up in accordance with the requirements of Section 230 of this law, except for the reasoning part, which shall indicate only the normative acts by which the court has been guided.

(3) The abbreviated decision referred to in paragraph 3 of the first part of this section shall be announced and sent in accordance with Section 231 of this law.
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 231. Section. Announcement and sending of a decision

(1) The court shall announce the decision at a court hearing by reading its introductory part and operative part or by setting a date within the next 14 days when the decision will be available in the online system. The date when the decision is available in the online system shall be considered the date of announcement of the decision. A decision adopted in written proceedings shall be considered drawn up on the date when it is available in the online system. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the decision to the online system on the date of announcement or drawing up of the decision, the decision shall be available at the court registry on the same date. In such a case, the date when the decision is available at the court registry shall be considered the date of announcement or drawing up of the decision.

(2) A court decision shall be sent within three days after the announcement of the decision to a party to the case who has not participated in the court hearing and to a person to whom it relates. A decision adopted in written proceedings shall be sent within three days from the drawing up of the decision.

(3) If a court decision in the cases referred to in the first and second parts of this section has been sent to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law and in cases provided for in this law a translation must be attached to the court decision, the court shall send the decision together with the translation immediately after the preparation of the translation.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 29.10.2015., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 232. Section. Supplementary decision of the court

(1) If, when examining a case, circumstances are established that indicate a possible violation of law, the court shall be entitled to adopt a supplementary decision, which shall be sent to the relevant institution.

(2) A supplementary decision of the court shall not be subject to appeal.

28.1 Chapter
Appeal of actions of a sworn notary

## (Chapter 15

In the wording of the law of 06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

232.1 Section. Jurisdiction of the court over complaints about actions of a sworn notary and procedure for submission

A complaint about the actions of a sworn notary in performing official duties, as well as a complaint about refusal to perform these duties, shall be submitted by a person whose rights have been affected to the district (city) court at the address of the sworn notary's place of practice within 30 days from the day when the sworn notary performed the action about which the complaint has been submitted or when he or she

refused to perform such an action.
(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

232.2 Section. Procedure for examining complaints

(1) The court shall examine a complaint within 30 days from the date of receipt of the complaint.

(2) The court shall examine a complaint in written proceedings without holding a court hearing, except when it considers it necessary to examine the case at a court hearing or when the complainant, sworn notary or other interested persons request that the case be examined at a court hearing, substantiating their request. The complainant, sworn notary and other interested persons shall be invited to the court hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examining the matter.

(3) The court shall send a copy of the decision adopted after examining the complaint to the complainant, sworn notary and other interested persons.
(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

232. 3 Section. Appeal of decisions adopted on complaints

(1) An appeal may be submitted against a court decision within the time limit and in the manner prescribed by this law.

(2) A court decision by which a complaint about the actions of a sworn notary in performing official duties in a case on the discharge of a natural person from debt obligations has been examined shall not be subject to appeal.
(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

Fifth Part
Specific features of examination of certain categories of cases

29. Chapter
Cases on non-existence or dissolution of marriage


This excerpt sits under: Publisher: Saeima Type: law Adopted: 14.10.1998. > (Chapter 31

### 233. Section. Procedure for Hearing Cases

Cases concerning the nullity or dissolution of marriage shall be heard by the court in the procedure of a claim according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

### 234. Section. Jurisdiction of Cases

A claim concerning the nullity of marriage or dissolution of marriage may also be brought before a court according to the plaintiff's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the plaintiff's place of residence, if:

1)	the plaintiff has minor children;  

2)	(deleted by the law of 29.11.2012.);  

3)	the marriage is to be dissolved with a person serving a sentence in a place of deprivation of liberty;  

4)	the marriage is to be dissolved with a person who has no declared place of residence and whose place of residence is unknown or who lives abroad.  
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 235. Section. Cases Concerning Dissolution of Marriage upon Application of Both Spouses

(Deleted by the law of 28.10.2010., which comes into force on 01.02.2011.)

235.	1 Section. Statement of Claim Concerning Dissolution of Marriage

In the statement of claim, in addition to that provided for in Section 128 of this law, the following shall be indicated:

1)	from what time the parties have lived separately;  

2)	whether the other spouse consents to the dissolution of marriage;  

3)	whether the parties have agreed on the custody of the child, the procedure for exercising the other parent's contact rights, maintenance and the division of property acquired during the marriage, or submit respective claims.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the law of 19.06.2003., which comes into force on 24.07.2003.)

### 236. Section. Participation of Parties in Court Session

(1)	A case concerning dissolution of marriage shall be heard with the participation of both parties.  

(11) Upon the request of one spouse, the court may hear each spouse in a separate court session if the dissolution of marriage is related to violence against the spouse who requests the dissolution of marriage, or against his or her child, or the spouses' common child.  

(2)	If the defendant fails to appear upon the court's summons without a valid reason, if it has been sent to the official electronic address or by registered mail, he or she may be brought to court by force.  

(3)	If one of the parties lives far away or for another reason cannot appear upon the court's summons, the court may recognise that written explanations of this party or the participation of its representative are sufficient for hearing the case.  

(4)	If the defendant's place of residence is unknown or it is not in Latvia, the case may be heard without the defendant's participation if he or she has been summoned to court in the procedure prescribed by law.  

(5)	In a case concerning dissolution or nullity of marriage, the representative of a party must be specially authorised to conduct this case. The authorisation for representation in a case concerning dissolution or nullity of marriage also extends to all other claims related thereto.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003., 29.11.2012., 23.11.2016. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 237. Section. Bringing a Claim Concerning Nullity of Marriage

A claim concerning the nullity of marriage may be brought by an interested person and the prosecutor.

### 238. Section. Prohibition of Division of Claim

(1)	In a case concerning dissolution or nullity of marriage, claims arising from family legal relations shall be adjudicated simultaneously. Such claims are disputes concerning:

1)	the establishment of custody;  

2)	the exercise of contact rights;  

3)	maintenance for a child, including maintenance in the minimum amount determined by the Cabinet of Ministers;  

4)	means for ensuring the previous standard of living of a spouse;  

5)	the common family dwelling and household or personal use items;  

6)	the division of spouses' property (also if it affects a third party).  

(2)	(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015.)

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015.)

(4)	(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015.)

(5)	(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015.)
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006., 04.08.2011., 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015. and
08.12.2016., which comes into force on 04.01.2017.)

238.	1 Section. Interim Decision in Certain Claims

(1)	Upon a party's request, the court or judge may adopt a decision by which, temporarily until the judgment is rendered concerning the dissolution of marriage or nullity of marriage, the child's place of residence, the procedure for the child's care, the procedure for exercising contact rights, maintenance for the child, a prohibition on the child's removal from the country, means for ensuring the other spouse's previous standard of living, the procedure for using the spouses' common dwelling are determined, or one party is ordered to deliver household and personal use items to the other party.  

(2)	A request concerning maintenance for a child and means for ensuring a spouse's previous standard of living shall be heard in written proceedings.  

(3)	A request concerning the child's place of residence, the procedure for the child's care, the procedure for exercising contact rights, a prohibition on the child's removal from the country, the procedure for using the spouses' common dwelling, or an order for one party to deliver household and personal use items to the other party shall be heard in a court session.  

(4)	In claims affecting a child (concerning the child's place of residence, the procedure for the child's care, the procedure for exercising contact rights, a prohibition on the child's removal from the country), a representative of the orphan's court, upon the court's request, shall provide any information that is relevant in the case concerning:

1)	the living conditions of the parties;  

2)	the child's opinion, if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity;  

3)	the child's contact with the parties and other persons who live or are known to be going to live with the child in one household;  

4)	the child's health care and education;  

5)	the parties' cooperation with the social service;  

6)	persons who live or are known to be going to live with the child in one household;  

7)	the parties' violence against the child or the child's parent.  

(5)	The parties shall be notified of the court session, but in claims affecting a child — a representative of the orphan's court shall be summoned to the court session. If the court considers it necessary to clarify the information provided by the orphan's court, it shall ascertain the child's opinion if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity. The non-appearance of the other spouse is not an obstacle to hearing the claim.  

(6)	If in claims concerning the procedure for exercising contact rights the court, upon a participant's request or on its own initiative, establishes that contact rights are to be exercised in the presence of a contact person, the court shall invite the contact person to participate in the court session. The court shall ascertain whether the contact person consents to contact rights being exercised in its presence.  

(7)	The court or judge shall hear the party's request and adopt a decision within one month from the date of receipt of the request. The decision shall be enforceable immediately. The decision shall lose force when a judgment enters into force in the case or when another decision is adopted, except in cases when the decision is enforceable immediately.  

(8)	A judge's decision concerning the claims referred to in Paragraph two of this Section is not subject to appeal. An interlocutory appeal may be filed against a court decision in a case concerning the claims referred to in Paragraph three of this Section.  

(9)	Upon a party's reasoned request, the court may review a decision concerning the request referred to in Paragraph three of this Section if circumstances have substantially changed and it is in the child's interests. Such a court decision is not subject to appeal.  

(10)	If the court does not establish grounds for reviewing the decision or adopting a new decision, or considers that it may commence hearing the case on the merits, it shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application. The court shall adopt the decision to refuse to accept the application in the form of a resolution, and it is not subject to appeal.  
(In the wording of the law of 29.10.2015. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 239. Section. Preparation and Examination of Divorce Cases

(1) In a case concerning divorce or non-existence of marriage, the court shall require evidence on its own initiative, in particular for the resolution of issues concerning the interests of the child.

(2) In matters concerning the granting of custody rights, child care and the procedure for exercising contact rights, the court shall request the opinion of the orphan's court and invite its representative to participate in the court hearing, as well as ascertain the child's opinion if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity.

(3) Divorce cases shall be examined and the judgment shall be announced in a closed court hearing. Copies of documents (full text of documents) shall be issued to third parties only if it directly relates to those persons.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006., 04.08.2011. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 240. Section. Postponement of Examination of Divorce Cases

(1) The court shall postpone the examination of the case on its own initiative in order to restore the cohabitation of the spouses or to facilitate a peaceful resolution of the case.

(2) The court may not postpone the examination of the case if the parties have lived separately for more than one year, if both parties object to the postponement of the examination, or if the divorce is related to violence against the spouse who requests the divorce, or against his or her child, or the common child of the spouses.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

### 241. Section. Settlement and Reconciliation of Parties

(1) In cases concerning divorce or non-existence of marriage, settlement by the parties is permissible only in disputes related to family legal relations (first part of Section 238).

(2) Withdrawal of a divorce claim or termination of proceedings concerning divorce shall not be an obstacle to the examination of other claims on the merits.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 242. Section. Court Judgment in Divorce Cases

When rendering a judgment in a divorce case, the court:

1) shall adjudicate all claims arising from family legal relations and for which actions have been brought;

2) shall determine whether the party who changed his or her surname upon entering into marriage shall be granted the pre-marital surname;

3) shall divide the litigation costs between the parties, excluding security deposit, taking into account their financial situation.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 243. Section. Court Judgment in Cases Concerning Non-existence of Marriage

When rendering a judgment on the non-existence of marriage, the court shall indicate in the judgment:

1) the basis for the non-existence of marriage in accordance with Sections 60 to 67 of the Civil Law;

2) whether the party who changed his or her surname upon entering into marriage shall be granted the pre-marital surname or retain the marital surname;

3) with which of the parents and which children shall remain, if there is a dispute about it;

4) from which of the parents and in what amount maintenance for the child shall be recovered, if there is a dispute about it.

### 244. Section. Sending and Issuing of Judgment

(1) After the judgment concerning the non-existence or dissolution of marriage has entered into legal force, the judgment or an extract from such judgment shall be sent to the civil registry office where the relevant civil status register is kept, but if the marriage was concluded before a clergyman, to the relevant church (parish clergyman) and to the civil registry office in whose area of operation the church (parish) is located.

(2) In a case where the defendant has no declared place of residence and his or her place of residence is not known, the court shall announce the non-existence of marriage in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(3) The court shall issue to the former spouses the judgment by which the marriage has been dissolved or declared invalid.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 29.1
Cases Arising from Custody and Contact Rights

## (Chapter 07

In the wording of the 09.2006. law, which comes into force on 11.10.2006.)

244.1 Article. Procedure for hearing cases

Cases arising from custody and contact rights shall be heard by the court in claim proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

244.2 Article. Filing a claim

(1) A claim in cases arising from custody rights may be filed by the child's parents, guardians, orphan's court or prosecutor.

(2) A claim in cases arising from contact rights may be filed by the persons specified in Article 181 of the Civil Law, as well as by a prosecutor or orphan's court.

(3) In cases arising from contact rights, the claimant in the statement of claim, in addition to that mentioned in Article 128 of this law, shall indicate:

1) the procedure, time and place for exercising contact rights;

2) if the claimant requests that contact rights be exercised in the presence of a contact person — information about the respective contact person (for natural persons — name, surname, personal identity number and address, for legal persons — name, legal address and registration number).

(4) If a claim in a case arising from custody rights is filed in accordance with point 5 of Article 29 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 of 25 June 2019 on jurisdiction, the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial matters and matters of parental responsibility, and on international child abduction (hereinafter — Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111), the claimant shall attach to the statement of claim, in addition to the documents mentioned in Article 129 of this law, the documents mentioned in point 5 of Article 29 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015. and 16.06.2022., which come into force on 07.07.2022. Part four comes into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision point 177)

244.3 Article. Jurisdiction of cases

(1) A claim in cases arising from custody and contact rights shall be filed in court according to the child's place of residence.

(11) The child's place of residence in cases arising from custody and contact rights shall be considered to be the declared place of residence of his or her parents. If the declared places of residence of the child's parents are located in different administrative territories, the child's place of residence shall be considered to be the declared place of residence of the parent with whom he or she lives. If the child's parents or the child do not have a declared place of residence, the child's place of residence shall be considered to be the place of residence of his or her parents.

(2) If cases arising from custody or contact rights are to be heard together with a case on divorce or nullity of marriage, the provisions of Chapter 29 of this law shall apply.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

244.4 Article. Participation of parties in court session

(1) A case arising from custody or contact rights shall be heard with the participation of the parties.

(11) If a claim for deprivation of custody rights has been filed by an orphan's court, the case may be heard without the participation of the defendant if he or she has been summoned to court in the manner prescribed by law.

(2) If the defendant does not appear following a court summons without a valid reason, he or she may be brought to court by force.

(3) If one of the parties lives far away or for another reason cannot appear following a court summons, the court may consider that a written explanation from this party or the participation of its representative is sufficient for hearing the case.

(4) If the defendant's place of residence is not known or is not located in Latvia, the case may be heard without the participation of the defendant if he or she has been summoned to court in the manner prescribed by law.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

244.5 Article. Preparation of cases for hearing and their hearing
(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015., which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

244.6 Article. Settlement between parties
(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015., which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

244.7 Article. Consequences of court judgment
(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015., which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

244.8 Article. Contact person

(1) A contact person is a participant in a case in cases arising from contact rights. A contact person has the following procedural rights and obligations:

1) the right to become acquainted with the request for summoning a contact person to participate in the case;

2) the right to participate in a court session;

3) the right to express consent to or objections against obligations being imposed on him or her by a decision;

4) the right to receive a court judgment or decision;

5) the obligation to appear in court following a court summons;

6) the obligation to notify in writing in a timely manner of reasons why he or she cannot appear at a court session, submitting evidence thereof;

7) to appeal a court judgment and decision in the part relating to the contact person.

(2) A contact person shall be summoned to participate in a case on the initiative of a participant in the case or the court.
(In the wording of the 29.10.2015. law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

244.9 Article. Preparation of cases for hearing and their hearing

(1) In a case arising from custody or contact rights, the court shall request evidence on its own initiative or at the request of a participant in the case.

(2) In a case arising from custody or contact rights, the court shall request the opinion of the respective orphan's court on its own initiative or at the request of a participant in the case and shall invite its representative to participate in the court session, as well as ascertain the child's view if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity.

(3) If in a case arising from contact rights the court, at the request of a participant in the case or on its own initiative, establishes that contact rights are to be exercised in the presence of a contact person, the court shall summon the contact person to participate in the court session. The court shall ascertain whether the contact person consents to contact rights being exercised in his or her presence.

(4) Upon commencing the hearing of the case on the merits, the court shall hear the contact person. The contact person shall not participate in the further hearing of the case on the merits.

(5) When hearing cases arising from custody or contact rights, the court shall, in addition to other circumstances, take into account all instances where the person who wishes to exercise custody or contact rights has used violence against the child or the child's parent. When hearing cases arising from custody rights, the court shall, in addition to other circumstances, take into account violations of the procedure for exercising contact rights established by it.

(6) The court, in cases provided for in international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia or in European Union legal norms, on its own initiative or at the request of a participant in the case, may adopt a decision on taking over the case for hearing in Latvia or transferring the case for hearing to a court in another country if the court of the respective country has agreed to transfer or take over international jurisdiction in the respective case.

(7) (Deleted by the law of 16.06.2022.)
(In the wording of the 29.10.2015. law with amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022., which comes into force on 07.07.2022.)

244.10 Article. Interim decision

(1) At the request of a party, the court or judge shall adopt a decision temporarily establishing, until the judgment is rendered, the child's place of residence, the procedure for caring for the child, the procedure for exercising contact rights, maintenance for the child, a prohibition on taking the child out of the country.

(2) A request for maintenance for the child shall be heard in written proceedings.

(3) A request for the child's place of residence, the procedure for caring for the child, the procedure for exercising contact rights, a prohibition on taking the child out of the country shall be heard in a court session.

(4) A representative of the orphan's court, at the request of the court, shall provide any information that is relevant in a case concerning:

1) the living conditions of the parties;

2) the child's view, if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity;

3) the child's contact with the parties and other persons who live or are known to be going to live with the child in one household;

4) the child's health care and education;

5) the cooperation of the parties with the social service;

6) persons who live or are known to be going to live with the child in one household;

7) violence by the parties against the child or the child's parent.

(5) The parties shall be notified of the court session and a representative of the orphan's court shall be invited to the court session. If the court considers it necessary to clarify the information provided by the orphan's court, it shall ascertain the child's view if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity. The non-appearance of the other party is not an obstacle to hearing the matter.

(6) If in claims concerning the procedure for exercising contact rights the court, at the request of a participant in the case or on its own initiative, establishes that contact rights are to be exercised in the presence of a contact person, it shall summon the contact person to participate in the court session. The court shall ascertain whether the contact person consents to contact rights being exercised in his or her presence.

(7) The court or judge shall hear the party's request and adopt a decision within one month from the date of receipt of the request. The decision shall be enforceable immediately. The decision shall lose force when a judgment in the case enters into force or when another decision is adopted, except in cases where the decision is enforceable immediately.

(8) A judge's decision on the claim mentioned in part two of this Article is not subject to appeal. An ancillary complaint may be filed against a court decision in a case concerning the claims mentioned in part three of this Article.

(9) The court, at the reasoned request of a party, may review a decision on the request mentioned in part three of this Article if circumstances have changed substantially and it is in the interests of the child. Such a court decision is not subject to appeal.

(10) If the court does not establish grounds for reviewing the decision or adopting a new decision or considers that it can commence hearing the case on the merits, it shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application. The court shall adopt the decision to refuse to accept the application in the form of a resolution, and it is not subject to appeal.
(In the wording of the 29.10.2015. law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

244.11 Article. Settlement between parties

(1) In cases arising from custody and contact rights, the parties are entitled to conclude a settlement.

(2) A settlement shall be approved, with the court requesting the opinion of the respective orphan's court on its own initiative or inviting its representative to participate in the court session.
(In the wording of the 29.10.2015. law, which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

244.12 Article. Court decision in cases arising from custody and contact rights

(1) In cases arising from contact rights, in addition to that provided for in Article 193 or Article 230 of this law, the court decision shall indicate:

1) information about the child — name, surname, personal identity number and place of residence;

2) the procedure, time and place for exercising contact rights;

3) if necessary, the obligations of the parties and the distribution of expenses between the parties for exercising contact rights;

4) if necessary, the restrictions mentioned in Article 182 of the Civil Law;

5) if necessary, other obligations of the parties.

(2) In cases arising from custody rights, in addition to that provided for in Article 193 or Article 230 of this law, the court decision shall indicate information about the child — name, surname, personal identity number and place of residence.

(3) In cases arising from custody and contact rights, the court shall warn the parties in the decision that if the judgment is not complied with voluntarily, a fine will be imposed in accordance with this law, the question of suspension or deprivation of custody rights will be decided, and the party will be liable under the Criminal Law for malicious non-compliance with the decision.
(In the wording of the 29.10.2015. law, which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

244.13 Article. Claims arising from impossibility of enforcing a decision on exercising contact rights

(1) If a bailiff establishes in accordance with Article 620.27 of this law that enforcement of the decision is not possible, the creditor may request the court to review the time and place for exercising contact rights established in the decision.

(2) The request mentioned in part one of this Article shall be submitted to the court that rendered the decision in the case arising from contact rights, or in whose territory of operation the decision is to be enforced if enforcement of a foreign court decision is not possible.

(3) The court shall request from the orphan's court, which evaluated the debtor's conduct in accordance with Article 620.26 of this law, information about the child's daily routine.

(4) The court, having received information that it is not possible for the orphan's court to ascertain the child's daily routine because the child's whereabouts are not known, shall adopt a decision on searching for the child or the debtor and the child with the assistance of the police.

(5) A request to review the time and place for exercising contact rights shall be heard in a court session, having previously notified the participants in the case thereof. The non-appearance of the other party is not an obstacle to hearing the application.

(6) The court, on its own initiative or at the request of interested persons, shall request that the bailiff who established in accordance with Article 620.27 of this law that enforcement of the decision is not possible provide information about the circumstances established in the enforcement case, including obstacles to enforcing the decision.

(7) The court shall invite a representative of the orphan's court to participate in the court session, as well as a psychologist if the orphan's court has summoned one or if the court considers it necessary.

(8) If the court, at the request of a participant in the case or on its own initiative, establishes that contact rights are to be exercised in the presence of a contact person, it shall summon the contact person to participate in the court session. The court shall ascertain whether the contact person consents to contact rights being exercised in his or her presence.

(9) The court shall adopt a decision on reviewing the time and place for exercising contact rights within one month, unless extraordinary circumstances make it impossible. The decision shall be enforceable immediately.

(10) The court, having established that there are circumstances that make enforcement of the decision difficult or impossible, may, in the interests of the child, establish a different procedure for exercising contact rights in the decision on reviewing the time and place for exercising contact rights.

(11) If exercising contact rights is not possible otherwise than by entering premises and it is foreseeable that the bailiff will not be allowed into the premises about which there is information that the child is located therein, the court may indicate in the decision on reviewing the time and place for contact rights that, in the interests of the child, the premises may be opened by force. In such a case, the court shall indicate in the decision the address of the respective premises and the time period during which the premises may be opened by force.

(12) If the court has indicated in the decision on reviewing the time and place for contact rights that, in the interests of the child, the premises may be opened by force, the decision shall be announced in the absence of the defendant, and the decision shall be sent to the defendant after the time period indicated in the decision for opening the premises by force has passed.

(13) If the court establishes that circumstances have changed so substantially that it is not possible to adopt a decision on reviewing the time and place for contact rights established in the judgment, the court shall reject the creditor's request and inform the creditor of his or her right to file a new claim in court in the general procedure. A change in the time and place for exercising contact rights shall not be considered a substantial change of circumstances if contact rights are preserved in the previous scope.

(14) A decision on reviewing the time and place for exercising contact rights is not subject to appeal. An ancillary complaint may be filed against a court decision rejecting the creditor's request to review the time and place for exercising contact rights established in an interim decision.
(In the wording of the 29.10.2015. law with amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022., which comes into force on 07.07.2022.)

244.14 Article. Consequences of court judgment

If, after a judgment in a case arising from custody or contact rights has entered into legal force, circumstances change, each party is entitled to file a new claim in court in the general procedure.
(In the wording of the 29.10.2015. law, which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

30. Chapter
Cases on establishing a child's origin


This excerpt sits under: Publisher: Saeima Type: law Adopted: 14.10.1998.

## (Chapter 19

Edition of the 06.2003. law, which comes into force on 24.07.2003.)

### Section 245. Procedure for Hearing Cases

The court hears cases concerning the determination of a child's origin or the contestation of paternity according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

### Section 246. Persons Who May Contest the Presumption of Paternity

(1)	The presumption of paternity may be contested in court by the child's mother, the child's mother's husband and the child himself or herself after reaching the age of majority.  

(2)	After the death of the child's mother's husband, such an action may be brought by the husband's parents if the husband did not know about the child's birth until the moment of death.  

(3)	After the death of the child's mother's husband, his legal heirs may enter the proceedings initiated by him as successors in title.  

(4)	If the presumption of paternity is contested by a person for whom guardianship has been established, a representative of the orphan's court shall be summoned to participate in the case.  

(5)	The action referred to in this Section may be brought in accordance with the provisions of Section 149 of the Civil Law.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006. and 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

### Section 247. Persons Who May Contest the Acknowledgement of Paternity

(1)	Paternity that has been acknowledged and registered in the civil registry office may be contested by the person who acknowledged paternity, the child's mother or a person who considers himself or herself to be the child's father.  

(2)	The child himself or herself may bring such an action after reaching the age of majority.  

(3)	After the death of the child's father, his legal heirs may enter the proceedings initiated by him as successors in title.  

(4)	Paternity that has been determined by a court judgment that has entered into legal force may not be contested.  

(5)	The action referred to in this Section may be brought in accordance with the provisions of Section 156 of the Civil Law.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 22.05.2014., which comes into force on 18.06.2014.)

### Section 248. Persons Who May Bring an Action for the Determination of Paternity

(1)	An action to determine the paternity of a child in court may be brought by the child's mother or the child's guardian, as well as the child's biological father.  

(2)	The child himself or herself may bring such an action after reaching the age of majority.  

(3)	The action referred to in this Section may be brought in accordance with the provisions of the first part of Section 158 of the Civil Law.

### Section 249. Procedure for Bringing an Action for the Determination of a Child's Paternity

(1)	The child's mother, the child himself or herself or his or her guardian may bring an action for the determination of paternity against the person from whom the child is descended.  

(2)	The person from whom the child is descended may bring an action for the determination of paternity against the child's mother in the event that she does not consent to the determination of paternity or there exist other obstacles specified by law to making an entry of paternity in the birth

register.  

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 07.09.2006.)

(4)	Claims for the contestation of the presumption of paternity and the determination of paternity may be joined.  
(With amendments made by the law of 07.09.2006., which comes into force on 11.10.2006.)

Section 249.1 Ordering of Forensic Examination

(1)	The court, at the request of a party to the case, orders an examination for the determination of the child's biological origin.  

(2)	If any of the parties to the case evades the examination, the court adopts a decision on the compulsory delivery of that person for the performance of the forensic examination.  

Section 249.2 Establishment of the Fact of Paternity

If the person from whom the child is descended has died, the fact of paternity may be established in special court proceedings.  

Section 249.3 Interim Decision

(1)	At the request of a party, the court or judge adopts a decision imposing a prohibition on the removal of the child from the country for the period until the rendering of the judgment in the case concerning the determination of the child's origin.  

(2)	The request for a prohibition on the removal of the child from the country shall be heard in a court session.  

(3)	A representative of the orphan's court, at the request of the court, shall provide information on the child's opinion, if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity, and other evidence that is relevant to the case.  

(4)	The parties shall be notified of the court session and a representative of the orphan's court shall be invited to the court session. If the court considers it necessary to clarify the information provided by the orphan's court, it shall ascertain the child's opinion, if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity. The non-appearance of the other party shall not be an obstacle to the hearing of the matter.  

(5)	The court or judge shall examine the party's request and adopt a decision within one month from the date of receipt of the request. The decision shall be enforceable immediately. The decision shall cease to have effect if another decision or judgment is adopted in the respective claim.  

(6)	An appeal may be lodged against the court's decision in the said claim.  
(Edition of the law of 29.10.2015., which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

Section 249.4 Opinion of the Orphan's Court

In a case concerning the contestation of the acknowledgement of paternity, the court, on its own initiative or at the request of interested persons, shall request the opinion of the relevant orphan's court and may invite its representative to participate in the court session.  
(Edition of the law of 29.10.2015., which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

### Section 250. Sending and Issuing of the Court Judgment

The court shall send the court judgment on the determination of paternity, the establishment of the fact of paternity and the declaration of the entry of paternity as invalid to the civil registry office where the child's birth was registered for amendment of the entry.  
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 30.1
Cases Concerning the Division of Inheritance

## (Chapter 31

Edition of law 10.2002, which enters into force 01.01.2003.)

Article 250.1 Jurisdiction

(1) An application for division of inheritance, if the heirs do not reach agreement on it in a domestic manner or before a notary, shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of one heir, but if there is none, — according to the place of residence, but if the composition of the inheritance includes immovable property, — according to its location.

(2) The application for division of inheritance shall indicate what property included in the inheritance is subject to division and which heirs claim it.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force 01.01.2013.)

Article 250.2 Actions of the judge in preparation of the case

(1) The judge shall set a preparatory hearing, of which the parties shall be notified.

(2) By decision of the judge, a notation of securing the claim or interim protection shall be made in the land register in accordance with the provisions on securing claims or interim protection.

(3) The judge may instruct the notary who issued the certificate of inheritance or the European Certificate of Succession, or another notary practising in the court district, to supervise the course of preparation of the inheritance division project.
(With amendments made by the laws of 28.05.2015 and 25.03.2021, which enters into force 20.04.2021.)

Article 250.3 Preparation of the inheritance division project

(1) The notary who has received the task to supervise the course of preparation of the inheritance division project shall, if necessary, invite a bailiff to prepare an inventory act of the inherited property and to carry out valuation of the property.

(2) The inventory of inherited property shall take place in accordance with the provisions of this law. The inventory act shall also indicate known debts, obligations and entries in the land register that encumber the inheritance.

(3) The notary shall take actions to bring the parties' views closer together and achieve agreement.

(4) The persons preparing the inheritance division project shall indicate in their opinion what justification they have taken into account.

(5) The notary shall submit the property inventory act, property valuation and inheritance division project to the judge.

Article 250.4 Actions of the judge after receipt of the inheritance division project

(1) The court shall send the documents submitted by the notary to the co-heirs and set a time limit for providing explanations.

(2) In addition to written explanations, the judge may invite all co-heirs for verification of calculations and clarification of the inheritance division project.
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.5 Sale of divisible property at auction

(1) Property shall be valued and sold at auction according to the general provisions of this law. If all heirs and in relevant cases also the orphan's court (Civil Law Articles 280.—283.) consent thereto, the property may be sold at a free price.

(2) The sale of immovable property for determination of its true value shall be carried out according to the provisions on voluntary sale at auction by judicial procedure, observing the provisions of Civil Law Articles 737 and 738, moreover, immovable property shall be inventoried and valued only if any of the co-heirs so requests.
(With amendments made by the law of 07.09.2006, which enters into force 11.10.2006. See transitional provisions.)

Article 250.6 State fee in property division cases

In property division cases, the state fee shall be divided among the heirs, taking into account the value of the property allocated to each.

Article 250.7 Division of common property

The provisions of this chapter shall also apply to the division of all types of common property, observing the provisions of the relevant laws in such division.

Chapter 30.2
Cases concerning infringement and protection of intellectual property rights

## (Chapter 14

Edition of law 12.2006, which enters into force 01.03.2007.)

Article 250.8 Procedure for Hearing Cases
