The court hears cases concerning infringement and protection of intellectual property rights in the procedure of claims according to general provisions, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

Article 250.9 Persons Who May Submit an Application Concerning Infringement and Protection of Intellectual Property Rights

An application concerning infringement and protection of intellectual property rights may be submitted by persons specified by law.

Article 250.10 Basis and Measures for Establishing Interim Protection

(1)	If there is reason to believe that the rights of an intellectual property rights holder are being infringed or could be infringed, the court, upon a reasoned application by the claimant, may adopt a decision on establishing an interim protection measure. The application for establishing an interim protection measure shall specify the interim protection measure.

(2)	It is permissible to examine the question of establishing an interim protection measure at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before bringing an action to court.

(3)	Interim protection measures are:

1)	seizure of movable property by which intellectual property rights are possibly being infringed;

2)	an obligation to recall goods by which intellectual property rights are possibly being infringed;

3)	a prohibition to perform certain actions both on the defendant and on persons whose services are used to infringe intellectual property rights, or persons who make possible the commission of such an infringement.

Article 250.11 Establishing an Interim Protection Measure Before Bringing an Action

(1)	Within three months from the day when the potential claimant learned of the infringement or possible infringement, he or she may request that an interim protection measure be established before bringing an action to court.

(2)	When submitting an application for establishing an interim protection measure before bringing an action, the potential claimant shall provide evidence confirming his or her intellectual property rights which are being infringed, and evidence that they are being infringed or could be infringed.

(3)	An application for establishing an interim protection measure before bringing an action shall be submitted to the court in which the action is to be brought.

(4)	When granting an application for establishing an interim protection measure before bringing an action, the judge shall set a time limit for the claimant to submit a statement of claim to the court, not exceeding 30 days.

Article 250.12 Examination of the Question of Establishing an Interim Protection Measure

(1)	The court or judge shall decide on an application for establishing an interim protection measure within 10 days after receipt of the application or initiation of the case, if the application is submitted simultaneously with bringing the action.

(2)	If delay could cause irreparable harm to the intellectual property rights holder, then the court or judge shall decide on the application for establishing an interim protection measure no later than the next day after receipt of the application, without prior notice to the defendant and other participants in the case. If a decision on establishing an interim protection measure is adopted without the presence of the defendant or other participants in the case, the defendant and other participants in the case shall be notified of this decision no earlier than the third day after adoption of the decision.

(3)	When granting an application for establishing an interim protection measure before bringing an action, the court or judge may instruct the claimant to secure damages that could arise for the defendant or other persons mentioned in paragraph 3 of the third part of Article 250.10 of this law in connection with the establishment of an interim protection measure, by depositing a specified sum of money in the bailiff's deposit account or providing an equivalent guarantee.

(4)	The court, upon application by the claimant, may replace the established interim protection measures with other measures.

(5)	Interim protection measures may be revoked by the same court upon application by a participant in the case.

(6)	When rejecting the claim, the court shall revoke the interim protection measure in the judgment. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force.

(7)	If the claim is left without examination or the proceedings are terminated, the court shall revoke the interim protection measure in the decision. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day the decision enters into legal force.

(8)	If a decision on establishing an interim protection measure is adopted before bringing an action and the action is not brought within the time limit set by the court, the judge, upon receipt of an application from the potential claimant or other potential participant in the case or the defendant, shall adopt a decision on revoking the interim protection measure.

(9)	The applications mentioned in the first, fourth and fifth parts of this article shall be decided in a court session, with prior notice to the participants in the case. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examination of the application.
(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.13 Appeal of Decisions Adopted Concerning Establishment of an Interim Protection Measure

(1)	A separate appeal may be submitted against the decisions mentioned in the fourth part of Article 250.12 of this law, a decision by which an application for establishing an interim protection measure is rejected, and a decision by which an application for revoking an interim protection measure is rejected.

(2)	If a decision on establishing an interim protection measure is adopted without the presence of a participant in the case, the time limit for submitting a separate appeal shall be counted from the day of issuance of the decision.
(With amendments made by the law of 04.08.2011, which enters into force 01.10.2011.)

Article 250.14 Execution of a Decision on Establishing an Interim Protection Measure

(1)	A decision on establishing an interim protection measure (first and second parts of Article 250.12) and a decision on revoking an interim protection measure (fifth part of Article 250.12) shall be executed immediately after its adoption.

(2)	A decision on establishing an interim protection measure adopted with the condition mentioned in the third part of Article 250.12 of this law shall be executed after the claimant has deposited the sum specified by the court or judge in the bailiff's deposit account or submitted an equivalent guarantee. The writ of execution shall be issued after deposit of the sum specified by the court or receipt of the equivalent guarantee.

(3)	A decision on establishing an interim protection measure by seizing movable property by which intellectual property rights are possibly being infringed shall be executed in the procedure specified in Chapter 71 of this law.

(4)	A decision on establishing an interim protection measure by establishing a prohibition to perform specific actions or an obligation to recall goods by which intellectual property rights are possibly being infringed shall be executed by the bailiff and in the procedure specified in Article 555 of this law the court decision shall be notified to the defendant or the relevant third party.

(5)	Revocation of an applied interim protection measure shall be executed pursuant to an order of the bailiff who executed the decision on establishing the interim protection measure.

(6)	A decision on replacing an interim protection measure shall be executed by the bailiff, first applying the replacement interim protection measure and then revoking the replaced interim protection measure.
(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.15 Compensation for Damages Caused by an Interim Protection Measure

The defendant is entitled to claim compensation for damages caused to him or her in connection with the establishment of an interim protection measure, if the interim protection measure is revoked in the case specified in the eighth part of Article 250.12 of this law, if the claim brought against him or her is rejected, left without examination or the proceedings are terminated in the cases specified in paragraphs 2 and 4 of Article 223 of this law.

Article 250.16 Right to Information

(1)	In cases concerning infringement of intellectual property rights, upon a reasoned request by the claimant, the court, observing the rights of participants in the case to protection of trade secrets, may request that information about the origin of goods or services and their distribution be provided by the defendant or a person:

1)	in whose possession are infringing goods (counterfeit copies) on a commercial scale;

2)	who on a commercial scale has provided or used services in connection with unlawful use of an intellectual property object;

3)	about whom the persons mentioned in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this part have provided information that it is involved in the production, distribution or offering of infringing goods (counterfeit copies) or the provision or offering of services related to unlawful use of an intellectual property object.

(2)	The information mentioned in the first part of this article shall specify information about the manufacturer, distributor, supplier, wholesaler and retailer of the relevant goods or the provider and distributor of the relevant services [for a natural person - name, surname, personal identity number (if it is known) and declared place of residence and place of residence, if it differs, for a legal person - name, legal address and registration number (if it is known)], information about the quantity of goods produced, distributed, received or ordered or services provided or ordered, as well as the price paid for them.

(3)	If there is obvious evidence of the fact of intellectual property infringement and the intellectual property rights holder has requested application of the securing of evidence, securing of the claim or establishment of an interim protection measure provided for in this law, then the intellectual property rights holder is entitled to request that the information mentioned in the first and second parts of this article also be secured before bringing an action to court within the framework of the procedure for securing evidence provided for in this law.
(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011 and 29.11.2012, which enter into force 01.01.2013.)

Article 250.17 Court Judgment in Cases of Infringement and Protection of Intellectual Property Rights

(1)	If the fact of infringement is proven, the court may establish in the judgment one or more of the following measures:

1)	cease and prohibit unlawful use of an intellectual property object;

2)	cease and prohibit measures that are recognisable as preparation for unlawful use of intellectual property objects;

3)	cease and prohibit the provision of services that are used for unlawful actions with intellectual property objects, to persons:

a)	whose services are used to infringe the rights of intellectual property holders,

b)	who make possible the commission of such an infringement;

4)	compensate in the procedure specified by law for damages and non-pecuniary harm caused in connection with unlawful use of an intellectual property object.

(2)	The court, upon application by the claimant, regardless of the harm caused to the claimant and compensation for harm, may establish one or more of the following measures to be carried out at the expense of the infringer:

1)	recall or completely withdraw from trade infringing goods (counterfeit copies);

2)	destroy infringing goods (counterfeit copies);

3)	recall or completely withdraw from trade or destroy devices and materials used or intended for the manufacture of infringing goods (counterfeit copies), if the owner knew or should have known from the circumstances of the case that these devices and materials were used or intended for the commission of unlawful actions;

4)	publish information about the judgment, including publish the court judgment in full or in part in the mass media.
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 30.3
Examination of Certain Categories of Cases in Written Proceedings

## (Chapter 08

In the wording of the 09.2011. law, which comes into force on 30.09.2011. Chapter title in the wording of the 10.12.2015. law, which comes into force on 01.01.2016.)

250.18 Article. Procedure for examination of cases

(1) Cases in simplified procedure and cases concerning rights in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board shall be examined by the court in claim proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

(2) The provisions of this chapter do not affect the application of Regulation No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council, except in the case specified in the second paragraph of Article 250.27 of this Law.

(3) Cases concerning rights in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board shall be examined by Riga City Court.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.03.2014., 10.12.2015., 14.12.2017. and 16.06.2022., which comes into force on 01.08.2022.)

250.19 Article. Initiation of cases

(1) Initiation and examination of cases in simplified procedure in the manner provided for in this chapter is permissible only in claims for recovery of money and recovery of maintenance (Article 35, paragraph 1, points 1 and 3).

(2) A judge shall initiate a case in simplified procedure on the basis of a written statement of claim if the principal debt or — in a claim for recovery of maintenance — the total amount of payments on the date of submission of the claim does not exceed 2500 euros. The total amount of payments in claims for recovery of maintenance shall apply to each child separately.

(21) The court shall initiate a case for recovery of maintenance for a child if:

1) the amount of the claim does not exceed the amount in which maintenance is paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund, and there exist the obstacles mentioned in the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Law which prevent a person from receiving maintenance from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund;

2) the amount of the claim exceeds the amount in which maintenance is paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund.

(3) Cases concerning rights in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board shall be initiated on the basis of a written statement of claim.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.09.2013., 10.12.2015., 08.12.2016., 14.12.2017. and 10.12.2020., which comes into force on 31.12.2020. Amendments to the second paragraph and paragraph 2.1 come into force on 01.01.2021. See transitional provision point 160)

250.20 Article. Content of statement of claim

(1) A statement of claim in simplified procedure shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(2) In the statement of claim, in addition to that specified in Article 128 of this Law, it shall be indicated whether the claimant requests a hearing of the case in a court session, substantiating his or her request.

(3) In the statement of claim in cases in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board, it shall be indicated how the incorrectness of the decision of the Industrial Property Appeal Board is manifested.

(4) The relevant decision of the Industrial Property Appeal Board shall be attached to the statement of claim in cases in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board. Evidence submitted to the Industrial Property Appeal Board need not be attached to the statement of claim.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015., 10.12.2015., 14.12.2017. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.21 Article. Sending of statement of claim and documents attached thereto to defendant

(1) Simultaneously with the sending of the statement of claim in simplified procedure to the defendant, an explanation form shall be sent, setting a time limit for submission of a written explanation — 30 days, counting from the day when the statement of claim in simplified procedure was sent to the defendant. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the statement of claim may also be sent to the defendant.

(2) The court shall additionally inform the defendant that failure to submit an explanation is not an obstacle to the making of a judgment in the case, and also that the defendant may request a hearing of the case in a court session.
(With amendments made by the laws of 10.12.2015., 14.12.2017., 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which comes into force on 07.07.2022.)

250.22 Article. Explanation of procedural rights to parties

(1) Simultaneously with the sending of documents to the parties (Article 148), the court shall explain to them the procedural rights, inform them of the composition of the court which will examine the case, and explain the right to challenge a judge.

(2) The civil procedural rights mentioned in this Law which are related to the preparation of a case for hearing may be exercised by the parties no later than seven days before the notified time for examination of the case (Article 250.25, paragraph 1).

250.23 Article. Defendant's explanation

(1) An explanation concerning a statement of claim in simplified procedure shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(2) In the explanation, the defendant shall indicate:

1) the name of the court to which the explanation has been submitted;

11) the claimant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;

12) the defendant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;

13) an e-mail address for communication with the court and, if he or she has registered his or her participation in the online system, also includes an indication of registration, if the defendant (or his or her representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia) agrees to electronic communication with the court. If the defendant's representative's address is outside Latvia, additionally an e-mail address shall be indicated or notification of registration of his or her participation in the online system shall be given;

14) the name of the credit institution and account number to which litigation costs are to be reimbursed;

2) (deleted by the law of 29.11.2012.);

3) the case number and subject matter of the claim;

4) whether he or she acknowledges the claim in full or in any part thereof;

5) his or her objections to the claim and the substantiation thereof, as well as the normative act on which they are based;

6) evidence confirming his or her objections to the claim;

7) requests for obtaining evidence;

8) whether he or she requests reimbursement of court costs;

9) whether he or she requests reimbursement of costs related to the conduct of the case, indicating the amount thereof and attaching documents substantiating the amount;

10) whether he or she requests a hearing of the case in a court session, substantiating his or her request;

11) other circumstances which he or she considers significant in the examination of the case;

12) other requests;

13) a list of documents attached to the explanation;

14) the time and place of drawing up the explanation.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015., 10.12.2015., 23.11.2016., 01.06.2017., 22.06.2017.,
14.12.2017. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.24 Article. Bringing of counterclaim

(1) The defendant is entitled to bring a counterclaim within the time limit set for giving an explanation.

(2) The court shall accept the counterclaim (Article 136, paragraph 3) and examine the case in the manner specified in Chapter 30.3 of this Law if the counterclaim complies with the amount of the claim specified in Article 250.19 of this Law and is drawn up in accordance with the provisions of Article 250.20 of this Law.

(3) The court shall accept the counterclaim (Article 136, paragraph 3), but continue to examine the case in claim proceedings according to general rules if the amount of the claim indicated in the counterclaim exceeds the amount of the claim specified in Article 250.19 of this Law or it is not a claim for recovery of money or recovery of maintenance (Article 35, paragraph 1, points 1 and 3).
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.25 Article. Examination of cases in written proceedings, drawing up, sending of judgment and request for drawing up of judgment

(1) If the court does not examine a case in simplified procedure in a court session in accordance with Article 250.26 of this Law, the case shall be examined

in written proceedings, notifying the parties in good time of the date when the summary judgment will be available in the online system, and also informing them of the composition of the court which will examine the case and explaining the right to challenge a judge. The date when the summary judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up of the judgment.

(11) If the court does not examine a case in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board in a court session in accordance with Article 250.26 of this Law, the case shall be examined in written proceedings, notifying the parties in good time of the date when the judgment will be available in the online system, and also informing them of the composition of the court which will examine the case and explaining the right to challenge a judge. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up of the judgment.

(2) (Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015.)

(21) The court shall draw up a judgment in a case in simplified procedure in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Article 193 of this Law if a party submits to it in writing a request for drawing up of a judgment. The request shall be submitted to the court within 10 days from the date of drawing up of the summary judgment, and the provision of the second sentence of the fourth paragraph of Article 48 of this Law does not apply to this time limit. The court may also on its own initiative draw up a judgment in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Article 193 of this Law in the manner specified in paragraph 2.3 of this Article.

(22) An unsigned request for drawing up of a judgment in a case in simplified procedure shall be considered not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter. A request for drawing up of a judgment which has been submitted after the expiry of the time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter. A decision on refusal to accept a request for drawing up of a judgment is not subject to appeal.

(23) In the case referred to in paragraph 2.1 of this Article, the judgment shall be drawn up within 20 days after the expiry of the time limit for submission of a request for drawing up of a judgment. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up of the judgment.

(3) At the written request of a party, the summary judgment or the judgment drawn up in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Article 193 of this Law shall be sent to the party without delay.

(4) (Deleted from 01.03.2018. by the law of 14.12.2017. See Transitional provision point 137)
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015., 10.12.2015., 14.12.2017., 25.10.2018., 28.02.2019. and 11.11.2021.
which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.26 Article. Hearing of cases in court session, drawing up, sending of judgment and request for drawing up of judgment

(1) The court, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter, shall hear a case in a court session if a substantiated request of a party has been received and the court considers it necessary to hear the case in a court session. The court may also hear a case in a court session on its own initiative. If the court refuses a request to hear a case in a court session, this shall be indicated in the judgment.

(2) When scheduling a case in simplified procedure for hearing in a court session, simultaneously with the summons the court shall notify that in the event that one of the parties does not appear at the court session, the court will complete the examination of the case in his or her absence, and shall set a date within the nearest 14 days after the notified date of the court session when the summary judgment will be available in the online system, and also explain the parties' right to submit a request for drawing up of a judgment.

(3) In a court session in a case in simplified procedure, the court shall set a date for drawing up of the summary judgment within the nearest 14 days when the summary judgment will be available in the online system. The date when the summary judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up of the summary judgment. The summary judgment shall also indicate the date when the judgment drawn up in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Article 193 of this Law will be available in the online system if a party has submitted a request for drawing up of a judgment.

(4) The court shall draw up a judgment in a case in simplified procedure in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Article 193 of this Law if a party submits to it in writing a request for drawing up of a judgment. The request shall be submitted to the court within 10 days from the date of drawing up of the summary judgment, and the provision of the second sentence of the fourth paragraph of Article 48 of this Law does not apply to this time limit. The court may also on its own initiative draw up a judgment in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Article 193 of this Law in the manner specified in the sixth paragraph of this Article.

(5) An unsigned request for drawing up of a judgment in a case in simplified procedure shall be considered not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter. A request for drawing up of a judgment which has been submitted after the expiry of the time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter. A decision on refusal to accept a request for drawing up of a judgment is not subject to appeal.

(6) If a request for drawing up of a judgment in a case in simplified procedure has been received, the court shall draw up the judgment in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Article 193 of this Law within 20 days after the expiry of the time limit specified in the fourth paragraph of this Article. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up of the judgment.

(7) At the written request of a party, the summary judgment or the judgment drawn up in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Article 193 of this Law shall be sent to the party without delay.
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the laws of 25.10.2018. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.27 Article. Content of summary judgment and entry into legal force of judgment

(1) In the operative part of the summary judgment, in addition to that specified in Article 194 of this Law, the court shall indicate that a request for drawing up of a judgment may be submitted within 10 days from the date of drawing up of the summary judgment, and also indicate the date when the judgment will be available in the online system if a party has submitted a request for drawing up of a judgment.

(2) A summary judgment in a case in simplified procedure shall enter into legal force after the expiry of the time limit for submission of a request for drawing up of a judgment and none of the parties has submitted a request for drawing up of a judgment. If, following a request for drawing up of a judgment, the court draws up a judgment, it shall enter into force in the manner specified in Article 203 of this Law.

(21) A court judgment in a case in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board shall enter into force in the manner specified in Article 203 of this Law.

(3) A court judgment drawn up in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Article 193 of this Law may be appealed by participants in the case by way of appeal within 20 days from the date of drawing up of the judgment if there exists one of the grounds for initiation of appeal proceedings specified in Article 440.2 of this Law.

(4) A participant in a case to whom a judgment has been sent in accordance with Article 56.2 of this Law may appeal the judgment by way of appeal within 20 days from the date of issue of a copy of the judgment.

(5) In cases concerning rights in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board, in the operative part of the judgment, in addition to that specified in the sixth paragraph of Article 193 of this Law, the court shall indicate the rights granted, confirmed or refused to a person or amendments to registration information in accordance with the provisions of normative acts.
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the laws of 25.10.2018. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.27A Article. Exception regarding availability of judgment

If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the judgment to the online system on the date of drawing up of the judgment, the judgment shall be available in the court office on the same date. The date of drawing up of the judgment in such a case shall be considered the date when the judgment is available in the court office.
(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

30.4 Chapter
Cases concerning recognition of decisions of meetings of participants (shareholders) of capital companies as invalid


This excerpt sits under: Publisher: Saeima Type: law Adopted: 14.10.1998.

## (Chapter 18

Version of the 04.2013 law, which enters into force on 22.05.2013. The provisions of the chapter are not applicable to the examination of claim applications received by the court until 30.06.2013. See transitional provision point 68)

250.28 Article. Jurisdiction and procedure for examination

Cases concerning the recognition of decisions of meetings of participants (shareholders) of capital companies as invalid shall be examined by the Economic Court in claim proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 14.12.2017 and 01.10.2020, which enter into force on 01.01.2021.)

250.29 Article. Persons who may submit a claim application

A claim application for the recognition of decisions of a meeting of participants (shareholders) of a capital company as invalid may be submitted by persons specified by law.  

250.30 Article. Initiation of a case

Initiation and examination of a case in the procedure provided for in this chapter is permissible in claims against a capital company for the recognition of the following decisions of its meeting of participants (shareholders) as invalid:

1) decision on changes in the composition of officials of the capital company (board, council, liquidator) or in the representation rights of board members;  

2) decision on changes in the amount of share capital;  

3) decision on making amendments to the articles of association;  

4) decision on termination of operations of the capital company, reorganisation or conclusion, amendment or termination of a group agreement.  

250.31 Article. Content of the claim application

(1) In the claim application, in addition to that specified in Article 128 of this law, the following shall be indicated:

1) whether the claimant requests examination of the case in a court session;  

2) an address in Latvia for communication with the court to receive court documents, if the claimant's place of residence or location is not in Latvia and the claimant has not consented to electronic communication with the court.  

(2) In the application, the claimant may request the establishment of an interim protection measure (Article 250.35).  
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.32 Article. Sending of the claim application and attached documents to the respondent

(1) The time limit for submission of an explanation is 15 days, counting from the day when the claim application was sent to the respondent.  

(2) The court shall inform the respondent that failure to submit an explanation is not an obstacle to making a judgment in the case, and also that the respondent may submit evidence and request examination of the case in a court session only in the explanation and within the time limit set for its submission.  
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.33 Article. Explanation of procedural rights to participants in the case

(1) Simultaneously with sending documents to participants in the case (Article 148), the court shall explain to them their procedural rights, inform them of the composition of the court that will examine the case, and explain the right to challenge a judge.  

(2) The civil procedural rights referred to in this law that are related to the preparation of a case for trial, except for the right to request examination of the case in a court session, may be exercised by participants in the case no later than seven days before the notified time for examination of the case (first part of Article 250.36).  

250.34 Article. Requesting a reply

(1) If the judge considers it necessary, he or she is entitled to request a reply from the claimant regarding the explanation,

setting a time limit of 15 days for submission of the reply, which shall be counted from the day when the explanation was sent to the claimant.  

(2) In the reply and within the time limit set for its submission, the claimant may request examination of the case in a court session if such a request has not been expressed in the claim application. If the respondent submits an explanation and a reply is not requested, then the claimant may request examination of the case in a court session no later than seven days before the notified time for examination of the case, if such a request has not been expressed in the claim application.  
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.35 Article. Interim protection measures

(1) If there is reason to believe that the claimant's rights are being violated or could be violated, the court or judge, upon a reasoned application by the claimant, may adopt a decision on establishing an interim protection measure. The application for establishing an interim protection measure shall specify the interim protection measure.  

(2) The question of establishing an interim protection measure may not be examined before bringing a claim to court.  

(3) Interim protection measures are:

1) entry of a prohibition note in the commercial register;  

2) prohibition for the respondent to perform certain actions.  

(4) The court or judge shall decide on the application for establishing an interim protection measure without prior notification to the respondent and other participants in the case, within 15 days after receipt of the application or simultaneously with the initiation of the case, if the application is submitted simultaneously with bringing the claim.  

(5) The court or judge shall notify the respondent of the decision on applying the interim protection measure specified in point 1 of the third part of this article no earlier than the third day after adoption of the decision, but shall notify the respondent of the decision on applying the interim protection measure specified in point 2 of the third part of this article simultaneously with notification of the decision to the claimant. The respondent is responsible for observing the prohibition on performing certain actions from the moment when this decision has been notified to him or her. The court or judge shall notify the commercial register institution of the entry of a prohibition note in the commercial register.  

(6) The court, upon application by the claimant, may replace the established interim protection measure with another interim protection measure.  

(7) The court, upon application by a party, may revoke an interim protection measure.  

(8) When rejecting a claim, the court shall revoke the interim protection measure in the judgment. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the judgment enters into legal force.  

(9) If a claim is left without examination or proceedings are terminated, the court shall revoke the interim protection measure in the decision. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision enters into legal force.  

(10) An appeal may not be submitted against a decision by which an interim protection measure has been established, replaced or revoked.  

(11) The respondent is entitled to claim compensation for losses caused to him or her in connection with the establishment of an interim protection measure if the claim brought against him or her has been rejected, left without examination or proceedings have been terminated in the cases specified in points 2 and 4 of Article 223 of this law.  
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.36 Article. Examination of a case in written proceedings and preparation and pronouncement of a judgment

(1) If the parties do not request examination of the case in a court session or the court does not consider it necessary to examine the case in a court session, the court shall examine the case in written proceedings no later than within one month after receipt of the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission or after receipt of the reply or expiry of the time limit for its submission, notifying participants in the case in a timely manner of the date when the judgment will be available in the online system. This date shall be considered the date of preparation of the judgment. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the judgment to the online system on the date of preparation of the judgment, the judgment on the same date shall be available at the court office. The date when the judgment is available at the court office shall be considered the date of preparation of the judgment

in such a case.  

(2) The court judgment shall be pronounced by issuing the judgment to participants in the case without delay after preparation of the judgment.  

(3) Upon written request of a participant in the case, the judgment shall be sent without delay after the date of preparation of the judgment. Receipt of the judgment does not affect the calculation of time limits.  

(4) In written proceedings, a decision may also be adopted on leaving a claim without examination, on termination of proceedings or on referring the case for examination in a court session.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 14.12.2017 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.37 Article. Examination of a case in a court session

(1) The court shall examine a case in a court session in claim proceedings if requested by one of the parties or if the court considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session.  

(2) The judge shall set the date of the court session no later than within 15 days after receipt of the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission or after receipt of the reply or expiry of the time limit for its submission.  

(3) If the court postpones examination of the case, then the date of the next court session shall be set no later than within 15 days, except in cases where there is an objective basis for a longer time limit. Postponement of the case is not permissible in the case provided for in point 4 of the first part of Article 210 of this law.  

250.38 Article. Entry of a judgment into legal force

(1) A court judgment may not be appealed in appeal proceedings.  

(2) Participants in the case may appeal a court judgment in cassation proceedings (tenth section). In this case, the actions of the judge of the court of appeal instance referred to in the tenth section of this law shall be performed by the judge of the court of first instance.  

(3) A court judgment shall enter into legal force after the time limit for appealing it in cassation proceedings has expired and a cassation appeal has not been submitted.  

(4) If a cassation appeal has been submitted, the court judgment shall enter into legal force simultaneously with:

1) the decision of the procedural session of the Supreme Court if initiation of cassation proceedings has been refused (third part of Article 464 and Article 464.1);  

2) the judgment of the court of cassation instance if the court judgment has not been revoked or the said judgment or part thereof has been revoked and the application has been left without examination or proceedings have been terminated (Article 474).  

(5) The provisions of the second, third, fourth and fifth parts of Article 203 of this law shall apply to the legal force of a court judgment.  

(6) If in relation to any participant in the case the time limit for submitting a cassation appeal against a court judgment is set in accordance with part 2.1 of Article 454 of this law, the court judgment shall enter into legal force after the time limit for appealing it has expired, calculating the time limit from the later date of issuance of the judgment, if a cassation appeal has not been submitted.  

(7) If in the cases referred to in the sixth part of this article the relevant confirmation of issuance of the judgment has not been received (Article 56.2), the judgment shall enter into legal force six months after its pronouncement.  

(8) A court judgment shall be executed in accordance with Articles 204, 204.1 of this law and the provisions of the first part of Article 205. Immediate execution of a judgment in the case provided for in point 7 of the first part of Article 205 of this law is permissible only by requiring from the claimant adequate security in the event that the court of cassation instance adopts the judgment referred to in point 2, 3 or 4 of Article 474 of this law.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.39 Article. Submission of an appeal

(1) An appeal may be submitted to the Supreme Court within 10 days from the date of adoption of a decision of the court or judge regarding the following decisions:

1) on refusal to accept a claim application;  

2) on a decision by which a claim application has been returned to the claimant;  

3) on leaving a claim without examination;  

4) on termination of proceedings.  

(2) For a decision adopted in written proceedings, the time limit for submission of an appeal shall be calculated from the date of receipt of the decision.  

(3) An appeal may not be submitted against other decisions of the court and judge, but objections to these decisions may be expressed in a cassation appeal.  
(With amendments made by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

250.40 Article. Content of a cassation appeal

If the claimant's place of residence or location is not in Latvia and the claimant has not consented to electronic communication with the court, the cassation appeal shall, in addition to that specified in Article 453 of this law, indicate the address of the appellant in Latvia for communication with the court to receive court documents.  
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.41 Article. Procedural session of the Supreme Court

A procedural session of the Supreme Court shall take place no later than within one month after expiry of the time limit for submission of explanations specified in the first part of Article 460 and the third part of Article 463 of this law.  
(With amendments made by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

250.42 Article. Time limits for examination of a case in the Supreme Court

(1) The case shall be examined in written proceedings and the judgment shall be prepared no later than within two months after the relevant procedural session of the Supreme Court.  

(2) The case shall be examined in a session of the Supreme Court no later than within two months after the relevant procedural session of the Supreme Court or after a decision has been adopted in written proceedings on referring the case for examination in a court session.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014 and 14.12.2017, which enters into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment in the first part regarding deletion of the word "full" enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provision point 137)

30.5 subchapter
Interim protection against violence

## (Chapter 13

In the wording of the 02.2014 law, which enters into force on 31.03.2014.)

Article 250.43 Admissibility of Temporary Protection Against Violence in Claims

Temporary protection against violence is admissible in claims for nullity or dissolution of marriage, in claims for personal injury, in claims for recovery of maintenance, in claims for division of the parties' common dwelling in which they live in one household, or for determination of the procedure for use of the dwelling in which the parties live in one household, and in cases arising from custody and contact rights.

Article 250.44 Persons Who May Submit an Application for Temporary Protection Against Violence

An application for temporary protection against violence may be submitted by spouses or former spouses; persons between whom there exists a parent-child relationship, there exists or has existed a guardianship or other out-of-family care relationship; persons between whom there exists a relationship of kinship or affinity; persons who live or have lived in one household; persons who have or are expecting a common child, regardless of whether these persons have ever been married or have ever lived together; persons between whom there exists or has existed a close personal or intimate relationship.

Article 250.45 Grounds for Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) If a person is subjected to any physical, sexual, psychological or economic violence that occurs between former or current spouses or other mutually related persons regardless of whether the offender lives or has lived in one household with the injured person, the court or judge, upon a reasoned application of the person or an application submitted through police intermediation, may adopt a decision on temporary protection against violence.

(2) The first paragraph of this Article shall also apply in cases where a person is subjected to violent control — such action or set of actions that includes injury, sexual coercion, threats, humiliation, intimidation or other violent actions whose purpose is to harm, punish or intimidate the injured person.

(3) It is permissible to examine the question of temporary protection against violence at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before filing a claim in court.

Article 250.46 Content of an Application for Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) An application for temporary protection against violence shall be formatted in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(2) The application for temporary protection against violence shall indicate:

1) the name of the court to which the application is submitted;

2) the claimant's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration and place of residence. If the claimant consents to electronic communication with the court, the email address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include an indication of registration. The claimant may additionally also indicate another address for communication with the court;

3) the respondent's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration and place of residence. The respondent's personal identity number shall be indicated if it is known;

4) the claimant's representative's (if the application is submitted by a representative) first name, surname, personal identity number and address for communication with the court; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant's representative, whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia, consents to electronic communication with the court, the email address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include an indication of registration. If the claimant's representative's address is outside Latvia, an email address shall additionally be indicated or notification of registration of participation in the online system shall be provided;

5) the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law and how these circumstances manifest themselves;

6) evidence confirming the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law, if such is in the claimant's possession and if the person from whom the said evidence is obtainable is known, but it is not in the claimant's possession or the claimant cannot obtain it himself or herself for objective reasons;

7) the applicable temporary protection against violence measure or measures;

8) a list of documents attached to the application;

9) a confirmation that truthful information about facts has been provided to the court and the claimant or the claimant and representative, if the application is submitted by a representative, has been informed of liability in accordance with the Criminal Law for submission of a false application;

10) the time of preparation of the application and other information if it is necessary for examination of the case.

(3) If the applicable temporary protection measure is an obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and a prohibition to return and remain therein, an annex shall be attached to the application indicating the claimant's contact information (telephone, email address, address) so that the State Police, by contacting the claimant, can carry out control of execution of the relevant decision. This annex is information of limited access, which in accordance with the fourth paragraph of Article 250.62 of this Law is sent to the State Police and is not attached to the case materials.

(31) In the application, the claimant may request the court to send the decision on temporary protection against violence to the social service at the claimant's place of residence.

(4) If the application does not contain the confirmation referred to in point 9 of the second paragraph of this Article, the application shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.

(With amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015, 23.11.2016, 01.06.2017, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.47 Temporary Protection Against Violence Measures

(1) Temporary protection against violence measures are:

1) an obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and a prohibition to return and remain therein;

2) a prohibition for the respondent to be closer to the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides than the distance specified in the court decision on temporary protection against violence;

3) a prohibition for the respondent to remain in specified places;

4) a prohibition for the respondent to meet with the claimant and maintain physical or visual contact with him or her;

5) a prohibition for the respondent to communicate with the claimant in any way;

6) a prohibition for the respondent to arrange, through the intermediation of another person, a meeting or any kind of communication with the claimant;

7) a prohibition for the respondent to use the claimant's personal data;

71) an obligation for the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour, the scope, procedure for receipt, payment, execution, interruption and termination of which shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers;

8) other prohibitions and obligations that the court or judge has imposed on the respondent and whose purpose is to ensure the claimant's temporary protection against violence.

(2) The temporary protection against violence measure referred to in points 1 and 2 of the first paragraph of this Article shall be imposed if the respondent has reached the age of majority.

(3) It is permissible to impose several temporary protection against violence measures simultaneously.

(With amendments made by the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021. Point 7.1 of the first paragraph enters into force on 01.07.2021. See transitional provision point 164)

Article 250.48 Obligation for the Respondent to Leave the Dwelling in Which the Claimant Permanently Resides, and Prohibition to Return and Remain Therein

(1) The obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and the prohibition to return and remain therein is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to stay and remain in this dwelling regardless of whether the respondent is the owner, possessor or user of this dwelling.

(2) If the respondent is subject to the restriction referred to in this Article, the respondent shall be ensured the right to take or shall be issued the necessary clothing, footwear, linen, books, instruments, tools, items necessary for health care and other items that the respondent needs on a daily basis located in the dwelling.

Article 250.49 Prohibition for the Respondent to Be Closer to the Dwelling in Which the Claimant Permanently Resides Than the Distance Specified in the Court Decision on Temporary Protection Against Violence

The prohibition for the respondent to be closer to the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides than the distance specified in the court or judge's decision on temporary protection against violence is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to visit the relevant dwelling and to be closer to it than the distance specified in the decision.

Article 250.50 Prohibition for the Respondent to Remain in Specified Places

(1) The prohibition for the respondent to remain in specified places is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to visit the relevant place, which is not the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, or to be closer to this place than the distance specified in the decision.

(2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the restriction referred to in this Article, may indicate that the prohibition for the respondent to remain in specified places applies to the address of a specific place or places that correspond to certain characteristics, or to public or other specified events. The court or judge shall, as far as possible, take into account the respondent's obligations to appear at the workplace and other obligations of the respondent related to appearing in specified places.

Article 250.51 Prohibition for the Respondent to Meet with the Claimant and Maintain Physical or Visual Contact with Him or Her

(1) The prohibition for the respondent to meet with the claimant and maintain physical or visual contact with him or her is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to deliberately approach or be closer to the claimant than the distance specified in the decision and to avoid physical or visual contact with the claimant.

(2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the restriction referred to in this Article, may indicate that the prohibition for the respondent to meet with the claimant and maintain physical or visual contact with him or her also applies to persons who are closely related to or dependent on the claimant.

Article 250.52 Prohibition for the Respondent to Communicate with the Claimant in Any Way

(1) The prohibition for the respondent to communicate with the claimant in any way is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to use means of communication, including electronic means of communication, or any other methods of transmitting information to contact the claimant.

(2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the restriction referred to in this Article, may indicate that the prohibition for the respondent to communicate with the claimant in any way also applies to persons who are closely related to or dependent on the claimant.

Article 250.53 Prohibition for the Respondent to Arrange, Through the Intermediation of Another Person, a Meeting or Any Kind of Communication with the Claimant

The prohibition for the respondent to arrange, through the intermediation of another person, a meeting or any kind of communication with the claimant is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to use the intermediation of another person to approach the claimant or arrange physical or visual contact with the claimant or to contact the claimant using any means of communication or any other methods of transmitting information.

Article 250.54 Prohibition for the Respondent to Use the Claimant's Personal Data

The prohibition for the respondent to use the claimant's personal data is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to process, publish, make known or otherwise use the claimant's personal data in any way, except in procedural actions related to legal proceedings.

Article 250.54A Obligation for the Respondent to Complete a Social Rehabilitation Course for Reduction of Violent Behaviour

(1) The obligation for the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour is an obligation imposed by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to complete this course in order to prevent or reduce further risks of violence.

(2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the obligation referred to in this Article, shall also impose on the respondent an obligation to partially cover the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour in the amount of 10 percent if the respondent begins to complete the course within six months, and in full if the respondent begins to complete the course after six months.

(In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 01.07.2021. The Article enters into force on 01.07.2021. See transitional provision point 164)

Article 250.55 Temporary Protection Against Violence Before Filing a Claim

(1) A potential claimant may submit a reasoned application requesting the court to ensure temporary protection against violence before filing a claim in court if the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law exist.

(2) If the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law relate to a child, the application referred to in the first paragraph of this Article may be submitted in the child's interests by one of the child's parents, a guardian, an orphan's court or a prosecutor.

(3) An application for temporary protection against violence before filing a claim shall be submitted to the court at the place where the injury was inflicted or the applicant's location.

(With amendments made by the law of 01.10.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2021.)

Article 250.56 Temporary Protection Against Violence Before Filing a Claim Upon an Application Submitted Through Police Intermediation

(1) If, before filing a claim, the police have adopted a decision that imposes an obligation on a potential respondent who poses a threat to leave the dwelling, not to return and not to remain therein or in its vicinity, or prohibits the potential respondent from contacting the potential claimant (police decision on separation), the police, at the request of the potential claimant, shall send to the court a copy of the police decision, the potential claimant's application indicating that the potential claimant wishes the court to examine the question of temporary protection against violence, as well as other information that is in the police's possession and relates to the question of temporary protection against violence.

(2) The application referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall be formatted in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(3) The application referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, as well as other information, shall be sent by the police to the court at the place where the injury was inflicted or the applicant's location.

(4) The potential claimant's application submitted through police intermediation need not contain authorisation for the police to submit the application on behalf of the applicant.

(5) The question of temporary protection against violence, based on the potential claimant's application submitted through police intermediation, shall be examined by the judge in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 250.58 of this Law.

(With amendments made by the law of 01.10.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2021.)

Article 250.57 Evidence in Cases of Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) In cases of temporary protection against violence, a party to the case shall confirm the circumstances significant to the case indicated in the application with a confirmation.

(2) If there is no other evidence or it is insufficient, the court on its own initiative may request in a court session that a party to the case confirm his or her explanations containing information about facts and circumstances on which his or her claims or objections are based.

(3) Before providing an explanation, a party to the case shall give orally a confirmation of the following content:

"I, (first name, surname), confirm that in good conscience I will tell only the truth and will not conceal anything. I confirm that the information I have provided to the court about facts and circumstances of the case is exhaustive and truthful. I have been warned that I may be held criminally liable in accordance with the Criminal Law for deliberately providing false explanations and deliberately concealing facts and circumstances of the case known to me."

(4) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)

(5) A party to the case may be held criminally liable in accordance with the Criminal Law for providing confirmed deliberately false explanations or an application to the court.

(6) Confirmation of explanations and an application as evidence is not admissible with respect to such circumstances that have been established by a court judgment that has entered into force, as well as for confirmation or refutation of generally known facts.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.58 Examination of the Question of Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) The court or judge shall decide on an application for temporary protection against violence no later than the next day after receipt of the application if it is not necessary to request additional evidence or delay could cause substantial infringement of the claimant's rights. The court or judge shall decide on the said application without prior notification to the parties to the case.

(2) If the evidence is insufficient or it must be requested from the state or local government institutions or other natural or legal persons indicated in the application, the court or judge, at the request of a party to the case or on its own initiative, shall request evidence or invite institutions to provide an opinion and shall decide on the application for temporary protection against violence within 20 days after its receipt.

(3) The court or judge shall decide on an application for temporary protection against violence even if the application does not indicate all the information referred to in Article 250.46 of this Law or documents are attached, provided that the lack of documents or necessary information does not substantially affect the possibility of deciding on the application.

(4) The court or judge, when deciding on an application for temporary protection against violence, shall take into account the proportionality between the infringement of rights or potential infringement and the temporary protection against violence measure to be applied. The court or judge may, at its discretion, also impose another temporary protection against violence measure that is not indicated in the application.

(5) If it appears prima facie from the application for temporary protection against violence that delay could cause substantial infringement of the claimant's rights, the court or judge shall decide on this application in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article and may grant it based on the confirmation contained in the application even in cases where there is no other evidence or it is insufficient.

(6) If it does not appear prima facie from the application for temporary protection against violence that delay could cause substantial infringement of the claimant's rights, and it has not been possible to obtain other evidence in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article, the court or judge shall decide on this application in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article and may grant it based on the confirmation contained in the application and confirmation of explanations provided in accordance with the second and third paragraphs of Article 250.57 of this Law.

(7) When granting an application for temporary protection against violence before filing a claim, the court or judge shall set a time limit for the claimant to submit a statement of claim to the court, not longer than one year, but when imposing temporary protection against violence measures referred to in points 1 and 2 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law on a respondent who permanently resides in the dwelling together with the claimant — not longer than 30 days.

(71) When examining a claim, the court or judge may, on its own initiative, apply the temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law.

(8) When granting a claim, temporary protection against violence shall be in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force, except for the temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law, which shall be in force until its execution.

(9) In individual cases, the court may determine in the judgment that temporary protection against violence shall also be in force after the judgment enters into legal force, but not longer than one year after the judgment enters into legal force. If a temporary protection against violence measure referred to in points 1 and 2 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law has been imposed on a respondent who permanently resides in the dwelling together with the claimant, the court may determine that temporary protection against violence shall be in force for not longer than 30 days after the judgment enters into legal force.

(10) When rejecting a claim, the court shall revoke temporary protection against violence in the judgment. Temporary protection against violence shall be in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force.

(11) If a claim is left without examination or proceedings are terminated, the court shall revoke temporary protection against violence by a decision. Temporary protection against violence shall be in force until the day the decision enters into legal force.

(12) If a decision on temporary protection against violence has been adopted before filing a claim and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the judge, upon receipt of a reasoned application from the potential claimant or respondent, shall adopt a decision on revocation of temporary protection against violence. In this case, litigation costs shall not be reimbursed.

(13) The application referred to in the second paragraph of this Article shall be examined in written proceedings. If the court considers it necessary, the application may be examined in a closed court session, with prior notification to the parties to the case. The court, at the request of one party, may hear each party in a separate court session. The respondent's failure to appear shall not be an obstacle to examination of the application.

(With amendments made by the laws of 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.59 Decision on Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) In addition to what is provided in Article 230 of this Law, the court or judge shall indicate in the decision information about the parties to the case [first name, surname, personal identity number (if it is known), declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration and place of residence].

(2) The court or judge, in a decision on imposition of a temporary protection against violence measure — obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides — shall, if necessary, indicate the time limit for voluntary execution of the decision.

(3) The court or judge shall warn the respondent in the decision on temporary protection against violence that the police will carry out control of execution of the decision and, if the decision is not executed voluntarily, the respondent will be liable in accordance with the Criminal Law.

(4) The court or judge shall indicate in the decision on imposition of a temporary protection against violence measure — obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides — that:

1) the respondent has an obligation to notify the court of his or her further address for communication with the court if this dwelling is the respondent's declared place of residence or additional address indicated in the declaration and the respondent has not consented to electronic communication with the court;

11) the respondent is prohibited from alienating or transferring the dwelling, hindering or obstructing the use of the dwelling or deteriorating the condition of the dwelling regardless of whether the respondent is the owner, possessor or user of the dwelling;

2) the respondent has the right to submit an application to the court for replacement or revocation of the temporary protection against violence measure;

3) the date when the State Police familiarises the respondent with the decision shall be considered the date when the said decision is notified to the respondent, and that the respondent's refusal to familiarise himself or herself with the decision does not affect its legal consequences;

4) the decision is available in the online system.

(41) The court or judge shall indicate in the decision on imposition of a temporary protection against violence measure — obligation for the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour:

1) the contact information of the violent behaviour reduction service provider and the respondent's obligation to contact the violent behaviour reduction service provider within 10 days from the date of receipt of the decision;

2) the respondent's obligation to complete the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour within one year from the date of receipt of the decision and a warning to the respondent that if this course is not completed within one year, he or she will be liable in accordance with the Criminal Law;

3) the respondent's obligation to partially cover the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour in the amount of 10 percent if the respondent has begun to complete this course within six months from the date of receipt of the decision, and in full if the respondent has begun to complete the course after six months from the date of receipt of the decision, as well as that if the respondent does not cover these costs voluntarily, they will be recovered in the procedure established in this Law;

4) a warning to the respondent that covering the costs of the rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour does not release him or her from the obligation to complete the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour and liability in accordance with the Criminal Law.

(5) A decision on temporary protection against violence (first and second paragraphs of Article 250.58) shall be executed immediately after its adoption, except for the decision part on covering the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour in accordance with what is provided in the second paragraph of Article 250.54A of this Law.

(With amendments made by the laws of 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.60 Revocation or Replacement of Ensuring Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) Temporary protection against violence measures, except for the temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law, may be replaced with other measures upon a reasoned application of a party by the same court that imposed the temporary protection against violence measures, or the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits.

(2) Temporary protection against violence measures may be revoked upon a reasoned application of a party by the same court that imposed the temporary protection against violence measures, or the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits.

(3) The application referred to in the first and second paragraphs of this Article shall be decided in a closed court session, with prior notification to the parties to the case. The court, at the request of one party, may hear each party in a separate court session. The failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to examination of the application.

(4) A decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure shall be executed immediately after its adoption.

(With amendments made by the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021. The amendment in the first paragraph enters into force on 01.07.2021. See transitional provision point 164)

Article 250.61 Appeal of Decisions Adopted on Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against the decisions referred to in the first paragraph of Article 250.60 of this Law, against a decision by which an application for temporary protection against violence has been rejected, and a decision by which an application for revocation of temporary protection against violence has been rejected.

(2) Submission of an interlocutory appeal against the decisions referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall not suspend their execution.

(3) If the decisions referred to in the first paragraph of this Article have been adopted without the presence of a party to the case, the time limit for submission of an interlocutory appeal shall be counted from the date of issuance of the relevant decision.

Article 250.62 Notification of a Decision on Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) The court shall notify the parties of a decision on temporary protection against violence, a decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure by issuing it against signature or by sending it to the official electronic address, or in a registered mail item. A decision by which an application for temporary protection against violence has been rejected, unless it has been examined with the participation of the parties, shall be notified only to the claimant.

(2) The court shall send a decision on temporary protection against violence, a decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure immediately after their adoption to the State Police for execution control to its indicated email address and also to the State Police structural unit at the claimant's place of residence.

(3) If a decision on the question of temporary protection against violence has been adopted upon an application submitted through police intermediation (Article 250.56), the decision shall be available to the potential respondent and potential claimant in the online system on the next day after the court has received the application and police information. This date shall be considered the date when the said decision is notified to the potential respondent, and failure to deliver the decision to the respondent does not affect its legal consequences. If, for technical reasons, it is not possible to attach the decision to the online system on the specified date, the decision shall be available at the court office on the same date. In such case, the date when the decision is available at the court office shall be considered the date of notification of the decision.

(4) If a temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law has been applied to the respondent upon a reasoned application of the claimant submitted without police intermediation, the court shall not send the decision to the respondent. The court shall send this decision and the claimant's contact information referred to in the third paragraph of Article 250.46 of this Law to the State Police in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article. The State Police, when commencing control of execution of this decision, shall familiarise the respondent with the decision. The date when the State Police has familiarised the respondent with the decision shall be considered the date when the decision is notified to the respondent, and failure to deliver the decision to the respondent does not affect its legal consequences. Only after notification of the decision shall the decision be available to the respondent in the online system.
