(5) If it appears from the materials of the case on temporary protection against violence that the interests of a minor child or a person with limited legal capacity are affected, the court shall additionally send a decision on temporary protection against violence or a decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure to the orphan's court and the social service at the child's or person's place of residence. In other cases, the court shall send a decision on temporary protection against violence or a decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure to the social service at the claimant's place of residence if the claimant has requested it.

(6) If the temporary protection against violence measure provided for in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law has been applied to the respondent, the court shall, immediately after its adoption, additionally send a decision on temporary protection against violence or a decision on revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure also to the violent behaviour reduction service provider to its indicated email address. The information referred to in point 3 of the second paragraph of Article 250.46 of this Law shall also be sent to the service provider. The court shall also inform the service provider of the day when the decision was notified to the respondent, except in cases when the decision is notified in accordance with the fourth paragraph of this Article. If the decision is notified in accordance with the fourth paragraph of this Article, the State Police shall inform the service provider of the day when the decision was notified to the respondent.

(With amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.62A Conditions for Execution and Execution Control if the Respondent Has Been Imposed an Obligation to Complete a Social Rehabilitation Course for Reduction of Violent Behaviour

(1) The court or judge, upon receipt from the violent behaviour reduction service provider of a certificate that the respondent has not completed the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour within one year, shall send this certificate and the decision by which the respondent was imposed the obligation to complete the said course to the State Police for execution control to its indicated email address and also to the State Police structural unit at the claimant's place of residence, so that it may decide on the question of initiating criminal proceedings against the respondent for malicious non-execution of a decision on protection against violence.

(2) The court or judge, upon receipt from the violent behaviour reduction service provider of a certificate that the respondent has not covered the costs of this course by the completion of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour, shall send a writ of execution to the bailiff at the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none — at the debtor's place of residence.

(3) The decision part by which the respondent has been imposed an obligation to cover the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour, if the respondent has not covered these costs voluntarily, shall be executed in the procedure established in Part E of this Law.

(In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

Article 250.63 Special Conditions for the Respondent's Communication with the Court if the Respondent Has Been Applied a Prohibition to Return and Remain in the Dwelling That Is the Respondent's Declared Place of Residence

(1) If a temporary protection against violence measure has been applied that imposes an obligation on the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and establishes a prohibition to return and remain therein, and this dwelling is the respondent's declared place of residence or additional address indicated in the declaration, further decisions on temporary protection against violence, decisions on replacement or revocation of this temporary protection against violence measure shall be notified by the court to the respondent electronically in accordance with Article 56in the manner prescribed in Article 56 of this Law, but if that is not possible, at the address indicated by him or her

for communication with the court. (2) If a provisional protection measure against violence has been applied which imposes an obligation on the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the applicant permanently resides, and establishes a prohibition to return and stay therein, and this dwelling is the respondent's declared place of residence or additional address indicated in the declaration, and if the applicant has brought an action within the time limit specified in the court decision on provisional protection against violence, the summonses and other court documents related to this action shall be communicated to the respondent electronically in the manner prescribed in Article 56 of this Law, but if that is not possible, at the address indicated by him or her for communication with the court. (3) If in the cases referred to in paragraphs one and two of this Article it is not possible to communicate to the respondent electronically or the respondent has not indicated his or her address for communication with the court, the respondent shall be summoned to court and other court documents shall be delivered and issued by summoning the respondent with a summons which is published in accordance with Article 59. (With amendments made by the Law of 11 November 2021, which enters into force on 1 December 2021.)

Article 250.64. Requesting and Hearing of Cases on Provisional Protection Against Violence Following an Application Submitted Before Bringing an Action

(1) If the applicant brings an action within the time limit specified in the decision on provisional protection against violence following an application submitted before bringing an action, in a court having jurisdiction which is not the court that determined the provisional protection measure against violence, the court having jurisdiction to hear the case on the merits shall request from the court that determined the provisional protection measure against violence the relevant case and attach it to the materials of the action case. (2) When examining the statement of claim, the court or judge, in relation to provisional protection against violence, at the request of a party to the case or on its own initiative, shall request evidence or invite institutions to provide an opinion. (In the wording of the Law of 25 March 2021, which enters into force on 20 April 2021.)

Chapter 30.6
Cases on Compensation for Damage Caused by Infringements of Competition Law

## (Chapter 19

In the wording of the law of 10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

250.65 Article. Procedure for hearing cases

(1) Cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law shall be heard by the Economic Court in the procedure of claims according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

(2) Cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law within the meaning of this chapter are cases related to such infringements of competition law as are defined in Article 101 or 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union or in the legal acts of Latvia or a Member State of the European Union whose main objective is the same as that of Articles 101 and 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017 with amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018 and 01.10.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2021.)

250.66 Article. Disclosure of evidence in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

(1) The court, upon a reasoned request of the parties to the case, which is substantiated by reasonably available information, in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law may order the disclosure of evidence, observing:

1) the extent to which the request or the respondent's objections to the request are substantiated by available information justifying the request to disclose evidence;

2) the status of the evidence and the costs of obtaining it, in particular in relation to persons who are not parties to the case;

3) whether the evidence that is requested to be disclosed contains information of limited accessibility, in particular concerning other persons who are not parties to the case, and the procedure provided for the protection of such information of limited accessibility.

(2) The person from whom evidence is requested to be disclosed has the right to notify the court in writing of the status of the information requested to be disclosed and the costs of submission, substantiating them.

(3) The court may reject a request for disclosure of evidence if it considers that the scope of the evidence requested to be disclosed or the costs associated with the disclosure of evidence are not proportionate to the amount of the claim brought.

(4) The court, observing the person's right to protection of information of limited accessibility, requires that the person whose information provided has been given the status of information of limited accessibility submit a derivative of the relevant written evidence without indicating the information of limited accessibility.

(5) The court may restrict the right of a party's authorised representative to examine such evidence in the case which contains information of limited accessibility but has been submitted in unredacted form, and the disclosure of such information may cause substantial harm to a party to the case or another person.

(6) The court, when ordering the disclosure of evidence that has been submitted to a competition authority or is in the case materials of a competition authority, shall assess whether the request indicates the evidence as precisely as possible, based on the information provided by the party, and whether the submission of the evidence to the court will not create obstacles to the effective application of competition law.

(7) In order to assess whether the submission of evidence to the court will not create obstacles to the effective application of competition law, the court shall request the opinion of the competition authority. After evaluating the opinion of the competition authority, the court shall decide on the question of disclosure of evidence.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

250.67 Article. Restrictions on disclosure of evidence in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

(1) The court shall not order disclosure from the parties or other persons of:

1) statements provided to a competition authority within the framework of a leniency programme;

2) settlement submissions for the conclusion of an administrative agreement with a competition authority.

(2) The court shall order disclosure of evidence from the case materials of a competition authority if it is not possible to obtain such evidence from the parties to the case or other persons.

(3) Upon a substantiated request of the claimant, the court, in order to ascertain that the materials submitted to the Competition Council comply with the provisions of paragraph one of this Article, shall request an opinion from the Competition Council and the view of the person who submitted such materials to the Competition Council.

(4) Having received the opinions referred to in paragraph three of this Article, the court may verify the information indicated in the opinions by requesting the submission of the authority's case materials, which shall not be attached to the civil case.

(5) The court shall adopt a decision on the attachment of materials submitted to the Competition Council to the case materials if the requirements set out in paragraph one of this Article do not apply to the materials submitted by the competition authority.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017 with amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

250.68 Article. Admissibility of evidence in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

(1) The evidence referred to in paragraph one of Article 250.67 of this law shall not be admissible if a person has obtained it by using access to the case materials of a competition authority.

(2) Information which a person has obtained by using access to the case materials of a competition authority may be used as evidence only by the said person or a person who is the successor to the rights and obligations of the said person.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

250.69 Article. Grounds for exemption from proving in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

(1) An infringement of competition law established by a decision of the Competition Council that has entered into force or by a court judgment that has entered into legal force shall not be proved anew when hearing a claim for compensation for damages brought in accordance with Article 101 or 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union or the Competition Law.

(2) An infringement of competition law established by a decision of a competition authority of another Member State that has entered into force shall be deemed to be proved unless a party to the case submits to the court evidence of the absence of an infringement of competition law.

(3) If one party refers to evidence that is in the possession of the other party, and the latter, following a request by the court, refuses to submit the relevant evidence to the court or has destroyed it without denying that this evidence is or has been in its possession, the court may recognise as proved those facts for the confirmation of which the opposing party has referred to this evidence.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

250.70 Article. Liability for failure to submit, destruction or unauthorised use of evidence in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

If the court does not establish objective circumstances for the failure to submit evidence or a person has violated the restrictions on admissibility of evidence specified in Article 250.68 of this law, or the court has established that evidence has been destroyed, the court may impose a fine on a natural person of up to 14,000 euros, but on a legal person — up to 140,000 euros.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

30.7 Chapter
Cases concerning disputes over rights and interim protection for claims in insolvency proceedings cases

## (Chapter 31

Wording of 05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018. See transitional provision 144)

250.71 Article. Jurisdiction and procedure for examination

(1) Cases concerning disputes about rights in insolvency proceedings shall be examined by the court in which the relevant insolvency proceedings have been declared, in the case provided for in the fourth part of Article 363.17 of this law and in the first part of Article 80 of the Insolvency Law. Cases shall be examined in claim proceedings according to general provisions, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

(2) Cases concerning disputes about rights in insolvency proceedings within the meaning of this chapter shall also include cases concerning creditor claims in accordance with the provisions of the second and third parts of Article 80 of the Insolvency Law.

(3) If a case for examination of a dispute about rights has been initiated before the commencement of insolvency proceedings in court and the examination of this case on the merits has not been commenced, the court shall transfer this case for examination to the court in which the relevant insolvency proceedings have been declared, if there is no procedural co-participation on the defendant's side among the parties to the case.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

250.72 Article. Content of statement of claim

In the statement of claim, in addition to that provided for in Article 128 of this law, the following shall be indicated:

1) an address in Latvia for communication with the court in order to receive court documents, if the plaintiff's place of residence or location is not in Latvia and the plaintiff has not consented to electronic communication with the court;

2) whether the plaintiff requests trial of the case in a court session, substantiating their request.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.73 Article. Leaving statement of claim without progress

(1) The court shall leave the statement of claim without progress if:

1) the statement of claim does not contain all the requisites provided for in the second or third part of Article 128 and in Article 250.72 of this law;

2) the documents provided for in Article 129 of this law are not attached to the statement of claim.

(2) On leaving the statement of claim without progress, the judge shall adopt a reasoned decision, send it to the plaintiff and set a time limit of up to 20 days for remedying deficiencies, counting from the day of sending the decision. The judge's decision may be appealed in the procedure provided for in this law. The appeal time limit shall be counted from the day when the decision is issued to the plaintiff.

(3) If the plaintiff remedies the deficiencies within the set time limit, the statement of claim shall be considered as submitted on the day when it was first submitted to the court.

(4) If the plaintiff does not remedy the deficiencies within the set time limit, the statement of claim shall be considered as not submitted and shall be returned to the plaintiff. The decision on returning the statement of claim to the plaintiff is not subject to appeal.

(5) The return of the statement of claim to the plaintiff is an obstacle to its repeated submission to the court.

(6) The court, simultaneously with the decision on returning the statement of claim to the plaintiff, shall adopt a decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case and shall revoke the interim protection measure.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

250.74 Article. Grounds for establishing interim protection and applicable measures in insolvency proceedings

(1) The court, upon a reasoned application by the complainant, may adopt a decision on establishing an interim protection measure if there is reason to believe that the administrator's decision could violate the creditor's rights provided for in the Insolvency Law. The establishment of an interim protection measure is permissible when examining the question of accepting a complaint about the administrator's decision in the cases provided for in parts 1.1 and four of Article 363.17 of this law, if the administrator's decision has been appealed by the person provided for in the second or third part of Article 80 of the Insolvency Law.

(2) The court, when examining the question of establishing an interim protection measure, in addition to the circumstances indicated in the complaint about the administrator's decision, shall also take into account other materials of the insolvency proceedings case.

(3) The application for establishing an interim protection measure shall indicate the interim protection measure which the court is requested to establish until the judgment is made.

(4) The complainant has the right to request the court to establish the following interim protection measures:

1) a prohibition to participate in the creditors' meeting with voting rights for the creditor whose recognised claim is the subject of the complaint;

2) a prohibition to submit objections regarding the information received under the first and second parts of Article 81 of the Insolvency Law for the creditor whose recognised claim is the subject of the complaint.

(5) The court shall decide on the application for establishing an interim protection measure no later than the next day after the complaint about the administrator's decision has been received, without prior notice to the administrator and creditors.

(6) The administrator is responsible for observing the prohibition on performing certain actions from the moment when this decision is communicated to them. The court shall notify the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register about the application of the interim protection measure.

(7) The court, upon a reasoned application by the complainant or interested person, may replace the established interim protection measure with another interim protection measure.

(8) The court, upon a reasoned application by an interested person, may revoke the interim protection measure.

(9) If an interim protection measure has been established but a claim for examination of a dispute about rights has not been brought and the court has not set a time limit for bringing the claim, then, when adopting a decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case, the court shall simultaneously revoke the interim protection measure.

(10) If an interim protection measure has been established before bringing a claim for examination of a dispute about rights and the claim has not been brought within the time limit set by the court, the court shall simultaneously decide on the complaint about the administrator's decision and revoke the interim protection measure. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case enters into legal force.

(11) When rejecting a claim for examination of a dispute about rights, the court shall simultaneously decide on the complaint about the administrator's decision and revoke the interim protection measure. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case enters into legal force.

(12) If a claim for examination of a dispute about rights has been left without examination or the proceedings have been terminated, the court shall simultaneously decide on the complaint about the administrator's decision and revoke the interim protection measure. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case enters into legal force.

(13) A separate complaint may not be submitted against a decision by which an interim protection measure has been established, replaced or revoked.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

250.75 Article. Examination of case in written proceedings and drafting of judgment

(1) The examination of the case in written proceedings shall be commenced no later than within 30 days after receipt of the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission, timely notifying the parties to the case of the date when the judgment will be available in the online system. The court shall inform about the composition of the court that will examine the case and shall explain the right to challenge the judge. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered as the date of drafting the judgment. If, for technical reasons, it is not possible to attach the judgment to the online system on the date of drafting the judgment, the judgment on the same date shall be available at the court office. In such case, the date when the judgment is available at the court office shall be considered as the date of drafting the judgment.

(2) Upon a written request by a party to the case, the judgment shall be sent immediately after the date of drafting the judgment. Receipt of the judgment does not affect the calculation of the time limit.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.76 Article. Trial of case in court session

(1) The court shall try the case in a court session if a reasoned request by a party to the case has been received and if the court considers it necessary to try the case in a court session.

(2) The court shall set the date of the court session no later than within 30 days after receipt of the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission.

(3) If the court postpones the examination of the case, the next court session date shall be set no later than within 15 days, except in cases where there is an objective ground for a longer time limit.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

250.77 Article. Appeal of judgment, entry into force and entry into force of decision on examination of complaint

(1) The parties to the case may appeal the court judgment in appeal proceedings if one of the grounds for initiating appeal proceedings provided for in Article 440.2 of this law exists.

(2) The judgment shall enter into force after the time limit for submitting an appeal has expired.

(3) If the judgment has been appealed and the appellate court refuses to initiate appeal proceedings, the judgment of the first instance court and the decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision shall enter into force simultaneously with the decision by which initiation of appeal proceedings has been refused.

(4) The court decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case provided for in the fourth part of Article 363.17 of this law shall enter into force if an appeal has not been submitted within the time limit provided for by law.

(5) After the entry into force of the decisions referred to in this Article, they shall also be sent to the administrator and the Insolvency Control Service.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

30.8 Chapter
Cases concerning protection of trade secrets against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure

## (Chapter 28

02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.78 Procedure for Examining Cases

Cases concerning unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure of trade secrets that has occurred or is reliably possible in the future (hereinafter – infringement) shall be examined by a court in claim proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.79 Protection of Information Containing Trade Secrets

(1)	If the court, upon a reasoned request of a party, recognises that the case contains a document containing trade secrets that has been submitted in non-redacted form, and the disclosure of this information may cause substantial harm to a participant in the case or another person, the court may restrict the right of a person participating in the examination of the case to become acquainted with this part of the case materials by including the relevant evidence in a separate volume.  

(2)	The court, observing a person's right to protection of trade secrets, requests that the person whose information provided has the status of a trade secret submit a derivative of the relevant written evidence without indicating information containing trade secrets or by submitting it in redacted form.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.80 Basis for Application of Provisional Protection Measure and General Rules

(1)	The court, upon a reasoned application of the claimant, may adopt a decision on the application of a provisional protection measure if there is a basis to consider that:

1)	a trade secret exists and the claimant is its holder;  

2)	the right to protection of a trade secret against unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure is being infringed or could be infringed.  

(2)	The court, when deciding on the satisfaction or rejection of the application or assessing the proportionality of the application of a provisional protection measure, takes into account what is provided for in Article 250.88 of this law.  

(3)	It is permissible to examine the question of the application of a provisional protection measure at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before bringing a claim to court.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.81 Provisional Protection Measures

(1)	The application for the application of a provisional protection measure shall indicate the relevant provisional protection measure.  

(2)	Provisional protection measures are:

1)	a prohibition on the respondent or a specific person who makes the commission of an infringement possible from using or disclosing a trade secret, producing, offering, placing on the market or using infringing goods for the said purposes;  

2)	seizure of movable property with which rights to protection of a trade secret against unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure are possibly being infringed.  

(3)	The court, when deciding on an application that is not related to the disclosure of a trade secret, may not apply the provisional protection measures provided for in paragraph two of this Article, but impose on the respondent an obligation to pay a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff or submit an equivalent guarantee to the court in order to ensure compensation to the trade secret holder.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.82 Application of Provisional Protection Measure Before Bringing a Claim

(1)	A potential claimant may request that a provisional protection measure be applied before bringing a claim within three months from the day when he or she learned or should have learned of the infringement of rights or a possible infringement.  

(2)	When submitting an application, the potential claimant shall provide evidence confirming the infringement of rights or a possible infringement.  

(3)	An application for the application of a provisional protection measure before bringing a claim shall be submitted to the court in which the claim is to be brought.  

(4)	When satisfying an application for the application of a provisional protection measure before bringing a claim, the judge shall set a time limit for the claimant to submit a claim application to the court, not longer than 30 days.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.83 Examination of the Question of Application of Provisional Protection Measure

(1)	An application for the application of a provisional protection measure before bringing a claim, as well as in cases where it is not possible to determine who will be the participants in the case, shall be decided by the court or judge within 10 days of receipt of the application, without holding a court session and without prior notice to the participants in the case. If the judge considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances, the application shall be decided within 15 days of its receipt, inviting the applicant and potential participants in the case to a court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.  

(2)	An application for the application of a provisional protection measure, if the application is submitted simultaneously with the bringing of a claim, shall be decided by the court or judge within 10 days of the initiation of the case, without holding a court session and without prior notice to the participants in the case, or within 10 days of receipt of the application if the case has already been initiated. If the judge considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances, the application shall be decided within 15 days of the initiation of the case or, if the case has already been initiated, within 15 days of its receipt, inviting the applicant and potential participants in the case to a court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.  

(3)	If delay could cause irreversible harm to the trade secret holder and if it is not necessary to request additional evidence, the judge shall decide the application for the application of a provisional protection measure no later than the next day after the initiation of the case or, if the case has already been initiated, no later than the next day after receipt of the application, without prior notice to the respondent and other participants in the case.  

(4)	If a decision on the application of a provisional protection measure has been adopted without the presence of the respondent or other participants in the case, the court shall notify the respondent and other participants in the case of this decision no earlier than the third day after the adoption of the decision.  

(5)	When satisfying an application for the application of a provisional protection measure, the court or judge may instruct the claimant to secure losses that could arise for the respondent or other persons mentioned in point 1 of paragraph two of Article 250.81 of this law in connection with the application of a provisional protection measure, by paying a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff or submitting an equivalent guarantee to the court. If the claimant has not fulfilled the imposed obligation or has not submitted to the court a certificate issued by a bailiff confirming the payment of the sum of money into his or her deposit account within the time limit set by the court or judge, the court or judge shall adopt a decision on the cancellation of the provisional protection measure. The decision on securing losses shall be notified to the respondent after the claimant has paid the sum of money determined by the court or judge into the deposit account of the bailiff.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.84 Replacement or Cancellation of Provisional Protection Measure

(1)	The court, upon an application of the claimant, may replace the determined provisional protection measure with another measure.  

(2)	A provisional protection measure may be cancelled by the same court upon an application of a participant in the case.  

(3)	The court, upon receipt of an application from the claimant, another potential participant in the case or a person to whom the applied provisional protection measure relates, shall adopt a decision on the cancellation of the provisional protection measure if:

1)	a decision on the application of a provisional protection measure was adopted before bringing a claim and the claim has not been brought within the time limit set by the court;  

2)	the relevant information that was considered a trade secret no longer meets the requirements for a trade secret provided for in the Trade Secret Protection Law for reasons that cannot be associated with the respondent.  

(4)	When rejecting a claim, the court shall cancel the provisional protection measure in the judgment. The provisional protection measure is in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force.  

(5)	If a claim is left without examination or proceedings are terminated, the court shall cancel the provisional protection measure in the decision. The provisional protection measure is in force until the day the decision enters into legal force.  

(6)	The applications mentioned in paragraphs one, two and three of this Article shall be decided in a court session, with prior notice to the participants in the case. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.85 Appeal of Decisions Adopted Regarding Application of Provisional Protection Measure

(1)	A separate complaint may be submitted against a decision by which the determined provisional protection measure has been replaced, a decision by which an application for the application of a provisional protection measure has been rejected, and a decision by which an application for the cancellation of a provisional protection measure has been rejected.  

(2)	If a decision on the application of a provisional protection measure has been adopted without the presence of a participant in the case, the time limit for submitting a separate complaint shall be counted from the day of issuance of the decision.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.86 Execution of Decision on Application of Provisional Protection Measure

(1)	A decision on the application of a provisional protection measure and a decision on the cancellation of a provisional protection measure shall be executed immediately after its adoption.  

(2)	A decision on the application of a provisional protection measure that has been adopted with the condition mentioned in paragraph five of Article 250.83 of this law shall be executed after the claimant has paid the sum of money determined by the court or judge into the deposit account of the bailiff or submitted an equivalent guarantee to the court. The writ of execution shall be issued after the payment of the sum of money determined by the court or receipt of the equivalent guarantee.  

(3)	A decision on the application of a provisional protection measure by seizing movable property with which an infringement has possibly been committed shall be executed in the procedure provided for in Chapter 71 of this law.  

(4)	A decision on the application of a provisional protection measure by establishing a prohibition on performing specific actions with which an infringement has possibly been committed shall be executed by a bailiff and notified of the court decision to the respondent or the relevant third party in the procedure provided for in Article 555 of this law.  

(5)	The cancellation of an applied provisional protection measure shall be executed pursuant to an order of the bailiff who executed the decision on the application of the provisional protection measure.  

(6)	A decision on the replacement of a provisional protection measure shall be executed by a bailiff, first applying the replacement provisional protection measure and then cancelling the replaced provisional protection measure.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.87 Compensation for Harm Caused by Provisional Protection Measure

The respondent is entitled to claim compensation for harm caused to him or her in connection with the determination of a provisional protection measure if the provisional protection measure has been cancelled in the case provided for in point 1 of paragraph three of Article 250.84 of this law, if the claim brought against him or her has been rejected, left without examination or proceedings have been terminated in the cases provided for in points 2 and 4 of Article 223 of this law.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.88 General Rules for Examination of Claim Application and Application of Legal Protection Measures

The court, when deciding on the full or partial satisfaction of a claim or on its full or partial rejection or assessing the proportionality of the application of a legal protection measure, takes into account the circumstances of the relevant case, including where possible:

1)	the value of the trade secret or other specific characteristics of the trade secret;  

2)	the measures taken to protect the trade secret;  

3)	the respondent's conduct in acquiring, using or disclosing the trade secret;  

4)	the consequences of the unlawful use or disclosure of the trade secret;  

5)	the legitimate interests of the parties and the impact of the application of a provisional protection measure on them;  

6)	the legitimate interests of third parties and society;  

7)	the protection of fundamental rights.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

30.9 Chapter
Cases Arising from Consumer Collective Claims

## (Chapter 14

09.2023. version of the law, which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

Article 250.89 Procedure for Hearing Cases

Cases arising from consumer collective actions shall be heard by the court in action proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.  
(14.09.2023. version of the law, which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

Article 250.90 Persons Who May Submit a Statement of Claim

A statement of claim on behalf of a group of consumers may be submitted by persons included in the list of Latvian qualified entities or in the list of qualified entities compiled by the European Commission.  
(14.09.2023. version of the law, which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

Article 250.91 Content of the Statement of Claim

In the statement of claim, in addition to that specified in Article 128 of this Law, the following shall be indicated:

1)	the name, surname, personal identity number of those consumers who have given consent to the claimant to represent them in the specific action;  

2)	justification for combining the claims of specific consumers in a consumer collective action;  

3)	specific compensation and its amount for each consumer indicated in the statement of claim.  
(14.09.2023. version of the law, which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

Article 250.92 Actions of the Judge in Preparing the Case

(1)	The judge shall set a preparatory hearing and notify the parties thereof.  

(2)	The judge shall set a time limit for the claimant, which shall not be shorter than 60 days, for the claimant to announce the repeated registration of consumers for the consumer collective action and to specify the statement of claim accordingly, supplementing it with new consumer claims.  
(14.09.2023. version of the law, which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

Article 250.93 Grounds for Exemption from Proving Consumer Rights Violations

(1)	A consumer rights violation established by a decision of the Consumer Rights Protection Centre that has entered into force or by a court judgment that has entered into legal force need not be proved anew when hearing a consumer collective action.  

(2)	A consumer rights violation established by a decision of another Member State's consumer protection authority that has entered into force shall be considered proven unless a party to the case submits to the court evidence of the absence of a consumer rights violation.  
(14.09.2023. version of the law, which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

Article 250.94 Settlement

(1)	In a settlement, in addition to that mentioned in Article 227 of this Law, specific consumers to whom the settlement applies shall also be indicated, as well as the obligations they voluntarily undertake to perform.  

(2)	A settlement approved by the court shall be binding on the claimant, the defendant and the consumers represented in the consumer collective action.  
(14.09.2023. version of the law, which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

Part Six Special Litigation Procedure

Chapter 31 General Provisions

### Article 251. Cases Which the Court Hears in Special Litigation Procedure

The court shall hear the following cases in special litigation procedure:

1)	on confirmation and revocation of adoption;  

2)	on restriction of a person's legal capacity due to mental or other health disorders, review and restoration of restriction of legal capacity;  

21) on establishment and termination of temporary guardianship;  

3)	on restriction of a person's legal capacity and establishment of guardianship for persons due to their wasteful or extravagant lifestyle, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances;  

31) on suspension of the rights of a future representative;  

4)	on establishment of guardianship over the property of absent or missing persons;  

5)	on declaring missing persons dead;  

6)	on establishing facts that have legal significance;  

7)	on extinguishment of rights by way of summons;  

8)	on restoration of rights under debt instruments or bearer securities;  

9)	on inheritance rights;  

10)	on redemption of immovable property;  

11)	on legal protection proceedings and insolvency proceedings;  

12)	on liquidation or insolvency of credit institutions;  

13)	on declaring a strike or strike notice unlawful;  

14)	on declaring a lockout or lockout notice unlawful;  

15)	on revocation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations;  

16)	on introduction of an acquirer of immovable property into possession.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 01.11.2007., 29.11.2012., 11.11.2021. and 15.06.2021., which
enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### Article 252. Initiation of Cases

A judge shall initiate a case to be heard in special litigation procedure on the basis of a written application.

### Article 253. Parties to the Case

(1)	In cases of special litigation procedure, the parties to the case are the applicant and their representative, the interested person and their representative, as well as, in cases provided for by law, the prosecutor, a state or local government institution.  

(2)	In cases of special litigation procedure, the parties to the case have the procedural rights of parties specified in the second part of Article 74 of this Law.

### Article 254. Application in Special Litigation Procedure

(1)	The application shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court to which the application is submitted;  

11)	the applicant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the applicant consents to electronic communication with the court, an email address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, an indication of registration shall also be included;  

12)	the interested person's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. The personal identity number or registration number of the interested person shall be indicated if it is known;  

13)	the email address of the applicant's representative or person entitled to submit the application and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also an indication of registration, if the applicant's representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia, or the person entitled to submit the application, consents to electronic communication with the court. If the applicant's representative's address is outside Latvia, an email address shall additionally be indicated or notice of registration of their participation in the online system shall be given;  

2)	(deleted by the law of 29.11.2012.);  

3)	the subject matter and grounds of the application;  

4)	the circumstances on which the application is based and the evidence confirming them;  

5)	the law on which the application is based;  

6)	the applicant's request;  

7)	the list of attached documents;  

8)	the time of preparation of the application.  

(2)	The application shall be signed by the applicant or their representative, or the applicant together with the representative if so determined by the court, except in the case specified in the fifth part of Article 72 of this Law. If the application is signed by a representative, a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to apply to the court shall be attached to the application.  

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.)

(4)	An unsigned application shall be considered not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 23.04.2015., 23.11.2016., 01.06.2017. and 11.11.2021., which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### Article 255. Refusal to Accept an Application and Leaving an Application Without Progress

(1)	If the application does not comply with the requirements of the second part of Article 254 of this Law, the judge shall refuse to accept it and the consequences provided for in Article 132 of this Law shall apply.  

(2)	If the application does not comply with the requirements of the first part of Article 254 of this Law and the requirements specified in individual chapters of this part or court costs have not been paid, the judge shall leave the application without progress and the consequences provided for in Article 133 of this Law shall apply.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### Article 256. Procedure for Hearing Cases

A case in special litigation procedure shall be prepared for hearing by a judge, and the court shall hear it in accordance with the provisions of this Law, observing the provisions of individual chapters of Part Six.

### Article 257. Judgment

A judgment in cases heard in special litigation procedure must comply with the requirements of Article 193 of this Law, observing the provisions of this part.


This excerpt sits under: Publisher: Saeima Type: law Adopted: 14.10.1998.

### 258. Section. Leaving an application without consideration

If in a case to be examined in special proceedings a dispute arises concerning rights and this dispute is to be resolved in court by way of action, the court, depending on the content of the dispute, leaves the application without consideration or suspends the proceedings until the dispute is resolved.

32. Chapter

Confirmation and revocation of adoption

### 259. Section. Jurisdiction

(1) An application for confirmation of adoption shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of the adoptee, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of the adoptee, but an application for revocation of adoption — to the court according to the declared place of residence of one applicant, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of the applicant.

(2) An application by a foreign national or a person residing abroad for confirmation of adoption shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of the person to be adopted, but if the person to be adopted is in out-of-family care — according to the address of the place where out-of-family care is provided.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003. and 29.11.2012., which enter into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 260. Section. Content of the application

(1) The application shall indicate the circumstances referred to in Sections 162-169 of the Civil Law.

(2) The application shall be accompanied by orphan's court decisions on the recognition of a person as an adopter and the compliance of the adoption with the interests of the child.

(3) If the applicant is a foreign national or a person residing abroad, the application shall be accompanied by the adoption file and a valid adoption permit issued by the responsible minister.
(In the wording of the law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

260. 1 Section. Requesting evidence from the orphan's court

After initiating the case, if necessary, the court shall request from the orphan's court evidence confirming the circumstances referred to in Sections 162-169 of the Civil Law.
(In the wording of the law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 261. Section. Examination of the application

(1) The case shall be examined with the participation of at least one adopter in person and a prosecutor.

(2) The orphan's court that decided on the compliance of the adoption with the interests of the child and the person to be adopted shall be invited to participate in the examination of the case, if it is necessary to hear them at the court session and they have reached 12 years of age.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015.)

(4) If the adopter dies before the court has confirmed the adoption, this is not an obstacle to the confirmation of the adoption, but if the person to be adopted dies before confirmation, the case shall be terminated.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003. and 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 262. Section. Court judgment on confirmation of adoption

(1) The court, having verified the validity of the application and compliance with the requirements of the law, shall make a judgment on the confirmation of the adoption or on the rejection of the application.

(2) The court judgment on the confirmation of the adoption shall indicate the information necessary to make an entry in the relevant birth register about the adopters and to annul the entry about the child's former parents.

(3) The court shall notify the child's former parents that the entry about the child's parents has been annulled in the relevant birth register.

(4) A court judgment on the confirmation of the adoption that has entered into legal force is the basis for making an entry in the relevant

birth register and issuing a new birth certificate for the adoptee.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 31.10.2002. and 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 263. Section. Revocation of adoption

(1) The court may revoke the adoption upon a joint application of the adopter and the adult adoptee or upon an application of the adult adoptee (Section 175 of the Civil Law).

(2) A court judgment on the revocation of the adoption that has entered into legal force is the basis for making an entry in the relevant birth register and issuing a new birth certificate.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 07.09.2006. and 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

33. Chapter
Restriction of legal capacity of a person and establishment of guardianship due to mental disorders or other health disorders
(Chapter title in the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 264. Section. Jurisdiction

An application for restriction of legal capacity of a person due to mental disorders or other health disorders shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of this person, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of this person; if the person is placed in a medical institution — according to the address of the medical institution.
(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

264. 1 Section. Applicants

An application for restriction of legal capacity of a person due to mental disorders or other health disorders and establishment of guardianship may be submitted by the person themselves, their children, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse or a prosecutor.
(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 265. Section. Content of the application

The application shall indicate the restriction of legal capacity to be imposed on the person. The application shall be accompanied by evidence confirming the necessity of restriction of legal capacity in the interests of the person.
(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 266. Section. Preparation of the case for trial and examination of the application

(1) The court shall examine the case concerning the determination of restriction of legal capacity of a person and establishment of guardianship due to mental disorders or other health disorders with the participation of a representative of the orphan's court and a prosecutor.

(2) The representative of the orphan's court shall participate by submitting evidence that is relevant to the case. The representative of the orphan's court has the right to familiarise themselves with the case materials, participate in the examination of evidence and submit requests.

(3) It is the duty of the court to summon to the court session the person whose restriction of legal capacity is being examined. The application shall be sent to the person for whom restriction of legal capacity and establishment of guardianship is proposed, except in cases where this person is the applicant themselves, setting a time, not longer than 30 days, for submission of an explanation.

(4) When examining the case, the court shall, on its own initiative, request a certificate from a medical institution and other evidence necessary for determining the scope of restriction of legal capacity of the person from the applicant and institutions.

(5) The court, when preparing the case for trial, may convene a preparatory session and, in case of insufficient evidence, order the performance of additional expert examinations or request other evidence.
(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 267. Section. Ordering forensic examination

(1) The court may decide on the ordering of forensic psychiatric and, if necessary, forensic psychological examination. The decision on ordering forensic examination is subject to appeal.

(2) If the person in respect of whom the case has been initiated evades the examination, the court, with the participation of a prosecutor, may adopt a decision on sending this person for forensic examination by compulsion.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 29.11.2012.)
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006., 29.11.2012. and 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

267. 1 Section. Establishment of temporary guardianship

(1) Upon request of the parties to the case, the court may adopt a decision by which temporary guardianship is established for the relevant person for the period until the judgment on restriction of legal capacity is made in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 33.2 of this Law on establishment of temporary guardianship.

(2) The decision enters into force immediately. It loses force if another decision is adopted in the relevant matter.

(3) An interlocutory appeal may be filed against the court decision to establish temporary guardianship. Filing an interlocutory appeal does not suspend the execution of the decision.
(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 268. Section. Court Judgment

(1) If the court establishes on the basis of evidence that a person's legal capacity is to be restricted, it shall render a judgment indicating the scope of the restriction of legal capacity and establishing guardianship for the person.

(2) The court, when determining the scope of the restriction of legal capacity, shall be guided by the circumstances for which evidence has been submitted. The court, when determining the scope of the restriction of legal capacity, may, at the request of a party to the case, assess the restriction of legal capacity in such areas as:

1) making and receiving payments;

2) concluding transactions;

3) dealing with and managing property, in particular alienation, pledging and encumbering immovable property with rights in rem;

4) engaging in commercial and economic activities.

(3) The court may also assess the scope of the restriction of legal capacity in other areas, except in the cases referred to in Section 356.1 of the Civil Law.

(4) The court, when assessing the person's abilities, shall determine whether and to what extent the guardian acts together with the person under guardianship, and only thereafter the extent to which the guardian will act independently.

(5) After the judgment has entered into legal force, the court shall send it to the orphan's court — for the appointment of a guardian, as well as to the prosecutor and to the person whose legal capacity has been restricted. The court shall also send information about the judgment to the Population Register and, if necessary, the judgment for the entry of a note in the land register, movable property register or other relevant public register.

(6) (Deleted by the Law of 25.03.2021.)
(As worded by the Law of 29.11.2012. with amendments made by the Laws of 23.04.2015., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 269. Section. Court Costs

(1) Court costs in these cases shall be covered from state funds.

(2) If the court finds that the applicant has knowingly submitted an unfounded application, the court costs shall be imposed on the applicant.
(With amendments made by the Law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 270. Section. Recognition of a Person as Having Legal Capacity and Termination of Guardianship

(Deleted by the Law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

33.1 Chapter
Review of a Person's Restriction of Legal Capacity Due to Mental or Other Health Disorders

## (Chapter 29

11.2012. Law wording, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

270.1 Section. Jurisdiction

An application for review of the scope of a person's restriction of legal capacity shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of the person whose legal capacity is proposed to be reviewed, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of that person; if the person is placed in a medical institution — according to the address of the medical institution.
(As worded by the Law of 23.04.2015., which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

270.2 Section. Applicants

(1) An application for review of the scope of a person's restriction of legal capacity may be submitted by the person himself or herself, his or her guardian, children, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse or prosecutor. A representative of the orphan's court shall participate in the examination of cases by submitting evidence that is relevant to the case. The representative of the orphan's court shall have the right to familiarise himself or herself with the case materials, participate in the examination of evidence and submit requests.

(2) The guardian shall have the obligation to submit to the court an application for review of the scope of the restriction of legal capacity not less frequently than once every seven years from the date on which the court judgment on the restriction of legal capacity entered into force.

270.3 Section. Content of the Application

(1) The application shall indicate the scope in which the restriction of legal capacity is to be reviewed.

(2) Evidence confirming this shall be attached to the application for review of the scope of the restriction of legal capacity.

270.4 Section. Preparation of the Case for Trial

(1) The application shall be sent to the person whose legal capacity is proposed to be reviewed, except in the case where that person is himself or herself the applicant. Then a time, not longer than 30 days, shall be set for the submission of an explanation.

(2) It shall be the duty of the court to summon to the court hearing the person whose restriction of legal capacity is being reviewed.

(3) When examining the case, the court shall, on its own initiative, request a certificate from the medical institution and other evidence from the applicant and institutions that is necessary for the review of the scope of the restriction of legal capacity.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 11.11.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

270.5 Section. Ordering a Forensic Examination

A forensic examination shall be ordered according to the rules applied in cases concerning the restriction of a person's legal capacity and the establishment of guardianship due to mental or other health disorders.

270.6 Section. Court Judgment

(1) If the court reviews a person's restriction of legal capacity, it shall indicate in the judgment whether the restriction is to be:

1) revoked in full;

2) revoked in part;

3) maintained;

4) amended.

(2) The operative part of the court judgment shall indicate the revoked and maintained scope of the restriction.

(3) After the judgment has entered into legal force, the court shall send it to the orphan's court — for amending the scope of the guardian's rights and obligations or for revoking the guardian, as well as to the prosecutor, the guardian and the person whose restriction of legal capacity has been reviewed. The court shall also send information about the judgment to the Population Register and, if necessary, the judgment for amending the note in the land register, movable property register or other relevant public register.

(4) (Deleted by the Law of 25.03.2021.)
(With amendments made by the Laws of 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

33.2 Chapter
Establishment of Temporary Guardianship

## (Chapter 29

In the version of the law of 11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

270.7 pants. Jurisdiction

An application for the establishment of temporary guardianship over a person shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of that person, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of that person; if the person is placed in a medical institution — according to the address of the medical institution.

270.8 pants. Applicants

An application for the establishment of temporary guardianship over a person may be submitted by the person themselves, their children, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse or the prosecutor.

270.9 pants. Content of the application

In the application, in addition to that specified in Section 254 of this law, the circumstances mentioned in Section 364.2 of the Civil Law shall be indicated, attaching evidence confirming these circumstances, and whether the applicant requests the hearing of the case in a court session.

270.10 pants. Actions of the court after initiation of the case

(1)	After a case concerning the establishment of temporary guardianship over a person has been initiated, the judge on their own initiative or at the request of a party to the case requests evidence, including a certificate from a medical institution as to whether, due to mental or other health disorders, the person has lost the ability to understand the meaning of their actions and to control them.

(2)	The application shall be sent to the person for whom the establishment of temporary guardianship has been initiated, except in cases where that person is the applicant themselves. Then a time limit, not longer than 15 days, shall be set for the submission of an explanation.

(3)	After the initiation of the case, without holding a court session, the court informs the prosecutor's office and the orphan's court about the initiation of the case. After the explanations, all evidence and the certificate from the medical institution have been received, the court requests the prosecutor to submit a written opinion in the case within 10 working days, and the orphan's court — evidence that is relevant to the case.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

270.11 pants. Examination of the application

(1)	The judge shall decide on the application for the establishment of temporary guardianship without delay.

(2)	If the applicant does not request the hearing of the case in a court session and the court does not consider it necessary to hear the case in a court session, the application shall be examined in written proceedings, notifying the parties to the case in a timely manner of the date when the decision will be available in the online system. This date shall be considered the date of preparation of the decision. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the decision to the online system on the date of preparation of the decision, the decision shall be available at the court office on the same date. In such a case, the date when the decision is available at the court office shall be considered the date of preparation of the decision.

(3)	If the application is examined by holding a court session, the prosecutor and a representative of the orphan's court shall participate in it. It is the duty of the court to summon to the court session the person for whom temporary guardianship is to be established.
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

270.12 pants. Court decision

(1)	If the court, based on evidence, establishes that temporary guardianship is to be established for a person, it shall make a decision on the establishment of such guardianship, indicating the guardian's duty to conduct certain matters and the term of validity of the decision, which shall not be longer than two years.

(2)	The decision on the establishment of temporary guardianship over a person shall enter into force without delay and shall be in force for the term specified in this decision.

(3)	The decision on the establishment of temporary guardianship shall be sent to the orphan's court — for the appointment of a temporary guardian, as well as to the prosecutor and the person for whom temporary guardianship has been established.

(4)	An appeal may be filed against the court decision to establish temporary guardianship. The filing of an appeal shall not suspend the execution of the decision.
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

270.13 pants. Termination of temporary guardianship

(1)	Temporary guardianship shall terminate within the time limit set by the court.

(2)	If before the time limit mentioned in the second part of Section 270.11 of this law the circumstances that were the basis for the establishment of temporary guardianship have ceased to exist, the same court, upon application of the guardian or the person under guardianship, shall terminate the established temporary guardianship.

(3)	The decision on the termination of temporary guardianship shall enter into force without delay.

(4)	The decision on the termination of the establishment of temporary guardianship shall be sent to the person for whom temporary guardianship had been established, the guardian, the prosecutor and the orphan's court — for the revocation of the temporary guardian.
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

270.14 pants. Court costs

If the court finds that the applicant has knowingly submitted an unfounded application, the court costs shall be imposed on the applicant.

34.	nodaļa
Restriction of a person's legal capacity and establishment of guardianship due to wasteful or extravagant living, as well as due to excessive

use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances
(Chapter title in the version of the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 271.pants. Jurisdiction

An application for the restriction of legal capacity and establishment of guardianship over a person due to wasteful or extravagant living, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of that person, but if there is none — according to their place of residence.
(In the version of the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

271.	1 pants. Applicants

An application for the restriction of a person's legal capacity and establishment of guardianship over a person due to wasteful or extravagant living, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances may be submitted by the person themselves, their children, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse or the prosecutor.
(In the version of the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 272. pants. Content of the application

(1)	The application shall indicate on what basis and to what extent the person's legal capacity is to be restricted and guardianship established due to wasteful or extravagant living, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances, and what evidence confirms this.

(2)	The application may request immediate security against the dissipation of property by applying the security measures provided for in Section 138 of this law. The judge shall decide on such a request no later than the next day after receipt of the application.
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006 and 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 273. pants. Preparation of the case for examination

(1)	The application shall be sent to the person for whom the restriction of legal capacity and establishment of guardianship has been initiated, except in cases where that person is the applicant themselves. Then a time limit, not longer than 30 days, shall be set for the submission of an explanation.

(2)	The court may impose on the applicant the duty to submit additional evidence.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 274. pants. Participation of a representative of the orphan's court and the prosecutor

A case concerning the establishment of guardianship over a person due to wasteful or extravagant living, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances shall be examined with the participation of a representative of the orphan's court and the prosecutor. The representative of the orphan's court shall participate in the examination of the case by submitting evidence that is relevant to the case. The representative of the orphan's court shall have the right to familiarize themselves with the case materials, participate in the verification of evidence and make requests.
(In the version of the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 275. Section. Court Judgment

(1) If the court has found that a person, by living carelessly or wastefully or by excessively using alcohol or other intoxicating substances, threatens to bring himself or herself or his or her family to want or poverty, the court by judgment deprives this person of the rights to administer his or her property, restricts his or her capacity to act in disposing of this property and establishes guardianship for the relevant person. If the court, based on evidence, establishes that the person's active legal capacity is to be restricted, it makes a judgment in which it indicates the restriction of active legal capacity and the joint action of the guardian with the person under guardianship or the independent action of the guardian.

(2) After the judgment enters into legal force, the court sends it to the orphan's court — for the appointment of a guardian, as well as to the prosecutor and the person whose active legal capacity has been restricted. The court also sends information about the judgment to the Population Register and, if necessary, the judgment for the entry of a notation in the land register, movable property register or other relevant public

register.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 25.03.2021.)
(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012. with amendments made by the laws of 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 276. Section. Court Costs

(1) If the application is granted, court costs shall be awarded from the property of the person whose active legal capacity has been restricted and for whom guardianship has been established.

(2) If the court has found the application to be unfounded, court costs shall be awarded from the person upon whose application the case was initiated, but if the case was initiated upon the application of the prosecutor — they shall be covered from state funds.
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006. and 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 277. Section. Review of Restriction of a Person's Active Legal Capacity

In reviewing the restriction of a person's active legal capacity for persons due to careless and wasteful living, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances, the provisions of Chapter 33.1 of this law shall apply.
(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

Chapter 34.1
Suspension of the Rights of a Future Attorney

## (Chapter in the wording of the law of 29

11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013. Chapter enters into force on 01.07.2013. See transitional provision point 64. and the law of 29.11.2012.)

Section 277.1 Jurisdiction

An application for the suspension of the rights of a future attorney according to the declared place of residence of the principal, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of the principal, may be submitted by the principal's children, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse or the prosecutor.

Section 277.2 Content of the Application

The application shall indicate the circumstances that are the basis for the suspension of the rights of the future attorney, and shall attach evidence confirming these circumstances.

Section 277.3 Examination of the Application

(1) The court shall examine the case concerning the suspension of the rights of a future attorney with the participation of the prosecutor.

(2) The person who has issued the future power of attorney shall be summoned to the court session.

Section 277.4 Preparation of the Case for Examination

The application shall be sent to the attorney, setting a time for him or her, not longer than 30 days, to submit an explanation.
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 277.5 Court Judgment

(1) If the court finds that the attorney's actions are contrary to the interests of the principal or the attorney does not perform his or her duties at all, it shall suspend the rights granted to him or her by the future power of attorney.

(2) After the judgment enters into legal force, it shall be sent to the attorney, the principal, the prosecutor and the Latvian Council of Sworn Notaries.
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 277. 6 Court Costs

If the court finds that the attorney's actions are contrary to the interests of the principal or the attorney does not perform his or her duties at all, court costs shall be awarded from the attorney.

Chapter 35. Establishment of Guardianship
over the Property of Absent or Missing Persons

### 278. Section. Jurisdiction

Cases concerning guardianship of the property of an absent or missing person shall be examined by the court according to the last place of residence of the absent or missing person.

### 279. Section. Content of the Application

(1) An application to establish guardianship over the property of an absent or missing person may be submitted by persons who are interested in the preservation of the property of the absent or missing person or in the protection of this person's rights, or by the prosecutor.

(2) The application shall indicate the circumstances confirming the person's absence and the place where the property of this person is located, for which guardianship needs to be established.
