(3) If the location of the absent or missing person is known, the court shall summon him or her as an interested person.

### 280. Section. Court Judgment

(1) The court, having found that the application is justified, shall make a judgment on the establishment of guardianship over the property of the absent or missing person.

(2) After the judgment enters into legal force, it shall be sent to the orphan's court for the appointment of a guardian and to the absent person, if his or her place of residence is known, but if it is not known, a notice shall be sent for publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(3) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.)
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006., 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 281. Section. Termination of Guardianship

Upon the occurrence of the circumstances specified in point 1 of Section 375 of the Civil Law, guardianship shall be terminated by a judgment of the court that established the guardianship.

Chapter 36.
Declaration of a Missing Person as Deceased

### 282. Section. Jurisdiction

An application for the declaration of a missing person as deceased shall be submitted to the court according to the last

known place of residence of this person.

### 283. Section. Content of the Application

The application shall indicate the name, surname, personal identity number, if it is known, year of birth of the missing person, as well as the time when he or she left the place of residence and when the last information about this person was received, and, if possible, the place of birth of the missing person, the names and surnames of his or her parents and other information.

### 284. Section. Notice of a Missing Person

(1) After accepting the application, the judge shall adopt a decision on the publication of a notice in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(2) The notice shall indicate:

1) the name of the court that received the application;

2) the name, surname and year of birth of the person who is proposed to be declared deceased, as well as other information indicated in the application about him or her;

3) a proposal for the missing person to appear in court within three months or to notify his or her location, and also indicates that otherwise he or she will be declared deceased;

4) a call to all who know the location of the missing person or who know about his or her death to notify the court about it within three months.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 285. Section. Participation of the Prosecutor

A case concerning the declaration of a person as deceased shall be examined with the participation of the prosecutor.

### 286. Section. Court Judgment

(1) The court, having found that the application is justified, shall make a judgment on the declaration of the missing person as deceased.

(2) If the court has established the presumed date of death of the missing person, it shall be indicated in the judgment.

(3) If the court cannot establish the presumed date of death, the date when the application was submitted to the court shall be considered the date of death of the missing person, which the court shall indicate in the judgment.

(4) After the judgment by which a person has been declared deceased has entered into legal force, it shall be sent to the civil registry office — for the registration of the death of the missing person and to the orphan's court — for the establishment of guardianship over the property of the person declared deceased.

(5) After the judgment by which a person has been declared deceased has entered into legal force, the court shall send for publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis" a notice in which it indicates:

1) the name of the court that made the judgment;

2) the name, surname, year of birth and other established personal data of the missing person;

3) that this person has been declared deceased;

4) the presumed date of death of the missing person or the date on which this person is considered deceased.
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006., 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 287. Section. Consequences of the appearance of a person declared dead

(1)	If a person who has been declared dead by a court judgment appears or if their whereabouts become known, the court that made the judgment shall, by a new judgment, revoke the judgment declaring that person dead.

(2)	An application for revocation of the judgment may be submitted by the person declared dead, the person upon whose application the case was initiated, or the prosecutor.

(3)	After the court judgment enters into legal force, it shall be sent to the civil registry office — for annulment of the death record and a corresponding notice — for publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 37
Establishment of Legal Facts

### 288. Section. Cases to be examined in court

(1)	The court examines cases concerning the establishment of such facts upon which the creation, modification or termination of property and non-property rights of natural and legal persons depends.

(2)	The court establishes facts concerning:

1)	family relationships of natural persons;

2)	persons being in dependency;

3)	registration of adoption, registration of marriage conclusion or dissolution, registration of death;

4)	ownership of rights-establishing documents (except passports and certificates issued by civil status registration institutions) by a natural person whose first name, patronymic, surname or birth data indicated in the document do not coincide with the first name, patronymic, surname or birth data of that person indicated in the passport or birth certificate;

5)	ownership of rights-establishing documents by a legal person whose name or registration data indicated in the document do not coincide with the name or registration data of that person indicated in the relevant register;

6)	death of a person at a specific time and in specific circumstances, if the civil registry office refuses to register the death.

(3)	The court also establishes other facts that have legal significance if the applicable normative acts do not provide for a different procedure for their establishment.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 289. Section. Requirements necessary for establishment of legal facts

The court establishes legal facts only if it is not possible for the applicant to obtain the relevant documents confirming these facts in another procedure, or if these documents have been lost, stolen or destroyed and the possibility to restore them has been lost.

### 290. Section. Jurisdiction

An application for establishment of a legal fact shall be submitted to the court according to the applicant's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the place of residence.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 291. Section. Content of application

(1)	The application shall indicate for what purpose the applicant needs to establish the relevant fact.

(2)	Evidence confirming that it is not possible for the applicant to obtain the relevant documents or that it is not possible to restore lost, stolen or destroyed documents shall be attached to the application.

### 292. Section. Court judgment

(1)	When granting the application, the court shall indicate in the judgment what fact has been established and for what purpose.

(2)	A court judgment on establishment of a fact that is to be registered in the civil registry office or to be processed in other institutions does not replace documents issued by these institutions, but after entering into legal force is the basis for registration or processing in these institutions.

Chapter 38
Cases on Cancellation of Rights by Summons Procedure

### 293. Section. Cases to be examined by summons procedure

(1)	The summons procedure is applicable only in cases specified by law.

(2)	A summons is issued on the basis of an application by an interested person, unless otherwise provided by law.

### 294. Section. Submission of application

(1)	An application for issuing a summons and cancellation of rights shall indicate:

1)	the circumstances on which the request for a summons is based, citing the evidence that confirms them;

2)	interested persons known to the applicant;

3)	the consequences of non-appearance of the persons summoned.

(2)	An application for cancellation of rights related to immovable property shall be submitted to the court according to the location of that property, but for other rights — according to the declared place of residence of the applicant — natural person, but if there is none — according to the place of residence or the legal address of the legal person, unless otherwise provided by law.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 295. Section. Preparation of case for examination

(1)	After acceptance of the application, the judge shall decide on publication of a notice in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(2)	The notice shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court where the application was received;

2)	the first name and surname of the applicant, but for legal persons — the name;

3)	the basis and subject of the summons;

4)	the time limit for claiming rights;

5)	the consequences of non-observance of the time limit.

(3)	The time limit, if not specified by law, shall be determined by the court, but it may not be less than three months from the date of publication of the notice.

(4)	If the summons relates to rights to immovable property or to claims secured by a mortgage, the notice shall also be posted in the relevant district (city) court.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 25.10.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 296. Section. Examination of application

(1)	The court shall examine the case after expiry of the time limit indicated in the notice, summoning the applicant, interested persons indicated by the applicant, as well as persons who have claimed their rights within the time limit.

(2)	An application for rights submitted after the time limit indicated in the notice but before the judgment is made in the case shall be deemed to have been submitted within the time limit.

(3)	If a dispute about rights arises in connection with the summons that may affect the judgment in the case, the court shall suspend the proceedings, setting a time limit for bringing an action.

(4)	If an action is not brought within the specified time limit or a judgment on resolution of the dispute has been submitted, the proceedings shall be resumed.

### 297. Section. Court judgment

(1)	When granting the application, the court shall make a judgment on recognition of all rights not claimed within the time limit as invalid.

(2)	(Deleted by the law of 25.10.2018)
(With amendments made by the law of 25.10.2018, which enters into force on 28.11.2018.)

Chapter 39
Restoration of Rights under Debt Instruments or Bearer Securities

### 298. Section. Submission of application

In cases where a debt instrument or bearer security has been lost, stolen or destroyed, the creditor or the person to whom the document has been pledged, deposited, entrusted for management or commission or otherwise entrusted, as well as its last holder, if the document was made out to the bearer or the document had a blank endorsement, may request the court to annul this document and restore the rights under it.

### 299. Section. Jurisdiction

An application for annulment of a lost, stolen or destroyed document and restoration of rights shall be submitted to the court according to the place of payment indicated in the document, but if the place of payment is not known — to the court according to the declared place of residence of the debtor — natural person, but if there is none — according to the place of residence or the legal address of the legal person; if that is also not known — according to the place of issue of the document.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 300. Section. Content of application

(1)	An application for annulment of a lost, stolen or destroyed document shall indicate:

1)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);

2)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);

3)	the name, content and distinguishing features of the document;

4)	the circumstances in which the document was lost, stolen or destroyed.

(2)	A copy of the document shall be attached to the application, if possible.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 23.11.2016 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 301. Section. Preparation of the Case for Hearing

(1)	After accepting the application, the judge decides:

1)	on the prohibition for the person who must fulfil an obligation according to the document to make payments or contributions according to this document;  

2)	on the publication of an announcement in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".  

(2)	The announcement indicates:

1)	the name of the court where the application was received;  

2)	the applicant's first name and surname, but if the applicant is a legal person — its name and legal address;  

3)	the name, content and distinguishing features of the lost, stolen or destroyed document;  

4)	a proposal to the holder of the document to submit to the court within three months, but to the holder of a bill of exchange or cheque — within two months from the date of publication of the announcement, an application regarding their rights to this document, and also indicates that otherwise the document may be declared annulled.  

(3)	The court sends the decision provided for in paragraph 1, point 1 of this Section to the person who must fulfil the obligation according to the document, and also notifies all persons mentioned in the document of the adopted decision, if possible.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 302. Section. Obligation of the Document Holder

(1)	After being notified of the loss, theft or destruction of the document, the document holder has the obligation to submit to the court that adopted the decision, within the time limit specified in the announcement, an application regarding their rights to this document together with the original document.  

(2)	If the document holder has not submitted such an application, but their rights are affected by the annulment of the document, they may defend their affected rights in the procedure of action proceedings.

### 303. Section. Court Action After Receiving an Application from the Document Holder

(1)	If within the time limit specified in the announcement the court receives an application from the document holder, the court leaves without examination the application of the person requesting the annulment of the document, and sets a time limit during which payments and contributions according to the document are prohibited. This time limit may not exceed two months.  

(2)	At the same time, the court explains to the applicant their right to bring an action against the document holder for the recovery of this document, but to the document holder — their right to claim from the submitter damages caused by the prohibition measures established by the court.  

(3)	An appeal may be submitted against the court decision.

### 304. Section. Examination of the Application

(1)	The court examines the case concerning the annulment of the document and restoration of rights after the expiry of the time limit specified in the announcement, if no application has been received from the document holder.  

(2)	The court notifies the submitter and the person who issued the document, as well as all persons mentioned in the document, if possible, of the time and place of the examination of the case. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the case.

### 305. Section. Court Judgment

(1)	If the court finds that the document specified in the application has been lost, stolen or destroyed and that the applicant was the lawful holder of this document, it makes a judgment on the annulment of this document and the restoration of the applicant's rights.  

(2)	A court judgment that has entered into legal force is the basis for issuing a new document in place of the annulled document, if provided for by law.  

(3)	If the law does not provide for the possibility of issuing a new document, the judgment is the basis for claiming satisfaction of the rights arising from the annulled document.

Confirmation of Inheritance Rights by Law

45.	Chapter Redemption of Immovable Property

### 336. Section. Jurisdiction of Cases

An application for the redemption of immovable property shall be submitted to the court according to the location of the immovable property to be redeemed.

### 337. Section. Content of the Application

(1)	The application indicates the location of the immovable property to be redeemed, its acquirer and the basis for the right of redemption (Section 1382 of the Civil Law).  

(2)	The following shall be attached to the application:

1)	a copy of the act on the basis of which the immovable property was alienated;  

2)	evidence of the submitter's rights to redeem the immovable property;  

3)	information on the sale price of the immovable property, alienation costs and duties and their payment.

### 338. Section. Sending the Application to the Acquirer of the Immovable Property

The court sends the application to the acquirer of the immovable property, setting a one-month time limit for submitting an explanation and providing information on necessary and useful expenses made for the immovable property.  
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 339. Section. Examination of the Application

The application is examined at a court session to which the applicant and the acquirer of the immovable property are invited.

### 340. Section. Court Judgment

Having found the application to be well-founded, the court makes a judgment on the submitter's right of redemption of the immovable property and the right of the acquirer of the property to be redeemed to reimbursement of expenses.

### 341. Section. Leaving the Application Without Examination

If the acquirer of the immovable property contests the submitter's right of redemption, the court leaves the application without examination, explaining to the parties that the dispute is to be resolved by way of action.  

45.1	Chapter
Legal Protection Process Cases

## (Chapter 30

09.2010. law version, which enters into force 01.11.2010.)

341.1 Article. Jurisdiction of legal protection process cases

The court examines legal protection process cases according to the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before submission of the application to the court.  
(08.12.2016. law version, which enters into force 04.01.2017.)

341.2 Article. Content of legal protection process application

(1) The legal protection process application shall indicate:

1) (deleted by 11.11.2021. law);  

2) that with respect to the debtor there do not exist the restrictions set out in the Insolvency Law for initiation of legal protection process proceedings;  

3) whether with respect to the debtor within a year legal protection process proceedings have been initiated, but implementation of the legal protection process has not been declared;  

4) the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before submission of the application to the court;  

5) the candidate for the position of legal protection process supervisor (hereinafter — the supervisor) and contact information;  

6) if the debtor is an individual merchant, — information about the relevant natural person (name, surname and personal identity number);  

7) if the debtor is an individual (family) enterprise, a farm or a fishery, — information about the owner (natural person's name, surname and personal identity number).  

(2) Documents shall be attached to the application confirming:

1) (deleted by 11.11.2021. law);  

2) the circumstances on which the application is based;  

3) payment of the legal person's insolvency proceedings deposit in the case when the legal protection process application is submitted repeatedly within a year;  

4) the candidate for the position of supervisor's consent to be appointed as supervisor and confirmation of compliance with the requirements of Article 12.3 of the Insolvency Law, as well as of the ability to ensure performance of duties if a cross-border element exists with respect to the debtor.  
(With amendments made by 29.11.2012., 08.12.2016., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

341.3 Article. Receipt and registration of legal protection process application

(1) The court accepts the legal protection process application from the debtor on whose behalf the application is submitted, or from a person who is authorised to submit the application. The legal protection process application shall be submitted in person in paper form or in an online system.  

(2) Having received the legal protection process application, the court verifies the identity of the applicant. If it is not possible to verify the identity of the applicant who submitted the application in person in paper form or the applicant does not have the relevant authorisation, the application shall not be accepted.  

(3) The legal protection process application shall be registered in a separate register, which is signed by the applicant and the recipient. If the legal protection process application is received in the online system, the entry in the register shall be made by the recipient.  
(With amendments made by 11.11.2021. law, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

341.4 Article. Initiation of legal protection process proceedings

(1) Within five days after receipt of the legal protection process application, the judge shall adopt a decision:

1) to leave the legal protection process application without progress;  

2) to refuse to accept the legal protection process application;  

3) to accept the legal protection process application and initiate proceedings.  

(2) If the legal protection process application is left without progress, the judge shall adopt a decision to accept the legal protection process application and initiate proceedings no later than the next day after elimination of the deficiencies indicated in the decision. If the time limit for elimination of the deficiencies indicated in the decision has expired and they have not been eliminated, the application shall be considered as not submitted and returned to the applicant.  

(3) When accepting the legal protection process application and initiating proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision on the candidate for the position of supervisor's compliance with performance of duties in the relevant legal protection process and on his or her appointment as supervisor, simultaneously indicating the supervisor's contact information.  

(4) Having established that with respect to the candidate for the position of supervisor recommended by the debtor there exist restrictions

on performance of duties in the specific legal protection process, the judge shall adopt a decision to leave the application without progress and send to the debtor an invitation to submit information about a new candidate for the position of supervisor.  
(With amendments made by 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

341.5 Article. Court actions to be performed and issues to be decided after a decision on initiation of legal protection process proceedings has been adopted

(1) The court decision on initiation of legal protection process proceedings shall be sent without delay to:

1) the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register;  

2) the Bank of Latvia, if the decision is adopted regarding a financial market participant whose activities are supervised by the Bank of Latvia in accordance with the requirements of regulatory enactments;  

3) the administrator of the procedure referred to in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if proceedings in Latvia are initiated following an application for commencement of insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.  

(2) After a decision on initiation of legal protection process proceedings has been adopted, the judge:

1) adopts a decision on dismissal of the supervisor, as well as on the compliance of a new candidate for the position of supervisor with performance of duties in the relevant legal protection process and on his or her appointment as supervisor;  

2) upon application of a secured creditor decides on permission to sell the debtor's pledged property (Article 37, paragraph two of the Insolvency Law);  

3) decides on extension or cancellation of the consequences set out in Article 37, paragraph one, points 1., 2., 4., 5., 6., 7., 8. and 9. of the Insolvency Law.  

(3) (Deleted by 16.03.2023. law)

(4) (Deleted by 01.06.2017. law)

(5) (Deleted by 16.03.2023. law)

(6) Having established that with respect to the candidate for the position of supervisor recommended by the debtor there exist restrictions on performance of the supervisor's duties in the specific legal protection process, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the supervisor and send to the debtor an invitation to submit information about a new candidate for the position of supervisor.  

(7) The decision on appointment of the supervisor shall be sent to the supervisor and to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.  
(With amendments made by 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

341.6 Article. Procedure for examination of legal protection process application and ruling in legal protection process cases

(1) The court shall examine the legal protection process application in written proceedings, except in the case when it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the legal protection process application is examined in a court session, the debtor and the supervisor shall be invited to the session. Non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examination of the case.  

(11) If the application is submitted for commencement of insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall examine the application within the time limit set out in paragraph two of this Article in written proceedings, except in the case when it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the insolvency proceedings application is examined in a court session, the applicant, the debtor and the administrators of insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) and (2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be invited to the session. Non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examination of the case.  

(2) The court shall examine the legal protection process application within 15 days from:

1) (deleted by 31.05.2018. law);  

2) the day when the legal protection process plan of measures was submitted to the court.  

(21) A creditor whose claim the supervisor has recognised as prima facie unfounded, or a creditor who has expressed doubts about the validity of another creditor's claim, may request the court to summon or admit him or her to the case as an interested person. The creditor shall attach evidence of the validity of his or her claim to the request. A decision by which a request for summoning or entry of an interested person to the case is granted or rejected shall not be subject to appeal.  

(3) The court shall grant the application and make a judgment on implementation of the legal protection process if, based on the supervisor's opinion and other evidence, as well as evaluating the sworn auditor's opinion, if such is attached to the legal protection process plan of measures, and creditors' objections, if such have been received, it establishes that the legal protection process plan of measures:

1) complies with the requirements of the Insolvency Law, including will ensure achievement of the objective of the legal protection process;  

2) is supported in the manner and time limit set out in the Insolvency Law.  

(31) If, based on the supervisor's opinion and other evidence, the court establishes that the legal protection process plan of measures contains obligations in respect of which there is a dispute about rights, and the amount of obligations materially affects coordination of the legal protection process plan of measures, the court shall leave the legal protection process application without examination.  

(32) The court shall evaluate the compliance of the legal protection process plan of measures with Article 40, paragraph four, point 15 of the Insolvency Law only in such case if creditors' objections have been received regarding non-compliance of the legal protection process plan of measures with the said norm of the Insolvency Law.  

(4) If insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been commenced against the debtor in Latvia and the main proceedings administrator has not coordinated the legal protection process plan of measures in the manner set out in the Insolvency Law, the court shall grant the application and make a judgment on implementation of the legal protection process if it establishes that implementation of the legal protection process is in the interests of the creditors of insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of the said regulation.  

(41) When examining an application for commencement of insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall take into account what is set out in Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.  

(42) When declaring insolvency proceedings in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall indicate in the judgment the type of insolvency proceedings, if insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are commenced, or in the decision referred to in paragraph 4.3 of this Article indicate the type of insolvency proceedings, if insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are commenced.  

(43) If the court establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia, it shall declare a judgment on commencement of insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and adopt a decision by which it establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to commence insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. Regarding the court decision by which it is established that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to commence insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the debtor or any creditor may submit an appeal in accordance with Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 30 days from the day of declaration of the decision. Submission of an appeal shall not suspend commencement of insolvency proceedings.  

(44) The court shall commence insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the debtor carries out or within a three-month period before submission of the application has carried out economic activity in Latvia within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The court, having established that the court of another Member State that commenced insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of this regulation against the debtor was entitled to commence such proceedings, shall make a judgment on

commencement of insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor. The court shall not commence insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the conditions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have occurred.  

(5) When making a judgment on implementation of the legal protection process, the court shall approve the legal protection process plan of measures and simultaneously decide on appointment of the supervisor, if it is provided for in the legal protection process plan of measures. Having established that with respect to the candidate for the position of supervisor indicated in the legal protection process plan of measures there exist restrictions on performance of duties in the specific legal protection process, the court shall leave the legal protection process application without examination.  

(6) In the judgment on implementation of the legal protection process, the court shall indicate the list of pledged property to which restrictions on secured creditors exercising their rights are applicable until termination of the legal protection process.  

(7) When rejecting the legal protection process application, the court shall simultaneously terminate the legal protection process and recover court costs from the applicant of the legal protection process application.  

(8) The court judgment in a legal protection process case may be appealed in the appellate procedure if one of the grounds for initiation of appellate proceedings set out in Article 440.2 of this law exists. Appeal of the court judgment shall not suspend its execution.  

(9) The judgment shall be issued to the applicant of the legal protection process application and to the supervisor, as well as sent to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.  
(With amendments made by 12.02.2015., 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

341.7 Article. Decision on implementation of the legal protection process in out-of-court legal protection process

(1) In legal protection process cases in out-of-court legal protection process, the provisions of this chapter shall apply unless otherwise provided for in this Article.  

(2) The court shall examine the legal protection process application in out-of-court legal protection process within 15 days in written proceedings, except in the case when it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the application in a legal protection process case is examined in a court session, the debtor and the supervisor shall be invited to the session. Non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examination of the case.  

(3) After a decision on initiation of legal protection process proceedings in out-of-court legal protection process has been adopted, the court shall not decide the issue of permission to sell the debtor's pledged property upon application of a secured creditor and on appointment of the supervisor.  

(4) If the conditions set out in the Insolvency Law for implementation of the legal protection process in out-of-court legal protection process exist, the court shall adopt a decision on implementation of the legal protection process in out-of-court legal protection process and approve the legal protection process plan of measures, as well as simultaneously appoint the supervisor indicated in the legal protection process plan of measures, if the debtor has requested approval of the legal protection process plan of measures in the manner set out in Article 42, paragraph 3.1 of the Insolvency Law or if appointment of the supervisor has been requested by the debtor or the majority of creditors set out in Article 42, paragraph three of the Insolvency Law.  

(5) An appeal may be submitted regarding the court decision in a legal protection process case in out-of-court legal protection process. Submission of an appeal shall not suspend execution of the decision.  

(6) The decision shall be issued to the applicant and to the supervisor, as well as sent to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.  
(With amendments made by 12.02.2015., 01.06.2017., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

341.8 Article. Issues to be decided after a ruling on implementation of the legal protection process has been adopted

(1) After a ruling on implementation of the legal protection process has been adopted, upon a relevant application the court shall decide on:

1) amendments to the legal protection process plan of measures;  

2) dismissal of the supervisor, setting a time limit for preparation of the document and property acceptance and transfer act and for transfer of documents and property;  

3) appointment of a new candidate for the position of supervisor as supervisor, if the previous supervisor has been dismissed from the relevant legal protection process;  

31) replacement of the supervisor;  

32) appointment of the supervisor for supervision of implementation of the legal protection process plan of measures, if the supervisor has not previously been appointed for supervision of implementation of the legal protection process plan of measures;  

4) performance of actions set out in Article 51 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council;  

5) termination of the legal protection process.  

(2) The court may dismiss the supervisor on its own initiative if, when examining an application in a legal protection process case, it establishes that the supervisor does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments or does not perform the court ruling, or does not comply with the requirements of the Insolvency Law.  

(3) The court shall send the decisions referred to in paragraph one of this Article to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. After adoption of the decision on dismissal of the supervisor, the court shall send this decision to the debtor without delay.  

(4) After receipt of an application from the majority of creditors set out in Article 42, paragraph three of the Insolvency Law, the court shall decide without delay on appointment of the candidate for the position of supervisor as supervisor, if with respect to him or her there do not exist the restrictions set out in the Insolvency Law on performance of this duty in the relevant legal protection process. If within 15 days from the day when the supervisor's application for withdrawal from the specific legal protection process was received or a decision on dismissal of the supervisor was adopted, which is not based on the supervisor's application for withdrawal from the specific legal protection process, and the majority of creditors set out in Article 42, paragraph three of the Insolvency Law has not submitted to the court a proposal regarding a candidate for the position of supervisor, the court shall decide on termination of the legal protection process. The decision shall be sent to the Insolvency Control Service, the debtor and the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.  

(5) For examination of the issue referred to in this Article, the court may request that the legal protection process supervisor submit a report on his or her activities or other information.  

(6) The court shall examine the application within 15 days from the day of its receipt. The judge shall examine the application in written proceedings, without holding a court session, except in the case when he or she considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session or it is requested by a participant in the proceedings whose interests are affected by the application. The applicant, the supervisor, the debtor's representative and other interested persons shall be invited to the court session. Non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examination of the issue.  

(7) Regarding examination of the application, the court shall adopt a decision that is not subject to appeal. The court decision on dismissal of the legal protection process supervisor on the basis of Article 12.4, paragraph two, point 1., 4. or 5. of the Insolvency Law is subject to appeal in the part regarding the established non-compliance with the requirements of regulatory enactments or non-performance of the court ruling, or non-compliance with the requirements of the Insolvency Law, by submitting an appeal. The regional court shall examine this appeal within 15 days.  

(8) The regional court, when examining the appeal referred to in paragraph seven of this Article, has the right to:

1) leave the decision unchanged, but reject the complaint;  

2) revoke the decision and with its own decision decide the issue on the merits.  

(9) The decision referred to in paragraph eight of this Article shall enter into force and be enforceable immediately.  

(10) The decision referred to in paragraph eight, point 1 of this Article shall be sent to the debtor.  

(11) The regional court shall examine within 15 days the debtor's or creditor's appeal regarding the court decision by which it is established that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to commence insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.  

(12) In the appeal referred to in paragraph eleven of this Article, in addition to what is provided for in Article 443.1 of this law, the following shall be indicated:

1) from what time the debtor's legal address is located or the main economic activity is carried out in the indicated European Union Member State;  

2) facts showing that the debtor usually exercises its main interests in the European Union Member State indicated in the appeal;  

3) information about creditors or a substantial part of assets, or economic activity in another European Union Member State;  

4) whether insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been commenced against the debtor in another European Union Member State.  

(13) The regional court, when examining the appeal referred to in paragraph eleven of this Article, has the right to:

1) leave the decision unchanged, but reject the complaint;  

2) revoke the decision in full.  

(14) If the regional court has revoked the decision, insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be continued as insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) or (4) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.  

(15) The court shall also send the decision on the appeal to the administrator and to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.  
(With amendments made by 21.06.2012., 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

341.9 Article. Examination in court of complaints regarding a decision adopted by the Insolvency Administration regarding the administrator's actions in the legal protection process or imposition of a legal obligation
(Deleted by 01.06.2017. law, which enters into force 01.07.2017. See Transitional provision 125. point)

341.10 Article. Decision on termination of the legal protection process

(1) The court shall examine the issue of termination of the legal protection process on its own initiative or upon the debtor's application.  

(2) The court on its own initiative shall adopt a decision on termination of the legal protection process in the case set out in Article 341.8, paragraph four of this law and Article 51, paragraph one of the Insolvency Law.  

(3) The court upon the debtor's application shall adopt a decision on termination of the legal protection process in the case set out in Article 51, paragraph four of the Insolvency Law.  

(4) In the case set out in paragraph three of this Article, the debtor shall attach to the application for termination of the legal protection process the supervisor's written opinion on implementation of the legal protection process plan of measures.  

(41) The court upon application of the administrator of the procedure referred to in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, submitted in accordance with Article 39 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, may terminate insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.  

(5) The court shall send the decision on termination of the legal protection process without delay to the applicant, the supervisor, as well as to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.  
(With amendments made by 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021. law, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

341.11 Article. Decision on termination of the legal protection process, declaring insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person

(1) The court on its own initiative shall adopt a decision on termination of the legal protection process if insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person are declared based on Article 57, paragraph one, point 8 or 9 of the Insolvency Law.  

(2) The court on its own initiative shall adopt a decision on termination of the legal protection process and declare insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person in the case set out in Article 51, paragraph two of the Insolvency Law.  

(3) The court shall adopt a decision on termination of the legal protection process and declare insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person upon application of the person referred to in Article 37(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if it establishes that performance of actions set out in Article 51 of this regulation is in the interests of the creditors of insolvency proceedings referred to in Article 3(1) of this regulation.  

(4) The application for insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person in the case set out in paragraph one of this Article shall be submitted to the court in whose proceedings the legal protection process case is located.  

(5) The court shall send the decision on termination of the legal protection process without delay to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.  
(With amendments made by 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

341.12 Article. Examination in court of complaints regarding a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service regarding the supervisor's actions in the legal protection process or imposition of a legal obligation

(1) The court shall examine a complaint by a creditor, the debtor's representative, the supervisor or a third person whose lawful rights are infringed, regarding a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service regarding the supervisor's actions in the legal protection process or imposition of a legal obligation. A complaint regarding a decision of the Insolvency Control Service adopted after termination of the relevant legal protection process shall be examined by the court in the manner set out in this Article.  

(2) If the court recognises that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and decide on:

1) revocation of the decision of the Insolvency Control Service in full or in part;  

2) imposition of an obligation on the Insolvency Control Service to adopt or examine a complaint regarding the supervisor's actions;  

3) imposition of an obligation on the supervisor to eliminate the committed violation, except in cases when a decision on termination of the relevant legal protection process has been adopted.  

(3) Having established that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall reject the complaint.  

(4) The complainant has the right to withdraw his or her complaint before its examination on the merits is completed. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision on termination of the complaint proceedings.  

(5) After examination of the complaint, the court shall send a copy of the decision without delay to the Insolvency Control Service.  

(6) If the decision of the Insolvency Control Service regarding the supervisor's actions in the legal protection process is adopted within a year after termination of the relevant legal protection process, the complaint regarding the decision of the Insolvency Control Service shall be submitted to the court in whose proceedings the relevant legal protection process case was located.  
(16.03.2023. law version, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

46. Chapter
Legal protection process cases
(Chapter deleted by 30.09.2010. law, which enters into force 01.11.2010.)

46.1 Chapter
Legal person insolvency proceedings cases


This excerpt sits under: Publisher: Saeima Type: law Adopted: 14.10.1998.

## (Chapter 30

In the wording of the 09.2010 law, which enters into force on 01.11.2010.)

Article 363.1 Jurisdiction over Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings

(1) The court shall examine a legal entity insolvency proceedings case in accordance with an application by the debtor, a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law, based on the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before the application was submitted to the court. (2) A case concerning the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be examined by the court based on the location of the debtor's centre of main interests, but in the case of initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation — based on the location of the debtor's establishment (within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council). (With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 08.12.2016, 01.06.2017 and 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Article 363.2 Content of a Creditor's or Majority of Creditors' Application for Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings

(1) A creditor shall indicate in an application for legal entity insolvency proceedings (hereinafter in this Chapter — insolvency proceedings application):

1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021); 2) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021); 3) the sign of insolvency proceedings; 4) the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before the application was submitted to the court. (11) If the application is submitted by several creditors or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law, the information referred to in point 1.1 of the first paragraph of Article 254 of this Law shall be indicated for each creditor on whose authority the insolvency proceedings application is submitted. (2) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application, the creditor shall attach a document certifying payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit. (3) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in point 1 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law, evidence of the substantiation and amount of the claim shall be attached to the application, as well as a document issued by a bailiff regarding the impossibility of recovering the debt from the debtor. (4) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in points 2 and 3 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law, evidence of the substantiation and amount of the claim, a copy of the warning of the intention to submit an insolvency proceedings application, documents regarding the issuance or sending of the warning (receipt for sending a document with confirmation of the content of the shipment) shall be attached to the application, and the application shall also certify that the debtor has not raised substantiated objections against it. (5) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in point 4 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law, the application shall indicate for what period wages and compensation for harm have not been paid, and a certificate issued by the employer regarding the amount of wages and mandatory social insurance contributions shall be attached to it, but if the employer has not issued the said certificate, this fact shall be indicated in the application. (51) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application in accordance with the sign referred to in point 7 or 8 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law, the application shall, in addition to the information referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, indicate the case number for legal protection proceedings. Documents substantiating the facts stated in the application shall be attached to the application. (6) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application that insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) or (2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been initiated against the debtor, the creditor shall indicate the substantiation of the application therein and attach evidence confirming the circumstances on which the application is based, if such evidence is in his or her possession. (7) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application that insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been initiated against the debtor, the creditor shall send it to the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of the said Regulation. (With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 08.12.2016, 01.06.2017, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021. The provision of the second paragraph regarding the payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit, insofar as it relates to employees whose only legal remedy is the declaration of the employer as insolvent, has been found to be incompatible with the first sentence of Article 92 of the Constitution of the Republic of Latvia by the judgment of the Constitutional Court of 20.04.2012, which enters into force on 24.04.2012.)

Article 363.3 Content of a Debtor's Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) An insolvency proceedings application on behalf of the debtor may be submitted by the management institution or partners of a general partnership who have representation rights, or a specially authorised person. (2) The debtor shall indicate in the insolvency proceedings application:

1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021); 2) the sign of insolvency proceedings; 3) information about the location of the debtor's centre of main interests within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; 4) whether the debtor conducts or has conducted in another European Union Member State within a three-month period before the submission of the application an establishment within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and its location; 5) the case number for legal protection proceedings, if the insolvency proceedings application is submitted in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in point 9 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law; 6) the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before the application was submitted to the court. (3) The debtor shall attach to the insolvency proceedings application:

1) a list of members of management institutions, auditors (members of audit institutions) and procurators, indicating the name, surname, address and other information by which they can be identified and reached; 2) evidence that the intention to submit an insolvency proceedings application has been notified to the members (shareholders) of the commercial company, members of the association or other founders or members of the legal entity; 3) evidence of representation rights; 4) a document certifying payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit. (4) When submitting an application for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the debtor shall, in addition to the documents specified in the third paragraph of this Article, attach to the insolvency proceedings application a certification regarding the location of the debtor's centre of main interests. (With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 18.04.2013, 08.12.2016, 01.06.2017, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.4 Content of a Debtor's Insolvency Proceedings Application in Liquidation Proceedings

(1) An insolvency proceedings application on behalf of the debtor shall be submitted by the liquidator in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in point 6 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law. (2) The provisions of the second, third and fourth paragraphs of Article 363.3 of this Law shall apply to the liquidator's insolvency proceedings application. (With amendments made by the law of 01.06.2017, which enters into force on 01.07.2017.)

Article 363.5 Content of an Insolvency Proceedings Application by a Person Referred to in Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council

(1) The person referred to in point (a) of Article 37(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall submit an insolvency proceedings application to the court to initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation against the debtor. (2) The person referred to in point (a) of Article 37(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall indicate in the insolvency proceedings application:

1) the debtor's firm (name), registration number and legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before the application was submitted to the court, and the legal address on the day of submission of the application; 2) the name of the court that has initiated insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, the date of adoption and entry into force of the court decision; 3) the substantiation for initiating insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor; 4) information on whether insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been initiated against the debtor in another European Union Member State (hereinafter — Member State). (3) The person referred to in point (a) of Article 37(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall attach to the insolvency proceedings application:

1) the court decision on the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor and a translation thereof certified in the prescribed manner in the official language; 2) the court decision or other certification regarding the appointment of an administrator in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and a translation thereof certified in the prescribed manner in the official language; 3) documents certifying that the debtor conducts or has conducted in Latvia within a three-month period before the submission of the application an establishment within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; 4) a document certifying payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit. (With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 08.12.2016, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.6 Content of an Administrator's Insolvency Proceedings Application
(Deleted by the law of 01.06.2017, which enters into force on 01.07.2017. See transitional provision point 125)

Article 363.7 Receipt and Registration of an Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) The court shall accept an insolvency proceedings application from the debtor on whose behalf the application is submitted or from a person who is authorised to submit the application. An insolvency proceedings application shall be submitted in person in paper form or in an online system. (2) Upon receiving an insolvency proceedings application, the court shall verify the identity of the applicant. If it is not possible to verify the identity of the applicant of an application submitted in person in paper form or the applicant does not have the appropriate authorisation, the application shall not be accepted. (3) An insolvency proceedings application shall be registered in a separate register, which shall be signed by the applicant and the recipient. If an insolvency proceedings application is received in the online system, the entry in the register shall be made by the recipient. (With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.8 Prohibition on Amending the Subject Matter of an Insolvency Proceedings Application and on the Debtor Withdrawing an Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) In insolvency proceedings cases, amendment of the subject matter of an insolvency proceedings application is not permitted. (2) The debtor is not entitled to withdraw an insolvency proceedings application. Article 363.9 Resolution of the Question of Acceptance of an Insolvency Proceedings Application and Initiation of a Case

(1) Within five days of receiving an insolvency proceedings application, the judge shall adopt a decision:

1) to leave the insolvency proceedings application without progress; 2) to refuse to accept the insolvency proceedings application; 3) to accept the insolvency proceedings application and initiate a case. (2) If an insolvency proceedings application is left without progress, the judge shall adopt a decision to accept the insolvency proceedings application and initiate a case no later than the next day after the deficiencies specified in the decision have been remedied. If the time limit for remedying the deficiencies specified in the decision has expired and they have not been remedied, the application shall be considered as not submitted and returned to the applicant. (3) The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application if it is established that a legal entity insolvency proceedings case has been initiated against the debtor following the debtor's insolvency proceedings application. (4) The court shall initiate a legal entity insolvency proceedings case on its own initiative if, when adopting a decision to terminate legal protection proceedings, it establishes the sign of legal entity insolvency proceedings specified in point 7 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law. (5) The judge shall adopt a decision to consolidate the initiated legal entity insolvency proceedings cases into one proceeding if, before the commencement of the examination on the merits of a legal entity insolvency proceedings case initiated following a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application, it is established that a legal entity insolvency proceedings case has been initiated against the debtor following another creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application. (6) The judge shall adopt a decision to suspend proceedings in a case following a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application if, before the commencement of the examination on the merits of a legal entity insolvency proceedings case initiated following a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application, it is established that a legal entity insolvency proceedings case has been initiated against the debtor following the debtor's insolvency proceedings application. Upon declaring legal entity insolvency proceedings following the debtor's insolvency proceedings application, the court shall resume proceedings in the suspended case following the creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application and terminate it. The state fee paid shall be refunded to the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law in full. (With amendments made by the laws of 18.04.2013, 01.06.2017 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

Article 363.10 Court Actions in Preparing a Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings Case for Examination

(1) The judge shall immediately send the decision on the initiation of a case to:

1) (deleted by the law of 31.05.2018); 2) the Bank of Latvia, if the decision has been adopted regarding a financial market participant whose activities are supervised by the Bank of Latvia in accordance with the requirements of regulatory enactments; 3) the administrator of the proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if a case has been initiated in Latvia following an application for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; 4) the debtor. (2) If a case has been initiated following a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application, the judge shall send the creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law application and the decision on the initiation of the case to the debtor, inform the debtor and the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law of the day of examination of the insolvency proceedings application, as well as of the debtor's right to raise substantiated objections against the claim stated in the insolvency proceedings application no later than three days before the day of examination of the insolvency proceedings application, including to provide evidence that the debtor is able to cover the obligations stated in the insolvency proceedings application. (3) After the initiation of a legal entity insolvency proceedings case, using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, an administrator candidate shall be selected from the list of administrator candidates (hereinafter — Candidate List) maintained in the Electronic Insolvency Accounting System of the Insolvency Control Service, and the judge shall assess his or her suitability for performing the duties of an administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings. (4) Having established that there are restrictions for the administrator candidate to perform the duties of an administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the administrator candidate as administrator. Using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, a new administrator candidate shall be selected from the Candidate List, and the judge shall assess his or her suitability for performing the duties of an administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings. (With amendments made by the laws of 18.04.2013, 01.06.2017, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

Article 363.11 Procedure for Examination of an Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) The court shall examine an insolvency proceedings application submitted by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law within 15 days from the day of initiation of the case. The applicant of the insolvency proceedings application and the debtor shall be invited to the court session. If several creditors' insolvency proceedings applications are consolidated into one proceeding, those applicants who can be notified of the court session at least seven days before the respective session shall be invited to the court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the case. (2) The court shall examine an insolvency proceedings application submitted by the debtor in written proceedings within seven days from the day of initiation of the case. The court shall examine the application in written proceedings, except in cases where it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the insolvency proceedings application is examined in a court session, the debtor shall be invited to the session. The non-appearance of this person is not an obstacle to the examination of the case. (3) (Deleted by the law of 01.06.2017)

(31) If an application has been submitted for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the application shall be examined in written proceedings within 15 days from the day of initiation of the case or, if the court considers it necessary, in a court session. If the insolvency proceedings application is examined in a court session, the applicant, the debtor and the administrator of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be invited to the session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the case. (4) If, before the drafting of the judgment, the court establishes that the applicant has not paid the state fee or the insolvency proceedings deposit, except in cases where the court has initiated a legal entity insolvency proceedings case on its own initiative or has exempted an employee from payment of the deposit, it shall leave the insolvency proceedings application without examination. The exception specified in this paragraph does not apply to cases where a legal protection proceedings application has been submitted repeatedly within one year. (5) The judge may adopt a decision on full or partial exemption of an employee from payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit if he or she submits the insolvency proceedings application after it has not been possible to execute a court decision on the recovery of a debt from the debtor by applying enforcement measures and the employee, taking into account his or her financial situation, cannot pay the insolvency proceedings deposit. (6) When examining an application for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall take into account the provisions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. (With amendments made by the laws of 18.04.2013, 12.02.2015, 01.06.2017 and 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. See transitional provision point 146)

Article 363.12 Sequence of Examination of an Insolvency Proceedings Application and a Legal Protection Proceedings Application

(1) The court shall suspend proceedings if, before the commencement of the examination on the merits of a legal entity insolvency proceedings case, it establishes that a legal protection proceedings case has been initiated in respect of the debtor. (2) Proceedings in a legal entity insolvency proceedings case shall be suspended until a decision is adopted in the legal protection proceedings case. (3) Proceedings in a legal entity insolvency proceedings case shall be terminated if, in accordance with the decision, legal protection proceedings are implemented in respect of the debtor. (4) Proceedings in a legal entity insolvency proceedings case shall be resumed and examined in the procedure specified in this Chapter if legal protection proceedings in respect of the debtor are terminated on the basis of the second paragraph of Article 341.10 of this Law. Article 363.13 Court Decision in a Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings Case

(1) Legal entity insolvency proceedings shall be declared by the court, and its judgment is not subject to appeal, except for a judgment by which an insolvency proceedings application for a legal entity has been rejected. A judgment by which an insolvency proceedings application for a legal entity has been rejected may be appealed in the appellate procedure if one of the grounds for initiating appellate proceedings specified in Article 440.2 of this Law exists. (2) The court shall declare legal entity insolvency proceedings if, on the day of examination of the application, it establishes the sign of insolvency proceedings indicated in the application. (3) Upon granting the application, the court shall appoint the administrator candidate selected in the procedure specified in Article 363.10 of this Law as administrator. (4) When declaring insolvency proceedings in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall indicate in the judgment the type of insolvency proceedings if insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated, or indicate in the decision referred to in the fifth paragraph of this Article the type of insolvency proceedings if insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated. (5) If the court establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia, it shall declare a judgment on the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and adopt a decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. Against the court decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the debtor or any creditor may submit an appeal in accordance with Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 30 days from the day of pronouncement of the decision. The submission of an appeal does not suspend the initiation of insolvency proceedings. (6) The court shall initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the debtor conducts or has conducted in Latvia within a three-month period before the submission of the application an establishment within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. Having established that the court of another Member State that has initiated insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor was entitled to initiate such proceedings, the court shall render a judgment on the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, without observing the provisions of the second paragraph of this Article. The court shall not initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the conditions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have occurred. (7) The court, when declaring legal entity insolvency proceedings and terminating legal protection proceedings, shall appoint the administrator candidate selected in the procedure specified in Article 363.10 of this Law as administrator.
