(8) When declaring legal entity insolvency proceedings, the court shall send the judgment to the appointed administrator, the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if it has initiated insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation against the debtor in Latvia, and to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. (9) If the sign of insolvency proceedings indicated in the application is not established, the court shall reject the insolvency proceedings application and terminate the legal entity insolvency proceedings case, and also decide the question of whether the insolvency proceedings application is to be recognised as unfounded or deliberately false. The court shall reject an insolvency proceedings application submitted in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in points 2 and 3 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law if it establishes that no later than three days before the day of examination of the case the debtor has raised substantiated objections against the claim stated in the insolvency proceedings application or that the obligations for which the insolvency proceedings application was submitted have been covered in full. (10) Having recognised the insolvency proceedings application as unfounded or deliberately false, the court shall recover litigation costs from the applicant of the insolvency proceedings application. If the applicant of the insolvency proceedings application withdraws his or her application because the debtor has voluntarily covered the obligations stated in the insolvency proceedings application before the day of examination of the case, the court, when deciding on the termination of the case, shall, at the request of the applicant of the insolvency proceedings application, award the court costs paid by the applicant from the debtor. In other cases, these costs shall be indicated in the court judgment and included in the insolvency proceedings costs. (11) When rejecting an insolvency proceedings application submitted in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in points 2 and 3 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law because on the day of examination of the application the court does not establish the sign of insolvency proceedings indicated therein, as the debtor has covered part of the obligations indicated in the application before the day of examination of the case in order to prevent the declaration of legal entity insolvency proceedings, it shall, when deciding on the termination of the case, award the court costs paid by the applicant from the debtor. (12) When rejecting an insolvency proceedings application, the court shall send the judgment to the Insolvency Control Service. (With amendments made by the laws of 18.04.2013, 12.02.2015, 01.06.2017, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.14 Questions to be Decided by the Court After Declaration of Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings

(1) After the declaration of the debtor's insolvency proceedings, the court shall, on the basis of a relevant application, decide on:

1) the removal of an administrator in the cases specified in the Insolvency Law, setting a time limit for the preparation of a document and property acceptance and transfer act and the transfer of documents and property to another administrator; 2) the appointment of a new administrator candidate as administrator if the previous administrator has been removed from the respective insolvency proceedings; 3) the performance of actions specified in Article 46 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; 4) the approval of an immovable property or enterprise auction act (Articles 611 and 613) and the registration of the sold immovable property in the name of the purchaser, as well as the deletion of the insolvency note in the land register; 5) (deleted by the law of 11.09.2014); 6) the termination of insolvency proceedings. (2) An administrator may be removed by the court on its own initiative if, when examining an application or complaint in an insolvency proceedings case, it establishes that the administrator does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments or does not execute a court decision. (3) If, after the declaration of insolvency proceedings, the court has adopted a decision to remove an administrator, after its adoption the court shall appoint an administrator candidate selected from the Candidate List using automated selection provided by the Court Information System as administrator. (4) (Deleted by the law of 31.05.2018)

(5) Having established that there are restrictions for the administrator candidate to perform the duties of an administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the administrator candidate as administrator. The judge shall adopt a decision to appoint an administrator candidate as administrator in the procedure specified in the third paragraph of this Article. (6) If, following an application by the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court establishes that the performance of actions specified in Article 46(1) of this Regulation No 2015/848 is in the interests of the creditors of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of this Regulation, it shall adopt a decision on the performance of actions specified in Article 46(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and determine appropriate measures to ensure the interests of the creditors of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation. (7) If, following an application by the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation or a creditor, the court establishes that the performance of actions specified in Article 46(1) of the said Regulation No 2015/848 is no longer justified, it shall adopt a decision on the performance of the action specified in Article 46(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. (8) The court shall send the decision on the performance of actions specified in Article 46 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council to the debtor's representative and the administrator. (9) The court shall send the decisions referred to in points 1, 2, 3 and 6 of the first paragraph of this Article to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. (10) The court shall examine a complaint against a creditors' meeting decision, a complaint against an administrator's decision, as well as a complaint against a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service regarding the actions of an administrator in insolvency proceedings or the imposition of a legal obligation. The court shall send the decision adopted after the examination of the said complaints, except for a decision on a complaint against a creditors' meeting decision, to the Insolvency Control Service. (11) The court shall examine an application and a complaint within 15 days from the day of receipt of the application or complaint. The judge shall examine an application in written proceedings without holding a court session, except in cases where he or she considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. The judge shall examine a complaint in written proceedings without holding a court session, except in cases where the administrator requests that the case be examined in a court session or the court considers it necessary to examine the complaint in a court session. The applicant or complainant, the administrator, the debtor's representative and other interested persons shall be invited to the court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the question. (12) A court decision on the examination of an application or complaint is not subject to appeal. A court decision on the removal of an administrator on the basis of point 1, 2, 3, 4 or 7 of the second paragraph of Article 22 of the Insolvency Law is subject to appeal in the part regarding the established non-compliance with the requirements of regulatory enactments or non-execution of a court decision, by submitting an appeal. The regional court shall examine this appeal within 15 days. (121) An appeal may be submitted against a court decision in a case on the approval of an auction act. (13) For the examination of the questions referred to in this Article, the court may request that the administrator submit a report on his or her activities or other information, but the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council — information necessary for the adoption of the decisions referred to in this Article. (14) The regional court, when examining the appeal referred to in the twelfth paragraph of this Article, has the right to:

1) leave the decision unchanged and reject the complaint; 2) revoke the decision and decide the question on the merits with its own decision. (15) The decision referred to in the fourteenth paragraph of this Article shall enter into force and be enforceable immediately. (16) The regional court shall send the decisions referred to in the fourteenth paragraph of this Article to the Insolvency Control Service.(17) The regional court shall examine within 15 days the ancillary appeal of the debtor or creditor against the court decision which established that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to commence the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. (18) In the ancillary appeal, in addition to that provided for in Section 443.1 of this Law, the following shall be indicated:

1) from what time the debtor's registered office is located or the main economic activity is carried out in the specified Member State of the European Union; 2) facts showing that the debtor usually pursues its main interests in the Member State of the European Union indicated in the ancillary appeal; 3) information about creditors or a substantial part of assets or economic activity in another Member State of the European Union; 4) whether insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been commenced against the debtor in another Member State of the European Union. (19) The regional court, when examining the ancillary appeal referred to in Paragraph seventeen of this Section, shall have the right to:

1) leave the decision unchanged but reject the appeal; 2) revoke the decision in full. (20) If the regional court has revoked the decision, the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall continue as insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) or (4) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. (21) The court shall also send the decision on the ancillary appeal to the administrator and to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. (With amendments made by the Laws of 21 June 2012, 29 November 2012, 18 April 2013, 11 September 2014, 31 May 2018, 25 October 2018 and
11 November 2021, which enter into force on 1 December 2021.)

Section 363.15 Decision on Approval of the Act of Sale of Property in Insolvency Proceedings

(1) If the administrator has sold immovable property or an enterprise by auction, the auction act shall be submitted to the court for approval after the successful bidder has paid the entire amount due from him or her. In the application, the administrator shall indicate information about the actions taken in the case related to the sale of the property, attaching documents confirming them, as well as documents confirming that the court costs for submitting the said application to the court have been paid. (2) The court shall approve the auction act in accordance with the provisions of this Law on the auction of immovable property (except as provided for in Paragraphs three and nine of Section 613 of this Law). The court shall examine the application for approval of the immovable property auction act (Sections 611 and 613) and for registration of the sold immovable property in the name of the acquirer in written proceedings within 15 days from the submission of the administrator's application to the court. Upon granting the application, the court shall simultaneously adopt the decisions provided for in Paragraph five of Section 613 of this Law. (3) The actions specified in this Section shall be performed by the court in whose proceedings the legal person's insolvency

proceedings case is located. (4) No later than within three days from the day when the court decision on approval of the auction act has entered into force, the administrator shall pay the state and chancellery fee referred to in Section 611, Paragraph two, Point 4 of this Law into the state budget and notify the acquirer and the district (city) court thereof. (In the wording of the Law of 11 September 2014 with amendments made by the Laws of 25 October 2018 and 16 June 2022, which enter into force on 1 August 2022.)

Section 363.16 Procedure for Examining an Application for Legal Protection Proceedings in Out-of-Court Legal Protection Proceedings After Declaration of Legal Person's Insolvency Proceedings

(1) After declaration of a legal person's insolvency proceedings, an application for legal protection proceedings in out-of-court legal protection proceedings shall be submitted to the court in whose proceedings the legal person's insolvency proceedings case is located. (2) After declaration of a legal person's insolvency proceedings, the court shall examine an application for legal protection proceedings in out-of-court legal protection proceedings in the procedure specified in Chapter 45.1 of this Law. Section 363.17 Examination in Court of Complaints Against Administrator's Decision in Legal Person's Insolvency Proceedings

(1) The court shall examine a complaint by a creditor, debtor's representative or third party whose lawful rights have been infringed against an administrator's decision or auction calculation in a legal person's insolvency proceedings in the cases specified in the Insolvency Law. (11) If there is reason to believe that the rights of the complainant may be infringed, the complainant shall have the right, simultaneously with the submission of a complaint against the administrator's decision, to request the court to impose interim protection measures in the procedure specified in Chapter 30.7 of this Law. (2) If the court finds that the appealed administrator's decision or auction calculation does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and instruct the administrator to remedy the violation committed. (3) If the court finds that the appealed administrator's decision or auction calculation complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall reject the complaint. (4) If, when examining a complaint against an administrator's decision, the court finds that there is a dispute over rights, it shall set a time limit, not longer than one month, within which the complainant may bring an action in the procedure specified in Chapter 30.7 of this Law. If the court on its own initiative finds that there is a dispute that is not to be examined in civil procedure, it shall set a time limit, not longer than 15 days, within which the complainant may submit an application to an institution or court in the general procedure. (5) The complainant shall have the right to withdraw his or her complaint before the examination of the complaint on the merits has been completed. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision to terminate the complaint proceedings. (With amendments made by the Laws of 18 April 2013, 12 February 2015 and 31 May 2018, which enter into force on 1 July 2018.)

Section 363.18 Examination in Court of Complaints Against Creditors' Meeting Decision in Legal Person's Insolvency Proceedings

(1) A complaint by a creditor, debtor's representative or administrator against a creditors' meeting decision in a legal person's insolvency proceedings shall be examined by the court. (2) Having found the appealed creditors' meeting decision to be non-compliant with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall revoke it. (3) When revoking a creditors' meeting decision on non-approval of insolvency proceedings expenses, non-approval of administrator's remuneration or refusal to extend the term of insolvency proceedings, the court may simultaneously decide on approval of insolvency proceedings costs, approval of administrator's remuneration or extension of the term of insolvency proceedings. (4) Having found that the appealed creditors' meeting decision complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall reject the complaint. (5) The complainant shall have the right to withdraw the complaint before the completion of its examination on the merits. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision to terminate the complaint proceedings. Section 363.19 Examination in Court of Complaints Against Decision Adopted by the Insolvency Control Service Regarding Administrator's Actions in Legal Person's Insolvency Proceedings or Imposition of Legal Obligation and Regarding Deposit Payment

(1) Courts shall examine a complaint by a creditor, debtor's representative, administrator or third party whose lawful rights have been infringed against a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service regarding administrator's actions in insolvency proceedings or imposition of a legal obligation and regarding deposit payment. A complaint against a decision of the Insolvency Control Service adopted after the termination of the respective legal person's insolvency proceedings, except for a decision on deposit payment, shall be examined by the court in the procedure specified in this Section. (2) If the court finds that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and decide on:

1) revocation of the decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service in full or in part; 2) imposition of an obligation on the Insolvency Control Service to adopt or examine a complaint regarding administrator's actions; 3) imposition of an obligation on the administrator to remedy the violation committed, except in cases where the debtor has been deleted from the relevant public register. (3) If the court finds that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall reject the complaint. (4) The complainant shall have the right to withdraw his or her complaint before the completion of its examination on the merits. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision to terminate the complaint proceedings. (5) The court shall, after examination of the complaint, immediately send the adopted decision to the Insolvency Control Service. (6) If a decision of the Insolvency Control Service regarding administrator's actions in a legal person's insolvency proceedings has been adopted within one year after the termination of the respective legal person's insolvency proceedings, a complaint against the decision of the Insolvency Control Service shall be submitted to the court in whose proceedings the respective legal person's insolvency proceedings case was located. (With amendments made by the Laws of 31 May 2018 and 11 November 2021, which enter into force on 1 December 2021.)

Section 363.20 Termination of Legal Person's Insolvency Proceedings Case

(1) The court shall terminate a legal person's insolvency proceedings case by rejecting the application for insolvency proceedings or by terminating the insolvency proceedings. (2) The court shall adopt a decision to terminate a legal person's insolvency proceedings if:

1) the debtor has settled all its obligations; 2) legal protection proceedings have been declared for the debtor (transition of insolvency proceedings to legal protection proceedings); 3) a proposal to terminate the insolvency proceedings has been expressed in the report on the absence of the debtor's property and no agreement has been reached on the source of financing for the insolvency proceedings; 4) the creditors' claims satisfaction plan has been fulfilled. (3) In the case referred to in Paragraph two, Point 2 of this Section, a legal protection proceedings action plan coordinated in the procedure specified in the Insolvency Law shall be attached to the application for termination of insolvency proceedings. (4) In the case referred to in Paragraph two, Point 3 of this Section, the administrator shall attach to the application for termination of insolvency proceedings a report on the absence of the debtor's property, creditors' objections, if any have been expressed, and the administrator's response provided. (5) In the case referred to in Paragraph two, Point 4 of this Section, the administrator shall indicate in the application information about creditors' objections not taken into account regarding the report on the fulfilment of the creditors' claims satisfaction plan and shall attach a report on the fulfilment of this plan. (6) The administrator shall attach to the application for termination of insolvency proceedings case his or her activity report and confirmation of payment of the cash balance to the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article
3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if the court has commenced against the debtor the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of the said regulation. (61) The court may, upon application of the administrator of the proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, submitted in accordance with Article
39 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, terminate the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. (7) The court shall send the decision on termination of insolvency proceedings to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. (With amendments made by the Laws of 31 May 2018 and 11 November 2021, which enter into force on 1 December 2021.)

Chapter 46.2
Natural Person's Insolvency Proceedings Cases

## (Chapter 30

In the wording of the 09.2010 law, which comes into force on 01.11.2010.)

Article 363.21. Norms Applicable to the Examination of Cases

In natural person insolvency proceedings, the court shall apply the provisions of Chapter 46.1 of this Law, insofar as this Chapter does not provide otherwise.

Article 363.22. Jurisdiction of Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings Cases

(1) The court shall examine a natural person insolvency proceedings case according to the debtor's application based on the debtor's declared place of residence that was registered for the debtor three months before submitting the application to the court, but if there is no such place — based on the place of residence.

(2) A case concerning the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be examined by the court based on the location of the debtor's centre of main interests, but in the case of initiating insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation — based on the location of the debtor's establishment (within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council).

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 08.12.2016 and 31.05.2018, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

Article 363.23. Content of a Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) In a natural person insolvency proceedings application (hereinafter in this Chapter — insolvency proceedings application), the debtor shall indicate:

1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);
2) the circumstances due to which the natural person is unable to fulfil obligations;
3) all obligations not fulfilled within the time limit and their amounts;
3¹) all obligations whose performance deadline will occur in accordance with the third part of Article 134 of the Insolvency Law;
4) the total amount of all obligations whose performance deadline will occur within one year;
5) the composition of the debtor's property, including the debtor's share in the spouses' joint property and other joint ownership;
6) whether the provisions of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are applicable to the insolvency proceedings;
7) the debtor's declared place of residence that was registered for the debtor three months before submitting the application to the court, but if there is no such place — the place of residence;
8) if the debtor is simultaneously an individual merchant — information about the respective individual merchant (firm (name) and registration number);
9) if the debtor is simultaneously the owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery — information about the respective individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery (firm (name) and registration number).

(1¹) If the insolvency proceedings application is submitted by the debtor together with their spouse or with a person who is related to the debtor by blood or affinity up to the second degree, then the information referred to in the first part of this Article shall be indicated for each applicant separately.

(1²) If the insolvency proceedings application is submitted by a person who is not the debtor, it shall be prepared observing:

1) the provisions of Article 363.2 of this Law, if the insolvency proceedings application is submitted by a creditor or a majority of creditors;
2) the provisions of Article 363.4 of this Law, if the insolvency proceedings application is submitted by a liquidator;
3) the provisions of Article 363.5 of this Law, if the insolvency proceedings application is submitted by the person referred to in Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(1³) In the cases referred to in Part 1² of this Article, the insolvency proceedings application shall additionally indicate the information referred to in point 8 or 9 of the first part of this Article.

(2) The following documents shall be attached to the insolvency proceedings application confirming:

1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);
2) payment of the natural person insolvency proceedings deposit;
3) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);
4) if the debtor is simultaneously the owner of a family enterprise — that the other owners of the family enterprise have been notified of the intention to submit an insolvency proceedings application.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015, 09.06.2016, 08.12.2016, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

Article 363.24. Receipt and Registration of an Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) The court shall accept an insolvency proceedings application from the debtor, their guardian or trustee, a creditor or a majority of creditors, a liquidator or the person referred to in Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The insolvency proceedings application shall be submitted in person in paper form or in an online system.

(2) Upon receiving an insolvency proceedings application, the court shall verify the identity of the applicant. If it is not possible to verify the identity of the applicant who submitted the application in person in paper form or the applicant does not have the appropriate authorisation, the application shall not be accepted.

(3) The insolvency proceedings application shall be registered in a separate register, which shall be signed by the applicant and the recipient. If the insolvency proceedings application is received in the online system, the entry in the register shall be made by the recipient.

(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021 with amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023, which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

Article 363.25. Decision on the Issue of Accepting an Insolvency Proceedings Application and Initiating a Case

(1) Within five days after receiving the insolvency proceedings application, the judge shall adopt a decision:

1) to leave the insolvency proceedings application without progress;
2) to refuse to accept the insolvency proceedings application;
3) to accept the insolvency proceedings application and initiate a case.

(2) If the insolvency proceedings application is left without progress, the judge shall adopt a decision to accept the insolvency proceedings application and initiate a case no later than the next day after the deficiencies indicated in the decision have been remedied. If the time limit for remedying the deficiencies indicated in the decision has expired and they have not been remedied, the application shall be considered as not submitted and returned to the applicant.

(3) The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the insolvency proceedings application if it is established that:

1) the debtor is not a subject of natural person insolvency proceedings;
2) (deleted by the law of 04.08.2011);
3) the applicant has not paid the natural person insolvency proceedings deposit;
4) against the debtor, who is simultaneously an individual merchant, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery or a person engaged in economic activity, a natural person insolvency proceedings case has been initiated based on the debtor's insolvency proceedings application.

(4) If the debtor is simultaneously an individual merchant or owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery, the court shall initiate a natural person insolvency proceedings case on its own initiative if, when adopting a decision to terminate legal protection proceedings, it establishes the sign of natural person insolvency proceedings specified in sub-point "b" of point 5 of the first part of Article 129 of the Insolvency Law.

(5) If the debtor is simultaneously an individual merchant, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery or a person engaged in economic activity, the judge shall adopt a decision to consolidate the initiated natural person insolvency proceedings cases into one proceeding if, by the day when the natural person insolvency proceedings case initiated based on the insolvency proceedings application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law begins to be examined on the merits, it is established that a natural person insolvency proceedings case has been initiated against the debtor based on the insolvency proceedings application of another creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law.

(6) If the debtor is simultaneously an individual merchant, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery or a person engaged in economic activity, the judge shall adopt a decision to suspend proceedings in the case based on the insolvency proceedings application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law if, by the day when the natural person insolvency proceedings case initiated based on the insolvency proceedings application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law begins to be examined on the merits, it is established that a natural person insolvency proceedings case has been initiated against the debtor based on the debtor's insolvency proceedings application. Upon declaring natural person insolvency proceedings based on the debtor's insolvency proceedings application, the court shall resume proceedings in the suspended case based on the insolvency proceedings application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law and terminate it. The paid state fee shall be refunded to the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law in full.

(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011, 12.02.2015 and 16.03.2023, which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

Article 363.26. Court Actions in Preparing a Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings Case for Examination

(1) After initiating a natural person insolvency proceedings case, using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, a candidate for the position of administrator shall be selected from the Candidates List and the judge shall assess their suitability for performing the duties of administrator in the respective natural person insolvency proceedings.

(2) Having established that there are restrictions for the candidate for the position of administrator to perform the duties of administrator in the respective natural person insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator. Using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, a new candidate for the position of administrator shall be selected from the Candidates List, and the judge shall assess their suitability for performing the duties of administrator in the respective natural person insolvency proceedings.

(3) The court shall immediately send the decision on initiating a case based on an application for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council to the administrator of the proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(4) If the debtor is simultaneously an individual merchant, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery or a person engaged in economic activity and the case has been initiated based on the insolvency proceedings application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law, the judge shall send to the debtor the application of the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law and the decision on initiating the case, inform the debtor and the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law about the day of examination of the insolvency proceedings application, as well as about the debtor's right to raise substantiated objections against the claim specified in the insolvency proceedings application no later than three days before the day of examination of the insolvency proceedings application, including to provide evidence that the debtor is able to cover the debt obligations specified in the insolvency proceedings application.

(In the wording of the law of 31.05.2018 with amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023, which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

Article 363.27. Examination of an Insolvency Proceedings Application and Judgment in a Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings Case

(1) The court shall examine a natural person insolvency proceedings case based on the debtor's application within seven days from the day of its initiation. The court shall examine the application in written proceedings, except when it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the insolvency proceedings application is examined in a court session, the debtor shall be invited to the session. The non-appearance of this person shall not be an obstacle to examining the case.

(1¹) If the application is submitted for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the application shall be examined within 15 days from the day of initiating the case or, if the court considers it necessary, in a court session. If the insolvency proceedings application is examined in a court session, the applicant, the debtor and the administrator of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be invited to the session. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examining the case.

(1²) If the debtor is simultaneously an individual merchant, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery or a person engaged in economic activity, then the court shall examine the insolvency proceedings application submitted by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third part of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law within 15 days from the day of initiating the case. The applicant of the insolvency proceedings application and the debtor shall be invited to the court session. If several creditors' insolvency proceedings applications are consolidated in one proceeding, the applicants shall be notified of the court session at least seven days before the respective session. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examining the case.

(1³) If by the time of drafting the judgment the court establishes that the applicant has not paid the state fee or the insolvency proceedings deposit, except when the court has initiated a natural person insolvency proceedings case on its own initiative or has exempted an employee from paying the deposit, it shall leave the insolvency proceedings application without examination. The exception specified in this part shall not apply to cases when a legal protection proceedings application is submitted repeatedly within one year.

(1⁴) If the debtor is simultaneously an individual merchant, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery or a person engaged in economic activity, the judge may adopt a decision on full or partial exemption of an employee from paying the insolvency proceedings deposit if they submit the insolvency proceedings application after it has not been possible to execute a court judgment on debt recovery from the debtor by applying enforcement measures and the employee, considering their financial situation, cannot pay the insolvency proceedings deposit.

(1⁵) The court shall suspend proceedings if, by the day when the natural person insolvency proceedings case begins to be examined on the merits, it establishes that a legal protection proceedings case has been initiated in respect of the debtor's individual merchant, individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery.

(1⁶) In the case referred to in Part 1⁵ of this Article, proceedings in the natural person insolvency proceedings case shall be suspended until a judgment is adopted in the legal protection proceedings case.

(1⁷) Proceedings in the natural person insolvency proceedings case shall be terminated if, according to the judgment, legal protection proceedings are implemented in respect of the debtor's individual merchant, individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery.

(1⁸) Proceedings in the natural person insolvency proceedings case shall be resumed and examined in the procedure specified in this Chapter if legal protection proceedings in respect of the debtor's individual merchant, individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery are terminated based on the second part of Article 341.10 of this Law.

(2) The court shall declare natural person insolvency proceedings for the debtor if it establishes that:

1) there is a sign of insolvency proceedings;
2) in the last year, natural person insolvency proceedings have not been declared that were terminated without discharging obligations;
3) in the last 10 years, natural person insolvency proceedings have not been declared within which obligations were discharged;
4) the applicant has paid the state fee for submitting a natural person insolvency proceedings application;
5) the applicant has paid the natural person insolvency proceedings deposit;
6) in respect of the debtor, an application for discharge of a natural person from debt obligations has not been accepted in the procedure specified in the Law on Discharge of a Natural Person from Debt Obligations.

(3) Upon granting the application, the court shall appoint the candidate for the position of administrator selected in the procedure specified in Article 363.26 of this Law as administrator.

(3¹) The court shall reject the insolvency proceedings application and terminate the natural person insolvency proceedings case if:

1) the sign of insolvency proceedings specified in the application is not established;
2) in the last 10 years, natural person insolvency proceedings have been declared for the debtor within which obligations were discharged;
3) the applicant has not paid the natural person insolvency proceedings deposit or the state fee for submitting a natural person insolvency proceedings application;
4) in the application submitted by the debtor for declaring natural person insolvency proceedings for an individual merchant, individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery, information about the respective natural person is not indicated;
5) in respect of the debtor, an application for discharge of a natural person from debt obligations has been accepted in the procedure specified in the Law on Discharge of a Natural Person from Debt Obligations.

(3²) If the court rejects an insolvency proceedings application whose applicant is not the debtor, it shall simultaneously decide the issue of whether the insolvency proceedings application is to be recognised as unfounded or deliberately false.

(3³) The court shall reject an insolvency proceedings application submitted in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in sub-point "b" of point 4 of the first part of Article 129 of the Insolvency Law if it establishes that no later than three days before the day of examining the case, the debtor has raised substantiated objections against the claim specified in the insolvency proceedings application or that the debt obligations for which the insolvency proceedings application was submitted have been covered in full.

(4) A court judgment in natural person insolvency proceedings shall not be appealable, except for a judgment on rejecting a natural person insolvency proceedings application. A judgment on rejecting a natural person insolvency proceedings application may be appealed in the appellate procedure if there is one of the grounds for initiating appellate proceedings specified in Article 440.2 of this Law.

(4¹) When examining an application for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall take into account the provisions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(4²) When declaring insolvency proceedings in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall indicate in the judgment the type of insolvency proceedings if the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated, or in the decision referred to in Part 4³ of this Article indicate the type of insolvency proceedings if the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated.

(4³) If the court establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia, it shall declare a judgment on the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and adopt a decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The debtor or creditor may submit an appeal against this court decision in accordance with Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 30 days from the day of declaring the decision. Submission of an appeal shall not suspend the initiation of insolvency proceedings.

(4⁴) The court, having established that the court of another Member State that initiated the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor was entitled to initiate such proceedings, shall issue a judgment on the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, without observing the provisions of the second part of this Article. The court shall not initiate the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the conditions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have occurred.

(5) The court shall issue the judgment to the applicant and the administrator, as well as to the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it has initiated the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation against the debtor in Latvia. The court shall send the judgment to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(6) The court, when declaring natural person insolvency proceedings for a debtor who is simultaneously an individual merchant or owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery, shall also indicate in the judgment the firm (name) and registration number of the individual merchant, individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery.

(7) When rejecting an insolvency proceedings application, the court shall send the judgment to the Insolvency Control Service.

(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011, 18.04.2013, 12.02.2015, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

Article 363.28. Issues to be Decided by the Court After Declaring Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings

(1) After declaring natural person insolvency proceedings, the court, based on a respective application, shall decide on:

1) removal of the administrator, setting a time limit for preparing a document and property acceptance and transfer act and transferring documents and property to another administrator;
2) appointment of a new candidate for the position of administrator as administrator if the previous administrator has been removed from the respective insolvency proceedings;
3) approval of the completion of bankruptcy proceedings;
4) approval of a natural person's obligations discharge plan and its amendments;
4¹) extension of the time limit for execution of a natural person's obligations discharge plan in the cases referred to in Part 2¹ of Article 164 of the Insolvency Law;
5) termination of natural person insolvency proceedings;
6) approval of a real estate auction act (Articles 611 and 613) and registration of the sold real estate in the name of the buyer, as well as deletion of the insolvency note in the land register;
7) (deleted by the law of 11.09.2014).

(1¹) An application for approval of a real estate auction act (Articles 611 and 613) and registration of the sold real estate in the name of the buyer shall be examined by the court in whose proceedings the insolvency proceedings case is located, in the procedure specified in Chapter 46.1 of this Law.

(2) The administrator may be removed by the court on its own initiative if, when examining an application or complaint in a natural person insolvency proceedings case, it establishes that the administrator does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments or does not execute court judgments.

(3) If after declaring insolvency proceedings the court has adopted a decision to remove the administrator, after adopting this decision it shall appoint as administrator the candidate for the position of administrator selected from the Candidates List using automated selection provided by the Court Information System.

(4) (Deleted by the law of 31.05.2018)

(5) Having established that there are restrictions for the candidate for the position of administrator to perform the duties of administrator in the respective natural person insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator. The judge shall adopt a decision to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator in the procedure specified in the third part of this Article.

(6) The court shall immediately send the decisions referred to in points 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 of the first part of this Article to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(7) The court shall examine a complaint against an administrator's decision, as well as a complaint against a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service regarding the administrator's actions in natural person insolvency proceedings or the imposition of a legal obligation. The court shall immediately send the decision adopted after examining the complaint to the Insolvency Control Service.

(8) The court shall examine an application and complaint within 15 days from the day of receiving the application or complaint. The judge shall examine the application in written proceedings without holding a court session, except when they consider it necessary to examine the case in a court session. The judge shall examine the complaint in written proceedings without holding a court session, except when the administrator requests to examine the case in a court session or the court considers it necessary to examine the complaint in a court session. The applicant or complainant, the administrator, the debtor's representative and other interested persons shall be invited to the court session. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examining the issue.

(9) A court decision on examining an application and complaint shall not be appealable. A court decision on removing an administrator on the basis of point 1, 2, 3, 4 or 7 of the second part of Article 22 of the Insolvency Law shall be appealable in the part concerning the established non-compliance with the requirements of regulatory enactments or non-execution of a court judgment by submitting an appeal. The regional court shall examine this appeal within 15 days.

(9¹) An appeal may be submitted against a court decision in a case on approval of an auction act.

(10) For examining the issues referred to in this Article, the court may request that the administrator submit a report on their activities or other information.

(11) The regional court, when examining the appeal referred to in the ninth part of this Article, shall have the right to:

1) leave the decision unchanged and reject the complaint;
2) revoke the decision and decide the issue on the merits with its own decision.

(12) The decision referred to in the eleventh part of this Article shall come into force and be executable immediately.

(13) The regional court shall send the decisions referred to in the eleventh part of this Article to the Insolvency Control Service.

(14) The regional court shall examine the debtor's or creditor's appeal against a court decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 15 days.

(15) In addition to what is referred to in Article 443.1 of this Law, the appeal shall indicate:

1) from what time the debtor's permanent place of residence has been in the European Union Member State indicated in the appeal;
2) whether the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been initiated against the debtor in another European Union Member State.

(16) The regional court, when examining the appeal referred to in the fourteenth part of this Article, shall have the right to:

1) leave the decision unchanged and reject the complaint;
2) revoke the decision in full.

(17) If the regional court has revoked the decision, the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be continued as the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) or (4) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(18) The court shall also send the decision on the appeal to the administrator and the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 21.06.2012, 29.11.2012, 18.04.2013, 11.09.2014, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

Article 363.29. Termination of Bankruptcy Proceedings

(1) Based on the administrator's application, the court shall decide on the termination of bankruptcy proceedings.

(2) In the application for termination of bankruptcy proceedings, the administrator shall indicate the grounds for terminating bankruptcy proceedings.

(2¹) Based on the debtor's application, the court shall decide on the termination of bankruptcy proceedings if no creditors' claims have been submitted against the debtor.

(2²) In the application for termination of bankruptcy proceedings in the case specified in Part 2¹ of this Article, the debtor shall indicate all their obligations and their basis.

(2³) If the court, when terminating bankruptcy proceedings, establishes that the debtor's obligations have become time-barred in the procedure specified in the Insolvency Law, it shall simultaneously adopt a decision to terminate natural person insolvency proceedings.

(2⁴) Based on the application of the debtor, who is simultaneously an individual merchant or owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery, the court shall decide on declaring legal protection proceedings in out-of-court legal protection proceedings for the individual merchant, individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishery, observing the provisions of Chapter 45.1 of this Law and simultaneously terminating natural person insolvency proceedings.

(3) The court shall terminate bankruptcy proceedings if it establishes restrictions on the application of natural person insolvency proceedings.

(4) When terminating bankruptcy proceedings, the court shall simultaneously adopt a decision to terminate insolvency proceedings.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015 and 16.03.2023, which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

Article 363.30. Completion of Bankruptcy Proceedings

(1) Based on the administrator's application, the court shall decide on the completion of bankruptcy proceedings.

(2) In the application for completion of bankruptcy proceedings, the administrator shall indicate:

1) the grounds for completing bankruptcy proceedings;
2) the measures taken within the bankruptcy proceedings;
3) a list of the debtor's sold property, including the sold debtor's property share in the spouses' joint property and other joint ownership and the income obtained from the sale of the debtor's property and its distribution;
4) whether the obligations discharge procedure is applicable to the debtor;
5) objections and proposals received from the debtor and creditors that have not been taken into account.

(3) If the obligations discharge procedure is intended to be applied to the debtor, the debtor shall submit for approval to the court an obligations discharge plan and the creditors' objections and proposals received and not taken into account regarding this plan.

(4) When examining the issue of completion of bankruptcy proceedings, the court shall verify whether the bankruptcy proceedings have taken place in the procedure specified by law.

(5) If the court approves the completion of bankruptcy proceedings and the obligations discharge procedure is not applied to the debtor, the court shall simultaneously adopt a decision to terminate insolvency proceedings.

Article 363.31. Approval of an Obligations Discharge Plan

(1) When approving the completion of bankruptcy proceedings, the court shall simultaneously examine the issue of approval of an obligations discharge plan.

(2) The court shall not approve an obligations discharge plan if it establishes restrictions on the application of the obligations discharge procedure.

(3) The court shall verify whether the obligations discharge plan complies with the requirements of law.

(4) If the court establishes deficiencies in the obligations discharge plan, it shall set a time limit for the debtor to remedy the deficiencies, and it may not be shorter than 10 and longer than 30 days.

(5) The court shall approve an obligations discharge plan if it complies with the requirements of law and no objections from creditors and debtors have been received or these objections are to be recognised as unfounded.

Article 363.32. Examination in Court of Complaints Against an Administrator's Decision in Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings

(1) The court shall examine a complaint by a creditor, debtor or third party whose legal rights have been violated against an administrator's decision in natural person insolvency proceedings.

(2) If the court recognises that the appealed administrator's decision does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and instruct the administrator to remedy the committed violation.

(3) If the court establishes that the appealed administrator's decision complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall reject the complaint.

(4) If, when examining a complaint against an administrator's decision, the court establishes that there is a dispute about rights, it shall set a time limit within which the complainant may bring an action in court in the general procedure or may request to resume the proceedings suspended regarding the subject of the dispute.

(5) The complainant shall have the right to withdraw their complaint before the examination of the complaint on the merits has been completed. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision to terminate the complaint proceedings.

(With amendments made by the law of 18.04.2013, which comes into force on 22.05.2013.)

Article 363.33. Examination in Court of Complaints Against a Creditors' Meeting Decision in Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings

(1) A complaint by a creditor, debtor's representative or administrator against a creditors' meeting decision in natural person insolvency proceedings shall be examined by the court.(2) Upon finding that the appealed decision of the creditors' meeting does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall revoke it.

(3) Upon revoking a decision of the creditors' meeting regarding non-approval of insolvency proceedings expenses, non-approval of the administrator's remuneration, or refusal to extend the term of insolvency proceedings, the court may simultaneously decide on the approval of insolvency proceedings costs, approval of the administrator's remuneration, or extension of the term of insolvency proceedings.

(4) Having established that the appealed decision of the creditors' meeting complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall reject the complaint.

(5) The complainant has the right to withdraw the complaint until the completion of its examination on the merits. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision on termination of the complaint proceedings.

363.34 Article. Examination in Court of Complaints Regarding a Decision Adopted by the Insolvency Control Service Concerning the Administrator's Actions in Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings or the Imposition of a Legal Obligation

(1) The court shall examine a complaint by a creditor, debtor, administrator, or third person whose legal rights have been infringed, regarding a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service concerning the administrator's actions in insolvency proceedings or the imposition of a legal obligation. A complaint regarding a decision of the Insolvency Control Service that has been adopted after the termination of the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings shall be examined by the court in the procedure specified in this Article.

(2) If the court finds that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and decide on:

1) revocation of the decision of the Insolvency Control Service in whole or in part;

2) imposition of an obligation on the Insolvency Control Service to adopt or examine a complaint regarding the administrator's actions;

3) imposition of an obligation on the administrator to remedy the committed violation, except in cases where the natural person insolvency proceedings have been terminated.

(3) If the court establishes that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall reject the complaint.

(4) The complainant has the right to withdraw his or her complaint until the completion of its examination on the merits. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision on termination of the complaint proceedings.

(5) The court shall immediately send the adopted decision to the Insolvency Control Service after examination of the complaint.

(6) If a decision of the Insolvency Control Service regarding the administrator's actions in natural person insolvency proceedings or the imposition of a legal obligation has been adopted within one year after the termination of the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings, the complaint regarding the decision of the Insolvency Control Service shall be submitted to the court in whose jurisdiction the relevant case concerning the natural person insolvency proceedings was located.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

363.35 Article. Termination of Debt Discharge Procedure

(1) The court shall examine the issue of termination of the debt discharge procedure upon application by the debtor or administrator.

(2) The court shall approve the termination of the debt discharge procedure if it establishes that the debtor has fulfilled the debt discharge plan and no objections have been received from creditors and the debtor, or the objections received are to be considered unfounded.

(3) Upon approving the termination of the debt discharge procedure, the court shall decide on the discharge of obligations that have not been fulfilled during the debt discharge process.

(4) The debtor, creditor, or administrator shall attach to the application for termination of the debt discharge procedure evidence confirming the circumstances indicated in the application.

(5) Upon approving the termination of the debt discharge procedure, the court shall simultaneously adopt a decision on termination of the insolvency proceedings.

363.36 Article. Termination of Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings

(1) The court shall adopt a decision on termination of natural person insolvency proceedings if:

1) after approval of the completion of bankruptcy procedure, the debt discharge procedure is not applied to the debtor;

2) the debtor has settled all his or her obligations;

3) it establishes restrictions on the application of natural person insolvency proceedings;

4) it establishes restrictions on the application of debt discharge procedure;

5) the debtor fails to fulfil the debt discharge plan;

6) the debt discharge plan has been fulfilled;

7) during the bankruptcy procedure, creditors' claims have not been submitted in accordance with the time limits specified in the Insolvency Law, simultaneously also terminating the bankruptcy procedure;

8) legal protection proceedings have been declared for the debtor's individual merchant, individual (family) enterprise, farm, or fishery in out-of-court legal protection proceedings, simultaneously terminating the natural person insolvency proceedings.

(2) If the court, upon terminating the debt discharge procedure, establishes that the debtor is to be released from debt obligations in accordance with Article 164 of the Insolvency Law, it shall simultaneously with the termination of the procedure release him or her from the obligations specified in the natural person debt discharge plan.

(21) The court, upon application by the administrator of the procedure specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, submitted in accordance with Article 39 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, may terminate the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(3) The court shall immediately send the decision on termination of natural person insolvency proceedings to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021, and 16.03.2023, which enter into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

363.37 Article. Application for Revocation of Debtor's Release from Obligations and Its Acceptance

(1) The debtor, creditor, or other person whose legal rights have been infringed has the right to submit an application for revocation of the debtor's release from obligations within the time limit and in the cases specified in Article 165.1 of the Insolvency Law.

(2) If the applicant is not the debtor, the application shall be sent to the debtor, setting a time limit for submission of an explanation, not exceeding 30 days. The application shall be sent to the administrator who was appointed in the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings, setting a time limit for submission of an opinion, not exceeding 30 days.

(3) Acceptance of the application shall not suspend the effect of the court decision on termination of natural person insolvency proceedings.

(4) The applicant may submit an appeal against the court decision refusing to accept the application.

(In the wording of the law of 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

363.38 Article. Examination of Application for Revocation of Debtor's Release from Obligations and Court Decision

(1) The application shall be examined in written proceedings without holding a court session, except in cases where the court considers it necessary to examine the application in a court session or a party to the case so requests, substantiating his or her request.

(2) The court shall grant the application if it establishes that there exists a basis specified in the second or third paragraph of Article 165.1 of the Insolvency Law for revoking the debtor's release from obligations.

(3) If the court grants the application, it shall send the decision to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register and to the administrator who was appointed in the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings.

(4) The applicant may submit an appeal against the court decision rejecting the application.

(In the wording of the law of 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Chapter 47
Credit Institution Insolvency and Liquidation Cases

### 364. pants. Case Jurisdiction

Insolvency or liquidation cases of a credit institution shall be heard by the court according to the legal address of the credit institution.  
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 365. pants. Applicants for Insolvency Petition

An insolvency petition may be submitted to the court by:

1)	a credit institution or a liquidator of a credit institution;  

2)	a creditor or a group of creditors;  

3)	an administrator in another insolvency proceeding;  

4)	Latvijas Banka.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 366. pants. Applicant for Liquidation Petition

A liquidation petition shall be submitted to the court by Latvijas Banka.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 367. pants. Procedure for Submission of Insolvency Petition

(1)	A credit institution, a liquidator of a credit institution, a creditor or a group of creditors, an administrator in another insolvency

proceeding may submit an insolvency petition of a credit institution to the court after it has been examined by Latvijas Banka.  

(2)	An insolvency petition shall be submitted to the court by Latvijas Banka, attaching thereto its decision on submission of the petition to the court and other documents that may be relevant to the case. In this case, the person in whose name the insolvency petition has been prepared and who has submitted it to Latvijas Banka shall be considered the applicant. The insolvency petition must comply with the requirements of Sections 368 and 369 of this Law.  

(3)	If Latvijas Banka has rejected an insolvency petition, the persons referred to in the first paragraph of this Section may submit it directly to the court. In such case, the decision of Latvijas Banka on refusal to submit the insolvency petition to the court shall be attached to the insolvency petition.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 368. pants

Content of an Insolvency Petition Submitted by a Creditor, a Group of Creditors or an Administrator in Another Insolvency Proceeding

(1)	An insolvency petition submitted by a creditor, a group of creditors or an administrator in another insolvency proceeding shall indicate:

1)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

2)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

3)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

4)	the circumstances of actual insolvency and evidence confirming these circumstances;  

5)	the documents attached to the insolvency petition.  

(2)	Documents confirming the actual insolvency of the credit institution, as well as the decision of Latvijas Banka on refusal to submit the insolvency petition to the court, shall be attached to the insolvency petition.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 29.11.2012., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 369. pants. Content of a Credit Institution's Insolvency Petition

(1)	An insolvency petition submitted by a credit institution shall indicate:

1)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

2)	the number of the licence issued for the credit institution's operations, the date of issue and re-registration, and the details of all accounts opened for the credit institution;  

3)	the circumstances of actual insolvency or the possibility of its occurrence and evidence confirming these circumstances;  

4)	the documents attached to the insolvency petition.  

(2)	The following shall be attached to the insolvency petition:

1)	a list of the chairpersons and members of the credit institution's council, board and audit institutions and representatives of the credit institution (name, surname, personal identity number and address);  

2)	the credit institution's last balance sheet prepared in accordance with the instructions of Latvijas Banka on the preparation of the annual report;  

3)	documents confirming the circumstances of the credit institution's actual insolvency or the possibility of its occurrence;  

4)	a list of property belonging to third parties in the possession or holding of the credit institution, excluding deposits and interest thereon;  

5)	the decision of Latvijas Banka on refusal to submit the insolvency petition to the court.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 29.11.2012., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 370. pants. Content of Latvijas Banka's Petition for Insolvency of a Credit Institution

(1)	An insolvency petition submitted by Latvijas Banka shall indicate:

1)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

2)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

3)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

4)	the circumstances of actual insolvency or the possibility of its occurrence and evidence confirming these circumstances;  

5)	the documents attached to the insolvency petition.  

(2)	Documents confirming the circumstances of the credit institution's actual insolvency or the possibility of its occurrence shall be attached to the insolvency petition.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 29.11.2012., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 371. pants. Content of a Credit Institution's Liquidation Petition

(1)	A liquidation petition of a credit institution shall indicate:

1)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

2)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

3)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

4)	the representatives of the credit institution and the persons whose participation in the liquidation of the credit institution is mandatory;  

5)	the circumstances due to which the licence issued for the credit institution's operations has been revoked, and evidence confirming these circumstances;  

6)	the documents attached to the petition.  

(2)	The decision of the European Central Bank on the revocation of the licence issued for the credit institution's operations and documents confirming the circumstances due to which the licence issued for the credit institution's operations has been revoked shall be attached to the liquidation petition.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 12.02.2009., 29.11.2012., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which
comes into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 372. pants

Submission and Registration of a Credit Institution's Insolvency Petition and Liquidation Petition

(1)	An insolvency petition or liquidation petition of a credit institution may be submitted to the court by a representative of Latvijas Banka, but in the case provided for in the third paragraph of Section 367 of this Law — by the applicant or his or her representative. An insolvency petition or liquidation petition of a credit institution shall be submitted in person in paper form or in an online system.  

(2)	Upon receipt of an insolvency petition or liquidation petition of a credit institution, the court shall verify the identity of the applicant. If it is not possible to verify the identity of the applicant who has submitted the petition in person in paper form or the applicant does not have the appropriate authorisation, the petition shall not be accepted.  

(3)	An insolvency petition and liquidation petition of a credit institution shall be registered in a separate register, which shall be signed by the applicant and the recipient. If an insolvency petition or liquidation petition of a credit institution has been received in the online system, the entry in the register shall be made by the recipient.  
(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021. with amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 373. pants. Initiation of Insolvency Case and Liquidation Case of a Credit Institution

(1)	A decision on the initiation of an insolvency case and liquidation case of a credit institution or on refusal to accept the petition shall be adopted by the judge no later than the next day after receipt of the petition by the court, but if the petition has been left without progress — no later than the next day after the deficiencies indicated in the judge's decision have been remedied or the time limit for remedying the deficiencies has expired.  

(2)	Upon initiating the case, the court shall seize the property of the credit institution, except in cases where the insolvency petition has been submitted in the procedure provided for in the third paragraph of Section 367 of this Law.

### 374. pants

Judge's actions in preparing a credit institution insolvency case for hearing

(1)	After initiation of a credit institution insolvency proceedings case, an administrator candidate is selected from the List of Candidates using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, and the judge evaluates his or her suitability for performing the administrator's duties in the respective credit institution insolvency proceedings.

(11) Having established that there are restrictions on the administrator candidate's performance of administrator duties in the specific credit institution insolvency proceedings, the judge adopts a decision to refuse to appoint the administrator candidate as administrator. Using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, another administrator candidate is selected from the List of Candidates, and the judge evaluates his or her suitability for performing the administrator's duties in the respective credit institution insolvency proceedings.

(2)	A person to whom the restrictions set out in the Credit Institution Law apply may not be appointed as administrator.

(3)	When appointing an administrator, he or she shall be instructed to:

1)	prepare a list of persons whose participation in the insolvency proceedings is mandatory;

2)	prepare a report on the credit institution's assets (property) at their actual (market) value;

3)	identify property belonging to third parties that is in the possession or holding of the credit institution and prepare a list of such property;

4)	prepare a list of creditors according to the data in the credit institution's accounts, indicating information about creditors, the amounts of debts and obligations and the performance deadlines;

5)	submit the said information to the court before the hearing of the case.
