(4)	A declaration signed by the administrator shall be attached to the case, which confirms his or her consent to assume office and to assume the liability provided for by law.

(5)	(Deleted as of 01.09.2023. by the law of 16.03.2023. See transitional provision 181)
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023. The new wording of the first part, part 1.1 and the amendment on the deletion of the fifth part enter into force on 01.09.2023. See transitional provision 181)

### 375. pants. Hearing of credit institution insolvency cases and liquidation cases

(1)	The court shall hear a credit institution insolvency case and liquidation case within 10 days from the date of initiation of the case.

(2)	The applicant, the representative of the credit institution, the representative of the Bank of Latvia, and in an insolvency case — also the administrator, shall be invited to the court session.

(3)	In a credit institution insolvency case and liquidation case, withdrawal from the application or amendment thereof is not permitted.

(4)	When hearing a credit institution insolvency case, the court shall verify whether there is any of the circumstances provided for in the Credit Institution Law indicating the insolvency of the credit institution and whether the pre-trial examination procedure for the application provided for in Section 367 of this Law has been observed.

(5)	When hearing a credit institution liquidation case, the court shall not assess the solvency of the credit institution.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 12.02.2009., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023. The amendment in the first part replacing the word "seven" with the number "10" enters into force on 01.09.2023. See transitional provision 181)

### 376. pants. Court judgment in a credit institution insolvency case

(1)	If the court establishes any of the circumstances indicating the insolvency of the credit institution, it shall, by its judgment, declare the credit institution insolvent and determine that the insolvency of the credit institution occurs on the day of pronouncement of the court judgment. The judgment is final and not subject to appeal.

(2)	When making a judgment on the insolvency of a credit institution, the court shall confirm the appointed administrator.

(3)	On the basis of the application of the Bank of Latvia and the list prepared by the administrator, the court shall determine those representatives of the credit institution and persons whose participation in the insolvency proceedings is mandatory.

(4)	The judgment is the basis for suspension of civil proceedings initiated against the credit institution and for termination of enforcement proceedings in cases concerning the recovery of amounts awarded but not recovered from the credit institution.

(5)	If the court does not establish circumstances indicating the insolvency of the credit institution, it shall reject the application, simultaneously terminating the insolvency proceedings and deciding the question of whether the application is to be recognised as knowingly false in accordance with the Credit Institution Law.

(6)	When recognising the application as knowingly false, the court shall recover from the applicant the court costs, as well as the remuneration of the administrator and the assistant administrator.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 08.09.2011., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 377. pants. Court judgment in a credit institution liquidation case

(1)	If the court establishes that the European Central Bank has revoked the licence issued for the operation of the credit institution in accordance with the Credit Institution Law, it shall recognise the credit institution as subject to liquidation. The judgment is final and not subject to appeal.

(2)	When making a judgment on the liquidation of a credit institution, the court shall appoint a liquidator of the credit institution. The court shall appoint as liquidator of the credit institution a person recommended by the Bank of Latvia.

(3)	A person to whom the restrictions set out in the Credit Institution Law apply may not be appointed as liquidator.

(4)	On the basis of the application of the Bank of Latvia, the court shall determine those representatives of the credit institution and persons whose participation in the liquidation of the credit institution is mandatory.

(5)	The judgment is the basis for suspension of civil proceedings initiated against the credit institution and for termination of enforcement proceedings in cases concerning the recovery of amounts awarded but not recovered from the credit institution.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 12.02.2009., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 378. pants

Court actions after declaration of insolvency or liquidation of a credit institution

(1)	After pronouncement of the judgment, the court shall issue to the administrator or liquidator the judgment with a note on the entry into force of the judgment.

(2)	The judge shall warn the representatives of the credit institution and persons designated in the judgment whose participation in the insolvency proceedings or liquidation of the credit institution is mandatory that:

1)	it is their duty to appear at all court sessions, their non-appearance is not an obstacle to the examination of the matter in a court session, but the court may consider their appearance mandatory and order them to be brought by force;

2)	they have a duty to provide the court and the administrator or liquidator with the necessary information;

3)	if the contact information for communication with the court changes, they must notify the court and the administrator or liquidator of the current contact information for communication with the court within three days;

4)	in case of failure to fulfil their duties, they may be held liable as provided for by law.

(21) After pronouncement of the judgment, the court shall inform the Bank of Latvia thereof, ensuring that the Bank of Latvia receives the relevant information on the day of pronouncement of the judgment. The procedure for informing the Bank of Latvia shall be determined by the Minister for Justice.

(3)	At the request of the administrator or liquidator, the court shall adopt a decision on the release of property from encumbrance and its transfer to the administrator or liquidator.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2004., 29.11.2012., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 379. pants

Issues to be decided by the court after declaration of insolvency of a credit institution

(1)	After declaration of insolvency of a credit institution, the court shall decide on the basis of a relevant application on:

1)	(deleted by the law of 16.03.2023.);  

2)	(deleted by the law of 16.03.2023.);  

3)	insolvency proceedings expenses;  

4)	the order and time limits for debt settlement;  

5)	completion of insolvency proceedings and approval of the administrator's report;  

6)	(deleted by the law of 16.03.2023.);  

7)	acceptance of the administrator's resignation or his or her removal and appointment of another administrator.  

(2)	The court shall also examine complaints about the administrator's actions and decide other issues related to insolvency proceedings.  

(3)	The court may, in connection with the examination of the issues referred to in this Article, request that the administrator submit a report on his or her activities or other information.  

(4)	The court shall examine applications and complaints within 15 days from the date of their receipt. The submitter of the application or complaint, the administrator, the representatives of the credit institution determined by the court and persons whose participation in insolvency proceedings is mandatory shall be invited to the court hearing. The non-appearance of invited persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the matter at the court hearing. However, the court may determine that the representatives of the credit institution or persons whose participation in insolvency proceedings is mandatory must appear at the court hearing and order them to be brought by force.  

(5)	The court shall adopt decisions on the examination of applications and complaints, which are not subject to appeal.  
(With amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 380. pants

Issues to be decided by the court after declaration of liquidation of a credit institution

(1)	After declaration of liquidation of a credit institution, the court shall decide on the basis of a relevant application on:

1)	appointment of several liquidators;  

2)	acceptance of the liquidator's resignation or his or her removal and appointment of another liquidator;  

3)	completion of liquidation and approval of the liquidator's report.  

(2)	The court shall also examine complaints about the liquidator's actions and decide other issues related to liquidation.  

(3)	The court may, in connection with the examination of the issues referred to in this Article, request that the liquidator submit a report on his or her activities or other information.  

(4)	The court shall examine applications and complaints within 15 days from the date of their receipt. The submitter of the application or complaint, the liquidator, the representatives of the credit institution determined by the court and persons whose participation in the liquidation of the credit institution is mandatory shall be invited to the court hearing. The non-appearance of invited persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the matter at the court hearing. However, the court may determine that the representatives of the credit institution or persons whose participation in liquidation is mandatory must appear at the court hearing and order them to be brought by force.  

(5)	The court shall adopt decisions on the examination of applications and complaints, which are not subject to appeal.

### 383. pants

Contesting the order of settlement of insolvency proceedings and liquidation expenses and debts

(1)	Upon application by a creditor or a group of creditors, the court shall decide whether the decision of the administrator or liquidator establishing the order of settlement of insolvency proceedings or liquidation expenses and debts complies with the law.  

(2)	If the court finds that the order of settlement of insolvency proceedings expenses and debts established by the administrator or the order of settlement of liquidation expenses and debts established by the liquidator does not comply with the law, it shall adopt a decision establishing the order of settlement of insolvency proceedings or liquidation expenses and debts, at the same time, if necessary, deciding the issue of settlement of unjustified insolvency proceedings or liquidation expenses from the administrator's or liquidator's security.

### 384. pants. Decision on completion of insolvency proceedings

The court shall decide on the completion of insolvency proceedings upon application by the administrator, to which documents certifying cash payments are attached.

### 385. pants. Decision on completion of liquidation

### 386. pants. Complaints about the actions of the administrator or liquidator

(1)	When examining a complaint about the actions of the administrator or liquidator, the court may request a report on the activities of the administrator or liquidator and the opinion of the Bank of Latvia on the activities of the administrator or liquidator and decide on his or her removal.  

(2)	If the court determines that the contested action does not comply with the law, it shall grant the complaint and instruct the administrator or liquidator to remedy the violation committed.  

(3)	If the court finds that the contested action is lawful, it shall reject the complaint.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 387. pants. Decision on acceptance of the administrator's or liquidator's resignation or his or her removal

(1)	The court shall accept the resignation of the administrator or liquidator if he or she submits a reasoned application to which a report on his or her activities is attached.  

(2)	The administrator or liquidator may be removed by the court upon application by the Bank of Latvia. The decision of the Bank of Latvia on expressing no confidence in the administrator or liquidator in connection with any of the following circumstances shall be attached to the application:

1)	the administrator or liquidator does not comply with the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 131 or the first paragraph of Article 131.1 of the Credit Institution Law or any of the circumstances referred to in Articles 132 or 132.1 is revealed;  

2)	the administrator or liquidator is not competent;  

3)	the administrator or liquidator abuses his or her powers.  

(3)	The court may examine the issue of removal of the administrator or liquidator upon application by a creditor or a group of creditors or on its own initiative if it has evidence that the administrator or liquidator, in performing his or her duties, does not comply with the provisions of the Credit Institution Law and other regulatory enactments and court decisions, does not comply with the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 131 or the first paragraph of Article 131.1 of the Credit Institution Law or any of the circumstances referred to in Articles 132 or
132.1 is revealed, the administrator or liquidator is not competent or abuses his or her powers.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 12.02.2009., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 388. pants

(1)	In case of resignation or removal of the administrator, the court shall immediately appoint as administrator a candidate for the position of administrator, who is selected from the List of Candidates using an automated selection provided by the Court Information System, and shall also determine the time limit for submission of a document confirming security.  

(2)	Having established that there are restrictions on the performance of the administrator's duties in the specific insolvency proceedings of the credit institution in relation to the candidate for the position of administrator, the judge shall adopt a decision on refusal to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator. The judge shall adopt a decision on the appointment of the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator in the manner specified in the first paragraph of this Article.  

(3)	In case of resignation or removal of the liquidator, the court shall, upon recommendation of the Bank of Latvia, immediately appoint another liquidator and shall also determine the time limit for submission of a document confirming security.  
(In the wording of the law of 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023. The new wording of the Article enters into force on 01.09.2023. See transitional provision point 181.)

48. nodaļa
Recognition of a strike or strike notice as unlawful

### 390. pants. Submission of an application

(1) An application for recognition of a strike or strike notice as unlawful in accordance with the grounds specified in the Strike Law and the procedure established therein may be submitted by the employer.

(2) An application for recognition of a strike or strike notice as unlawful shall be submitted to the court according to the place where the strike occurs.

### 391. pants. Content of the application

(1) The application shall indicate the strike initiators, the demands of the strike initiators or strikers, the head of the strike committee, its composition, location, the grounds specified in the Strike Law according to which the strike or strike notice is to be recognised as unlawful.

(2) The application shall be accompanied by the protocol of strike negotiations between the employer and the employees or the employees' trade union.

### 392. pants. Examination of the application

(1) The court shall examine the application within 10 days from the date of its receipt. The application shall be examined at a court hearing, of which the employer, the State Labour Inspectorate and the strike committee are notified in advance.

(2) The participation of the applicant in the court hearing is mandatory. In case of his or her non-appearance, the court has grounds to terminate the case.

### 393. pants. Mandatory participation of the prosecutor

Cases concerning applications for recognition of a strike or strike notice as unlawful shall be examined by the court with the mandatory participation of the prosecutor.

### 394. pants. Court judgment on the application

(1) Having examined the application, the court shall render a judgment by which it:

1) recognises the employer's application as unfounded and rejects it;

2) recognises the employer's application as founded, but the strike or strike notice as unlawful.

(2) The court judgment is final and not subject to appeal.

Recognition of a lockout or lockout notice as unlawful

394.1 pants. Submission of an application

(1) An application for recognition of a lockout or lockout notice as unlawful in accordance with the grounds specified in the Labour Disputes Law and the procedure established therein may be submitted by employee representatives.

(2) An application for recognition of a lockout or lockout notice as unlawful shall be submitted to the court according to the place where the lockout occurs.

394.2 pants. Content of the application

The application shall indicate the lockout initiator and the grounds specified in the Labour Disputes Law according to which the lockout or lockout notice is to be recognised as unlawful.

394.3 pants. Examination of the application

(1) The court shall examine the application within 10 days from the date of its receipt. The application shall be examined at a court hearing, of which the employee representatives, the State Labour Inspectorate and the lockout initiators are notified in advance.

(2) The participation of the applicant in the court hearing is mandatory. If the applicant does not appear at the court hearing, the court has grounds to terminate the case.

394.4 pants. Mandatory participation of the prosecutor

Cases concerning applications for recognition of a lockout or lockout notice as unlawful shall be examined by the court with the mandatory participation of the prosecutor.

394.5 pants. Court judgment on the application

(1) Having examined the application, the court shall render a judgment by which it recognises the application of the employee representatives as:

2) founded, but the lockout or lockout notice as unlawful.

(2) The court judgment is final and not subject to appeal.

48.2 nodaļa
Cases concerning cancellation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations

## (Nodaļa 15

06.2021. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2022.)

394.6 pants. Jurisdiction over cases concerning cancellation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations

(1) Cases concerning cancellation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations shall be examined by the court according to the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the place of residence.

(2) The case shall be examined on the basis of an application for cancellation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations, which shall be submitted by a creditor, a sworn notary who has drawn up the notarial act on discharge of a natural person from debt obligations, or another person whose legal rights have been infringed.
(15.06.2021. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2022.)

394.7 pants. Decision on an application for cancellation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations

(1) A copy of the application shall be sent to the person concerning whose cancellation of discharge from debt obligations the application has been submitted, setting a time limit for submission of explanations, not exceeding 30 days.

(2) If the applicant is not the sworn notary who has drawn up the notarial act on discharge of a natural person from debt obligations, the court shall inform the sworn notary who has drawn up the notarial act on discharge of a natural person from debt obligations of the initiation of the case, at the same time setting a time limit, not exceeding 30 days, for submission to the court of copies of the notarial act on discharge of a natural person from debt obligations and other case materials.

(3) Acceptance of the application shall not suspend the operation of the notarial act by which the natural person has been discharged from debt obligations.

(4) The applicant may submit an appeal against the court decision to refuse to accept the application.

(5) If, when examining the appeal referred to in paragraph four of this Section, the court revokes the decision, the court shall refer the matter for examination to the court that adopted the decision.

(15.06.2021. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2022.)

394.8 pants. Examination of an application for cancellation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations and court judgment

(1) The application shall be examined in written proceedings without holding a court hearing, except in cases where the court considers it necessary to examine the application at a court hearing or a party to the case so requests, substantiating its request.

(2) If the court grants the application, it shall send a copy of the judgment after the judgment enters into force to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register and to the sworn bailiff in whose proceedings there is an enforcement case against the debtor.

(3) The parties to the case may appeal the judgment within 20 days from the date of drawing up the judgment if there is any of the grounds for initiating appellate proceedings referred to in Section 440.2 of this Law.
(15.06.2021. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2022.)

Introduction of the acquirer of immovable property into possession

394.9 Article. Jurisdiction

An application for the introduction of the acquirer of immovable property into possession of the immovable property shall be submitted to the court that confirmed the auction act of the immovable property (Article 613), after the decision on the confirmation of the auction act has entered into force.  
(11.11.2021. law version, which comes into force 01.12.2021.)

394.10 Article. Content of the application

(1)	The application shall indicate information about the immovable property into the possession of which the introduction is to be carried out, and the acquirer.  

(2)	If introduction into possession is requested in immovable property in which premises are used on the basis of a previously concluded lease agreement, the following shall be attached to the application:

1)	documents certifying compliance with the requirements established by law regarding informing the tenant about the change of owner of the immovable property and the obligation to vacate the residential premises within two months, or

2)	a certificate issued by a sworn notary about persons who have submitted a notification about residential premises lease agreements within the time limit specified in the notary's invitation, together with documents certifying compliance with the requirements established by law regarding informing the tenant about the obligation to vacate the residential premises within one month, or

3)	a certificate issued by a sworn notary that no person who has the right to rent the residential premises has applied within the time limit specified in the notary's invitation.  
(11.11.2021. law version, which comes into force 01.12.2021.)

394.11 Article. Examination of the application

(1)	The application shall be examined in written proceedings within 20 days from the date of receipt of the application, after notifying the applicant in advance.  

(2)	When examining the application, Article 258 of this law shall not be applicable.  
(11.11.2021. law version, which comes into force 01.12.2021.)

394.	12 Article. Court decision

Having found the application to be well-founded, the court shall make a decision on the introduction of the applicant into possession of the immovable property.  
The applicant may appeal the court's refusal to introduce into possession of the immovable property by way of appeal.  
(11.11.2021. law version, which comes into force 01.12.2021.)

Seventh section Enforcement of obligations through court proceedings

49.	chapter
Voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings

### 395. Article. Jurisdiction

An application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the location of the immovable property.

### 396. Article. Application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings

(1)	An application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings may be submitted by the owner or the pledgee who has the right to sell the pledge at a free price.  

(2)	The application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings shall be accompanied by the terms of sale and a printout from the relevant land register section indicating the valid entries and notes, but if the application has been submitted by the pledgee, also the pledge agreement, evidence of warning to the debtor, unless it follows from the law that such warning is not necessary. Confirmation of the issuance of the warning may also be an act drawn up by a sworn bailiff or his assistant regarding refusal to receive the warning.  

(3)	The terms of sale shall indicate:

1)	the composition of the immovable property to be sold;  

2)	encumbrances and mortgages on the immovable property;  

3)	the starting price of the auction;  

4)	the method and procedure for payment of the highest price bid;  

5)	rights in the immovable property that the owner retains;  

6)	other terms of sale that the seller considers necessary.  

(4)	If the immovable property to be sold is in the joint ownership of several persons, then, when determining the sale at auction through court proceedings upon the owner's application, the consent of all co-owners is required.  

(5)	If the same pledgee has first mortgages registered on immovable properties of the same debtor and they are functionally related to each other or have a common border, the applicant has the right to request the court to auction the immovable properties specified in the application as a whole.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 05.02.2009., Constitutional Court judgment of 24.11.2010., laws of 20.12.2010., 08.09.2011. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force 01.12.2021.)

### 397. Article. Judge's decision

(1)	The application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction shall be examined by a judge individually on the basis of the submitted application and the documents attached thereto within seven days from the date of submission of the application, without notifying the applicant and the debtor.  

(2)	The judge shall make a decision to allow the sale at auction, having ascertained that:

1)	the immovable property belongs to the applicant or the pledgee's debtor and the pledgee has the right to sell the immovable property at a free price;  

2)	there are no lawful obstacles to the sale of this immovable property with the terms specified in the application.  
(31.10.2002. law version, which comes into force 01.01.2003.)

### 398. Article. Auction procedure

The sale at auction shall be carried out by a bailiff in the manner established in this law for the enforcement of court judgments, observing the provisions of Articles 2075, 2083, 2084, 2087, 2089 and 2090 of the Civil Law and the following conditions:

1)	the immovable property shall be described and appraised only if requested by the person on whose application the sale is taking place;  

2)	the announcement shall indicate the terms of sale, as well as that the sale is voluntary;  

3)	the auction shall begin by reading out the terms of sale;  

4)	at the request of the applicant, the auction may be considered to have taken place even if only one buyer has appeared;  

5)	if, in accordance with the terms of sale, the acceptance of the highest price bid depends on the person on whose application the sale is taking place, and if he has not expressed his opinion within the time provided for in the terms of sale or determined by the court, it shall be considered that he has tacitly agreed to the highest price bid.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002., which comes into force 01.01.2003.)

### 399. Article. Documents to be issued to the buyer

(1)	After the buyer of the immovable property has fulfilled all the terms of sale, the district (city) court shall decide on the confirmation of the auction act (Articles 611 and 613) and the registration of the sold immovable property in the buyer's name. If insolvency proceedings have been declared for the owner of the immovable property, the district (city) court in whose jurisdiction the legal person's insolvency proceedings case is located shall decide on the confirmation of the auction act and the registration of the sold immovable property in the buyer's name.  

(2)	A copy of the court decision together with the auction terms and the auction act shall be issued to the buyer.  
(19.06.2003. law version with amendments made by the laws of 30.09.2010., 11.09.2014. and 25.10.2018., which comes into force 28.11.2018. The amendment in the first paragraph replacing the words "land register department of the district (city) court" with the words "district (city) court" comes into force 01.06.2019. See transitional provision point 151)

50.	chapter
Undisputed compulsory enforcement of obligations

### 400. pants. Obligations for which uncontested enforcement is permissible

(1)	Uncontested enforcement of obligations is permissible:

1)	under agreements for obligations secured by a public mortgage or commercial pledge;  

2)	under notarised and legally equivalent fixed-term agreements for payment of money or delivery of movable property;  

3)	under notarised or land register-recorded fixed-term property lease or rental agreements that provide for the lessee's or tenant's obligation to vacate the leased or rented property due to expiry of the term or non-payment of lease or rental payments, as well as the obligation to pay the lease or rental payment;  

4)	under protested bills of exchange that have not been issued in the form of a notarial deed.  

(11) The first paragraph of this section does not apply to notarial deeds drawn up in the procedure established in Section D1 of the Notaries Law.  

(2)	The obligations specified in the first paragraph of this section are not subject to uncontested enforcement if:

1)	such enforcement is directed against state or municipal property;  

2)	the obligation has been extinguished by limitation, the expiry of which is clearly evident from the deed itself.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 23.05.2013., 25.03.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enter into force on 07.07.2022.  
The new wording of paragraph 1, point 4 enters into force on 01.10.2022. See transitional provision 178)

### 401. pants

Persons who may submit an application for uncontested enforcement

An application for uncontested enforcement may be submitted by:

1)	a person in whose name the deed (agreement, bill of exchange) has been issued;  

2)	a person to whom the deed has been transferred by a separate land register deed or notarial deed;  

3)	the heir of the said persons, if his or her inheritance rights have been proven by a court judgment, certificate of inheritance or European Certificate of Succession regarding the entry into legal force of a will or confirmation of inheritance rights, or a court decision by which he or she has been placed in possession of the bequeathed property (Section 638 of the Civil Law), or a court decision or notarial confirmation by which it is recognised that he or she has accepted the inheritance (Section 697 of the Civil Law);  

4)	a guarantor who has paid in place of the debtor on the basis of a court judgment or in the procedure of enforcement, or whose payment has been confirmed by an inscription on the deed;  

5)	under immovable property lease or rental agreements — the acquirer of such property, if the acquirer's rights are certified by a land register deed or by the documents specified in point 3 of this section regarding the transfer of property by way of inheritance;  

6)	under protested bills of exchange — the holder of the bill in whose name the bill has been protested, as well as the guarantor, endorser (girant) and intermediary who have paid the bill and bring a recourse claim.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 23.05.2013. and 28.05.2015., which enter into force on 02.07.2015.  
The amendment to point 3 enters into force on 17.08.2015. See transitional provision 108)

### 402. pants. Persons against whom uncontested enforcement is permissible

Uncontested enforcement is permissible:

1)	against a person in whose name the deed has been issued (contracting party), but under a protested bill of exchange — against all persons liable for it;  

2)	against a guarantor if he or she has assumed the obligation as the debtor himself or herself (second paragraph of Section 1702 of the Civil Law);  

3)	against the heir of the person who assumed the obligations, if there is evidence of acceptance of the inheritance as specified in point 3 of Section 401 of this Law.

### 403. pants. Jurisdiction

(1)	Applications for uncontested enforcement in monetary payment obligations, movable property delivery obligations or obligations under agreements secured by a commercial pledge shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the place of residence or registered address.  

(2)	Applications for uncontested enforcement under immovable property mortgage deeds and under obligations to vacate or return leased or rented immovable property shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the location of the immovable property

. If the obligation is secured by several immovable properties and the applications fall within the jurisdiction of different district (city) courts, the application shall be examined by the district (city) court at the applicant's choice — according to the location of one immovable property.  

(3)	Applications for uncontested enforcement under a ship mortgage bond shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the place of registration of the mortgage.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011., 04.08.2011., 29.11.2012. and 25.10.2018., which enter into force on 28.11.2018. Amendments to the section enter into force on 01.06.2019. See transitional provision 151)

### 404. pants. Content of the application

(1)	The application shall indicate which obligation and under which deed the creditor requests to be subjected to uncontested enforcement.  

(11) The application shall include a confirmation that the court has been provided with truthful information about the facts and that the applicant or representative, if the application is submitted by a representative, has been informed that the Criminal Law provides for liability for submitting a false application.  

(2)	An application for uncontested enforcement for payment of money shall indicate the principal debt to be recovered, contractual penalties and interest — both agreed and statutory, but under a bill of exchange — also expenses related to the protest and statutory compensation, as well as the name of the credit institution and account number to which payment is to be made.  

(3)	The following shall be attached to the application:

1)	the deed to be executed in uncontested procedure;  

11)	under a protested paper form bill of exchange — the bill, its derivative and protest deed in paper form;  

12)	under a protested electronic bill of exchange — the electronic bill and electronic protest deed;  

2)	a document on payment of the state fee, except where the application has been submitted and payment made in the online system;  

3)	proof of issuance of a warning to the debtor (including to the owner of immovable property or the pledgor of a commercial pledge), unless it follows from the law that such a warning is not necessary. Confirmation of issuance of the warning may also be a deed drawn up by a sworn bailiff or his or her assistant regarding refusal to receive the warning.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011., 19.12.2013., 22.06.2017., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which
enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 405. pants. Judge's decision

(1)	An application for uncontested enforcement of obligations shall be decided by a judge sitting alone on the basis of the submitted application and attached documents within seven days from the date of submission of the application, without notifying the applicant and the debtor.  

(2)	The judge, having verified the validity of the submitted application and having found it to be satisfiable, shall adopt a decision determining which obligation and in what amount is to be executed in uncontested procedure. The decision shall be communicated to the applicant and the debtor.  

(21) If the decision establishes a person's obligation to vacate leased or rented property before the end of the term specified in the agreement, the judge shall in this paragraph set a two-month period for voluntary execution of the decision.  

(3)	The judge's decision enters into force immediately and has the force of an enforcement document. The decision is enforceable in accordance with the rules for execution of judgments. It shall be submitted for execution together with a copy of the deed subjected to uncontested enforcement.  

(4)	If the judge finds that the application is not justified or that the amount of the contractual penalty specified in the application is disproportionate to the principal debt, or that the enforceable deed contains unfair contract terms infringing consumer rights, he or she shall adopt a decision to reject it. The judge shall send the decision together with the submitted documents to the applicant.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 406. Section. Procedure for Contesting Undisputed Enforcement

(1) If the debtor considers that the creditor's claim is not substantiated on the merits, he or she may, within six months from the date of sending the decision, bring an action against the creditor to contest the claim. The action shall be brought in court in accordance with the general procedure for bringing an action established in this law.

(2) If the debtor considers that the creditor's claim is not substantiated on the merits, he or she may, within six months from the date on which the notarial writ of execution issued by a sworn notary has been sent to the debtor, bring an action against the creditor to contest the claim.

(3) When bringing an action, the debtor may request suspension of undisputed enforcement or execution of a notarial writ of execution issued by a sworn notary, but if the claimant has already received satisfaction in such manner — request security for the claim.

(31) When bringing an action against the creditor to contest a claim based on a court decision on undisputed enforcement of obligations, an insolvency administrator may request the court to apply an interim protective measure — deprivation of voting rights.

(4) When adopting a decision on the debtor's application for suspension of undisputed enforcement or execution of a notarial writ of execution, the court or judge shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the claim.

(41) When adopting a decision on the insolvency administrator's application for an interim protective measure — deprivation of voting rights, the court shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the claim. The court's decision is not subject to appeal.

(5) A decision on the debtor's application for suspension of undisputed enforcement or execution of a notarial writ of execution, by which the debtor's application has been satisfied, is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. Regarding a decision by which the application has been rejected, the debtor may submit an appeal.

(6) Upon a reasoned application by the creditor, the court which has suspended execution or in whose proceedings the case to be examined on the merits is pending may revoke the suspension of execution. A decision on revocation of suspension of execution is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. Regarding a decision by which the application has been rejected, the creditor may submit an appeal.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 23.05.2013., 30.10.2014., 12.02.2015. and 11.11.2021., which
enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 50.1
Enforcement of Obligations by Way of Warning

## (Chapter 31

Edition of law 10.2002, which enters into force 01.01.2003.)

Article 406.1 Obligations for which enforcement by warning procedure is permissible

(1) Enforcement of obligations by warning procedure is permissible for payment obligations that are substantiated by a document and for which the performance deadline has arrived, as well as for payment obligations for such remuneration as agreed in a contract for the supply of goods, purchase of goods or provision of services, if these obligations are substantiated by a document and no performance deadline has been set for them.

(2) Enforcement of obligations by warning procedure is not permissible:

1) for payments that are connected with unperformed counter-performance;

2) if the debtor's declared place of residence or place of residence is not known;

3) if the debtor's declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is not in the Republic of Latvia;

4) if the requested contractual penalty exceeds 10 percent of the principal debt amount;

5) if the requested interest exceeds the principal debt amount;

6) for payment obligations if the debt amount exceeds 15 000 euros;

7) for joint and several payment obligations.
(With amendments made by laws of 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012. and 19.12.2013., which
enter into force 04.01.2014.)

Article 406.2 Jurisdiction

(1) Enforcement of obligations by warning procedure is initiated upon the creditor's application.

(2) An application for enforcement of an obligation by warning procedure has jurisdiction in the district (city) court if the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none, — place of residence or legal address is in the Republic of Latvia.
(With amendments made by laws of 04.08.2011., 29.11.2012., 25.10.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 406.3 Submission of application

(1) The application shall be submitted using the online form available in the online system.

(2) The application shall indicate:

1) (deleted by law of 11.11.2021.);

2) the applicant's first name, surname, personal identity number, for a legal person — its name, registration number and indication that the applicant agrees to communicate with the court using the online system;

3) the debtor's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there is none, — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;

4) the applicant's representative's (if the application is submitted by a representative) first name, surname, personal identity number, for a legal person
— its name, registration number and indication that the applicant's representative agrees to communicate with the court using the online system;

5) the payment obligation in connection with which the application is submitted, indicating identifying information of the document substantiating the obligation and the performance deadline of the obligation, as well as the name of the credit institution and account number to which payment is to be made, if such exists;

6) the requested amount and its calculation, indicating the principal debt, contractual penalty, agreed or statutory interest and court costs;

7) the applicant's confirmation that the claim is not dependent on counter-performance or that counter-performance has been made, or that the payment obligation is not joint and several;

8) a request to the court to issue a warning to the debtor;

9) a request to decide on the enforcement of the payment obligation and recovery of court costs;

10) confirmation that truthful information about facts has been provided to the court and the applicant or representative, if the application is submitted by a representative, has been informed that the Criminal Law provides for liability for submitting a false application.

(21) In the application, the applicant may include an indication for the court to issue a warning to the debtor through a bailiff.

(3) Documents confirming payment of the state fee and costs associated with the issuance of court documents shall be attached to the application, except when payment has been made in the online system.

(4) Non-compliance of the application with the requirements of Articles 406.1, 406.2 and 406.3 of this law is an obstacle to the submission of the application. If non-compliance of the application with the requirements of Articles 406.1, 406.2 and 406.3 of this law has not been an obstacle to the submission of the application in the procedure specified in the first paragraph of this Article, the judge shall adopt a reasoned decision to refuse to accept the application and send it to the applicant. The decision to refuse to accept the application is not subject to appeal.

(5) The judge's refusal to accept the application is not an obstacle to the submission of the same application to the court when the deficiencies have been remedied, or to bringing an action in the procedure of action proceedings. In these cases, the paid state fee and costs associated with the issuance of the warning shall be credited if, after remedying the deficiencies, the same application is submitted to the court or an action is brought in the procedure of action proceedings.
(With amendments made by laws of 05.02.2009., 29.11.2012., 19.12.2013., 23.04.2015., 23.11.2016., 01.06.2017.,
01.03.2018., 11.11.2021., 09.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force 07.07.2022.)

Article 406.4 Ground for non-acceptance of application
(Deleted by law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 406.5 Content of warning

(1) The warning shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(2) The warning shall indicate:

1) the warning number and the name of the court issuing the warning;

2) the applicant, the payment obligation, identifying information of the documents substantiating the obligation, the performance deadline of the obligation, the requested amount and its calculation, the name of the credit institution and account number to which payment is to be made, if such exists;

3) the debtor;

4) that the court has not verified the validity of the claim;

5) a proposal to the debtor to pay the amount indicated in the application within 14 days from the date of issuance of the warning, notifying the court thereof, or to submit objections to the court;

6) that the obligation indicated in the warning will be submitted for enforcement if objections or evidence of payment are not submitted within the specified 14 days.

(3) The warning shall be certified with a qualified electronic seal within the meaning of Article 3(27) of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 July 2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC (hereinafter — Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council).
(With amendments made by laws of 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 406.6 Issuance of warning to debtor

(1) The warning and response form, which is drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers, shall be issued to the debtor against signature. The document with signature for receipt and notation of the date of issuance of the warning shall be submitted to the court.

(11) If the application contains an indication of issuance of the warning to the debtor through a bailiff, the warning and response form referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall be issued to the applicant for delivery to the debtor. In such case, confirmation of the issuance of the warning is the bailiff's or his assistant's act on delivery of the warning or act on refusal to receive the warning submitted to the court. The bailiff shall deliver the warning at the applicant's expense, and the costs associated with delivery are not recoverable from the debtor.

(2) In the event that issuance of the warning to the debtor is not possible, or in the case referred to in paragraph 1.1 of this Article — within one month from the day the warning was sent to the applicant for delivery to the debtor and the bailiff or his assistant does not submit to the court an act on delivery of the warning or an act on refusal to receive the warning,
— the judge shall adopt a decision to leave the application without consideration. The decision shall be communicated to the applicant in the online system.

(3) Leaving the application without consideration is not an obstacle to repeated submission of an application for enforcement of an obligation by warning procedure or to bringing an action in the procedure of action proceedings. In these cases, the paid state fee shall be credited.
(With amendments made by laws of 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 01.03.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 406.7 Debtor's response

(1) The debtor's response shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers. The debtor may provide a response using the online form available in the online system. In such case, the debtor has agreed to communicate with the court using the online system.

(2) Objections by the debtor against the validity of the payment obligation or payment of the debt submitted within the deadline are grounds for termination of proceedings for enforcement of the obligation by warning procedure.

(3) (Deleted by law of 11.11.2021.)

(4) (Deleted by law of 11.11.2021.)

(5) If the debtor acknowledges the application in part, the judge shall adopt a decision in the acknowledged part in accordance with the requirements of Article 406.9 of this law, but in the remaining part the proceedings shall be terminated.

(6) A debtor's response submitted after the specified deadline but before the adoption of a decision in the case shall be considered as submitted within the deadline.

(7) If the debtor's response does not contain confirmation that truthful information has been provided to the court and the debtor or representative, if the response is submitted by a representative, has been informed that the Criminal Law provides for liability for submitting a false response, the debtor's response shall be considered as not submitted and sent back to the submitter.
(With amendments made by laws of 19.06.2003., 05.02.2009., 23.04.2015. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 406.8 Termination of proceedings

(1) The judge shall adopt a decision on termination of proceedings for enforcement of an obligation by warning procedure. The decision on termination of proceedings is not subject to appeal.

(2) The decision and the debtor's response shall be communicated to the applicant.

(3) A decision on termination of proceedings for enforcement of an obligation by warning procedure due to the debtor's objections is not an obstacle to bringing an action in the procedure of action proceedings. In these cases, the paid state fee shall be credited.
(With amendments made by laws of 19.06.2003., 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 406.9 Judge's decision on enforcement of obligation

(1) If the debtor has not submitted objections within the deadline specified in the warning, the judge shall adopt a decision on enforcement of the payment obligation indicated in the application and recovery of court costs within seven days from the expiry date of the objection deadline. The decision shall be sent to the debtor within three days. The decision shall be communicated to the applicant.

(2) The judge's decision enters into force immediately, has the force of an enforcement document, and is enforceable in accordance with the rules for enforcement of court judgments.
(With amendments made by law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 406.10 Procedure for contesting enforcement of obligation

(1) If the debtor considers that the applicant's claim is not substantiated on the merits, he may bring an action against the creditor within three months from the date of sending the decision to contest the claim. The action shall be brought in court in the general procedure for bringing an action specified in this law.

(2) When bringing an action, the debtor may request suspension of enforcement of the obligation, but if the creditor has already received satisfaction in such procedure, request security for the action.

(3) When adopting a decision on the debtor's application for suspension of enforcement by warning procedure, the court or judge shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the action.

(4) A decision by which the application is granted is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. The debtor may file an appeal against a decision by which the application is rejected.

(5) Upon a reasoned application by the creditor, the court that suspended enforcement or in whose proceedings the case to be examined on the merits is located may revoke the suspension of enforcement. A decision to revoke the suspension of enforcement is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. The creditor may file an appeal against a decision by which the application is rejected.

(6) When bringing an action against the creditor to contest a claim substantiated by a court decision on enforcement of an obligation by warning procedure, the insolvency administrator may request the court to apply an interim protective measure — deprivation of voting rights.

(7) When adopting a decision on the insolvency administrator's application for an interim protective measure — deprivation of voting rights, the court shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the action. The court's decision is not subject to appeal.
(With amendments made by laws of 29.11.2012., 23.05.2013., 30.10.2014., 12.02.2015. and 11.11.2021., which
enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Filing an Appeal

### 413. pants. Right to File an Appeal or an Appeal Protest

(1)	Parties to a case may file an appeal, and a prosecutor may file an appeal protest, against a judgment (supplementary judgment) of a court of first instance in the procedure specified in this chapter, except for judgments for which the law does not provide for appeal by way of appeal. A representative shall file an appeal in accordance with the requirements of Section 86 of this Law.  

(2)	An appeal protest shall be filed and examined in the same procedure as an appeal, unless otherwise provided in this section.

### 414. pants. Procedure for Filing an Appeal

(1)	A judgment of a district (city) court that has not entered into legal force may be appealed by way of appeal to the respective regional court.  

(2)	(Deleted by the law of 30.10.2014.)

(3)	An appeal addressed to the appellate court shall be filed with the court that issued the judgment.  

(4)	If an appeal is filed directly with the appellate court within the time limit, the time limit shall not be considered missed.  
(With amendments made by the law of 30.10.2014., which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

### 415. pants. Time Limits for Filing an Appeal

(1)	An appeal against a judgment of a court of first instance may be filed within 20 days from the day of pronouncement of the judgment.  

(2)	If a judgment is prepared after a date set by the court (Section 199), the time limit for appealing the judgment shall be counted from the day of actual preparation of the judgment.  

(21)	(Deleted by the law of 22.05.2008.)

(22)	In the cases provided for in the first and second paragraphs of this Section, a party to whom the judgment has been sent in accordance with Section 56.2 of this Law may file an appeal within 20 days from the day of issuance of the judgment.  

(3)	An appeal filed after expiry of the time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the filer.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 01.11.2007., 22.05.2008., 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 14.12.2017. and
11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 416. pants. Content of an Appeal and Documents to be Attached Thereto

(1)	An appeal shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court to which the appeal is addressed;  

2)	the name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence of the filer of the appeal, or, if there is none, the place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the filer of the appeal consents to electronic communication with the court, the email address shall also be indicated and, if the person has registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included;  

21) the email address of the representative and, if the representative has registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included, if the appeal is filed by a representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia and the representative consents to electronic communication with the court. If the representative's address is outside Latvia, the email address shall additionally be indicated or notification of registration of participation in the online system shall be provided;  

3)	the judgment about which the appeal is filed and the court that issued the judgment;  

4)	to what extent the judgment is being appealed;  

5)	how the incorrectness of the judgment is manifested, with reasoning as to why the filer of the appeal considers that the facts in the case were incorrectly established or the evidence was incorrectly evaluated, an incorrect legal assessment of the circumstances of the case was given or a substantive legal norm was incorrectly applied, or a procedural legal norm was violated;  

6)	whether new evidence is being submitted, what evidence, about what circumstances and why this evidence was not submitted to the court of first instance;  

7)	the request of the filer of the appeal;  

8)	a list of documents attached to the appeal.  

(2)	An appeal shall be signed by the filer or his or her authorised representative. An appeal protest shall be signed by a prosecutorial official as provided by law.  

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 23.04.2015.)

(4)	An unsigned appeal shall be considered not filed and shall be sent back to the filer.  

(5)	A judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept an appeal if a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to appeal the court judgment is not attached thereto.  

(6)	In cases provided for by law, a translation certified in the prescribed manner shall be attached to the appeal and the documents attached thereto if the documents are intended for issuance to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this Law. A person who is exempt from payment of court costs shall not attach a translation.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 29.11.2012., 23.04.2015., 28.05.2015., 23.11.2016., 01.06.2017. and
11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 417. pants. Copies of an Appeal

(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 418. pants. Limits of an Appeal

(1)	An appeal may not change the subject matter or basis of a claim, or include new claims that were not raised in the court of first instance.  

(2)	The following shall not be considered new claims:

1)	clarification of claims;  

2)	correction of obvious errors in a claim;  

3)	addition of interest and increments to a claim;  

4)	a claim to compensate for the value of property in connection with alienation, loss or changes in the composition of the claimed property;  

5)	amendment of components of the total amount of a claim within the limits of that amount;  

6)	amendment of a claim requesting recognition of rights to a claim for restoration of violated rights due to circumstances that have changed during the course of the case;  

7)	increase in the amount of a claim in connection with market prices that have increased during the course of the case.

### 419. pants. Joining an Appeal

(1)	Co-participants and third parties participating in the proceedings on the side of the person who filed the appeal may join the filed appeal.  

(2)	Notice of joining an appeal shall be given in writing to the appellate court no later than 10 days before examination of the case in the appellate instance.  

(3)	An application to join an appeal shall not be subject to a state fee.

### 420. pants. Leaving an Appeal Without Progress

(1)	A judge of the court of first instance shall adopt a decision to leave an appeal without progress and shall set a time limit for the filer to remedy deficiencies if:

1)	an appeal has been filed that does not comply with the requirements of the first paragraph of Section 416 of this Law;  

2)	in cases provided for by law, a translation of the appeal and the documents attached thereto certified in the prescribed manner has not been attached;  

3)	an appeal has been filed for which a state fee has not been paid;  

4)	the power of attorney or other document attached to the appeal does not show authorisation for the representative to appeal the court judgment.  

(2)	If the deficiencies are remedied within the set time limit, the appeal shall be considered filed on the day it was first filed. Otherwise, the appeal shall be considered not filed and shall be returned to the filer.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 23.04.2015. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 421. pants. Appeal of a Judge's Decision

A separate appeal may be filed against a judge's decision to refuse to accept an appeal, except in the case referred to in the fifth paragraph of Section 416 of this Law.  
(With amendments made by the law of 23.04.2015., which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

### 422. Section. Actions of the first instance court after receiving an appeal

(1)	The judge of the first instance court, having ascertained that the appeal complies with the requirements of Section 416 of this Law, shall immediately notify the other participants in the case of this appeal and send them the appeal, indicating the time limit for submitting a written explanation. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the appeal may also be sent to the other participants in the case.

(2)	After the expiry of the time limit for submitting an appeal, the judge shall immediately send the case with the appeal and the documents attached to it to the appellate court.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which enter into force on 07.07.2022.)

### 423. Section. Written explanation of a participant in the case

(1)	A participant in the case may submit a written explanation regarding the submitted appeal to the appellate court within 30 days from the day when the appeal was sent to him or her, but in cases concerning children — within 15 days from the day when the appeal was sent to him or her.

(2)	The court shall send the explanation to the other participants in the case.

(3)	(Deleted by the Law of 22.05.2008.)

(4)	If the appeal has been sent to a participant in the case in accordance with Section 56.2 of this Law, the time limit for submitting a written explanation shall be counted from the day when the appeal was issued to the participant in the case.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 01.11.2007, 22.05.2008, 05.02.2009, 29.10.2015 and 11.11.2021, which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 424. Section. Counter-appeal

(1) After the appeal has been issued, a party is entitled to submit a counter-appeal. (2) The counter-appeal must comply with the requirements of Sections 413, 416 and 418 of this Law.
(3)	The counter-appeal shall be submitted to the appellate court within the time limit provided for in Section 423 of this Law.

(4)	After receiving the counter-appeal, the appellate court shall immediately send it to the other participants in the case.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 05.02.2009 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 53
Examination of a case in the appellate instance

### 425. Section. Initiation of appellate proceedings

(1)	Having ascertained that the procedure for submitting an appeal has been observed, the judge, after receiving an explanation or after the expiry of the time limit set for its submission, shall adopt a decision to initiate appellate proceedings and schedule the case for examination at a session of the appellate court.

(11)	In cases concerning the reinstatement of an employee at work and in cases concerning the recognition of an employer's notice as invalid, the date of the court session shall be set no later than within 15 days after receiving the explanation or the expiry of the time limit for its submission.

(12)	In cases concerning claims by administrators on behalf of insolvent debtors in the cases specified in Chapter XVII of the Insolvency Law and concerning the recovery of losses from members of management institutions of a legal person and participants (shareholders) of a capital company, based on their obligation to be liable for losses caused, as well as from personally liable members of a partnership, based on their obligation to be liable for the obligations of the partnership, the court session shall be set no later than within three months after receiving the explanation or the expiry of the time limit for its submission.

(2)	Having established that the appeal has been sent to the appellate court in violation of the procedure for submitting appeals established in this Law, the judge shall adopt one of the following decisions:

1)	to refuse to initiate appellate proceedings if the time limit set for submitting an appeal has been missed or if a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to appeal the court judgment has not been attached to the appeal; in this case, the appeal together with the case shall be sent to the first instance court, which shall return the appeal to the submitter;

2)	to send the case to the first instance court for the performance of actions established by law if, when submitting the appeal, the deficiencies specified in the first paragraph of Section 416 of this Law have been committed, the state fee has not been paid, or the power of attorney attached to the appeal or other document does not show the authority of the representative to appeal the court judgment.

(3)	If the circumstances specified in paragraph 1 of the second part of this Section are established at a session of the appellate court, the court shall adopt a decision to leave the appeal without examination.

(4)	Before the appellate court initiates the transfer for examination to another regional court of an appeal case under its examination in accordance with Section 32.1 of this Law, the court shall send information to the participants in the case about the court's proposal to transfer the case for examination to another court and about the obligation to notify the court within the specified time limit if the transfer of the case for examination to another court will create significant obstacles for any of the participants in the case to appear at the court session.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002, 07.04.2004, 01.11.2007, 22.05.2008, 30.09.2010, 21.01.2021 and
16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 426. Section. Limits of case examination in the appellate instance

(1)	The appellate court shall examine the case on the merits in connection with the appeal and counter-appeal to the extent requested in these appeals.

(2)	The appellate instance shall examine only those claims that have been examined in the first instance court. Amendment of the subject matter or basis of the claim is not permitted.

(3)	The appellate court shall examine the case on the merits without sending it for new examination to the first instance court, except in the cases specified in Section 427 of this Law.

### 427. Section

Cases when the judgment of the first instance court is to be set aside and the case sent for new examination to the first instance court

(1)	The appellate court, regardless of the grounds of the appeal, shall by decision set aside the judgment of the first instance court and send the case for new examination to the first instance court if the appellate court establishes that:

1)	the court examined the case in an unlawful composition;

2)	the court examined the case in violation of procedural law norms that establish the obligation to notify the participants in the case of the time and place of the court session;

3)	procedural law norms concerning the language of proceedings have been violated;

4)	the court judgment grants rights or imposes obligations on a person who has not been summoned to the case as a participant in the case;

5)	there is no court session protocol or court judgment in the case.

(2)	The appellate court, recognizing as justified an appeal against a court judgment in the part by which the proceedings in the case have been terminated or the claim has been left without examination, shall set aside the judgment of the first instance in this part and send the case for examination to the first instance court.
(With amendments made by the Law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 428. Section. Procedure for trial in the appellate court

(1)	Participants in the case shall be invited and other persons summoned to court in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 6 of this Law.

(2)	The session of the appellate court shall take place in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 21 of this Law, observing the specific features established in this chapter.

### 429. Section. Provision of explanations in the appellate court

(1)	At the session of the appellate court, explanations shall be provided first by the submitter of the appeal, but if both parties have submitted appeals — by the plaintiff.

(2)	If the prosecutor has submitted an appellate protest, he or she shall provide explanations before the explanations of the other participants in the case.

### 430. pants. Examination of Evidence in the Court of Appeal

(1)	The court of appeal itself decides which evidence to examine in the court session.  

(2)	In examining and evaluating evidence, the court of appeal observes the provisions of the third part of this law.  

(3)	Facts established in the court of first instance need not be examined in the court of appeal if they have not been contested in the appeal.  

(4)	If in the court of appeal a party to the case submits or requests examination of evidence which it was possible for them to present in the examination of the case in the court of first instance, and if the court of appeal does not establish justifiable reasons why the evidence was not submitted in the court of first instance, the court of appeal shall not accept the evidence.  
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 431. pants. Termination of Appellate Proceedings

(1)	The submitter of the appeal (counter-appeal) is entitled to withdraw it until the examination of the case on the merits has been completed.  

(2)	If the appeal is withdrawn, the court of appeal shall adopt a decision on termination of the appellate proceedings, except in cases where other parties to the case have submitted appeals (counter-appeals) or where an appeal protest has been submitted.  

(3)	If the submitter of the appeal fails to appear at the court session twice without justifiable reason and has not requested that the case be examined in their absence, the court may terminate the appellate proceedings.  

(4)	If the appellate proceedings are terminated, the state fee shall not be refunded.  

54.	nodaļa
Judgment or Decision of the Court of Appeal

### 432. pants. Judgment of the Court of Appeal

(1)	The decision of the court of appeal by which the case is adjudicated on the merits shall be made by the court in the form of a judgment.  

(2)	The court of appeal shall make the judgment in the procedure established in Articles 189—198 of this law, unless otherwise provided in this Article.  

(3)	In the introductory part of the judgment, in addition to the circumstances mentioned in the third part of Article 193 of this law, the court shall indicate the submitter of the appeal and the court judgment about which the complaint has been submitted.  

(4)	In the descriptive part of the judgment, the court shall include a brief exposition of the reasoning and operative part of the judgment of the court of first instance, as well as a brief content of the appeal (counter-appeal) and objections.  

(5)	In the reasoning part of the judgment, the circumstances mentioned in the fifth part of Article 193 of this law shall be indicated, as well as the attitude towards the judgment of the court of first instance shall be reasoned. If the court, in examining the case, recognises that the reasoning contained in the judgment of the lower instance court is correct and fully sufficient, it may indicate in the reasoning part of the judgment that it joins the argumentation of the judgment of the lower instance court. In such a case, the considerations provided in the fifth part of Article 193 of this law need not be indicated in the reasoning part of the judgment.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011., 28.05.2015. and 09.06.2016., which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

### 433. pants. Pronouncement of the Judgment of the Court of Appeal

(1)	The court of appeal shall pronounce the judgment in the procedure established in Article 199 of this law.  

(2)	The judgment shall be sent to the parties to the case in the cases and procedure provided for in Article 208 of this law.  
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 434. pants. Entry into Legal Force of the Judgment of the Court of Appeal

(1)	The judgment of the court of appeal shall enter into legal force when the time limit for appealing it in cassation has expired and a cassation appeal has not been submitted.  

(2)	If a cassation appeal has been submitted, the judgment of the court of appeal shall enter into legal force simultaneously with:

1)	the decision of the procedural session of the Supreme Court, if initiation of cassation proceedings has been refused (third part of Article 464 and Article 464.1);  

2)	the judgment of the court of cassation, if the judgment of the court of appeal has not been set aside or the judgment or part thereof has been set aside and the application has been left without examination or the proceedings have been terminated (Article 474).  

(3)	The provisions of the second, third, fourth and fifth parts of Article 203 of this law shall apply to the legal force of the judgment of the court of appeal.  

(31)	If in relation to any party to the case the time limit for submitting a cassation appeal about the judgment of the court of appeal is determined in accordance with Part 2.2 of Article 454 of this law, the judgment of the court of appeal shall enter into legal force after the time limit for appealing it has elapsed, counting the time limit from the later date of issuance of the judgment, if a cassation appeal has not been submitted.  

(32)	If in the cases mentioned in Part 3.1 of this Article the relevant confirmation of issuance of the judgment has not been received (Article 56.2), the judgment shall enter into legal force six months after its pronouncement.  

(4)	The judgment of the court of appeal shall be executed in accordance with Articles 204, 204.1 of this law and the provisions of the first part of Article 205. Immediate execution of the judgment in the case provided for in Point 7 of the first part of Article 205 of this law shall be permissible only by requiring from the claimant adequate security in the event that the court of cassation adopts the judgment mentioned in Points 2, 3 or 4 of Article 474 of this law.  
(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008. with amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 30.10.2014., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 435. pants

Correction of Clerical and Mathematical Calculation Errors in the Judgment of the Court of Appeal

(1)	The court of appeal on its own initiative or upon application of a party to the case is entitled to correct clerical or mathematical calculation errors in the judgment.  

(2)	The question of correcting errors shall be decided in written proceedings, having previously notified the parties to the case thereof. If the application has been submitted by a party to the case, simultaneously with sending the notification to the parties to the case, the court shall send them the application for correction of clerical or mathematical calculation errors in the judgment.  

(3)	A party to the case may submit an ancillary complaint about the court's decision to make a correction of an error in the judgment.  
(With amendments made by the law of 08.09.2011., which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

### 436. pants. Supplementary Judgment of the Court of Appeal

(1)	The court of appeal may on its own initiative or upon application of a party to the case make a supplementary judgment if:

1)	a judgment has not been made regarding any of the claims that has been the subject of examination by the court of appeal;  

2)	the court has not determined the amount of the sum awarded, the property to be transferred, or the action to be performed;  

3)	the judgment has not decided on reimbursement of litigation costs.  

(2)	Initiation of making a supplementary judgment may be requested within the time limit for appealing the judgment established by law.
