(3)	The court shall make the supplementary judgment after examination of the question in a court session, having previously notified the parties to the case thereof. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to making the supplementary judgment or rejecting the application.  

(4)	(Deleted by the law of 05.02.2009.)

(5)	An ancillary complaint may be submitted about the court's decision to refuse to make a supplementary judgment.  
(With amendments made by the law of 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

### 437. pants. Clarification of the Judgment of the Court of Appeal

(1)	The court of appeal may upon application of a party to the case clarify the judgment by its decision, without changing its content.  

(2)	Clarification of the judgment shall be permissible if it has not yet been executed and the time limit for compulsory execution of the judgment has not elapsed.  

(3)	The question of clarification of the judgment shall be examined in written proceedings, having previously notified the parties to the case thereof. Simultaneously with the notification, the court shall send to the parties to the case the application for clarification of the judgment.  

(4)	An ancillary complaint may be submitted about the court's decision on the question of clarification of the judgment.  
(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 438. pants

Postponement, division into instalments, modification of the manner and procedure of execution of the judgment of the court of appeal

(1)	The court of appeal is entitled, upon application by a participant in the case, taking into account the financial situation of the parties or other important circumstances, to postpone the execution of the judgment or divide it into instalments, as well as to modify the manner and procedure of its execution. A decision on postponement of execution of the judgment, division into instalments or modification of the manner and procedure of execution shall be executed immediately.

(2)	The application shall be examined in written proceedings, after prior notification thereof to the participants in the case. Simultaneously with the notification, the court, setting a time limit for submission of explanations, shall send to the participants in the case the application for postponement of execution of the judgment, division into instalments, modification of the manner or procedure of its execution.

(3)	An ancillary complaint may be submitted against a court decision to postpone execution of the judgment or divide it into instalments, as well as to modify the manner and procedure of its execution. Submission of an ancillary complaint shall not suspend execution of the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 29.10.2015, which enter into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 439. pants

Action of the court of appeal if the judgment is not appealed in cassation proceedings

After expiry of the time limit provided for submission of a cassation complaint, if a cassation complaint has not been submitted, the court of appeal shall send the case to the court of first instance.

439.1 pants. Action of the court of appeal after performance of actions by the court of cassation

After the court of appeal, following performance of the actions by the court of cassation specified in Section 477.1 of this Law, has received the case, it shall issue a writ of execution. After issuing the writ of execution, the court of appeal shall send the case to the court of first instance.
(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008, which enters into force on 25.06.2008. See transitional provisions.)

### 440.pants

Suspension of proceedings, leaving a claim without examination, termination of proceedings in the court of appeal

The court of appeal shall suspend proceedings, leave a claim without examination or terminate proceedings in the cases and procedure specified in Chapters 24, 25 or 26 of this Law.

54.1	nodaļa
Specific features of examination of certain categories of cases in the court of appeal

## (Chapter 20

03.2014. law version; chapter title in 12.02.2015. law version, which enters into force
01.03.2015.)

440.1 Article. Procedure for examination of cases in the appellate instance

Appeals in simplified procedure cases and in cases concerning rights, disputes about which were examined by the Industrial Property Appeals Board, concerning judgments by which an application for legal protection proceedings has been satisfied or rejected, an application for insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person has been rejected, in cases concerning disputes about rights in insolvency proceedings cases, in cases of cancellation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations, are examined in the appellate instance in the procedure specified in Chapters 52, 53 and 54 of this law, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.
(15.06.2021. law version with amendments made by 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

440.2 Article. Right to submit an appeal or appeal protest

The judgments referred to in Article 440.1 of this law may be appealed in the appellate procedure if:

1) the court of first instance has incorrectly applied or interpreted a substantive law norm and this has led to incorrect adjudication of the case;

2) the court of first instance has violated a procedural law norm and this has led to incorrect adjudication of the case;

3) the court of first instance has incorrectly established facts or incorrectly evaluated evidence or provided an incorrect legal assessment of the circumstances of the case and this has led to incorrect adjudication of the case.
(With amendments made by 12.02.2015. law, which enters into force 01.03.2015.)

440.3 Article. Time limit for submitting an appeal

If the judgment was made in written proceedings, in addition to that specified in Article 415 of this law, the appeal time limit is counted from the day of preparation of the judgment.
(With amendments made by 12.02.2015. and 11.11.2021. law, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

440.4 Article. Content of the appeal

In the appeal regarding the incorrectness of the judgment, in addition to that specified in Article 416 of this law, the following shall be indicated:

1) which substantive law norm the court of first instance has incorrectly applied or interpreted, which procedural law norm has been violated and how this has affected the adjudication of the case;

2) which facts the court of first instance has incorrectly established, which evidence has been incorrectly evaluated, how the incorrectness of the legal assessment of the circumstances of the case is manifested and how this has affected the adjudication of the case.

440.5 Article. Leaving the appeal without movement

(1) The judge of the court of first instance adopts a decision on leaving the appeal without movement and sets a time limit for the submitter to remedy deficiencies if:

1) an appeal has been submitted that does not comply with the requirements of the first part of Article 416 and Article 440.4 of this law;

2) in cases provided for by law, a translation of the appeal and the documents attached to it, certified in the prescribed manner, has not been attached.

(2) If the deficiencies are remedied within the set time limit, the appeal shall be considered submitted on the day it was submitted for the first time. Otherwise, the complaint shall be considered not submitted and returned to the submitter.
(With amendments made by 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022. law, which enters into force 07.07.2022.)

440.6 Article. Non-acceptance of the appeal

(1) An appeal that is not signed or that has been submitted by a person who is not authorized to appeal the court judgment, or for which the state fee has not been paid, shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter.

(2) A decision on refusal to accept an appeal is not subject to appeal.

440.7 Article. Actions of the court of first instance after receiving the appeal

(1) The judge of the court of first instance, having verified that the appeal complies with the requirements of Articles 416, 440.2 and 440.4 of this law, immediately notifies the other participants in the case of this complaint and sends them the complaint. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the complaint may also be sent to the other participants in the case.

(2) The judge of the court of first instance, when sending the appeal and the documents attached to it to the other participants in the case, informs them that written explanations shall be submitted after the appellate instance has sent the participants in the case a notification of the initiation of appellate proceedings.

(3) After the expiry of the time limit for submitting the appeal, the judge of the court of first instance immediately sends the case with the appeal and the documents attached to it to the court of the appellate instance.
(With amendments made by 12.02.2015., 19.10.2017., 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022. law, which enters into force 07.07.2022.)

440.8 Article. Initiation of appellate proceedings in the court of the appellate instance

(1) Having verified that the procedure for submitting the appeal has been observed, the judge or, in the case specified in the fifth part of this article, three judges collegially within 30 days after receiving the appeal shall decide on the initiation of appellate proceedings.

(2) Having established that the appeal was sent to the court of the appellate instance in violation of the procedure for submitting appeals specified in this law, the judge shall adopt one of the following decisions:

1) a decision on refusal to initiate appellate proceedings if the time limit set for submitting the appeal has been missed, the appeal has been submitted by a person who is not authorized to appeal the court judgment, or if the state fee has not been paid;

2) a decision on sending the case to the court of first instance for performance of actions specified by law if, when submitting the appeal, the deficiencies specified in the first part of Article 416 or Article 440.4 of this law have been committed.

(3) In the case specified in point 1 of the second part of this article, the complaint together with the case shall be sent to the court of first instance, which shall return the complaint to the submitter.

(4) If at least one of the grounds for initiating appellate proceedings referred to in Article 440.2 of this law exists, the judge shall adopt a decision on initiating appellate proceedings and immediately notify the participants in the case thereof, indicating the time limit for submitting written explanations.

(5) If the judge to whom the appeal has been assigned for decision considers that the initiation of appellate proceedings should be refused, the question of initiating appellate proceedings shall be decided by three judges collegially.

(6) If at least one of the three judges considers that at least one of the grounds for initiating appellate proceedings referred to in Article 440.2 of this law exists, the judges shall adopt a decision on initiating appellate proceedings and immediately notify the participants in the case thereof.

(7) If the judges unanimously recognize that none of the grounds for initiating appellate proceedings referred to in Article 440.2 of this law exists, they shall adopt a decision on refusal to initiate appellate proceedings and immediately notify the participants in the case thereof.

(8) The decision referred to in the seventh part of this article shall be prepared in the form of a resolution and is not subject to appeal.

(9) The decision on refusal to initiate appellate proceedings together with the submitted appeal shall be returned to the submitter of the appeal.

440.9 Article. Written explanation of a participant in the case

A participant in the case may submit a written explanation regarding the submitted appeal to the court of the appellate instance within 20 days from the day the appellate instance sent the participants in the case a notification of the initiation of appellate proceedings.
(11.11.2021. law version, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

440.10 Article. Counter-appeal

(1) After a notification of the initiation of appellate proceedings has been sent, a party is entitled to submit a counter-appeal within 20 days.

(2) The counter-appeal must comply with the requirements of Articles 250.27, 416., 418. and 440.4 of this law.

(3) After receiving the counter-appeal, the court of the appellate instance immediately sends it to the other participants in the case.
(With amendments made by 11.11.2021. law, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

440.11 Article. Examination of cases in written proceedings, preparation of judgment and sending of copy

(1) The cases referred to in this chapter shall be examined by the court in written proceedings, timely notifying the parties of the date when the judgment will be available in the online system, informing them of the composition of the court that will examine the case, and explaining the right to file a challenge against the judge. This date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of preparation of the judgment. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach to the online system on the date of preparation of the judgment, the judgment on the same date is available at the court office. The date when the judgment is available at the court office shall be considered the date of preparation of the judgment in such a case.

(11) Examination of cases concerning disputes about rights in insolvency proceedings cases in written proceedings shall be commenced no later than within 30 days after receiving the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission.

(12) When examining an appeal regarding a court judgment by which an application for legal protection proceedings has been satisfied, if the appeal is based on non-compliance of the plan of legal protection proceedings measures with point 15 of the fourth part of Article 40 of the Insolvency Law or point 2 of part 3.1 of Article 42, the court shall set a time limit for the appointed supervisory person or the last appointed supervisory person within which an assessment of the debtor's economic activity shall be submitted.

(2) At the written request of a party, the judgment shall be immediately sent to the party.

(3) If the court considers it necessary, the case may be tried in a court session. In cases concerning disputes about rights in insolvency proceedings cases, the court shall set the date of the court session no later than within 30 days after receiving the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission.
(With amendments made by 12.02.2015., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179. point)

440.12 Article. Entry into legal force of the judgment of the court of the appellate instance

The judgment of the court of the appellate instance is not subject to appeal in the cassation instance and enters into force on the day of its pronouncement or, if the case was examined in written proceedings, on the day of its preparation.

Ninth part
Appeal of decisions of the court of first instance and the court of the appellate instance

55. chapter
Submission and examination of collateral complaints

### 441.pants

Grounds for appealing or protesting decisions of first instance courts and appellate instance courts

(1)	Decisions of first instance courts and appellate instance courts may be appealed separately from the court judgment by parties to the case by submitting an interlocutory appeal, as well as by a prosecutor by submitting an interlocutory protest:

1)	in cases provided for in this law;  

2)	if the court decision impedes the progress of the case.  

(2)	Interlocutory appeals shall not be submitted regarding other decisions of first instance courts and appellate instance courts, but objections to these decisions may be expressed in an appeal or cassation complaint.  

(3)	An interlocutory protest shall be submitted and examined in the same procedure as an interlocutory appeal.

### 442. pants. Time limit for submitting an interlocutory appeal

(1)	An interlocutory appeal may be submitted within 10 days from the day of pronouncement of the decision, unless otherwise provided for in this law. The time limit by which an interlocutory appeal must be submitted regarding a decision adopted in written proceedings or regarding procedural actions outside a court session shall be calculated from the day the decision was issued.  

(11) A party to the case to whom the court decision has been sent in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law may submit an interlocutory appeal within 15 days from the day of issuance of the decision.  

(2)	An interlocutory appeal submitted after the expiry of the said time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter with a refund of the security deposit.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021.  
which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 443.pants. Procedure for submitting an interlocutory appeal

(1)	An interlocutory appeal shall be submitted to the court that adopted this decision and shall be addressed:

1)	regarding a decision of a first instance court — to the respective appellate instance court;  

2)	regarding a decision of an appellate instance court — to the cassation instance court;  

3)	(deleted by the law of 30.10.2014.).  

(2)	(Deleted by the law of 05.02.2009.)
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 30.10.2014. and 25.10.2018., which enter into force on 28.11.2018. The amendment regarding the deletion of the words "and the judge of the land registry department of the district (city) court" in paragraph 1, point 1 enters into force on 01.06.2019. See transitional provision point 151)

443.1 pants. Content of an interlocutory appeal and documents to be attached to it

(1)	An interlocutory appeal shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court to which the appeal is addressed;  

2)	the name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence of the submitter of the appeal, but if there is none — place of residence, for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the submitter of the appeal agrees to electronic communication with the court, the email address shall also be indicated and, if the submitter of the appeal has registered in the online system for communication with the court, an indication of registration shall also be included;  

3)	if the appeal is submitted by a representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia and he or she agrees to electronic communication with the court — the representative's email address and, if he or she has registered in the online system for communication with the court, an indication of registration shall also be included. If the representative's address is outside Latvia, an email address shall additionally be indicated or notification of registration of his or her participation in the online system shall be provided;  

4)	the decision regarding which the appeal is submitted and the court that adopted this decision;  

5)	how the incorrectness of the decision manifests itself and the justification thereof;  

6)	evidence confirming the objections of the submitter of the appeal;  

7)	the request of the submitter of the appeal and the extent to which the decision is being appealed;  

8)	a list of documents attached to the appeal.  

(2)	In cases provided for by law, certified translations of documents shall be attached to the interlocutory appeal and the documents attached to it in the prescribed manner if the documents are intended for issuance to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law. A translation need not be attached by a person who is exempt from payment of court costs.  
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 444.pants. Copies of an interlocutory appeal

(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

444.1 pants. Security deposit for an interlocutory appeal

(1)	When submitting an interlocutory appeal, a security deposit shall be paid in the amount specified in Section 43.1, paragraph one, point 1 of this law.  

(2)	If the court revokes or amends the appealed court decision in full or in any part thereof, the security deposit shall be refunded. If the interlocutory appeal is rejected or it has been submitted regarding a decision that is not appealable, the security deposit shall not be refunded, except in cases where the appealed decision erroneously indicates that it is appealable.  

(21) If the interlocutory appeal is withdrawn, the security deposit shall not be refunded.  

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 25.03.2021.)
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018., 01.10.2020. and 25.03.2021., which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 445.pants. Grounds for non-acceptance of an interlocutory appeal and leaving it without progress

(1)	An unsigned interlocutory appeal shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter with a refund of the security deposit.  

(2)	A judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept an interlocutory appeal if the security deposit has not been paid in the manner and amount prescribed by law or if a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to appeal the court decision has not been attached to the interlocutory appeal.  

(3)	A judge's decision to refuse to accept an interlocutory appeal is not appealable. In the cases referred to in paragraph two of this Section, the paid security deposit shall be refunded.  

(4)	If an interlocutory appeal has been submitted that does not comply with the requirements of Section 443.1 of this law, or in cases provided for by law a certified translation of the interlocutory appeal and the documents attached to it has not been attached in the prescribed manner, or the authority of the representative to appeal the court decision does not follow from the power of attorney or other document attached to the interlocutory appeal, the judge shall adopt a decision to leave the interlocutory appeal without progress and shall set a time limit for remedying the deficiencies.  

(5)	If the submitter remedies the deficiencies indicated in the decision to leave the interlocutory appeal without progress within the set time limit, the interlocutory appeal shall be considered as submitted on the day it was first submitted to the court. Otherwise, the interlocutory appeal shall be considered as not submitted and shall be returned to the submitter without refunding the security deposit.  
(In the wording of the law of 23.04.2015. with amendments made by the laws of 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 446.pants. Actions of the court upon receipt of an interlocutory appeal

(1)	Upon receipt of an interlocutory appeal, the judge shall immediately send the appeal to the parties to the case. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the interlocutory appeal may also be sent to the parties to the case.  

(2)	Upon expiry of the appeal time limit, the judge shall immediately send the case with the interlocutory appeal to the court instance to which the appeal is addressed.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enter into force on 07.07.2022.)

### 447th Section. Procedure for Examining Interlocutory Appeals

(1)	An interlocutory appeal shall be examined in written proceedings. The court shall notify the parties of the date of examination of the interlocutory appeal. The decision shall be sent to the parties within three days from the date of examination of the interlocutory appeal.

(2)	If an interlocutory appeal is examined at a court session, then its examination shall take place in the procedure established in this law for the examination of cases in the court of appeal.

(3)	An interlocutory appeal regarding the decisions of a judge referred to in Sections 640 and 651.5 of this law shall be examined at a court session.

(4)	In cases concerning disputes over rights in insolvency proceedings (Sub-chapter 30.7), the court shall examine an interlocutory appeal within 15 days from the date of receipt of the appeal.
(In the wording of the law of 04.08.2011 with amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 23.04.2015., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

447th Section 1. Decision Adopted Regarding an Interlocutory Appeal

(1)	In a decision regarding an interlocutory appeal, in addition to what is referred to in Section 230 of this law, the court shall indicate the submitter of the interlocutory appeal, include a statement of the interlocutory appeal and the appealed decision, and also provide reasons for its position regarding the appealed decision.

(2)	If the court, when examining an interlocutory appeal, finds that the reasons contained in the appealed decision are correct and sufficient, it may indicate in the decision that it agrees with the reasons of the appealed decision. In such a case, the reasoning part specified in Section 230 of this law may not be included.
(In the wording of the law of 04.08.2011 with amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015., which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 448. Section. Competence of the Regional Court and the Supreme Court

(1)	The regional court and the Supreme Court, when examining an interlocutory appeal, shall have the right to:

1)	leave the decision unchanged and reject the appeal;

2)	annul the decision in whole or in part and refer the matter for new examination to the court that adopted the decision;

3)	annul the decision in whole or in part and decide the matter on the merits by its own decision;

4)	amend the decision.

(2)	The regional court, when examining an interlocutory appeal regarding a decision by which an application for resumption of proceedings and re-examination of a case in which a default judgment has been made has been rejected, shall have the right to:

1)	leave the decision unchanged and reject the appeal;

2)	annul the decision, resume proceedings and send the case for re-examination to the court of first instance.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 30.10.2014., which comes into force on 01.01.2015.)

### 449. Section. Legal Force of a Decision Adopted Regarding an Interlocutory Appeal

(1)	A decision adopted regarding an interlocutory appeal shall not be subject to appeal and shall enter into legal force at the moment of its adoption, except in the cases provided for in this section and Section 641 of this law.

(2)	A decision of the regional court regarding an interlocutory appeal, except in cases concerning disputes over rights in insolvency proceedings (Sub-chapter 30.7), may be appealed to the Supreme Court within 10 days from the date of issuance of the decision, if by this decision:

1)	an interlocutory appeal regarding a decision to refuse to accept a claim based on Section 132, paragraph one, points 1 and 2 of this law has been rejected;

2)	an interlocutory appeal regarding termination of proceedings based on Section 223, points 1 and 2 of this law has been rejected;

3)	when deciding the matter on the merits in accordance with Section 448, point 3 of this law, a decision has been adopted to refuse to accept a claim based on Section 132, paragraph one, points 1 and 2 of this law, or a decision to terminate proceedings based on Section 223, points 1 and 2 of this law.

(3)	A decision of the regional court regarding an interlocutory appeal concerning a decision of a district (city) court in land register cases, except for a decision regarding an interlocutory appeal concerning an application for registration of immovable property in the name of the acquirer, may be appealed to the Supreme Court, observing the time limits specified in Section 442 of this law.

(31) The time limits referred to in paragraphs two and three of this section with respect to a party to whom the decision has been sent in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law shall be calculated from the date of issuance of the decision.

(4)	When appealing to the Supreme Court the decisions provided for in paragraphs two and three of this section, as well as in paragraph one of Section 641 of this law, security money shall be paid in the amount specified in Section 43.1, paragraph one, point 1 of this law. The procedure for refunding security money shall be determined in accordance with the requirements of Section 43.2 of this law and this chapter.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 07.04.2004., the judgment of the Constitutional Court of 14.03.2006., the laws of 25.05.2006., 05.02.2009., 12.09.2013., 30.10.2014., 29.10.2015., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018., 25.10.2018., 25.03.2021.
and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

Part Ten Cassation Proceedings

56th Chapter
Submission of a Cassation Appeal

### 450. Section. Right to Submit a Cassation Appeal or Cassation Protest

(1)	Parties may appeal in cassation a judgment of a court of first instance made by applying the provisions of Sub-chapter 30.4 of this law and a judgment (supplementary judgment) of a court of appeal, and a prosecutor may submit a cassation protest.

(2)	A cassation protest shall be submitted and examined in the same procedure as a cassation appeal, unless otherwise provided in this part.

(3)	A judgment of a court of first instance made by applying the provisions of Sub-chapter 30.4 of this law and a judgment of a court of appeal may be appealed in cassation if the court has incorrectly applied a substantive law norm, violated a procedural law norm, or exceeded the limits of its competence when examining the case.
(With amendments made by the laws of 22.05.2008., 08.09.2011., 18.04.2013., 20.03.2014. and 09.06.2016., which
comes into force on 13.07.2016.)

### 451. Section. Incorrect Application of Substantive Law Norms

(1)	The court has applied a substantive law norm incorrectly if it has been incorrectly applied to the circumstances established by the court or if the substantive law norm has been incorrectly interpreted.

(2)	Incorrect application of a substantive law norm may be grounds for appealing a judgment in cassation if it has led or could have led to incorrect adjudication of the case.
(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008 with amendments made by the law of 09.06.2016., which comes into force on 13.07.2016.)

### 452. Section. Violation of Procedural Law Norms

(1)	The court has committed a violation of a procedural law norm if during the proceedings it has not ensured a procedural procedure in accordance with the law or observance of the procedural rights of persons, by not applying or incorrectly interpreting the relevant law norm.

(2)	A violation of a procedural law norm may be grounds for appealing a judgment in cassation if it has led or could have led to incorrect adjudication of the case.

(3)	A violation of a procedural law norm that could have led to incorrect adjudication of the case shall in any case be considered to be that:

1)	the court has examined the case in an unlawful composition;

2)	the court has examined the case in violation of the procedural law norms that establish the obligation to notify the participants in the proceedings of the time and place of the court session;

3)	procedural law norms regarding the language of proceedings have been violated;

4)	the court judgment grants rights or imposes obligations on a person who has not been summoned to the case as a participant in the proceedings;

5)	there is no court session protocol or court judgment in the case.
(With amendments made by the laws of 22.05.2008., 09.06.2016., 14.12.2017. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 453. Section. Content of cassation appeal and documents to be attached thereto

(1)	The cassation appeal shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court to which the appeal is addressed (Civil Cases Department of the Supreme Court);  

2)	the name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence of the appellant, but if there is none — place of residence, for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the appellant agrees to electronic communication with the court, the e-mail address shall also be indicated and, if the person has registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included;  

21) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

3)	the judgment about which the appeal is submitted and the court that issued the judgment;  

4)	to what extent the judgment is being appealed;  

5)	which substantive law provision the court applied incorrectly, which procedural law provision was violated and how it affected the adjudication of the case or how the violation of the limits of the court's competence was manifested;  

6)	(deleted by the law of 09.06.2016.);  

7)	the request made to the Supreme Court.  

(11) If the appellant of the cassation appeal considers that the examination of the cassation appeal in cassation proceedings is of essential importance in ensuring uniform court practice or in the further development of law, he or she shall indicate this with reasoning in the cassation appeal.  

(2)	The cassation appeal shall be signed by the appellant — natural person, the official indicated in the fourth part of Section 82.1 of this law, an advocate or — in accordance with the fifth part of Section 82.1 of this law — a professional patent attorney. If the cassation appeal is signed by a professional patent attorney or an official of a legal person, a document certifying the person's right to represent the appellant shall be attached to the appeal. If the cassation appeal is signed by an advocate, a power of attorney and a warrant shall be attached to the appeal. The cassation protest shall be signed by an official of the prosecutor's office as provided by law.  

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 23.04.2015.)

(4)	A document certifying the payment of the security deposit shall be attached to the cassation appeal, except in cases where the cassation appeal has been submitted and payment has been made in the online system.  

(41) In cases provided for by law, a translation certified in the prescribed manner shall be attached to the cassation appeal if the document is intended for issuance to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law. A person who is exempt from payment of court costs shall not attach a translation.  

(5)	An unsigned cassation appeal shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the appellant, refunding the security deposit.  

(6)	A judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept a cassation appeal if:

1)	the security deposit has not been paid in the manner and amount prescribed by law;  

2)	a document certifying the right of the person referred to in the second part of this Section to appeal the court judgment in cassation proceedings has not been attached to the cassation appeal or has not been submitted in the case.  

(7)	In the case referred to in point 2 of the sixth part of this Section, the security deposit shall be refunded.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., the Constitutional Court judgment of 27.06.2003., 12.02.2004., 22.05.2008., 29.11.2012., 30.10.2014., 23.04.2015., 09.06.2016., 23.11.2016. and 11.11.2021., which enters into
force on 01.12.2021.)

### 454. Section. Time limit for submitting a cassation appeal

(1)	A cassation appeal may be submitted within 30 days from the day of pronouncement of the judgment.  

(2)	If the judgment is prepared after the date set by the court (Section 199), the time limit for appealing the judgment shall be counted from the day of actual preparation of the judgment. If the judgment is issued in written proceedings, the time limit for appeal shall be counted from the day of preparation of the judgment.  

(21) A party to whom the judgment has been sent in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law may submit a cassation appeal within 30 days from the day of issuance of the judgment.  

(3)	An appeal submitted after the expiry of this time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the appellant, refunding the security deposit.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 22.05.2008., 05.02.2009., 29.10.2015., 14.12.2017. and 11.11.2021.  
which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 455. Section. Appeal of a judge's decision

An ancillary appeal may be submitted against a judge's decision to refuse to accept a cassation appeal, except in the cases referred to in the sixth part of Section 453 of this law.  
(With amendments made by the law of 23.04.2015., which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

### 456. Section. Procedure for submitting a cassation appeal

(1)	A cassation appeal shall be submitted to the court that issued the judgment.  

(2)	If a cassation appeal is submitted directly to the cassation instance court within the time limit, the time limit shall not be considered as missed.

### 457. Section. Copies of cassation appeal

(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 458. Section. Security deposit

(1)	When submitting a cassation appeal, a security deposit in the amount specified in point 2 of the first part of Section 43.1 of this law shall be paid into the deposit account of the Supreme Court.  

(2)	If the Supreme Court fully or partially revokes or amends the appealed court judgment, the security deposit shall be refunded. If the cassation appeal is rejected, the security deposit shall not be refunded.  

(3)	If the cassation appeal is withdrawn before the session of the Supreme Court, the security deposit shall be refunded to the appellant.  

(4)	(Deleted by the law of 25.03.2021.)
(With amendments made by the laws of 22.05.2008., 20.12.2010., 12.09.2013., 30.10.2014. 09.06.2016., 25.03.2021. and
11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 459. Section. Leaving a cassation appeal without progress

(1)	If, in cases provided for by law, a translation of the cassation appeal and the documents attached thereto certified in the prescribed manner has not been attached, the judge shall adopt a decision to leave the cassation appeal without progress and shall set a time limit for remedying the deficiencies.  

(2)	If the appellant remedies the deficiencies indicated in the decision within the set time limit, the cassation appeal shall be considered as submitted on the day it was first submitted to the court.  

(3)	If the appellant has not remedied the deficiencies indicated in the decision within the set time limit, the cassation appeal shall be considered as not submitted and shall be returned to the appellant, without refunding the security deposit.  

(4)	An ancillary appeal may be submitted against a judge's decision by which the cassation appeal is returned to the appellant.  

(5)	If the deficiencies referred to in the first part of this Section, the fifth and sixth parts of Section 453 of this law are identified in the Supreme Court, the cassation appeal shall be returned to the court of appeal, but in the case referred to in the first part of Section 450 of this law — to the court of first instance, for the performance of the actions provided for in the second, third, fourth parts of this Section, the fifth and sixth parts of Section 453 of this law.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003., 05.02.2009., 30.10.2014., 23.04.2015., 09.06.2016., 31.05.2018. and
11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 460. Section. Actions of the court after receiving a cassation appeal

(1)	A judge of the court of appeal or, in the case referred to in the first part of Section 450 of this law, a judge of the court of first instance shall send the cassation appeal to the other parties to the case and notify them that they have the right to submit an explanation to the Supreme Court in connection with the cassation appeal within 30 days from the day of its sending.  

(11) If the cassation appeal has been sent to a party in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law, the time limit for submitting an explanation shall be counted from the day the cassation appeal is issued to the party.  

(2)	Upon expiry of the time limit for appealing the judgment, the court shall immediately send the civil case together with the cassation appeal to the Supreme Court.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 30.10.2014., 09.06.2016., 09.06.2016. and 11.11.2021., which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 461. Section. Joining a cassation appeal

(1)	Co-participants and third parties participating in the proceedings on the side of the person who submitted the cassation appeal may join the submitted appeal within 30 days from the day of sending the cassation appeal by submitting a respective application to the Supreme Court.  

(2)	When submitting an application to join a cassation appeal, a security deposit need not be paid.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 09.06.2016. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 462. Section. Withdrawal of cassation appeal

(1)	A person who has submitted a cassation appeal has the right to withdraw it until the cassation instance court session.  

(2)	If the cassation appeal is withdrawn before the Supreme Court procedural session, cassation proceedings are not initiated; if after the Supreme Court procedural session, — cassation proceedings in the case are terminated.  
(As amended by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

### 463. Section. Submission of counter-appeal

(1)	A party to the case may submit its own counter-appeal to the Supreme Court within 30 days from the date of dispatch of the cassation appeal. A party to the case to whom the cassation appeal has been sent in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law may submit its own counter-appeal to the Supreme Court within 30 days from the date of issuance of the cassation appeal.  

(2)	When submitting a counter-appeal, the provisions of Sections 450, 451, 452, 453 and 458 of this law must be observed.  

(3)	The Supreme Court sends the counter-appeal to the other participants in the proceedings and notifies them that within 30 days from the date of its dispatch they have the right to submit an explanation to the Supreme Court in connection with the counter-appeal.  

(4)	If the cassation appeal is withdrawn, the counter-appeal is examined independently.  
(As amended by the laws of 22.05.2008., 05.02.2009., 30.10.2014. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

57.	Chapter
Initiation of cassation proceedings and examination of cases in cassation instance
(Chapter title in the wording of the law of 22.05.2008., which enters into force on 25.06.2008.)

### 464. Section. Supreme Court procedural session

(1)	In order to decide the question of initiating cassation proceedings, cassation appeals, counter-appeals and protests after the expiry of the time limit for submission of explanations specified in the first part of Section 460 and the third part of Section 463 of this law are examined at a Supreme Court procedural session by a panel of judges formed of three judges in the order determined by the chairman of the department.  

(2)	If at least one of the judges considers that the case should be examined in cassation instance, the panel of judges adopts a decision to initiate cassation proceedings. The decision determines the examination of the case in written proceedings or examination in a court session.  

(3)	If the panel of judges unanimously recognises that the initiation of cassation proceedings should be refused, it refuses to initiate cassation proceedings by its procedural session decision.  

(4)	By unanimous decision of the panel of judges, the case may be referred for examination in cassation procedure to the Supreme Court in extended composition.  

(41) The decisions referred to in the second, third, fourth and seventh parts of this section may be drafted in the form of a resolution, observing the provisions of the second part of Section 229 of this law.  

(5)	If cassation proceedings are initiated, at the request of a party the panel of judges may adopt a decision to suspend the execution of the judgment until the examination of the case in cassation procedure.  

(6)	At the Supreme Court procedural session, the panel of judges may also decide the question of refusal to accept a submitted ancillary appeal and other procedural questions for the resolution of which a court session is not necessary, as well as adopt a decision to refer a question to the Court of Justice of the European Union for a preliminary ruling or submit an application to the Constitutional Court regarding the compliance of legal norms with the Constitution or an international legal norm (act).  

(7)	If the panel of judges has no obvious grounds to consider that, when examining the ancillary appeal, the appealed decision will be fully or partially annulled or amended, it may refuse to accept the ancillary appeal by unanimous decision at the Supreme Court procedural session. In such case, the security deposit paid for the ancillary appeal shall not be refunded.  
(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008. as amended by the laws of 08.09.2011., 15.03.2012., 30.10.2014., 12.02.2015., 09.06.2016. and 14.12.2017., which enters into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment in the seventh part replacing the words "state fee" with the words "security deposit" enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provisions points 139 and 140)

464.1 Section. Grounds for refusal to initiate cassation proceedings

(1)	The panel of judges refuses to initiate cassation proceedings if the cassation appeal does not comply with the requirements of Sections 450-454 of this law.  

(2)	If the cassation appeal formally complies with the requirements referred to in the first part of this section and if the court that issued the appealed judgment has not committed a violation of the provisions of the third part of Section 452 of this law, the panel of judges may also refuse to initiate cassation proceedings in the following cases:

1)	in the questions of application of legal norms indicated in the cassation appeal, Supreme Court case law has been established, and the appealed judgment complies with it;  

2)	evaluating the arguments mentioned in the cassation appeal, there are no obvious grounds to consider that the outcome of the case contained in the appealed judgment is incorrect and that the case to be examined has significant importance in ensuring uniform court practice or further development of law.  

(3)	If the cassation appeal formally complies with the requirements referred to in the first part of this section and if the court has not violated the provisions of the third part of Section 452 of this law and the case to be examined does not have significant importance in ensuring uniform court practice and further development of law, the panel of judges may also refuse to initiate cassation proceedings in disputes of a proprietary nature if the part in respect of which the judgment is being appealed is less than 2000 euros.  
(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008. as amended by the laws of 30.10.2014., 12.02.2015. and 09.06.2016., which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

464.2 Section. Determination of case examination

The examination of a case is determined in written proceedings if it is possible to adopt a decision according to the materials in the case. If additional explanations from the parties to the case are necessary or according to the Supreme Court's opinion the respective case may have special significance in the interpretation of legal norms, the examination of the case in a court session is determined.  
(In the wording of the law of 15.03.2012. as amended by the laws of 30.10.2014. and 09.06.2016., which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

464.	3 Section. Examination of case in written proceedings and drafting and pronouncement of judgment

(1)	The case is examined in written proceedings according to the materials in the case, observing the competence of the cassation instance court.  

(2)	Persons who have submitted an appeal or protest, as well as those persons whose interests are affected by the appeal or protest, are notified that the case will be examined in written proceedings, their procedural rights are explained to them, they are informed about the composition of the court that will examine the case, the right to file a challenge against a judge is explained, and they are informed about the date when the judgment will be available in the online system. This date is considered the date of pronouncement of the judgment. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the judgment to the online system on the date of pronouncement of the judgment, the judgment on the same date is available at the court registry. The date when the judgment is available at the court registry is considered the date of pronouncement of the judgment in such case.  

(21) If during the drafting of the judgment the court establishes that due to the complexity of the case a longer time limit is necessary for drafting the judgment, it may extend the said time limit, but not longer than two months. The court immediately informs the parties to the case referred to in the second part of this section about the new date when the judgment will be available in the online system.  

(3)	The civil procedural rights referred to in this law that are related to the preparation of the case for trial may be exercised by the parties no later than seven days before the date when the judgment will be available in the online system.  

(4)	If necessary, the court requests the submission of the prosecutor's opinion within 10 days.  

(5)	(Deleted from 01.03.2018. by the law of 14.12.2017. See Transitional provisions point 137)

(6)	At the written request of a party, the judgment is immediately sent to the party.  

(7)	In written proceedings, a decision may also be adopted to refer the case for examination in a court session.  
(In the wording of the law of 15.03.2012. as amended by the laws of 09.06.2016., 14.12.2017. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 465. Section. Scheduling of a Case for Hearing in a Supreme Court Session

(1)	The time of case hearing, the composition of the court and the rapporteur shall be determined by the President of the Department of the Supreme Court. The participants in the case shall be notified of the time and place of the case hearing.

(2)	In the cassation instance, a case shall be heard by three judges, but in cases provided for in this law — by a panel of judges consisting of not less than seven judges.
(As amended by the laws of 30.10.2014 and 12.02.2015, which enter into force on 01.03.2015.)

### 466. Section. Commencement of Case Hearing

(1)	The presiding judge shall open the court session and announce which case the Supreme Court is hearing.

(2)	The presiding judge shall ascertain which participants in the case have appeared, their identity and the authorisation of representatives.
(As amended by the laws of 31.10.2002, 12.02.2004 and 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

### 467. Section. Explanation of Rights and Obligations to Participants in the Case

(1)	The presiding judge shall announce the composition of the court, as well as name the prosecutor and interpreter, if one participates in the court session, and shall explain to the participants in the case their right to file challenges, as well as other procedural rights and obligations.

(2)	The grounds for challenge and the procedure for deciding a challenge shall be determined by Sections 19 to 21 of this law.
(As amended by the laws of 31.10.2002 and 12.02.2004, which enters into force on 10.03.2004.)

### 468. Section. Consequences Arising if Participants in the Case Do Not Appear at the Court Session

The non-appearance of those participants in the case who have been duly notified of the time and place of the cassation instance court session shall not be an obstacle to the hearing of the case.

### 469. Section. Decision on an Application

Applications by participants in the case related to the hearing of the case shall be decided after hearing the opinion of other participants in the case.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002 as amended by the law of 12.02.2004, which enters into force on 10.03.2004.)

### 470. Section. Report on the Case

The hearing of a case shall commence with the report on the case by the rapporteur judge.
(As amended by the law of 12.02.2015, which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

### 471. Section. Explanations of Participants in the Case and Opinion of the Prosecutor

(1)	After the judge's report, the court shall hear the explanations of the parties or their representatives. The court may determine in advance the time for giving explanations, but it must be granted equally to both parties.

(2)	The first to speak shall be the participant in the case who has submitted the cassation complaint, or the prosecutor, if he or she has submitted a protest. If both parties have appealed the judgment, the plaintiff shall speak first.

(3)	Judges may ask questions to the participants in the case.

(4)	Each party shall have the right to one rebuttal.

(5)	If the prosecutor participates in a case in which no cassation protest has been submitted, he or she shall give an opinion after the parties' explanations and rebuttals.
(As amended by the laws of 31.10.2002, 12.02.2004 and 12.02.2015, which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

### 472. Section. Procedure for Rendering a Judgment

(1)	After the explanations of the participants in the case and the opinion of the prosecutor, the court shall retire to deliberation in order to render a judgment.

(2)	If, when hearing a case in a composition of three judges, the court does not reach a unanimous opinion or all judges consider that the case should be heard in an extended composition, the court shall adopt a decision to refer the case for hearing in an extended composition of the Supreme Court.

(3)	When hearing a case in an extended composition, the judgment shall be rendered by a majority of votes and shall be signed by all judges.

(4)	After the judges' deliberation, the court shall return to the courtroom and the presiding judge shall announce the judgment by reading its operative part and shall notify when the participants in the case may familiarise themselves with the judgment.

(5)	A judge who, when hearing a case in the extended composition of the Supreme Court, has had a different opinion on the interpretation of the law or the application of the law, shall have the right within 15 days after the drafting of the judgment to express in writing his or her separate opinion, which shall be attached to the case.

(6)	If the judges acknowledge that it is not possible to render a judgment in this court session, the Supreme Court shall schedule the next court session, which shall take place within the next 14 days and at which it shall announce the judgment.
(As amended by the laws of 19.06.2003, 05.02.2009, 30.10.2014, 12.02.2015, 09.06.2016, 14.12.2017 and
11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

472.1 Section. Suspension of Proceedings in the Cassation Instance

If the cassation instance court adopts a decision to refer a question to the Court of Justice of the European Union for the adoption of a preliminary ruling, it shall suspend the proceedings until the decision of the Court of Justice of the European Union enters into legal force.
(In the wording of the law of 07.04.2004 as amended by the law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

58. Chapter
Judgment of the Cassation Instance Court

### 473. Section. Limits of Case Hearing

(1)	The court, when hearing a case in cassation proceedings, shall verify the legality of the judgment in the case in the appealed part with respect to the persons who have appealed the judgment or joined the cassation complaint, and with respect to the arguments stated in the cassation complaint.

(2)	The court may set aside the entire judgment, even though only a part of it has been appealed, if it finds such violations of law that have led to incorrect adjudication of the entire case.

### 474. Section. Rights of the Cassation Instance Court

The court, having heard the case, may render one of the following judgments:

1)	leave the judgment unchanged and dismiss the complaint;

2)	set aside the entire judgment or a part thereof and refer the case for new hearing to the appellate or first instance court;

3)	set aside the entire judgment or a part thereof and leave the application without examination or terminate the proceedings if the second instance court has not complied with the provisions of Section 219 or 223 of this law;

4)	amend the judgment in the part concerning the amount of the claim if it has been incorrectly determined by erroneously applying a substantive law provision.
(As amended by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 475. Section. Content of the Cassation Instance Court Judgment

(1)	The judgment of the cassation instance court shall consist of an introductory, descriptive, reasoning and operative part.

(2)	In the introductory part, the court shall indicate:

1)	the name and composition of the court;

2)	the time of rendering the judgment;

3)	the participants in the case and the subject of the dispute;

4)	the persons who have submitted a cassation complaint (counter-complaint) or joined it.

(3)	In the descriptive part, the court shall indicate:

1)	a brief statement of the circumstances of the case;

2)	the essence of the judgment of the appellate instance court;

3)	the arguments of the cassation complaint;

4)	the arguments of the counter-complaint or the essence of the explanation.

(4)	In the reasoning part, the court shall indicate:

1)	when dismissing the cassation complaint — the arguments for which the complaint has been dismissed;

2)	when granting the cassation complaint — the arguments concerning the violations of legal provisions committed by the court, their incorrect application or violation of the limits of competence.

(5)	In the operative part, the court shall indicate the decision in accordance with the relevant point of Section 474 of this law.

(6)	If the court, when hearing a case, acknowledges that the reasoning contained in the appealed judgment on the issue of application of legal provisions is correct, it may indicate in the reasoning part of the judgment that it acknowledges the respective argumentation as correct. In such a case, the arguments provided for in point 1 of paragraph four of this Section may not be indicated in the reasoning part of the judgment.

(7)	If the court, when hearing a case, acknowledges that the appealed judgment does not comply with the case-law of the Supreme Court that has been established in other similar cases and the appealed judgment does not indicate with reasoning why there has been a departure from the case-law, the court may render a judgment in the reasoning part of which it indicates the case-law that has not been observed or the non-observance of which has not been justified. In such a case, the descriptive part may not be included in the judgment and the arguments provided for in point
2 of paragraph four of this Section may not be indicated in the reasoning part of the judgment.
(As amended by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

### 476. Section. Binding Nature of Instructions of the Cassation Instance Court

(1)	The interpretation of law expressed in the judgment of the cassation instance court shall be binding on the court that hears this case anew.

(2)	The cassation instance court shall not indicate in its judgment what judgment should be rendered when hearing the case anew.

### 477. Section. Legal Force of the Judgment of the Court of Cassation

The judgment of the court of cassation is not subject to appeal and enters into force at the moment of its pronouncement.

Section 477.1 Actions of the Court of Cassation After Examination of the Cassation Complaint and Cassation Protest

After making (adopting) the decision referred to in the second part of Section 462, the third part of Section 464, the second part of Section 464.3 and points 1 and 4 of Section 474 of this Law, the court of cassation immediately sends the case to the court of appeal for the issuance of a writ of execution.
(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008 with amendments made by the laws of 15.03.2012 and 14.12.2017, which enters into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment to the section regarding the exclusion of the word "full" enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provision point 137)

Eleventh Division Reopening of a Case in Which a Judgment or Decision
Has Entered into Legal Force

Chapter 59
Reopening of a Case Due to Newly Discovered Circumstances

### Section 478. Submission of an Application

(1) Reopening of a case due to newly discovered circumstances is initiated upon the application of a party to the case. The application is submitted to the same court whose judgment or decision completed the examination of the case on the merits.

(2) The application may be submitted within three months from the day when the circumstances that constitute grounds for reopening the case were established.

(3) The application may not be submitted if more than 10 years have passed since the entry into force of the judgment or decision. This condition does not apply to cases where the newly discovered circumstances are a decision of the European Court of Human Rights or another international or supranational court (point 6 of Section 479).

(31) An unsigned application is considered not submitted and is sent back to the submitter, refunding the security deposit.

(4) The judge adopts a decision to refuse to accept the application if:

1) the application is not accompanied by a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to apply to the court with the application;

2) the security deposit has not been paid in the manner and amount prescribed by law;

3) the time limit specified in the second or third part of this section has been missed;

4) the application does not specify circumstances which, in accordance with Section 479 of this Law, may be recognised as newly discovered circumstances;

5) the application has been submitted repeatedly and it does not follow from it that the factual or legal circumstances material to the resolution of the matter have substantially changed.

(5) The judge's decision to refuse to accept the application in accordance with points 1 and 2 of the fourth part of this section is not subject to appeal. An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against the judge's decision to refuse to accept the application in accordance with points 3, 4 and 5 of the fourth part of this section.

(6) If it does not follow from the power of attorney or other document attached to the application that the representative is authorised to apply to the court with this application, the judge leaves the application without progress and the consequences provided for in Section 133 of this Law ensue.

(7) When submitting the application, a security deposit is payable in the amount specified in point 4 of the first part of Section 43.1 of this Law. If the court fully or partially revokes the contested court decision or if the application is withdrawn before its examination, the security deposit is refundable.

(8) If the court refuses to accept the application on the basis of points 1 and 2 of the fourth part of this section, the paid security deposit is refunded. If the court refuses to accept the application on the basis of points 3, 4 and 5 of the fourth part of this section, the security deposit is not refunded.

(9) The security deposit need not be paid by persons who, in accordance with law, are exempt from state duty. The court or judge, taking into account the financial situation of a natural person, may fully or partially exempt the person from payment of the security deposit.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009, 30.10.2014, 09.06.2016, 19.10.2017, 01.10.2020, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### Section 479. Newly Discovered Circumstances

The following are recognised as newly discovered circumstances:

1) material circumstances of the case that existed at the time of examination of the case but were not and could not have been known to the applicant;

2) deliberately false witness testimony, deliberately false expert opinion, deliberately false translation, forged written or material evidence, on the basis of which the judgment was made, established by a judgment in a criminal case that has entered into legal force;

3) criminal activities, due to which an unlawful or unfounded judgment was made or a decision was adopted, established by a judgment in a criminal case that has entered into legal force;

4) the revocation of the judgment of that court or decision of another institution on the basis of which the judgment was made or decision was adopted in this case;

5) the recognition of the legal norm applied in adjudicating the case as inconsistent with a legal norm of higher legal force;

6) a decision of the European Court of Human Rights or another international or supranational court in this case, from which it follows that proceedings must be initiated anew. In such a case, when adopting a decision in the reopened case, the court must base itself on the facts established in the decision of the European Court of Human Rights or another international or supranational court and their legal assessment.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001 and 22.05.2008, which enters into force on 25.06.2008.)

### Section 480. Time Limit for Submission of an Application

The time limit for submission of an application is calculated:

1) for the circumstances specified in point 1 of Section 479 of this Law — from the day of discovery of these circumstances;

2) in the cases specified in points 2 and 3 of Section 479 of this Law — from the day when the judgment in the criminal case entered into legal force;

3) in the cases specified in point 4 of Section 479 of this Law — from the day when the court decision entered into legal force, by which the judgment in a civil case or criminal case was revoked, or when the decision of another institution was revoked, on the basis of which the judgment or decision is based that is requested to be revoked due to newly discovered circumstances;

4) in the case specified in point 5 of Section 479 of this Law — from the day when the judgment or other decision entered into force, in connection with which the applied legal norm loses force as inconsistent with a legal norm of higher legal force.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### Section 481. Examination of the Application

(1) The application due to newly discovered circumstances is examined in written proceedings.

(2) When examining the application, the provisions of law on the inadmissibility of a judge participating in the repeated examination of a case are not applicable.
(In the wording of the law of 05.02.2009 with amendments made by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

### Section 482. Court Decision

(1) The court, having examined the application, verifies whether the circumstances indicated by the applicant are to be recognised as newly discovered circumstances in accordance with Section 479 of this Law.

(2) If the court establishes newly discovered circumstances, it revokes the contested judgment or decision in full or in part thereof and refers the case for new examination to the same court or to a lower instance court.

(3) If the court recognises that the circumstances specified in the application are not to be considered newly discovered, it rejects the application.

(4) An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against the court decision by which the application for reopening of the case due to newly discovered circumstances has been rejected.
(With amendments made by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

Chapter 60
Reopening of Cases Due to Material Violations of Substantive and Procedural Legal Norms

### Section 483. Submission of a Protest

A protest against a court decision that has entered into force may be submitted to the Supreme Court by the Prosecutor General if no more than 10 years have passed since the entry into force of the decision.
(In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### Section 484. Grounds for Submission of a Protest

The grounds for submission of a protest against a court decision that has entered into force are material violations of substantive or procedural legal norms established in cases that have been examined only in the court of first instance, if the court decision has not been appealed in the manner prescribed by law for reasons independent of the parties to the case, or if the court decision has infringed the rights of state or municipal institutions or the rights of persons who have not been parties to the case.

### 485. pants. Protest Review Procedure

Protests shall be reviewed by the Supreme Court in the procedure specified in Sections 464-477 of this Law.  
(With amendments made by the Law of 30.10.2014, which comes into force on 01.01.2015.)

60.1	nodaļa
Reopening of a Case in Connection with Review of a Decision in Cases Provided for in European Union Legal Norms

## (Chapter 08

09.2011. Law version, which comes into force on 30.09.2011.)

485.1 pants. Submission of Application

(1)	Reopening of a case in connection with review of a decision may be initiated by the defendant, based on Article 19 of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 April 2004 creating a European Enforcement Order for uncontested claims (hereinafter – European Parliament and Council Regulation No 805/2004), Article 18 of European Parliament and Council Regulation No 861/2007, Article 20 of European Parliament and Council Regulation No 1896/2006, or Article 19 of Council Regulation (EC) No 4/2009 of 18 December 2008 on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions and cooperation in matters relating to maintenance obligations (hereinafter – Council Regulation No 4/2009), by submitting an application:

1)	for review of a judgment or decision of a district (city) court – to the relevant regional court;  

2)	for review of a judgment or decision of a regional court – to the Supreme Court;  

3)	for review of a judgment or decision of the Court Chamber – to the Civil Cases Department of the Supreme Court.  

(2)	An application may be submitted within 45 days, but in accordance with European Parliament and Council Regulation No 861/2007 within 30 days from the day when the review circumstances provided for in the European Union legal norms mentioned in paragraph one of this Section became known.  

(3)	An application may not be submitted if the limitation period has expired for submitting for enforcement the enforcement document concerning the relevant decision.  

(4)	An application which does not specify circumstances that in accordance with the European Union legal norms mentioned in paragraph one of this Section may be recognised as circumstances for review of a decision shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter. A judge shall refuse to accept for review an application for reopening of a case in connection with review of a decision also if the application has been submitted repeatedly and it does not follow therefrom that the circumstances for review of the decision have changed for resolution of the matter. An appeal may be submitted against such decision of a judge.  
(With amendments made by the Laws of 30.10.2014, 29.10.2015 and 01.06.2017, which comes into force on 01.07.2017. The amendment in paragraph two in connection with European Parliament and Council Regulation No 861/2007 comes into force on 14.07.2017. See transitional provision Point 126)

485.2 pants. Review of Application

An application for review of a decision shall be reviewed in written proceedings.  

485.3 pants. Court Decision

(1)	The court, having reviewed the application, shall verify whether the circumstances indicated by the applicant are to be recognised as circumstances for review of a decision in accordance with the European Union legal norms mentioned in paragraph one of Section 485.1 of this Law.  

(2)	If the court establishes circumstances for review of a decision, it shall set aside the contested decision in full and refer the case for new review to the court of first instance.  

(3)	If the court finds that the circumstances indicated in the application are not to be regarded as circumstances for review of a decision, it shall reject the application.  

(4)	An appeal may be submitted against the court decision.
