### 534. pants

Submission of Application for Issuance of Writ of Execution for Forced Enforcement of Permanent Arbitration Award

(1)	If a permanent arbitration award is enforceable in Latvia and is not voluntarily complied with, the interested party may submit an application for issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of the permanent arbitration award to the district (city) court according to the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none, — according to the debtor's place of residence or registered address or according to the place of enforcement of the arbitration award.  

(2)	The following shall be attached to the application for issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award:

1)	the permanent arbitration award;  

2)	the arbitration agreement certifying the parties' written agreement to submit the civil dispute for consideration to arbitration;  

3)	(deleted by law of 11.11.2021.);  

4)	documents confirming payment of the state fee and expenses related to the application for issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of the permanent arbitration award.  

(3)	The documents referred to in Paragraph (2), Clause 4 of this Section may not be attached if the application has been submitted and payment has been made in the online system or if the application includes information about the state fee payment made and payment of expenses related to the application for issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of the permanent arbitration award, indicating the payer's identification data — name, surname, personal identity number or title and registration number, if they differ from the applicant's data, as well as the date and number of the payment order. When making the payment, information about the debtor shall be indicated in the purpose of the payment order — his or her name, surname, personal identity number or title and registration number. In this case, the district (city) court shall recognise the said payments as received in the state budget using the budget electronic settlement system.  

(4)	(Deleted by law of 11.11.2021.)
(As worded by law of 11.09.2014. with amendments made by law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

534.	1 pants. Sending of Application for Issuance of Writ of Execution for Forced Enforcement of Permanent Arbitration Award to Participants in the Case

(1)	When an application for issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award has been received by the district (city) court, it shall be immediately sent to the other participants in the case to their official electronic addresses or by registered mail, setting a time limit for submission of written explanations, which shall not be shorter than 20 days from the date of sending the application.  

(2)	In the explanations, the participant in the case shall indicate:

1)	whether he or she acknowledges the application in full or in part;  

2)	his or her objections to the application and their justification;  

3)	evidence confirming his or her objections and their justification, as well as the law on which they are based;  

4)	requests for admission or obtaining of evidence;  

5)	other circumstances which he or she considers significant in the examination of the application.  

(3)	(Deleted by law of 11.11.2021.)

(4)	After receipt of the explanations, the judge shall immediately send them to the other participants in the case.  

(5)	Failure to submit explanations shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application for issuance of a writ of execution.  
(As worded by law of 17.02.2005. with amendments made by laws of 11.09.2014. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

### 535. pants

Determination of Application for Issuance of Writ of Execution for Forced Enforcement of Permanent Arbitration Award

(1)	A decision on issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award or a decision on refusal to issue a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award shall be adopted by the judge on the basis of the submitted documents, without summoning the participants in the case, within 20 days from the date when the explanations have been sent to the other participants in the case, or within 20 days from the date when the time limit for providing explanations has expired. When adopting a decision on issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award, the judge shall also decide the question of whether the state fee for issuance of such writ of execution is to be reimbursed and whether the expenses related to the examination of the case are to be reimbursed. The decision shall be sent to the parties within three days. A decision on refusal to issue a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award shall be sent to the permanent arbitration to the e-mail address indicated on its website.  

(2)	The court may request from the permanent arbitration the case file or other information if it is necessary for adoption of the decision referred to in Paragraph one of this Section.  

(3)	A decision on issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award shall not be subject to appeal.  

(4)	An appeal may be lodged against a decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award within 10 days from the date of receipt of the decision.  

(5)	A decision on refusal to issue a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award shall enter into force after the time limit for lodging an appeal has expired and an appeal has not been lodged.  
(As worded by law of 11.09.2014. with amendments made by law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

### 536. pants

Grounds for refusal to issue a writ of execution for the enforcement of a permanent arbitral tribunal award

(1)	A judge shall refuse to issue a writ of execution for the enforcement of a permanent arbitral tribunal award if:

1)	the specific civil dispute may be resolved only by a court;  

2)	the arbitration agreement has been concluded by a natural person with limited legal capacity or by a minor;  

3)	the arbitration agreement has been revoked or declared invalid in the manner prescribed by law;  

4)	a party was not duly notified of the arbitration proceedings or for other reasons was unable to submit its explanations and this materially affected the arbitration proceedings;  

5)	a party was not duly notified of the appointment of arbitrators and this materially affected the arbitration proceedings;  

6)	the arbitrator does not meet the requirements of the Arbitration Law, the arbitral tribunal was not established or the arbitration proceedings did not take place in accordance with the provisions of the arbitration agreement or the Arbitration Law;  

7)	the arbitral award was made in respect of a civil dispute that is not provided for in the arbitration agreement or does not comply with the provisions of the arbitration agreement, or it has resolved issues not covered by the arbitration agreement.  

(2)	If it is not possible to issue a writ of execution for the enforcement of a permanent arbitral tribunal award for the reasons referred to in paragraph one of this Section in respect of any part of the permanent arbitral tribunal award, it may be issued in respect of the remaining part of the arbitral award.  
(11.09.2014. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.11.2014. Panta jaunā redakcija stājas spēkā 01.01.2015. Sk. pārejas noteikumu 83.punktu)

### 537. pants

Consequences of refusal to issue a writ of execution for the enforcement of a permanent arbitral tribunal award

After a decision refusing to issue a writ of execution for the enforcement of a permanent arbitral tribunal award has entered into force:

1)	the civil dispute may be resolved by a court in the general procedure if the refusal to issue a writ of execution for the enforcement of a permanent arbitral tribunal award is based on points 1, 2, 3 and 7 of paragraph one of Section 536 of this Law;  

2)	the civil dispute may be referred again for resolution to an arbitral tribunal if the refusal to issue a writ of execution for the enforcement of a permanent arbitral tribunal award is based on points 4, 5 and 6 of paragraph one of Section 536 of this Law.  
(11.09.2014. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.11.2014. Panta jaunā redakcija stājas spēkā 01.01.2015. Sk. pārejas noteikumu 83.punktu)

### 538. pants. Enforcement of court judgments and decisions

Court judgments and decisions shall be enforceable after they have entered into legal force, except in cases where, in accordance with law or a court judgment, they are enforceable immediately. The indication that a judgment or decision is enforceable immediately must be in the writ of execution itself.  
(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 31.10.2002. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2003.)

### 539. pants. Decisions of courts and other institutions that must be enforced

(1)	The following decisions of courts, decisions of judges or decisions of other institutions shall be enforceable in the procedure for enforcement of court judgments established in this Law:

1)	court judgments and court or judge decisions in civil cases, as well as in cases arising from administrative legal relations;  

2)	court decisions and decisions of the person directing the proceedings or instructions of the prosecutor in criminal cases in the part concerning pecuniary recoveries;  

3)	judge or court decisions in cases concerning administrative offences in the part concerning pecuniary recoveries;  

4)	court decisions on the approval of a settlement;  

5)	decisions of permanent arbitral tribunals;  

6)	decisions of foreign courts or competent authorities and foreign arbitral tribunals in cases provided for by law;  

7)	court or judge decisions on the imposition of procedural sanctions — fines or penalty payments;  

8)	decisions of labour dispute commissions;  

9)	decisions of the public utilities regulator (hereinafter — the regulator) on the examination of disputes or

disagreements.  

(2)	Unless otherwise provided by law, the following shall also be enforceable in the procedure established for the enforcement of court judgments:

1)	decisions of institutions and officials in administrative offence proceedings and in cases of violations of law in cases provided for by law;  

2)	administrative acts issued by institutions and officials vested with state authority directed at monetary payments;  

3)	decisions of persons belonging to the judicial system (notaries, advocates, bailiffs) on remuneration, remuneration for legal assistance provided and on expenses related to services provided, and state fees;  

4)	acts adopted by the European Council, the Commission or the European Central Bank in accordance with Article 299 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.  

5)	notarial acts drawn up in the procedure established in Section D1 of the Notarial Law.  

6)	protest acts concerning promissory notes issued in the form of a notarial act.

### 541. Article. Preparation of a writ of execution

(1)	A writ of execution is prepared by the court of first instance or the court of appeal after the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the pronouncement of the judgment or the adoption of the decision.

(2)	If a time limit for voluntary execution has been set for the enforcement of a court judgment and the judgment has not been executed, the writ of execution is available in the online system for compulsory enforcement after the expiry of the time limit for voluntary execution.

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.)

(31)	In the case referred to in point 4 of the second part of Article 539 of this Law, the writ of execution is prepared by the Riga City Court.

(32)	In the cases referred to in Articles 544.1 and 544.2 of this Law, the writ of execution is prepared by the district (city) court according to the place of execution of the decision or according to the declared place of residence of the debtor — natural person, but if there is none — according to the debtor's place of residence or the legal address of the legal person.

(33)	If several writs of execution are to be prepared for one judgment or a writ of execution is necessary in a case in which a settlement has been concluded, then the writ of execution, on the basis of a written request of the creditor, is prepared by the court that adopted the decision.

(4)	If, in accordance with a court judgment, monetary amounts are to be recovered as state revenue, the court, after the expiry of the time limit for voluntary execution set by the court, sends the writ of execution to the bailiff according to the declared place of residence of the debtor — natural person — but if there is none — according to the debtor's place of residence or the legal address of the legal person.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 17.02.2005., 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012., 30.10.2014.,
11.11.2021., 16.06.2022. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 01.08.2022.)

541.1 Article. Issuance of European Union enforcement documents and documents related to enforcement

(1)	A European Enforcement Order, on the basis of Regulation No. 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council, is issued by the court at the request of the creditor when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the pronouncement of the judgment or the adoption of the decision.

(2)	The certificate referred to in point 1 of Article 41 or point 1 of Article 42 of Council Regulation No. 2201/2003, on the basis of the provisions of this Regulation, is issued by the court on its own initiative or at the request of a party to the case when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the pronouncement of the judgment or the adoption of the decision.

(3)	The certificate referred to in Articles 54 and 58 of the Lugano Convention of 30 October 2007 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters and the certificate referred to in Article 39 of Council Regulation No. 2201/2003 is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case.

(4)	The forms referred to in points 2 and 3 of Article 6 of Regulation No. 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council are issued by the court at the request of a party to the case.

(41)	The certificate referred to in point 2 of Article 20 of Regulation No. 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case. The court, at the request of a party to the case, issues the certificate referred to in this part in any other language in accordance with point 2 of Article 20 of Regulation No. 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(42)	A European payment order is issued by the court in accordance with Article 18 of Regulation No. 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(43)	The extract of the decision referred to in subparagraph "b" of point 1 of Article 20 of Council Regulation No. 4/2009 is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the pronouncement of the judgment or the adoption of the decision.

(44)	The certificate referred to in Articles 53 and 60 of Regulation No. 1215/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the pronouncement of the judgment or the adoption of the decision.

(45)	The certificate referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 June 2013 on mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters (hereinafter — Regulation No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council) is issued by the court at the request of the applicant when the decision has been adopted. The court informs the defendant of the issuance of the certificate referred to in this part in accordance with Article 8 of Regulation No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The court, at the request of the applicant, performs transliteration and translation of the certificate referred to in this part on the basis of point 3 of Article 5 of Regulation No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(46)	The certificate referred to in Article 14 of Regulation No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case.

(47)	The certificates referred to in Article 36 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 are issued by the court at the request of a party when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the pronouncement of the judgment or the adoption of the decision.

(48)	The certificates referred to in Article 47 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 are issued by the court at the request of a party when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the pronouncement of the judgment or the adoption of the decision.

(5)	The documents referred to in the first, second, third, fourth part, parts 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 and 4.8 of this Article are issued by the court in which the case is located at that time.

(6)	The court adopts a reasoned decision on refusal to issue the documents referred to in the first, second, parts 4.5 and 4.8 of this Article.

(7)	An ancillary complaint may be submitted against the court's decision to refuse to issue the documents referred to in the first, second, parts 4.5 and 4.8 of this Article.

### 542. Article. Preparation of several writs of execution for one judgment

(1)	One writ of execution is prepared for each judgment, except in the cases specified in the second part of this Article.

(2)	Several writs of execution are prepared for one judgment if:

1)	the execution of the judgment is to be carried out in different places;

2)	the judgment is immediately enforceable in any part thereof;

3)	the judgment is made in favour of several applicants or is directed against several defendants;

4)	a different enforcement procedure is provided for by law for the execution of the claim satisfied or partially satisfied by the judgment.

(3)	When preparing several writs of execution, each of them precisely indicates the place of execution or the part of the judgment which is enforceable under this writ of execution, as well as the creditor in whose favour and the debtor against whom recovery is to be directed under this writ of execution.  
(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 543.pants. Content of the writ of execution

(1)	The writ of execution shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court that issued the writ of execution;  

2)	the case in which the writ of execution was issued;  

3)	the time of making the decision;  

4)	the operative part of the decision or a part thereof;  

5)	the time when the decision enters into legal force, or an indication that the decision is to be executed immediately;  

6)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

7)	information about the creditor and debtor: for natural persons — name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address(es) indicated in the declaration and place of residence if it differs, and for legal persons — name, legal address and registration number;  

8)	information about the child — name, surname, personal identity number and location — in cases where a decision on the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence or a decision in a case arising from custody or contact rights is to be executed;  

9)	information about the contact person in whose presence contact rights are to be exercised (for natural persons — name, surname, personal identity number and address, for legal persons — name, legal address and registration number), if the decision in a case arising from contact rights has designated a contact person in whose presence contact is to be exercised, and the said person is not a representative of the orphan's court or a person authorised by the orphan's court;  

10)	information about the place where contact rights are to be exercised, if the decision in a case arising from contact rights has designated a place for the exercise of contact that is not the premises of the orphan's court;  

11)	information about the forced opening of premises — the address and the time period when the premises are to be opened — if the court has determined in the decision on the review of the time and place of exercise of contact rights that the premises are to be opened by force (eleventh paragraph of Section 244.13 of this Law).  

(2)	The writ of execution shall be signed by the judge.  

(3)	The content of other enforcement documents shall be determined by the respective laws.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 04.08.2011., 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015. and 11.11.2021., which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

543.1 pants. Correction of errors in European Union enforcement documents

(1)	The court that made the judgment or adopted the decision may, upon application of a party to the case or, if provided for in European Union legal norms, also on its own initiative, correct errors:

1)	in the European Enforcement Order, based on Article 10 of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council;  

2)	in the certificate referred to in Article 41(1) or Article 42(1) of Council Regulation No 2201/2003, based on Council Regulation No 2201/2003;  

3)	in the certificate referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council, based on point (a) of Article 9(1) of Council Regulation No 606/2013;  

4)	in the certificate referred to in Article 36 or 47 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111, based on Article 37 or 48 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.  

(2)	When submitting an application for the correction of a European Enforcement Order, the form referred to in Article 10(3) of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be used.  

(3)	The question of correction of errors shall be examined at a court hearing, after prior notification to the parties to the case. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the question.  

(4)	Errors in the enforcement documents referred to in paragraph one of this Section shall be corrected by a court decision.  

(5)	An appeal may be lodged against the court decision to make a correction of errors in enforcement documents.  
(In the wording of the law of 07.09.2006. with amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 07.07.2022. The new wording of paragraph one enters into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision 177)

### 544.pants. Issuance of a duplicate of the writ of execution

(1)	If a writ of execution has been lost, stolen or destroyed, the court that adopted the decision may, upon application of the creditor, or, if it occurred during the enforcement proceedings, upon application of the bailiff, issue a duplicate of the writ of execution. The application shall indicate the circumstances in which the writ of execution was lost, stolen or destroyed.  

(2)	The application for the issuance of a duplicate shall be examined at a court hearing, after prior notification to the creditor and debtor. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application for the issuance of a duplicate of the writ of execution.  

(3)	When adopting a decision on the issuance of a duplicate of the writ of execution, the court shall simultaneously declare the lost, stolen or destroyed writ of execution invalid and release the creditor from payment of the state fee if his or her fault in the loss, destruction or theft of the writ of execution has not been established.  

(4)	An appeal may be lodged against the court decision.  

(5)	A duplicate of the writ of execution shall be issued to the creditor after the decision enters into force and payment of the state fee, if the creditor has not been released from it.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

544.1 Enforcement of a decision of a labour dispute commission

(1)	The decision of the labour dispute commission shall be attached to the application submitted to the court for the issuance of a writ of execution.  

(2)	The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution or a reasoned refusal to issue it shall be adopted by the judge individually on the basis of the submitted application and the decision of the labour dispute commission attached to it within three days from the date of submission of the application, without summoning the parties.  

(3)	The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution shall enter into force immediately.  

(4)	An appeal may be lodged against the decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution within 10 days from the date when the decision was issued to the claimant.  

(5)	The court shall refuse to issue a writ of execution if it establishes that, in accordance with the law, the specific dispute may only be resolved in court.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

544.2 pants. Enforcement of a regulator's decision on the examination of a dispute or disagreement

(1)	The regulator's decision on the examination of a dispute or disagreement shall be attached to the application submitted to the court for the issuance of a writ of execution.  

(2)	The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution or a reasoned refusal to issue it shall be adopted by the judge individually on the basis of the submitted application and the regulator's decision on the examination of a dispute or disagreement attached to it within three days from the date of submission of the application, without summoning the parties.  

(3)	The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution shall enter into force immediately.  

(4)	An appeal may be lodged against the decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution within 10 days from the date when the decision was issued to the claimant.  

(5)	The court shall refuse to issue a writ of execution if it establishes that, in accordance with the law, the specific dispute or disagreement may only be resolved in court.  
(In the wording of the law of 08.09.2011. with amendments made by the laws of 22.06.2017. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 545.pants. Liability for the preservation of an enforcement document

(Repealed by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

545.1 pants. Withdrawal of European Union enforcement documents

(1)	The court which has delivered the judgment or adopted the decision, upon receipt of an application from a party to the case, using the form referred to in Article 10(3) of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council, may withdraw the European Enforcement Order on the basis of Article 10 of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council.  

(11)	The court which has adopted the decision, upon receipt of an application from a party to the case or on its own initiative, using the certificate referred to in Article 14 of Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council, may withdraw the certificate referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the basis of point (b) of Article 9(1) of Council Regulation No 606/2013.  

(12)	The court which has delivered the judgment or adopted the decision, upon receipt of an application from a party to the case or on its own initiative, using the certificate referred to in Article 49 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111, shall withdraw the certificate referred to in point (a) or (b) of Article 47(1) of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 on the basis of Article 48(2) of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.  

(2)	An application for the withdrawal of a European Enforcement Order, the withdrawal of the certificate referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council, or the withdrawal of the certificate referred to in point (a) or (b) of Article 47(1) of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 shall be examined at a court hearing, after prior notification to the parties to the case. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the matter.  

(3)	An appeal may be lodged against the decision of the court.  
(As worded by the law of 07.09.2006 with amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022. The new wording of the title of the Section, Paragraph 1.2 and the amendment to Paragraph 2 enter into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision 177)

### 546.pants. Time limits within which enforcement documents must be submitted for enforcement

(1)	An enforcement document may be submitted for compulsory enforcement within 10 years from the date of entry into force of the court or judge's decision, unless other limitation periods are provided for by law.  

(2)	If periodic payments are recovered pursuant to a court judgment, the enforcement document shall retain its validity for the entire period for which the payments have been awarded, but the running of the time limit provided for in Paragraph 1 of this Section shall commence from the date of expiry of each payment.  

(3)	The time limits within which other enforcement documents referred to in Section 540 of this Law must be submitted for enforcement shall be determined by the respective laws.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 547.pants. Interruption of the limitation period for submission of an enforcement document

(1)	The limitation period shall be interrupted by submitting the enforcement document for enforcement. The limitation period shall also be interrupted by partial voluntary execution of the decision.  

(2)	After the interruption, the running of the time limit shall recommence, without counting the time that has elapsed before. If full recovery has not been made pursuant to the enforcement document and it has been returned to the creditor, the new time limit for submission of the document shall be counted from the day on which it was issued to the creditor.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

547.	1 pants. Time limits within which requests for assistance from foreign authorities for recovery must be executed

If an enforcement document has been issued for the enforcement of a foreign tax claim, compulsory enforcement shall be carried out within the time limit specified in the request for assistance for recovery from the foreign authority, but in the event of a change thereof, within the time limit specified by the foreign authority in the notification submitted to the State Revenue Service.  
(As worded by the law of 15.03.2012, which enters into force on 01.04.2012.)

Status of bailiffs

### 548. pants. Bailiff

(1)	Court and other decisions referred to in Section 539 of this Law shall be enforced by a bailiff.  

(2)	Supervision of the activities of a bailiff shall take place in the manner provided for in this Law and the Law on Bailiffs.  
(As worded by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 549. pants. General provisions for the activities of a bailiff

(1)	A bailiff shall commence enforcement actions upon a written application by the creditor and, in cases provided for by law, upon the initiative of the Latvian Council of Sworn Bailiffs, the responsible authority or the court, on the basis of an enforcement document.  

(2)	A bailiff must accept for enforcement an enforcement document if the debtor's place of residence (for legal persons — legal address), the location of property or place of work is within the boundaries (district) established for the bailiff's place of office. A bailiff may also accept other enforcement documents the enforcement of which is to be carried out in the territory of operation of the regional court to which he or she is attached.  

(21)	(Repealed by the law of 16.06.2022)

(22)	A bailiff must accept for enforcement an enforcement document concerning the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence or an enforcement document in a case arising from custody or contact rights, including a European Union enforcement document, if the child's location is within the boundaries (district) established for the bailiff's place of office.  

(23)	If the debtor's place of residence (for legal persons — legal address), the location of property or place of work is not in Latvia, the bailiff must accept for enforcement the enforcement document referred to in Paragraph 19 of Section 540 of this Law, irrespective of the debtor's place of residence (for legal persons — legal address), the location of property or place of work.  

(3)	Outside the boundaries of his or her district, as well as in relation to a debtor whose place of residence (for legal persons — legal address) is in another district, a bailiff shall carry out enforcement of the judgment in communication with the bailiff of the relevant district in the manner determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.  

(4)	Enforcement of a judgment on Sundays and public holidays shall be permitted only in urgent cases.  

(5)	Enforcement of a judgment between the hours of 24 and 6 shall not be permitted.  

(6)	The creditor and the debtor shall have the right to be present during enforcement actions, to invite no more than two witnesses and to receive information related to the enforcement of the judgment.  

(7)	A bailiff, on his or her own initiative or at the request of an interested person, by adopting a relevant decision, may correct clerical errors in procedural documents drawn up in enforcement cases in his or her records. Before correcting errors, he or she shall request a response from the persons who participated in the drawing up of the document. Obvious errors may be corrected without requesting a response. A bailiff's decision pursuant to which errors are corrected shall have no consequences in relation to persons whose rights or obligations arise from the procedural document.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002, 19.06.2003, 07.09.2006, 26.10.2006, 04.08.2011, 29.10.2015,
08.12.2016 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

### 550. pants. Recusal or rejection of a bailiff

(1)	A bailiff is prohibited from performing enforcement actions in cases where one of the parties is the bailiff himself or herself, his or her spouse, including former spouse, a relative of his or hers or of his or her spouse in direct line in all degrees, in collateral line — up to the fourth degree and in affinity relations — up to the third degree, a person under the guardianship or curatorship of his or hers or of his or her spouse, or adoptive parents or adopted children of his or hers or of his or her spouse, as well as when there are other circumstances under the influence of which the bailiff justifiably cannot maintain objectivity and neutrality.

(2)	A rejection of a bailiff may be declared by the creditor or debtor by submitting a written application to him or her if there are circumstances that give rise to justified doubts about the bailiff's objectivity. The bailiff shall decide on the application immediately. A decision by which the application is left without satisfaction may be appealed to the district (city) court according to the bailiff's place of office. The filing of a complaint does not suspend enforcement actions.

(3)	An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding a court decision to refuse the rejection of a bailiff.

(4)	If a bailiff has recused himself or herself or has been rejected, he or she shall transfer the enforcement document for further execution to another bailiff in the procedure established by the Council of Sworn Bailiffs of Latvia.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 05.02.2009. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.03.2009.)

### 551. pants. Obligation of bailiff's demands or orders

(1)	A bailiff's demands and orders in executing court judgments and other decisions are obligatory for natural and legal persons throughout the entire territory of the state. State institutions shall provide information necessary for ensuring the execution of judgments and other decisions to a sworn bailiff free of charge.

(2)	If a bailiff's demands or orders are not executed, the bailiff shall draw up a report thereof and submit it to the court for it to decide the question of liability. The court may impose a fine on the guilty persons: on a natural person up to 360 euros, but on an official — up to 750 euros. An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding the court decision.

(3)	The court may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on a person (employer) who, pursuant to a court decision, was required to withhold maintenance for a child or parent and who has not notified the bailiff and the recipient of maintenance within the time period specified by law of the release of the maintenance payer from work, as well as of his or her new place of work or residence, if it is known to that person. An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding the court decision.

(4)	If resistance is shown in executing a judgment, the bailiff, in the presence of invited persons, but if it is not possible to invite persons — unilaterally, shall draw up a report thereof and, in order to remove obstacles, shall seek assistance from the police. The report shall be submitted to the court for it to decide the question of liability of those persons who resisted the execution of the judgment.

(5)	If the creditor or debtor refuses to sign a report drawn up by the bailiff, a note thereof shall be made in the drawn-up report, indicating the reasons for refusal. Refusal to sign a report drawn up by the bailiff does not affect the validity of the report.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003., 09.06.2011., 23.05.2013., 12.09.2013. un 09.06.2016.  
likumu, kas stājas spēkā 13.07.2016.)

### 552. pants. Debtor's obligations and consequences of their non-performance

(1)	The debtor shall appear before the bailiff upon summons and provide explanations regarding his or her financial situation and place of work, at the same time informing of amounts on which enforcement may not be levied (Section 596).

(2)	The debtor shall notify the bailiff of a change of place of work or declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration or place of residence during the execution of the decision, as well as of additional sources of income.

(3)	If the debtor does not appear before the bailiff upon summons, refuses to provide explanations or does not provide the information specified by law, the bailiff may apply to the court for it to decide the question of liability of that person. The court may adopt a decision on the compulsory bringing of the debtor, as well as impose a fine on him or her: on a natural person up to 80 euros, but on an official — up to 360 euros. An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding the court decision.

(4)	If it is established that the debtor has provided false information, the bailiff shall send a submission to the prosecutor.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012., 12.09.2013., 29.10.2015. un
09.06.2016. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 13.07.2016.)

69.	nodaļa
General provisions of enforcement proceedings

552.1 pants. Opening of an enforcement case

(1)	A bailiff shall open a separate enforcement case for each received enforcement document.

(2)	If an enforcement document is not executed in the procedure established by law or the documents necessary in accordance with international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia or European Union legal norms are not attached to it, the state fee or other expenses of execution of the judgment have not been paid, the bailiff shall set a time period for remedying the deficiencies, which may not be less than 10 days.

(3)	If the deficiencies are remedied within the set time period, an enforcement case shall be opened and the enforcement document shall be deemed submitted on the day when it was first submitted to the bailiff.

(4)	If the creditor does not remedy the deficiencies within the set time period, the enforcement document shall be deemed not submitted and shall be returned to the creditor.

(5)	The return of an enforcement document to the creditor is not an obstacle to its repeated submission to the bailiff, observing the procedure for submission of enforcement documents established by law.

(6)	If the bailiff establishes that insolvency proceedings have been declared for the debtor, or a sworn notary has accepted an application for the release of a natural person from debt obligations, which includes debt obligations for which the received enforcement document has been issued, an enforcement case shall not be opened and the enforcement document shall be returned to the submitter, except in cases where the enforcement document has been issued in claims the execution of which is not related to levying enforcement on the debtor's property or funds. An enforcement case shall also not be opened for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction or the transfer of movable property.

(7)	If the bailiff establishes that sanctions apply to the creditor in accordance with the International and National Sanctions Law of the Republic of Latvia (hereinafter — sanctions), including such sanctions established by a member state of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization that have been applied to the creditor, which, in accordance with the regulations of the Bank of Latvia, significantly affect the interests of financial market participants or the financial market, an enforcement case shall not be opened and the enforcement document shall be returned to the submitter, except in cases where the execution of a specific decision would not result in a violation, circumvention or evasion of the requirements established by sanctions for that person.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 30.09.2010., 18.04.2013., 30.10.2014., 11.11.2021.,
15.06.2021. un 16.03.2023. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 29.03.2023.)

### 553.pants. Clarification of an enforceable court decision

If an enforceable court decision is not clear, the bailiff is entitled to request the court that adopted the decision to clarify it. Clarification of a decision shall take place in the procedure established in Section 202 or 437 of this Law.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2003.)

### 554.pants

Postponement of execution of a judgment, division into instalments, amendment of its method and procedure of execution

(1)	If there are circumstances that make the execution of a court judgment difficult or make it impossible, the bailiff is entitled to submit to the court that rendered the judgment in the case a proposal for postponement of execution of the judgment, division into instalments, amendment of its method or procedure of execution.

(2)	The court shall examine the bailiff's application for postponement of execution of a judgment, division into instalments, amendment of its method or procedure of execution in the procedure established in Section 206 or 438 of this Law.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2003.)

### 555th Section. Notice of Obligation to Execute Decision

(1)	Upon commencing execution, the bailiff notifies the debtor, by sending or issuing a notice, of the obligation to execute the decision within 10 days. If the decision is to be executed immediately, the time limit for execution shall be set at no less than three days. In cases concerning the execution of confiscation of property and the execution of a decision on securing a claim or applying interim protection that does not impose a prohibition or obligation on the defendant to perform certain actions, a notice of the obligation to execute the decision shall not be sent.

(11) Upon commencing execution of the writ of execution referred to in point 17 of Section 540 of this law, except in cases where the writ of execution provides for the execution of a measure for securing a claim or interim protection, or execution of the writ of execution referred to in point
20 of Section 540 of this law, the bailiff, together with the notice, sends or issues the writ of execution to the debtor. If it is not evident from the documents submitted to the bailiff that the enforceable court decision, public act or settlement has been issued to the debtor, the enforceable court decision, public act or settlement shall also be attached to the writ of execution.

(2)	If the debtor is a natural person, the bailiff sends the notice to the debtor at the official electronic address, but if this is not possible, by registered mail to his or her last known place of residence or issues it to the debtor personally against signature. If the bailiff does not find the debtor at his or her place of residence, he or she issues the notice to one of the adult family members living together with the debtor.

(3)	If the debtor — a natural person — does not have an official electronic address and his or her place of residence is not known, the notice of the obligation to execute the decision shall be published in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(4)	If the debtor is a legal person, the bailiff sends the notice to the official electronic address, but if this is not possible, by registered mail to the debtor's legal address or issues it personally against signature to a representative of the debtor's executive body.

(5)	If the debtor or a representative of the debtor's executive body refuses to accept or sign the notice, the bailiff or the deliverer of the proposal shall draw up a record thereof. Refusal to accept or sign the notice shall not be an obstacle to the enforcement of the decision.

(6)	If the notice (in the case referred to in paragraph 1.1 of this Section — also the specified documents) has been delivered in the manner prescribed in this Section, it shall be deemed that the debtor has been notified of the decision and its execution time limit.

(7)	The bailiff may at any stage of the enforcement proceedings:

1)	request that the debtor declare his or her financial situation and changes therein during the last year, warning the debtor of criminal liability;

2)	attach the debtor's property, including attaching funds and deposits at a credit institution or with other payment service providers, funds due from other persons, or property held by other persons;

3)	submit a request for confirmation to the district (city) court for the entry of a recovery note in the land register or send an order to another public register for the entry of a prohibition on alienation or other actions.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003, 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 04.08.2011,
29.11.2012, 30.10.2014, 29.10.2015, 23.11.2016, 22.06.2017, 25.10.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which
enters into force on 07.07.2022. The new wording of the first sentence of paragraph 1.1 enters into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision
point 177)

Section 555.1 Sending of Documents

Documents drawn up by the bailiff and other documents related to the execution of the decision provided for in this law shall be sent electronically to the addressee's official electronic address or to the electronic mail address indicated by the addressee, if he or she has notified the bailiff that he or she agrees to use electronic mail for communication with the bailiff. If it is not possible to send documents electronically, they shall be sent by ordinary mail, but the documents to be sent specified in the fourth paragraph of Section 581, the first paragraph of Section 583.1, the third paragraph of Section 584, the first and third paragraphs of Section 600, the second paragraph of Section 604, the fifth paragraph of Section 606, the first and third paragraphs of Section 618.2, the first paragraph of Section 618.6 and the fourth paragraph of Section 644.33 of this law — by registered mail. If it is not possible to send electronically the notice specified in point 1 of the first paragraph of Section 620.14 and point 1 of the first paragraph of Section 620.28 of this law, it shall be issued to the creditor against signature or sent by registered mail, or forwarded through the Ministry of Justice.
(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### Section 556. Enforcement of Court Judgment

(Deleted by the law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

### Section 557. Means of Enforcement

Means of enforcement are:

1)	recovery against the debtor's movable property, including property held by other persons, and intangible things, by selling them;

2)	recovery against money due to the debtor from other persons (wages, payments equivalent thereto, other income of the debtor, deposits at credit institutions or with other payment service providers);

3)	recovery against the debtor's immovable property, by selling it;

31) recovery against the debtor's building rights, by selling them;

4)	transfer of property awarded by the court to the creditor and performance of actions imposed by the court judgment;

5)	eviction of persons and property specified in the judgment from premises;

6)	introduction into possession;

61) return of a child to the country where he or she has his or her place of residence;

7)	other means specified in the judgment.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011, 23.11.2016 and 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### Section 558. Inspection of Debtor's Premises

(1)	The bailiff is entitled, if necessary for making recovery, to carry out an inspection of the debtor's premises and his or her storage facilities. If the debtor does not participate in the inspection of premises and storage facilities, it shall be carried out in the presence of invited persons.

(2)	If the debtor refuses to admit the bailiff to premises which he or she occupies, or to the location of property, or refuses to open storage facilities, the bailiff shall invite a police representative, in whose presence the premises or storage facilities shall be opened and their inspection carried out.

(3)	If the manager of immovable property belonging to the debtor evades or refuses to admit the bailiff to the immovable property during enforcement of the decision and the manager has been notified in writing of the time of inspection of the immovable property at least five days in advance, the bailiff may carry out the inspection of the immovable property in the presence of a police representative without the participation of the manager.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002 and 19.06.2003, which enters into force on 24.07.2003.)

### 559. pants. Postponement of enforcement actions

(1)	A bailiff postpones enforcement action on the basis of an application by the creditor or a decision of a court or judge on the postponement of enforcement action or the suspension of the sale of property, adopted in accordance with point 7 of the first paragraph of Article 138 or point 4 of the first paragraph of Article 138.1 of this Law, or a court decision on the postponement of the execution of a judgment or its division into instalments, adopted in accordance with Articles 206, 438, 644.1, 620.16 of this Law.

(2)	A bailiff postpones enforcement action on the basis of a court decision on the replacement of the execution of a decision of a foreign court or competent authority with the measures provided for in Article 138 of this Law to secure the execution of that decision (Article 644.2).

(21) A bailiff postpones the enforcement of recovery on property which has been placed under arrest in criminal proceedings and for the realisation of which the person directing the proceedings has not given permission, until the lifting of the arrest of the property in the criminal proceedings or the receipt of permission from the person directing the proceedings.

(3)	A bailiff notifies the creditor and the debtor of the postponement of enforcement action if it is not possible to carry it out due to technical or other reasons beyond the bailiff's control.

(4)	If, within 30 days from the date of dispatch of the documents referred to in paragraph 1.1 of Article 555 of this Law, the bailiff receives a request from the debtor to send a translation of the enforceable court decision, public instrument or settlement, the bailiff, having established the circumstances referred to in the legal norms of the European Union which provide for the debtor's right to request a translation of the documents to be issued, postpones enforcement action until the translation is sent to the debtor.
(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the Laws of 19.06.2003, 07.09.2006, 05.02.2009, 04.08.2011, 30.10.2014, 29.10.2015 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022. The amendment in the first paragraph regarding the deletion of the numbers and words "620.22 or 620.29" enters into force on 01.08.2022. See point 177 of the transitional provisions)

### 560. pants. Obligation of a bailiff to suspend enforcement proceedings

(1)	A bailiff suspends enforcement proceedings if:

1)	a natural person who is a debtor or creditor has died or a legal person who is a debtor or creditor has ceased to exist and the legal relationship established by the court allows for succession of rights;

2)	the debtor's legal capacity has been restricted by a court judgment to the extent to which enforcement proceedings are taking place;

3)	the Supreme Court has adopted a decision in a procedural hearing to suspend the execution of the judgment;

4)	the execution of a decision of an institution or official is to be suspended in accordance with law or a court decision;

5)	a court or judge has adopted a decision to suspend the compulsory execution of an obligation (Articles 406 and 406.10);

6)	a court has adopted a decision to suspend the execution of a decision of a foreign court or competent authority (Article 644.2);

7)	legal protection proceedings have been initiated against the debtor or a decision has been adopted on the implementation of legal protection proceedings in the case of out-of-court legal protection proceedings;

71) a court has declared legal protection proceedings and approved a plan of legal protection measures, if the consequences provided for in points 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 of the first paragraph of Article 37 of the Insolvency Law have previously been revoked or have lapsed by operation of law;

8)	insolvency proceedings of a natural person have been declared against the debtor;

9)	in a case concerning the return of a child to the country of his or her residence or in a case arising from custody rights, it is not possible for the orphan's court to ascertain the child's daily routine or it is not possible to meet the child;

10)	a certificate of non-compliance with a decision in a case arising from contact rights has been sent to the orphan's court;

11)	a notification has been received from a sworn notary of the acceptance of an application for the release of a natural person from debt obligations, which includes debt obligations for the recovery of which an enforcement case has been entered;

12)	sanctions apply to the creditor, the restrictions imposed by which are incompatible with the execution of the decision in question.

(2)	If a decision on the privatisation of an enterprise or a commercial company has been adopted in the manner prescribed by law, enforcement proceedings shall be suspended at the request of the institution carrying out the privatisation, except for enforcement proceedings for compensation for damage in connection with an accident at work or an occupational disease.

(21)	If a debtor whose debt is being recovered on the basis of a uniform instrument allowing execution in the requested Member State has contested or appealed the claim in the applicant Member State or has lodged a complaint concerning enforcement actions carried out in the applicant Member State and a complaint examination procedure has been initiated in an institution of the Member State, enforcement proceedings shall be suspended at the request of the State Revenue Service in respect of the contested or appealed part of the claim and in accordance with the request of the institution of the Member State which has requested mutual assistance in the recovery of claims.

(22)	If a debtor whose debt is being recovered on the basis of a decision of a competent authority of a Member State of the European Union or a State of the European Economic Area on the imposition of an administrative fine in connection with infringements in the field of posting of workers has contested or appealed the decision in the applicant Member State, enforcement proceedings shall be suspended at the request of the State Labour Inspectorate in respect of the contested or appealed part of the decision and in accordance with the notification of the applicant Member State.

(3)	In the cases referred to in points 7 and 7.1 of the first paragraph of this Article, the bailiff shall deduct the costs of execution of the judgment from the amount of money recovered and satisfy the creditor's claim in the manner prescribed by this Law. If a plan of legal protection measures has been approved, the bailiff shall deduct the costs of execution of the judgment from the amount of money recovered and satisfy the creditor's claim in the amount and manner specified in the plan of legal protection measures.

(4)	In the case referred to in point 8 of the first paragraph of this Article, the bailiff shall complete the sale of property that has been initiated if it has already been announced or the property has been handed over to a trading company for sale, except in cases where the sale of housing is provided for in the plan for the sale of property of a natural person to be postponed in accordance with Article 148 of the Insolvency Law. From the money received from the sale, the bailiff shall deduct the costs of execution of the judgment, but shall transfer the remaining money to the administrator for the satisfaction of creditors' claims in accordance with the procedure laid down in the Insolvency Law, respecting the rights of the secured creditor.

(5)	The provisions of point 8 of the first paragraph of this Article do not apply to enforcement cases concerning claims the execution of which is not connected with the enforcement of recovery on the debtor's property or funds. A bailiff shall also suspend enforcement proceedings if an enforcement document has been issued in claims the execution of which is connected with the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction or the transfer of movable property.

(6)	The application of sanctions to a debtor is not a ground for suspending enforcement proceedings, but until the sanctions are revoked, the enforcement measures applied to the debtor's property shall not be revoked and funds shall not be paid to the debtor if such are due to him or her in the case.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002, 07.09.2006, 05.02.2009, 11.06.2009, 30.09.2010, 04.08.2011,
15.03.2012, 29.11.2012, 18.04.2013, 30.10.2014, 29.10.2015, 04.02.2016, 11.11.2021, 15.06.2021 and
16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. See point 179 of the transitional provisions)

### 561. pants. Right of a bailiff to suspend enforcement proceedings

A bailiff may suspend enforcement proceedings if:

1)	the debtor is in a medical institution and this hinders the performance of enforcement actions;

2)	a complaint has been submitted concerning the actions of the bailiff;

3)	(deleted by the Law of 31.10.2002);

4)	(deleted by the Law of 14.12.2006).
(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002, 19.06.2003 and 14.12.2006, which enters into force on 01.03.2007.)

### 562. Section. Terms for Suspension of Enforcement Proceedings

(1)	Enforcement proceedings shall be suspended:

1)	in the cases provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 1 of this Law — until the determination of the successor in title of the debtor or creditor;

2)	in the cases provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 2 of this Law — until the appointment of a guardian;

3)	in the cases provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clauses 3, 5 and 6 of this Law — until the time specified in the court decision, or until the revocation of this decision;

4)	(deleted by the Law of 19.06.2003);

5)	in the cases provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 4 of this Law — until the time when the suspension ceases in accordance with law, or the time specified in the court ruling, or until the revocation of this ruling;

6)	in the case provided for in Section 560, Paragraph two of this Law — until the determination of the successor in title of the debtor and the transfer of the enterprise to him or her or the making of amendments to the founding documents of the company in the Enterprise Register;

7)	in the case provided for in Section 561, Clause 1 of this Law — until the moment when the circumstances mentioned in this clause have ceased;

8)	in the cases provided for in Section 561, Clause 2 of this Law — until the moment when a court judgment or decision in connection with a complaint enters into legal force;

9)	(deleted by the Law of 19.06.2003);

10)	in the cases provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 7 of this Law — until the moment when one of the following circumstances has occurred:

a)	the legal protection process has been terminated in respect of the debtor,

b)	the implementation of the legal protection process has been declared in respect of the debtor and the judgment on the implementation of the legal protection process does not specify that the debtor's property serving as security (pledged) is included in the legal protection process action plan and restrictions apply to it, according to which secured creditors may not exercise their rights to this property,

c)	the court has given permission to sell the pledged property of the debtor in the case referred to in Section 341.5, Paragraph two, Clause 2 of this Law;

d)	the consequences provided for in Section 37, Paragraph one, Clauses 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 of the Insolvency Law have been revoked by a court decision or have ceased to be effective on the basis of law in accordance with the information provided by the legal protection process supervisor and a legal protection process action plan has not been submitted to the court;

101)	in the cases provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 7.1 of this Law — until the moment when one of the following circumstances has occurred:

a)	the legal protection process has been terminated in respect of the debtor,

b)	the implementation of the legal protection process has been declared in respect of the debtor and the judgment on the implementation of the legal protection process does not specify that the debtor's property serving as security (pledged) is included in the legal protection process action plan and restrictions apply to it, according to which secured creditors may not exercise their rights to this property;

11)	in the case provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 8 of this Law — until the court ruling on the termination of bankruptcy proceedings or until the end of the term specified in Section 165.1, Paragraph one of the Insolvency Law, if the debtor's discharge from obligations has not been revoked, or until the moment when the debtor's discharge from obligations is revoked. Enforcement proceedings shall be resumed in the amount of the remaining debt;

12)	in the case provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 9 of this Law — until the determination of the child's whereabouts;

13)	in the case provided for in Section 560, Paragraph 2.1 of this Law — until the moment when a notification is received from the State Revenue Service that, in accordance with the information provided by the authority of the Member State that has requested mutual assistance in the recovery of claims, the decision on the contestation of the claim or enforcement adopted in the complaint examination procedure has become enforceable;

14)	in the case referred to in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 10 of this Law — until the moment when an orphan's court decision has entered into force or an orphan's court assessment has been received;

15)	in the case provided for in Section 560, Paragraph 2.2 of this Law — until the moment when a notification is received from the State Labour Inspectorate that, in accordance with the information provided by the requesting Member State, the decision on the contestation or appeal of the decision adopted in the complaint examination procedure has become enforceable;

16)	in the cases provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 11 of this Law — until the day when:

a)	an entry has been made in the insolvency register regarding the result of the examination of the application for the discharge of a natural person from debt obligations and the natural person has not been discharged from debt obligations,

b)	the term for submitting an application for the revocation of the discharge of a natural person from debt obligations has expired, if an entry has been made in the insolvency register regarding the discharge of a natural person from debt obligations,

c)	a court judgment revoking the discharge of a natural person from debt obligations has entered into force;

17)	in the case provided for in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clause 12 of this Law — until the revocation of the sanctions applicable to the creditor.

(2)	During the time when enforcement proceedings are suspended, the bailiff shall not perform enforcement actions. The bailiff shall revoke the operation of the issued order for the duration of the suspension of enforcement proceedings, retaining the registered prohibition and recovery notes.

(21)	In the cases referred to in Section 560, Paragraph one, Clauses 7 and 8 of this Law, the bailiff shall notify the custodian of the property of the obligation to hand over to the legal protection process supervisor or administrator the property the sale of which has not been commenced. The registered prohibition and recovery notes shall be deleted if:

1)	a legal protection process action plan has been submitted to the bailiff, which provides for action with respect to the property belonging to the debtor to which the bailiff has applied enforcement measures;

2)	an application from the administrator has been submitted regarding the necessity of the property within the framework of bankruptcy proceedings.

(3)	Enforcement proceedings shall be resumed upon the creditor's application or on the bailiff's initiative.

(4)	In the cases referred to in Paragraph one, Clause 10, sub-clauses "b" and "c" of this Section and in Paragraph one, Clause 10.1, sub-clause "b" of this Section, in the resumed enforcement proceedings the bailiff shall perform only the sale of the pledged property.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003., 07.09.2006., 14.12.2006., 11.06.2009., 30.09.2010.,
04.08.2011., 15.03.2012., 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015., 04.02.2016., 01.10.2020., 11.11.2021., 15.06.2021. and
16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision Clause 179)
