### 563. Section. Termination of enforcement proceedings

(1) Enforcement proceedings shall be terminated at the request of an interested person if:

1) the creditor has waived the claim and the court has adopted a respective decision thereon;

2) a settlement between the creditor and the debtor approved by the court has been submitted;

3) the claim or obligation cannot pass to a successor in law upon the death of the natural person or termination of the legal person who was the creditor or debtor;

4) the limitation period provided for by law for this type of claim has expired;

5) the court judgment or the decision of the relevant institution or official on the basis of which the enforcement document was issued has been revoked;

6) the time limit for submitting an appeal, cassation appeal or ancillary complaint regarding the court judgment on the basis of which the enforcement document was issued has been restored;

7) enforcement of a foreign court or competent authority decision has been refused (Section 644.3);

8) the foreign court or competent authority revokes the issued European Union enforcement document;

9) a court judgment has been adopted on the termination of legal protection proceedings in connection with the performance of the legal protection proceedings plan;

91) enforcement of a decision on the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence has been refused;

92) (deleted by the law of 16.06.2022);

10) a court judgment has been adopted on the termination of the natural person's debt discharge procedure, releasing the natural person from its debt obligations and the time limit provided for in the first paragraph of Section 165.1 of the Insolvency Law has expired, and the debtor's release from obligations has not been revoked, or a court judgment has been adopted on the termination of bankruptcy proceedings if creditors' claims have not been submitted in the procedure provided for by the Insolvency Law, simultaneously terminating the natural person's insolvency proceedings;

11) the foreign authority revokes the request for assistance regarding the recovery of tax, duty, costs related to recovery or other mandatory payments;

12) a notification has been received from the State Labour Inspectorate that, in accordance with information provided by the requesting Member State, the decision of the competent authority of a European Union Member State or European Economic Area State on the imposition of an administrative fine related to violations in the field of posting of workers has been revoked;

13) (deleted by the law of 16.06.2022);

14) an entry has been made in the insolvency register regarding the results of examination of the application for the release of a natural person from debt obligations, the natural person has been released from debt obligations and the specified time limit for submitting an application for the revocation of the release of a natural person from debt obligations has expired.

(2) Enforcement proceedings for the recovery of an adjudged sum of money from legal persons, partnerships, individual merchants, persons registered abroad who carry out permanent economic activity in Latvia, and agricultural product producers shall be terminated at the request of the administrator if insolvency has been declared for the debtor in the procedure provided for by law. In this case, the bailiff shall complete the commenced sale of property if it has already been announced or the property has been handed over to a trading company for sale, unless the administrator has requested the cancellation of the announced auction in order to ensure the sale of property as part of the estate. From the money received from the sale, the bailiff shall withhold the costs of enforcement of the judgment, but shall transfer the remaining money to the administrator for the satisfaction of creditors' claims in accordance with the procedure provided for by the Insolvency Law, observing the rights of the secured creditor. The bailiff shall notify the custodian of the property of the obligation to hand over to the administrator the property the sale of which has not been commenced.

(3) In the cases provided for in points 3 and 4 of the first paragraph of this Section, the bailiff may also terminate enforcement proceedings on his or her own initiative.

(31) In the cases provided for in point 10 of the first paragraph of this Section, enforcement proceedings shall not be terminated for:

1) recovery of maintenance;

2) claims arising from unlawful acts;

3) claims for penalties provided for in the Criminal Law and in regulatory enactments that provide for administrative violations;

4) claims for compensation for harm caused by a criminal offence or administrative violation;

5) claims arising from the violations referred to in Chapters IV and V of the Commercial Activity Support Control Law, in cases where the creditor, following a request by the bailiff, has provided information that the enforcement proceedings are to be resumed.

(32) If, in the case referred to in point 3 of the first paragraph of this Section, the legal person who is the debtor in the enforcement case has been liquidated, the bailiff shall continue enforcement proceedings in the part concerning the enforcement of the claim against the debtor's property. The recovered amounts remaining after satisfaction of the creditor's claim shall be credited to the state budget.

(4) If enforcement proceedings are terminated, after covering the costs of enforcement of the judgment, all compulsory enforcement measures adopted by the bailiff shall be revoked.

(5) Terminated enforcement proceedings cannot be commenced anew.

(6) If a foreign court or competent authority corrects a European Enforcement Order issued on the basis of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council, enforcement of the decision in the revoked part shall be terminated and enforcement shall be continued in accordance with the corrected European Enforcement Order.

(7) If a court, foreign court or competent authority amends a European Account Preservation Order on the basis of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, enforcement of the decision in the revoked part shall be terminated and enforcement shall be continued in accordance with the amended European Account Preservation Order.

(8) If a foreign court amends a certificate issued in accordance with Article 47 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111, enforcement of the decision in the revoked part shall be terminated and enforcement shall be continued in accordance with the certificate issued by the foreign court in accordance with Article 49 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.

(As amended by the laws of 31.10.2002., 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009., 30.09.2010., 04.08.2011., 15.03.2012.,
29.11.2012., 12.02.2015., 29.10.2015., 04.02.2016., 08.12.2016., 28.02.2019., 11.11.2021., 15.06.2021., 16.06.2022.
and 16.03.2023. law, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

### 564. Section

Procedure for postponement of enforcement actions, suspension, resumption or termination of enforcement proceedings

(1) The decision on postponement of enforcement actions, suspension, resumption or termination of enforcement proceedings shall be made by the bailiff in whose proceedings the enforcement document is located.

(2) The bailiff shall adopt the decision before the action to be postponed or enforced, but not later than within three days from the day of receipt of the application.

(3) The bailiff shall notify the creditor, the debtor and the relevant third person who has submitted the request of the decision within three days after adoption of the decision.

(As worded by the law of 19.06.2003., which enters into force on 24.07.2003.)

### 565. Section. Return of the enforcement document to the creditor

(1)	An enforcement document under which enforcement has not been carried out or has been carried out incompletely shall be returned to the creditor:

1)	upon application of the creditor;  

2)	if the debtor has no property or income against which enforcement can be directed;  

3)	if the creditor has refused to receive the items seized from the debtor that are specified in the court judgment;  

4)	if the debtor does not live or work at the address indicated by the creditor or his or her property is not located there;  

5)	if the creditor, who has not been exempted from payment of the costs of enforcement of the judgment, has not paid them;  

6)	if it is not possible to enforce the judgment by applying the means of enforcement indicated by the creditor and the creditor has not notified of the application of another means of enforcement within 10 days of the issuance of the summons;  

7)	if in a case concerning the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence or in a case arising from custody or access rights, the bailiff establishes that the child's whereabouts are outside the territory of operation of the regional court to which this bailiff is attached, or abroad;  

8)	if in a case concerning the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence, the creditor, following a summons from the bailiff, the Ministry of Justice or the orphan's court, has twice failed to indicate the time and place when and where the child is to be delivered to him or her, or the time and place (as close as possible to the child's whereabouts) when and where he or she will meet with the child in order to restore the bond between the creditor and the child;  

9)	if in an enforcement case arising from custody and access rights, the creditor repeatedly fails to appear at the time set by the bailiff to receive or meet with the child;  

10)	if the debtor's custody rights have been terminated in connection with non-compliance with the decision in a case arising from custody or access rights;  

11)	if the bailiff establishes in accordance with Section 620.27 of this Law that enforcement of the decision is not possible.  

12)	if the debtor has died and within one year from the suspension of enforcement proceedings no succession case has been initiated in respect of his or her estate.  

(2)	In the cases referred to in points 2, 3 and 4 of paragraph one of this Section, the bailiff shall draw up a relevant act.  

(21)	If in an enforcement case concerning the recovery of periodic payments the debt and the costs of enforcement of the judgment are fully covered, the enforcement document shall be issued to the creditor.  

(22)	If in an enforcement case arising from access rights the bailiff has established that the court decision is being complied with and the costs of enforcement of the judgment have been covered, the enforcement document shall be issued to the creditor.  

(3)	An enforcement document shall be issued to the creditor if the costs of enforcement of the judgment have been covered, except in cases where the costs of enforcement of the judgment are paid by the creditor in accordance with the provisions of this Law. When issuing the enforcement document

to the creditor, the bailiff shall revoke all means of enforcement that have been adopted.  

(4)	The return of an enforcement document to the creditor shall not be an obstacle to the resubmission of this document for enforcement within the time limit prescribed by law.  

(5)	An enforcement document under which enforcement is to be made into State revenue shall be issued by the bailiff to the State Revenue Service.  

(6)	(Deleted by the Law of 05.02.2009.)

(7)	A writ of execution shall not be issued to the creditor, but a note shall be appended to it concerning the reason for the completion of the enforcement case and the amount recovered. The notes made by the bailiff are an integral part of the writ of execution.  
(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003., 17.06.2004., 05.02.2009., 04.08.2011., 29.10.2015.,
25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 566. Section. Costs of enforcement of the judgment

(1)	The costs of enforcement of the judgment include the State fee and the costs associated with the enforcement of the court judgment (Section 39): the bailiff's remuneration in the amount of the tariff and the costs necessary for carrying out enforcement actions. They are:

1)	costs associated with the delivery and issuance of summonses and other documents;  

2)	costs in connection with the receipt of information necessary in the enforcement case;  

3)	costs in connection with the services of banks and other institutions;  

4)	costs in connection with the storage, transportation or destruction of the debtor's property;  

5)	travel costs to reach the place of enforcement of the judgment;  

6)	payment to an expert;  

7)	costs for organising an auction on an electronic auction site;  

71) costs associated with the examination of the case that have arisen in connection with the submission to the court of the bailiff's application for the registration of immovable property in the name of the acquirer;  

8)	other costs necessary for carrying out enforcement actions.  

(2)	(Deleted from 01.01.2012. by the Law of 31.10.2002.)

(3)	When determining the costs associated with securing a claim or interim protection, the provisions on the costs of enforcement of the judgment shall apply insofar as these actions have been carried out by the bailiff.  
(In the wording of the Law of 20.06.2001. with amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 20.12.2010., 04.08.2011., 25.03.2021. and
11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 567. pants. Procedure for Payment of Judgment Enforcement Costs in Enforcement Proceedings

(1)	When submitting an enforcement document for execution, the creditor shall indicate the means of compulsory enforcement, observing the provisions of Sections 570 and 572 of this Law, pay the state fee and cover other judgment enforcement costs in the amount necessary to commence enforcement in the manner indicated by the creditor. During judgment enforcement, the creditor shall pay in additional judgment enforcement costs as necessary upon instruction of the bailiff. In cases specified by law, during judgment enforcement the judgment enforcement costs for individual procedural actions shall be paid by the debtor.

(11) A creditor — natural person — in a claim for recovery of compensation for harm in a criminal case is released from the obligation to indicate the means of compulsory enforcement. The applicable means of compulsory enforcement, observing the provisions of Section 570 of this Law, shall be determined by the bailiff.

(2)	The following creditors are released from payment of judgment enforcement costs to the bailiff:

1)	in claims for recovery of wages and other claims of employees and persons in service that arise from or are related to employment or service legal relations;

2)	in claims arising from personal injuries that have caused mutilation or other health damage or resulted in death of a person;

21) in cases where recovery is made in favour of an injured party — natural person — in connection with a satisfied claim for compensation for harm in a criminal case;

3)	in claims for recovery of maintenance for a child or parent;

4)	in cases where recovery is made into state revenues;

5)	in cases where a person has been released from payment of court costs by a court decision — in full or in part in accordance with the court decision;

6)	in cases where recovery is made in accordance with a uniform instrument permitting enforcement in the requested Member State, except in cases where the State Revenue Service has agreed with the authority of the Member State that has requested mutual assistance in the recovery of claims on a special procedure for reimbursement of enforcement costs;

7)	who are whistleblowers and their relatives or related persons in claims brought with such status, including in applications for securing a claim or interim protection.

(3)	In cases where the creditor is released from payment of judgment enforcement costs, compensation shall be paid to the sworn bailiff from state budget funds to cover costs related to the performance of enforcement actions.

(4)	The amount of costs necessary for the performance of enforcement actions and the procedure for their payment, as well as the procedure for determining and paying compensation in cases where the creditor is released from payment of judgment enforcement costs, shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(41) If, when recovering compensation for harm in the case referred to in point 2.1 of the second paragraph of this Section, the amount recovered from the debtor is insufficient to cover the judgment enforcement costs in full, the remuneration in the amount of the fee and the costs necessary for the performance of enforcement actions in the uncovered part shall be covered to the bailiff from state budget funds in the procedure determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(5)	(Deleted as of 01.03.2016. by the law of 04.02.2016. See point 113 of Transitional Provisions)

(6)	The bailiff may submit to the State Revenue Service a request for judgment enforcement costs necessary for the performance of enforcement and request that it agree with the authority of the respective Member State that has requested mutual assistance in the recovery of claims on a special procedure for reimbursement of costs if it establishes at least one of the following cases:

1)	judgment enforcement costs in a very large amount are necessary for the recovery of a tax claim;

2)	recovery is directed at property of a member of an organised group that has been confiscated by a judgment in a criminal case (Article 20 of Council Directive 2010/24/EU).
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003., 26.10.2006., 05.02.2009., 09.06.2011.,
15.03.2012., 19.12.2013., 04.02.2016., 22.06.2017., 25.03.2021.	and 16.03.2023.  which  enters  into  force
29.03.2023.)

### 568. pants. Recovery of Judgment Enforcement Costs

(1)	Judgment enforcement takes place at the debtor's expense. After an enforcement document has been submitted for execution, voluntary enforcement of the judgment or enforcement of the judgment directly to the creditor does not release the debtor from reimbursement of judgment enforcement costs.

(11)	If an enforcement document is issued to the creditor in accordance with points 1, 3, 6, 8, 9 or
12 of the first paragraph of Section 565 of this Law or after the opening of an enforcement case the bailiff establishes that the debtor has fulfilled its obligations before submission of the enforcement document, the judgment enforcement costs shall be covered by the creditor. This provision also applies to the cases referred to in points 1, 2, 2.1, 3 and 5 of the second paragraph of Section 567 of this

Law.

(12)	If enforcement proceedings are to be terminated, except in the cases specified in points 4 and 11 of the first paragraph of Section 563 of this Law, as well as in cases where an enforcement document is issued to the creditor on the basis of point 2 or 7 of the first paragraph of Section 565 of this Law, the judgment enforcement costs, insofar as they have not been recovered from the debtor, shall be covered by the creditor if it has not been released from their payment to the bailiff in accordance with this Law.

(13)	If enforcement proceedings have been terminated in accordance with point 14 of the first paragraph of Section 563 of this Law, the judgment enforcement costs, insofar as they have not been recovered from the debtor, shall be covered by the creditor if it has not been released from payment of judgment enforcement costs to the bailiff in accordance with this Law.

(2)	The bailiff shall prepare a calculation of judgment enforcement costs and send it to the debtor and the creditor. The calculation may be appealed in the procedure specified in Section 632 of this Law.

(3)	The calculation shall indicate the extent to which judgment enforcement costs are to be reimbursed to the bailiff (remuneration), to the creditor (the state fee paid by it and other judgment enforcement costs) or credited to state revenues.

(4)	If it is not possible to recover judgment enforcement costs from the debtor or in the cases referred to in paragraphs 1.1, 1.2 and six of this Section they have not been covered by the creditor, the bailiff shall issue an invoice on the basis of the prepared calculation and submit it for compulsory enforcement.

(5)	An invoice shall be submitted for compulsory enforcement after the time limit for appealing the calculation of judgment enforcement costs prepared by the bailiff has expired, but if it has been appealed — after the court decision has entered into legal force.

(6)	Costs related to a court decision on securing a claim, establishing an interim protection measure or executing a European account preservation order shall be covered by the claimant.

(61) If enforcement proceedings have been terminated in accordance with point 4 of the first paragraph of Section 563 of this Law and judgment enforcement costs have not been recovered from the debtor, enforcement proceedings shall be terminated in the part concerning execution of the decision, but continued in the part concerning recovery of judgment enforcement costs.

(7)	If enforcement proceedings have been terminated in accordance with point 11 of the first paragraph of Section 563 of this Law and the reason for withdrawal of the request for assistance is cancellation of the claim to be recovered or the document issued for its execution, the bailiff shall submit to the State Revenue Service a calculation of enforcement costs and request that it agree with the authority of the Member State that has requested mutual assistance in the recovery of claims on reimbursement of enforcement costs.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 15.03.2012., 08.12.2016., 25.03.2021. and
15.06.2021. which enters into force 01.01.2022.)

### 569th Article. Search for Debtor or Child

(1)	If the debtor's whereabouts are unknown, the judge, at the request of the interested party, shall adopt a decision on the search for the debtor with the assistance of the police in the following cases:

1)	regarding the recovery of maintenance for a child or parent;  

2)	regarding claims for personal injury resulting in mutilation or other health damage or the death of a person;  

3)	regarding recovery into state revenues.  

(11)	If the whereabouts of the child or the debtor and child are unknown, the judge, at the request of the bailiff, shall adopt a decision on the search for the said persons with the assistance of the police in the following cases:

1)	in cases concerning the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence;  

2)	when a European Union enforceable instrument has been received for the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence;  

3)	in cases arising from custody rights.  

(2)	Upon application by the police institution, the court shall adopt a decision on the recovery of search costs from the debtor.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 09.06.2011., 04.08.2011., 29.10.2015. and 16.06.2022., which enter into force on 07.07.2022.)

Chapter 70
General Provisions on Recovery

### 570th Article. Enforcement Against the Property of a Natural Person

(1)	Enforcement shall be directed against the property of a natural person, including this person's share in co-ownership and in the joint property of spouses, as well as in cases provided by law — against the community of property of spouses.  

(2)	Enforcement against the debtor's property shall not be directed if the debtor works or receives a pension or scholarship and the amount of enforcement does not exceed the portion of monthly income against which enforcement may be directed by law.  

(3)	Enforcement against the debtor's immovable property is permissible if, by applying other enforcement measures, it is not possible to satisfy the creditor's claim within a reasonable time. This procedure does not apply to the recovery of debts secured by pledging the respective immovable property.  
(With amendments made by the law of 22.05.2014., which enters into force on 05.06.2014.)

### 571st Article. Property Against Which Enforcement May Not Be Directed

When executing judgments, enforcement may not be directed against the property referred to in Annex 1 of this law, except for the recovery of debts secured by pledging the respective items.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 572nd Article. Enforcement Against a Legal Person

(1)	Pursuant to enforcement documents, the bailiff shall first direct enforcement against the legal person's monetary funds held at credit institutions or with other payment service providers.  

(2)	If, by directing enforcement against the legal person's monetary funds at credit institutions or with other payment service providers, the creditor's claim is not satisfied, enforcement shall be directed against the legal person's property.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the law of 23.11.2016., which enters into force on 01.01.2017.  
Amendments to the article enter into force on 01.07.2017. See transitional provision point 120)

Article 572.1 Enforcement in Favour of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration

(1)	If the creditor has expressed a corresponding request, as well as a request to apply all the enforcement measures specified in points 1, 2 and 3 of Article 557 of this law, and if the debtor has not paid the amount specified in the notice into the bailiff's deposit account within the time limit set in the notice of the obligation to execute the decision, the bailiff shall notify the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration that the decision on the recovery of maintenance or the notarial deed containing an agreement on periodic maintenance payments and enforceable in the manner of execution of court judgments is not being fulfilled.  

(2)	If the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration, on the basis of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Law, has been substituted for the creditor in a maintenance recovery case in the part concerning the recovery from the debtor of maintenance paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund, it shall have all the rights and obligations of the creditor provided for in this law.  

(3)	The enforcement order of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration for the recovery from the applicant of the amount of maintenance paid without justification shall not be returned to the creditor. If the bailiff, at the request of the creditor, has provided the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration with the information specified in the first paragraph of this article, the enforcement document shall be issued to the creditor only after a confirmation of the non-existence of the claim has been received from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration.  
(In the wording of the law of 05.02.2009. with amendments made by the laws of 12.06.2009., 19.12.2013. and 08.12.2016., which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The new wording of the first and third paragraphs on enforcement in favour of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration enters into force on 01.02.2017. and applies to enforcement cases instituted as of 01.02.2017. See transitional provision point 123)

Article 572.2 Rights and Obligations of the State Revenue Service in Enforcement Cases Concerning the Execution of Confiscation of Property

In enforcement cases concerning the execution of confiscation of property, the State Revenue Service shall have all the rights and obligations of the creditor provided for in this law.  
(In the wording of the law of 22.06.2017., which enters into force on 01.08.2017.)

(1)	Seizure of the debtor's movable property is expressed in the description, photographic recording and safeguarding of this property, insofar as a different procedure for seizure is not provided for individual items in this chapter.  

(2)	(Deleted by the law of 05.02.2009.)

### 574. Section. General provisions for seizure of debtor's movable property

(1) The bailiff shall seize the debtor's movable property in such quantity as is necessary to satisfy the amount to be recovered and to cover the costs of enforcement of the judgment. The bailiff shall not seize accessories of principal things separately from the principal thing.

(2) The bailiff may seize the debtor's movable property whose value exceeds the amount awarded to the creditor and the costs of enforcement of the judgment, if the debtor has no other property subject to seizure or the value of such property does not cover the amount to be recovered and the costs of enforcement of the judgment.

(3) After seizure of movable property, the bailiff shall request information from movable property registers regarding ownership of such things by the debtor, and shall also ascertain in the commercial pledge register whether the movable property belonging to the debtor has been pledged. If the bailiff establishes that the seized property belongs to third parties, he or she shall immediately release it from seizure. If a commercial pledge in favour of third parties is registered in the commercial pledge register on the debtor's movable property, the bailiff shall request that the debtor and the pledgee notify of the remaining amount of the debt.

(4) The bailiff may enforce against movable things pledged as a commercial pledge or possessory pledge to secure claims of third parties with the consent of the respective pledgee, and may also enforce against the surplus of money in the event of sale of the pledge. If the pledgee does not consent to the sale and himself or herself delays selling the pledged thing without justifiable reason, the bailiff shall explain to the creditor that he or she may request the court to set a time for sale of the pledged things in order to be able to enforce against the surplus of money, and shall also explain the right to establish a commercial pledge.

(5) If the bailiff establishes that the movable property has already been seized for another enforcement, he or she shall compare the property with the property inventory act drawn up in the previous seizure and shall seize only those items which are not entered in the earlier inventory act, but if he or she has already carried out the seizure — shall immediately release the items seized for the second time from seizure.

(6) If the debtor is absent or evades enforcement of the judgment, the movable property shall be seized by the bailiff with the participation of a representative of the municipality or the police.

(7) During seizure of the debtor's movable property, the debtor and the creditor have the right to invite no more than two witnesses. Non-appearance of witnesses shall not suspend the seizure of property.

(8) During seizure of movable property, the debtor has the right to notify the bailiff as to which items enforcement should be directed first. The bailiff shall satisfy such application if it does not contradict the provisions of this law and does not hinder enforcement of the judgment.

(9) (Deleted by law of 05.02.2009.)

(10) (Deleted by law of 01.03.2018.)

(11) (Deleted by law of 01.03.2018.)
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009. and 01.03.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 575. Section

Seizure of debtor's movable property if the property is with another person

(1) If there is evidence that the debtor's property is with another person, the bailiff shall seize this property in the general procedure. If the person refuses to admit the bailiff to the location of the movable property, the bailiff shall invite a police representative to ensure public order, in whose presence he or she shall open the premises or storage facility and carry out the seizure. Locked premises or storage facilities regarding which there is evidence that they contain the debtor's property, and which no person opens, may be opened by force in the presence of a police representative, or the bailiff, having assessed the specific circumstances, shall adopt a decision to postpone the seizure.

(2) If no adult person is found in the premises or other storage facilities after their opening, the bailiff shall, after forced opening of the premises, ensure their secure closure and sealing. The bailiff shall leave at the respective premises or storage facility a notice with an invitation to appear at the bailiff's place of practice to receive the keys to the premises.

(3) Things located in premises or storage facilities opened in the procedure specified in this section, which the bailiff does not seize, shall not be indicated in the property inventory act.

(4) If the debtor's property is with another person pursuant to a mutually concluded contract, the bailiff shall seize this property, but the question of preservation of the other person's rights arising from the contract shall be decided by the court in claim proceedings.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 576. Section. Inventory of corporeal things

(1) When inventorying corporeal things, their individual characteristics and quantity shall be precisely indicated, and photographic recording of the things shall be carried out.

(2) When inventorying corporeal things, new items shall be distinguished from used ones.

(3) When inventorying precious metals, the fineness (assay) shall be indicated if it is known. If things decorated with precious stones are inventoried, the number and colour of these stones shall be indicated, as well as the size and name if they are known.

(4) When inventorying goods, as well as products and materials in goods packaging, the numbers or marks on the packaging and the name and description of the goods stored in such packaging shall be indicated.

(5) The bailiff may package items of one type in bundles, indicating in the property inventory act the general name of the packaged items. Individual items may be packaged in bundles, indicating on the packaging the names of the inventoried items.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 577. Section. Inventory record

(1) The inventory record shall indicate:

1) the time and place of drawing up the record;

2) the official seat and place of practice of the bailiff, the name and surname of the bailiff;

3) the decision of the court or other institution or official being executed;

4) the name and surname of the creditor and debtor or their authorised representatives present at the inventory;

5) the name, surname, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration of witnesses, but if there are none — the place of residence, but for an official — the name, surname and position held;

6) the name of each item inventoried, its special characteristics (Section 576), the valuation of each item separately and the value of all property;

7) (deleted by the law of 31.10.2002.);

8) the name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there are none — the place of residence of the natural person to whom the inventoried property has been entrusted for safekeeping, or the name, registration number, legal address of the legal person and the name, surname, personal identity number and declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there are none — the place of residence of the representative of this legal person to whom the inventoried property has been entrusted for safekeeping;

81) the place of storage of the items;

9) that the creditor and debtor have been informed of the procedure and time limit for appealing the bailiff's actions;

10) that the custodian of the property has been informed of the procedure for storing the inventoried property, his or her civil liability, as well as criminal liability if he or she wastes, alienates, conceals or exchanges the property entrusted for safekeeping;

11) remarks and objections expressed by the creditor, debtor or other persons present at the inventory.

(11) Photographs (first paragraph of Section 576) shall be stored electronically in the enforcement case materials and attached to the inventory record as an annex thereto only at the request of the creditor or debtor.

(2) The inventory record shall be signed by the bailiff, the creditor, the debtor, the custodian of the property and other persons who participated in the inventory. If the creditor, debtor or their representatives do not sign the inventory record, the bailiff shall make a note thereof in the record.

(3) A creditor or debtor who has signed the inventory record without any remarks shall not have the right to subsequently submit a complaint regarding the incorrectness of the inventory record.

(4) The inventory record shall be issued to the creditor, the debtor and the custodian of the property. If the creditor or debtor has not participated in the inventory, the inventory record shall be sent to him or her within three days after completion of the inventory.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 29.11.2012. and 01.03.2018., which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 578. Section. Valuation of inventoried tangible items

(1) The inventoried tangible items, taking into account their degree of wear, shall be valued by the bailiff, determining the forced sale value of the items according to the prices prevailing in this area. If, due to the item or its characteristics, special knowledge in science or art is required to perform the valuation or if precious stones, precious metals and their products are to be valued, the bailiff shall engage an expert to determine the forced sale value of the item. The bailiff may also engage an expert to determine the forced sale value of the item in other cases. If it is not possible to engage an expert on the day of the inventory, the bailiff shall indicate in the inventory record the value of the property determined by himself or herself, which shall subsequently be replaced by the expert's valuation.

(2) The creditor or debtor may request the bailiff to engage an expert for re-valuation of the items within 10 days after the inventory has been completed or the written inventory record has been sent, but if an expert was initially engaged to determine the value — after the bailiff's notice of the valuation has been sent. Before engaging the expert, the bailiff shall notify in writing the person who requested the engagement of the expert of the amount of valuation costs. The valuation costs shall be covered by the person who requested the engagement of the expert by paying

within the time limit set by the bailiff, which shall not be shorter than five days, the necessary sum of money to the bailiff's account. If the sum of money necessary for the valuation has not been paid, the bailiff shall reject the request to engage an expert.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018., which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 579. Section. Protection of property

(1) To ensure the protection of the pledged property, the bailiff shall appoint a custodian of the property. The pledged property shall be entrusted for safekeeping to the debtor or a member of the debtor's family, unless there are circumstances that give rise to reasonable doubts about the custodian's ability to ensure the performance of his or her duties or that during the protection period the property entrusted for safekeeping could be wasted, alienated, concealed, exchanged or its value otherwise significantly reduced. The bailiff shall entrust the inventoried property of the debtor for safekeeping to a natural person against signature. In the cases provided for in this Law, items may also be entrusted for safekeeping to a legal person against the signature of its representative. If the custodian of the property cannot ensure the protection of the property at the address where it was inventoried, the bailiff shall remove the property and hand it over to the custodian of the property, indicating in the inventory record the address at which the custodian of the property has undertaken to store the property. The bailiff shall have the right at any stage of the execution of the decision to adopt a decision on the replacement of the custodian of the property if the custodian cannot continue to perform his or her duties, does not ensure proper storage of the items or does not comply with the bailiff's order.

(2) The debtor or members of his or her family may use the property left in their safekeeping if, due to the characteristics of this property, its use does not destroy the property or significantly reduce its value.

(3) If the custodian is not the debtor or a member of the debtor's family, he or she shall receive remuneration for safekeeping.

(4) When pledging movable property, a signature shall be obtained from the debtor or custodian that he or she will not alienate, pledge or use it for another task or purpose and that he or she may be held criminally liable for wasting, alienating, concealing or exchanging it.

(5) The custodian of the property may change the place of storage of the pledged items after coordinating it with the bailiff. The custodian of the property shall, at the request of the bailiff, show him or her the property entrusted for safekeeping, if necessary, delivering it to the place designated by the bailiff.

(6) When cancelling the pledge or replacing the custodian of the property, the bailiff shall issue an order to the custodian to hand over the property entrusted for safekeeping to the person indicated in the order at the time and place designated by the bailiff. The bailiff shall draw up a record of the handover of the property. If the custodian of the property does not hand over the property or has not ensured its proper safekeeping, the bailiff shall draw up a record thereof and send it to the prosecutor for resolution of the issue of the liability of the custodian of the property.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 01.03.2018., which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 580. Section. Storage of money and valuables seized from the debtor

(1)	The bailiff seizes the described gold and silver articles and other valuables and, if unable to ensure their safekeeping, deposits them for storage in a credit institution.

(2)	The bailiff seizes money found at the debtor's premises in the amount necessary to discharge the debt to be recovered and the enforcement costs, and deposits it into the bailiff's deposit account.
(As amended by the laws of 31.10.2002 and 01.03.2018, which enter into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.1 Section. Attachment and sale of corporeal things subject to registration

(1)	The bailiff issues an order to the institution whose duties include maintaining the registration of things subject to registration, to register, or, if technically possible, registers himself or herself a prohibition on alienation or other actions in respect of the debtor's vehicle or other corporeal thing subject to registration.

(2)	Simultaneously with the placement of the auction notice on the electronic auction website or the adoption of a decision on the sale of attached property without auction, the bailiff notifies the persons in whose favour a pledge right or prohibition note is entered in the register of the auction or sale of property without auction. If the attached vehicle is sold, the bailiff, after the acquirer has paid the entire amount due from the acquirer, within five days notifies the State Revenue Service of the date of alienation of the vehicle and the acquirer and makes a note thereof in the State Register of Vehicles and their Drivers.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.2 Section. Attachment and sale of a ship and floating structure

(1)	Ships and floating structures registered in the Latvian Ship Register of the state joint-stock company "Latvian Maritime Administration" (hereinafter — the Ship Register) are attached in the procedure laid down in this chapter, insofar as this section does not provide otherwise. Watercraft registered in the state joint-stock company "Road Traffic Safety Directorate" are attached and sold in the procedure laid down in Section 580.1 of this law.

(2)	The attachment of a ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register extends not only to the hull of the ship or floating structure, but also to all accessories of the ship or floating structure, including those that ensure navigation. A ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register held in co-ownership is attached in its entirety, without previously separating the debtor's rights to his or her share. The Ship Register is notified of the attachment of the ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register. An expert is invited to evaluate the ship and floating structure registered in the Ship Register. A legal person may also be appointed as the custodian of the ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register.

(3)	A ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register is sold at auction in the procedure laid down in this law for the sale of immovable property. The notice of the auction of the ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register is also sent to the persons specified in Section 55 of the Maritime Code.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.3 Section. Procedure for attachment and sale of incorporeal things

(1)	The bailiff attaches incorporeal things (rights) by adopting a decision in which he or she indicates the attached right, the legal basis for its creation and the valuation. The bailiff sends the decision within three days to the person who, in accordance with the attached right, has the obligation to perform to the debtor (the obligated person), indicating that from the date of receipt of the decision, performance under the obligation is to be given to the bailiff, not to the debtor. After sending the decision to the obligated person, the bailiff sends the decision on the attachment of the right to the creditor and the debtor.

(2)	From the date of receipt of the bailiff's decision, the debtor is prohibited from demanding or receiving performance under the attached right. The debtor and the obligated person have the obligation, at the bailiff's request, to provide all requested information relating to the attached right.

(3)	Rights that are purely personal or whose alienation is prohibited by law or court decision may not be attached.

(4)	Incorporeal things are valued by the bailiff, determining their forced sale value according to the prices prevailing in this area. If necessary, the bailiff may, on his or her own initiative, invite an expert to determine the forced sale value.

(5)	When sending the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this section to the creditor and the debtor, the bailiff explains their right to request the bailiff within 10 days from the date of sending the decision to invite an expert for repeated valuation of the things. The person who has requested repeated valuation covers the valuation costs within the time limit set by the bailiff, which is not shorter than five days, by depositing the necessary amount of money into the bailiff's account. If the amount of money necessary for valuation has not been deposited, the bailiff rejects the request to invite an expert.

(6)	The bailiff sells attached incorporeal things at auction or without auction in the procedure laid down in Section 583.1 of this law.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.4 Section. Procedure for attachment and sale of capital company shares or stocks and cooperative society shares

(1)	The bailiff adopts a decision on the attachment of capital company shares or stocks or cooperative society shares belonging to the debtor, in which he or she indicates the attached things and their valuation.

(2)	The forced sale value of shares or stocks or shares is determined by the bailiff, but not lower than the nominal value of the share or stock or share. If necessary, the bailiff may, on his or her own initiative, invite an expert to determine the forced sale value.

(3)	The bailiff sends the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this section within three days to the creditor and the debtor,

simultaneously explaining their right to request the bailiff within 10 days from the date of sending the decision to invite an expert for repeated valuation of the things. The person who has requested repeated valuation covers the valuation costs within the time limit set by the bailiff, which is not shorter than five days, by depositing the necessary amount of money into the bailiff's account. If the amount of money necessary for valuation has not been deposited, the bailiff rejects the request to invite an expert.

(4)	From the date of receipt of the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this section, the debtor is prohibited from alienating the attached shares or stocks or shares, encumbering them with other property or obligation rights, changing their nominal value, as well as performing other actions that reduce the value of the shares or stocks or shares.

(5)	Simultaneously with the adoption of the decision on the attachment of shares, the bailiff issues an order to the board of the limited liability company and the commercial register institution to observe the prohibition on alienating or pledging the shares belonging to the debtor, encumbering them with other property or obligation rights and, if necessary to ensure the sale of the attached shares, — also the prohibition on changing the nominal value of the shares and performing other actions that reduce the value of the shares belonging to the debtor.

(6)	Simultaneously with the adoption of the decision on the attachment of stocks or shares, the bailiff issues an order to the board of the joint-stock company or cooperative society, respectively, to observe the prohibition on alienating or pledging the stocks or shares belonging to the debtor, encumbering them with other property or obligation rights and, if necessary to ensure the sale of the attached stocks or shares, — also the prohibition on changing their nominal value and performing other actions that reduce the value of the stocks or shares belonging to the debtor.

(7)	Simultaneously with the adoption of the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this section, the bailiff may issue an order to the board of the capital company or cooperative society to deposit all money due to the debtor into the bailiff's deposit account.

(8)	The bailiff sells shares or stocks or shares at auction, but if this has not been successful and no one has applied to retain the shares or stocks or shares after an unsuccessful auction in the procedure laid down in this chapter, they may also be sold without auction, observing the procedure for determining the forced sale value laid down in the second paragraph of this section. After the alienation of shares or stocks or shares, the bailiff notifies the board of the capital company or cooperative society and the commercial register of the cancellation of the attachment.

(9)	Simultaneously with the placement of the share auction notice on the electronic auction website, the bailiff notifies the board of the limited liability company of the auction.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.5 Section. Procedure for exercising the right of pre-emption of shares of a limited liability company

(1)	The bailiff immediately notifies the board of the limited liability company that other members of the company may exercise the right of pre-emption of the attached shares if:

1)	the auction of shares has been declared unsuccessful for the reasons provided for in points 1 or 2 of the first paragraph of Section 589 of this law and the creditor has deposited the necessary amount into the bailiff's deposit account in the procedure laid down in Section 590 of this law to retain the shares for himself or herself;

2)	the successful bidder or the last overbidder has deposited into the bailiff's deposit account the entire amount due from him or her;

3)	the bailiff sells the attached shares without auction in the procedure laid down in Section 583.1 of this law, and the buyer has deposited the purchase price into the bailiff's deposit account.

(2)	In the notice to the board of the limited liability company, the bailiff indicates the amount to be deposited into the bailiff's deposit account within the time limit set by the bailiff, which may not be shorter than 10 days from the date of sending the notice, as well as that if the board organises a closed auction among the members in accordance with the ninth paragraph of Section 189 of the Commercial Law, the board has the obligation to deposit into the bailiff's deposit account the additional part of the purchase price obtained therein that exceeds the amount transferred indicated in the notice to the bailiff, within 10 days from the date of payment of the purchase price bid at the closed auction.

(3)	If the indicated amount has not been deposited into the bailiff's deposit account within the time limit specified in the notice, the bailiff notifies the buyer, the successful bidder, the creditor or the last overbidder, respectively, that the members of the company have not exercised their right of pre-emption.

(4)	If the entire indicated amount is deposited into the bailiff's deposit account within the time limit specified in the notice, the bailiff draws up an act on the transfer of the attached shares to the limited liability company and sends it to the board of the company. After sending the act, the bailiff notifies the creditor, the debtor and the person who bid or expressed a wish to retain the shares for himself or herself or was the last overbidder of the exercise of the right of pre-emption, immediately refunding to that person the amount deposited by it.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.6 Section. Procedure for attachment and sale of financial instruments

(1)	If the debtor owns financial instruments, the bailiff issues an order to the credit institution or investment brokerage company in which the debtor's financial instruments account is opened and which acts with the debtor's financial instruments on the debtor's instructions, prohibiting the alienation, pledging or otherwise encumbering with property or obligation rights the financial instruments belonging to the debtor. If the attached financial instruments are located in the initial register of the central securities depository (within the meaning of the Financial Instrument Market Law), such an order is issued to the central securities depository.

(2)	Only paper-form securities are described in the procedure laid down in Section 576 of this law. When describing securities, their number, class, numbers and nominal value, if known, are indicated. If the nominal value is not known, the bailiff values paper-form securities in the procedure laid down in the first paragraph of Section 578 of this law. The creditor or debtor may request the bailiff to invite an expert for repeated valuation of securities in the procedure laid down in the second paragraph of Section 578 of this law. The bailiff seizes the described securities and, if unable to ensure their safekeeping, deposits them for storage in a credit institution.

(3)	For the sale of financial instruments, the bailiff issues an order to the credit institution or investment brokerage company in which the debtor's financial instruments account is opened and which acts with the debtor's financial instruments on the debtor's instructions, to sell the attached financial instruments on the regulated market at the market price of these financial instruments within a time limit not exceeding one month and to transfer the money obtained to the bailiff's deposit account. If it has not been possible to sell all of the debtor's financial instruments or part of them within the time limit set by the bailiff, the bailiff may extend the sale time limit by issuing a new order.

(4)	If the debtor owns such financial instruments that are held in the debtor's financial instruments account but which cannot be sold in the procedure laid down in the third paragraph of this section because they are not included in the regulated market, the bailiff issues an order to the credit institution or investment brokerage company to realise these financial instruments in accordance with the procedure established for determining the value and sale of financial instruments in the relevant market.

(5)	The bailiff sells paper-form securities at a movable property auction. In such a case, the starting price is set as the nominal value of the paper-form securities or the forced sale value determined by the bailiff or expert, if the bailiff has invited an expert to determine it. If two expert valuations have been performed, the starting price is the highest expert valuation.

(6)	The bailiff sells rights to financial instruments that are located in the initial register of the central securities depository at a movable property auction. In such a case, the starting price is determined as the average market price of the financial instruments in the previous month before the announcement of the auction. If the debtor owns several types and categories of financial instruments, their sale in parts is permissible, provided that all financial instruments of one type and one category are sold in one transaction. After the successful bidder has paid the purchase price in full into the bailiff's deposit account and informed the bailiff of his or her financial instruments account in a credit institution or investment brokerage company, the bailiff draws up an act thereof and issues an order to the central securities depository to perform the deregistration of the financial instruments to the acquirer's financial instruments account.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.7 Section. Procedure for attachment and sale of things with restricted circulation

(1)	Things with restricted circulation may be deposited for storage only with such a natural or legal person who has been issued a special permit (licence) necessary for performing operations with the relevant type of things.

(2)	The bailiff sells things with restricted circulation at auction or without auction in the procedure laid down in Section 583.1 of this law. A person who wishes to acquire a thing with restricted circulation presents to the bailiff documents certifying his or her right to acquire such things as property.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 581. pants. Sale of Pledged Property

(1)	The bailiff has the right to sell the debtor's property if, within the time limit specified in this law, no request has been submitted for the involvement of an expert for re-evaluation of the property, but if a request for the involvement of an expert has been submitted — after re-evaluation of the property or rejection of the request.  

(2)	If, due to special circumstances, delay in the execution of the judgment may cause significant losses to the creditor or debtor or the enforcement itself may become impossible, the property shall be seized and sold immediately in the manner specified in Section
583.1 of this law. In such cases, the creditor or debtor may not request re-evaluation of the property and an appeal of the bailiff's decision on the sale of property without auction does not suspend the sale of the property, except in the case referred to in the third paragraph of Section 632 of this law. If the debtor is a registered value added tax payer, the bailiff shall apply value added tax to the sale price.  

(3)	The bailiff may sell pledged items as one object if identical items are pledged or the main item and its accessory items are pledged or it is impractical to sell the pledged items separately.  

(4)	If the debtor is a registered value added tax payer, the bailiff, before selling the pledged property, except in the case referred to in the second paragraph of this Section, shall send the debtor a request to provide information on whether, when selling his or her pledged property, the sale or auction price is subject to value added tax in accordance with the regulatory enactments governing value added tax and what is the taxable value of this price.  
(01.03.2018. version of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 582. pants. Procedure for Sale of Pledged Property

(1)	The bailiff shall sell the pledged property at auction, but in cases and in the manner specified in this law, the pledged property may also be sold without auction.  

(2)	The bailiff may seize the pledged movable property:

1)	before sale at auction, if necessary;  

2)	in order to transfer it in the cases specified in this law to the purchaser, successful bidder, creditor or debtor of the movable property.  

(3)	If the debtor fully pays the debt and the costs of execution of the judgment before the sale of the pledged property, but if the property is sold at auction — no later than seven days before the auction closing date specified in the auction notice, the sale shall be cancelled, the auction already commenced shall be terminated and the pledged property shall be returned to the debtor, drawing up a record thereof.  

(4)	After the sale of the pledged property or its transfer to the creditor, the bailiff shall adopt a decision on the release of the sold property from the pledge, and shall also send to the relevant keeper of the movable property register or other public register a notification of the cancellation of the prohibition and the release of the property from the pledge.  
(01.03.2018. version of the law, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 583.pants. Sale of Pledged Property on Commission

(Deleted by the law of 01.03.2018., which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

583.1 pants. Sale of Pledged Property Without Auction

(1)	The bailiff shall sell the pledged property to a specific person (purchaser) without auction in cases specifically indicated in this law, as well as when it might be impossible to sell the pledged property at auction or it has not been possible to sell it at auction. The bailiff shall adopt a decision on the sale of pledged property without auction, indicating the circumstances that permit the sale of the property without auction. The decision shall be sent to the debtor and the creditor. The decision may be appealed in the manner specified in Section 632 of this law.  

(2)	The restrictions specified in Section 586 of this law on persons who do not have the right to participate in bidding shall apply to the purchaser of the pledged property.  

(3)	After the time limit for appealing the decision drawn up by the bailiff has expired, but if the bailiff's

decision has been appealed — after a court decision rejecting the complaint has entered into legal force, the bailiff shall notify the purchaser of the time limit, which may not exceed one month, within which the purchase price must be paid into the bailiff's deposit account.  

(4)	The price for which the pledged property is permitted to be sold (purchase price) may not be lower than that indicated by the bailiff in the property description record, but if an expert has been involved — than the forced sale value determined by the expert. If two expert evaluations have been carried out, the purchase price may not be lower than the highest forced sale value determined by the expert. After the purchase price has been received in full in the bailiff's deposit account, the bailiff shall transfer the pledged property to the purchaser, drawing up a record thereof, and shall inform the State Revenue Service of the fact of the sale of the property and the price for which the property was sold.  

(5)	If the purchaser of the pledged property is the creditor, he or she is permitted to set off his or her claim, which is substantiated by an enforcement document, against the purchase price. If the purchase price is insufficient to satisfy all enforcement claims and commercial pledgee claims, the creditor may set off his or her claims against the purchase price only in the amount that is due to him or her according to the calculation after those claims that have priority over his or her claim have been covered.  

(6)	If several persons have expressed a wish to purchase the pledged property, an auction shall be held.  

(7)	If the purchaser does not pay the purchase price into the bailiff's deposit account within the time limit specified in the third paragraph of this Section, the bailiff may sell the pledged property at auction or without auction in the manner specified in this Section.  
(01.03.2018. version of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

583.2 pants. Sale of Movable Property at Auction

For the sale of movable property and the organisation of auctions, the procedure shall apply by which actions are carried out on the electronic auction website and by which information about a person is included in, updated in and deleted from the auction participants register (Sections 605.1 and 605.2).  
(01.03.2018. version of the law, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 584. Section. Announcement of movable property auction

(1)	The bailiff shall place the announcement of the movable property auction on the electronic auction website and, if considered appropriate, also post it at his or her place of practice. An interested person may, at his or her own expense, place the auction announcement in newspapers and other mass media, as well as post the announcement in public places in accordance with the procedure established by the respective municipality.

(2)	The announcement of the movable property auction shall indicate:

1)	the bailiff's first name, surname, official location and place of practice;

2)	the debtor's first name and surname, for a legal person — the name and legal address;

3)	the item to be sold and its valuation;

4)	which auction in sequence it is;

5)	the starting price of the auction and the auction step;

6)	the auction start date and closing date and time;

7)	whether the auction price is subject to value added tax and what is the taxable value of this price;

8)	the security amount to be paid into the bailiff's deposit account;

9)	the date by which a person wishing to participate in the auction may request the bailiff to authorise him or her for participation in the auction and pay the security amount;

10)	a reference to the website where information is available on the auction procedure and conditions under which persons may register for participation in the auction and participate in bidding.

(3)	Simultaneously with the placement of the auction announcement on the electronic auction website, the bailiff shall notify the creditor and the debtor of the auction.

(4)	The movable property auction shall be commenced from the bailiff's valuation, but if one or two expert valuations have been carried out — from the highest expert valuation.

(5)	The bailiff shall determine the auction step, not less than one per cent and not more than 10 per cent of the starting price of the movable property auction.

(6)	During the period from the day of announcement of the auction until the day set for submission of the request for authorisation to participate in the auction, persons wishing to participate in the auction shall have the right to inspect the item to be sold. The bailiff shall notify the custodian of the property of the time and place of inspection of the property. If several persons have expressed a wish to inspect the item to be sold, the bailiff shall ensure that the inspection of the property, if possible, is organised simultaneously.
(As amended by the law of 01.03.2018, with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

584.1 Section. Security for purchase of movable property and authorisation of auction participants

(1)	A person wishing to participate in a movable property auction, using the electronic auction website, within 10 days from the auction start date indicated in the movable property auction announcement, shall send a request to the bailiff to authorise him or her for participation in the auction and transfer to the bailiff's deposit account indicated in the auction announcement a security in the amount of 10 per cent of the valuation of the item to be sold.

(2)	If the valuation of the item to be sold is 10 000 euros or more, the time limit within which a person sends a request to the bailiff to authorise him or her for participation in the auction and transfers the security to the bailiff's deposit account in the procedure laid down in the first paragraph of this Section shall be 20 days from the auction start date indicated in the movable property auction announcement.

(3)	The bailiff shall authorise a person for participation in the auction within three, but in the case referred to in the second paragraph of this Section — five working days from the date of receipt of the security and the person's request, if the restrictions referred to in Section 586 of this Law do not exist. If the security or the authorisation request has not been received within the time limit specified in the first or second paragraph of this Section or the person does not have the right to participate in the auction in accordance with Section 586 of this Law, the bailiff shall refuse to authorise the person for participation in the auction.

(4)	The security paid by the person who has bid the item to be sold shall be included in the purchase price. The security paid by the other auction participants, except for the last outbid bidder, shall be returned immediately after the conclusion of the auction. The security paid by the last outbid bidder shall be returned to him or her within two working days after the successful bidder has paid the full amount bid. If, after an unsuccessful auction, the property is retained by the last outbid bidder, his or her security paid shall be included in the purchase price.
(As amended by the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 585. Section. Announcement of ship auction

(Deleted by the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 586. Section. Persons who do not have the right to participate in bidding

The debtor, his or her guardian or custodian, the person who has carried out the valuation referred to in Section 578 of this Law, as well as the bailiff organising the auction, shall not have the right to participate in bidding. The creditor shall have the right to participate in the auction in the general procedure. The auction participants themselves shall be responsible for compliance with the restrictions established in other regulatory enactments regarding the acquisition of the item to be auctioned.
(As amended by the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 587. Section. Procedure for auction of movable items

(1)	An auction participant may make bids electronically from the moment he or she is authorised for participation in the auction in the procedure laid down in Section 584.1 of this Law until the moment the auction has concluded.

(2)	Bidding shall take place in the procedure laid down in the second and third paragraphs of Section 608 of this Law.

(3)	The auction shall conclude on the twentieth day from the auction start date indicated in the movable property auction announcement at 13.00, but if the twentieth day falls on a day off or a public holiday — on the next working day at 13.00. If the valuation of the item to be sold is 10 000 euros or more, the auction shall conclude on the thirtieth day from the auction start date indicated in the movable property auction announcement at 13.00, but if the thirtieth day falls on a day off or a public holiday — on the next working day at 13.00.

(4)	If a bid is registered during the last five minutes before the time set for the conclusion of the auction, the auction time shall be automatically extended by five minutes. If significant technical disruptions that may affect the auction result are detected during the last hour before the conclusion of the auction and they are not related to system security breaches, the auction time shall be automatically extended until 13.00 on the next working day. After the conclusion of the auction, bids shall no longer be registered and the electronic auction website shall indicate the auction closing date, time and the last bid made.

(5)	The bailiff may suspend the movable property auction in the cases provided for in this Law. A notice of suspension of the auction shall be published on the electronic auction website.

(6)	The creditor, by submitting an application to the bailiff, may request to postpone the auction or issue an enforcement document under which enforcement has not been carried out or has been carried out incompletely, if such a request from the creditor is received no later than seven days before the auction closing date indicated in the auction announcement.

(7)	After the conclusion of the auction, the successful bidder shall be sent electronically to the electronic auction website user account registered in the Auction Participants Register a notice that he or she has bid a higher price than others and the obligation to pay the entire amount due from him or her has arisen.
(As amended by the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 588. Section. Auction Record

(1)	In the auction record, the bailiff shall indicate:

1)	the auction start date and end date and time;  

2)	the bailiff's first name, surname, place of office and place of practice;  

3)	the decision being enforced;  

4)	the name of the item being sold;  

5)	the starting price of the item being sold at auction;  

6)	the persons authorised to participate in the auction, indicating their first name, surname, personal identity number or date of birth (for a person who has not been assigned a personal identity number), the contact address indicated in the Auction Participants Register; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;  

7)	the prices bid at the auction and the bidder's first name and surname or company name (title);  

8)	the highest price bid, the successful bidder's first name and surname or name, personal identity number or registration number and address.  

(2)	An auction record prepared electronically on the electronic auction website is valid without the bailiff's signature.  
(As amended by the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

588.1 Section. Consequences of Auction

(1)	The person who has successfully bid for the item being sold shall pay the full amount bid and value added tax, if the auction price is subject to value added tax, no later than within two working days after the end of the auction. If the amount bid exceeds 1420 euros, the bailiff may, at the successful bidder's request, postpone payment of the full purchase price and value added tax for a period of up to seven days. If the amount bid exceeds 142 280 euros, the bailiff may, at the successful bidder's request, postpone payment of the full purchase price and value added tax for a period of up to 14 days. When the amount bid and value added tax have been paid in full, the bailiff shall draw up a record indicating to whom and for what price the auctioned items have been sold, and shall also inform the State Revenue Service of the fact of sale of the property and the price. The record and the purchased items shall be handed over to the successful bidder.  

(2)	After the time limit for appealing the calculation prepared by the bailiff has expired and this calculation has not been appealed or, if this calculation has been appealed, — after the court decision on the calculation prepared has entered into force, the bailiff shall pay the value added tax paid by the successful bidder into the state budget and notify the debtor and the State Revenue Service thereof.  
(As amended by the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

588.2 Section. Set-off of Purchase Payment

(1)	The successful bidder is permitted to set off against the purchase amount his or her claim that is substantiated by an enforcement document.  

(2)	If the amount received from the sale is insufficient to satisfy all claims and claims of commercial pledgees, the successful bidder may set off against the purchase price his or her claims only to the extent of the amount due to him or her according to the calculation after those claims which have priority over his or her claim have been covered.  
(As amended by the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 589. Section. Auction Not Held

(1)	The bailiff shall declare the auction not held if:

1)	no auction participant has been authorised for the auction;  

2)	none of the participants authorised for the auction outbids the starting price;  

3)	the successful bidder does not pay within the specified time limit the full amount due from him or her (Section 588.1, paragraph one);  

4)	during the course of the auction, except in the case referred to in Section 587, paragraph four of this law, or within 24 hours after the end of the auction, a notification has been received from the electronic auction website security administrator about significant technical disruptions that may affect the auction result, or about a breach of system security.  

(2)	The fact that the auction has been declared not held in the case referred to in points 1 or 2 of paragraph one of this Section shall be recorded by the bailiff in a record and notified to the claimant and the debtor. Notification shall be sent to participants authorised to participate in the auction using the electronic auction website.  

(3)	The fact that the auction has been declared not held in the case referred to in point 3 of paragraph one of this Section shall be recorded by the bailiff in a record and notified to the successful bidder, the debtor and the claimant.  

(4)	If the notification referred to in point 4 of paragraph one of this Section is received during the course of the auction, the bailiff shall suspend the auction and post a notification thereof on the electronic auction website.  

(5)	The fact that the auction has been declared not held in the case referred to in point 4 of paragraph one of this Section shall be recorded by the bailiff in a record and notified to the claimant and the debtor. Notification shall be sent to participants authorised to participate in the auction using the electronic auction website.  

(6)	In the case referred to in point 3 of paragraph one of this Section, the security paid shall not be refunded but shall be added to the total amount received for the property.
