### 618. pants. Sale of Immovable Property Held in Co-ownership

(1)	When enforcing against one or more owners of undivided immovable property, this property shall be described in its entire composition, but only the debtor's right to his share shall be sold at auction, without separating it in advance.

(2)	Immovable properties held in co-ownership may also be sold in their entire composition if all co-owners so wish and if creditors do not raise objections thereto. The money received from the sale shall be divided among the owners of the immovable property, but the sum due to the debtor shall be used to discharge the debt.

618.1 pants. Procedure for Enforcement of Confiscation of Immovable Property

(1)	The bailiff shall sell the confiscated immovable property specified in the writ of execution and the extract of the protocol or decision attached thereto on the imposition of seizure on property in the procedure laid down in this Chapter.

(2)	A person whose confiscation of immovable property is being enforced does not have the rights of a debtor as laid down in this law.

(3)	If an auction is declared not to have taken place, the right to retain the immovable property in the procedure laid down in this Chapter belongs to the last outbid bidder, the debtor's co-owner and the creditor in the enforcement case for recovery from the person whose immovable property is being confiscated. If the second auction has not taken place and no one has wished to retain the immovable property for themselves, the bailiff shall send a notice to the State Revenue Service, by which the immovable property is transferred to its disposal.
(22.06.2017. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.08.2017.)

73.1 nodaļa
Enforcement Against the Right to Build

## (Chapter 01

In the wording of the law of 03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Article 618.2 Notice of enforcement against building rights

(1) If the creditor has requested enforcement against building rights, the bailiff sends a notice to the debtor and invites him to settle the debt, as well as to provide information on whether the debtor is registered as a value added tax payer, whether, when selling his building rights at auction, the auction price is subject to value added tax and what is the taxable value of this price. When executing such decisions that provide for the voluntary sale of building rights at auction through court proceedings or the sale of building rights at forced auction, the notice does not indicate an invitation to the debtor to settle the debt.

(2) The bailiff submits to the district (city) court a request for registration to enter an enforcement note. The consequences of this note are specified in the first part of Article 1077, Articles 1081 and 1305 of the Civil Law, as well as Article 46 of the Land Register Law. An enforcement note shall also be entered when executing such decisions that provide for the voluntary sale of building rights at auction through court proceedings or the sale of building rights at forced auction.

(3) The bailiff, in accordance with the relevant land register section, sends a notice to the owner of the land plot, to the building rights holders who own an ideal share of the building rights, as well as to all mortgage creditors, including persons in whose favour a pledge right or prohibition note has been entered in respect of the building rights, indicating:

1) for the satisfaction of which person's claim enforcement is being directed against the building rights;

2) how large the debt amount is and whether the debt is secured by a mortgage on the respective building rights.

(4) In the notice referred to in paragraph three of this Article, the bailiff requests that the mortgage creditors submit information on the amount of the remaining mortgage debt within the time limit set by the bailiff, which shall not be less than 10 days.

(5) The bailiff requests from the municipality information on real estate tax debt and invites the municipality

to submit a decision on the recovery of tax debt, if such exists.

(6) The bailiff requests from the relevant land register section a copy of the building contract and other documents certifying registration, if such exist.

(7) If the information necessary for the valuation of building rights regarding the construction process commenced on the basis of the building rights is not obtainable from state information system databases, the bailiff, specifically indicating the necessary documents, requests them from the construction board or the institution that performs the functions of the construction board, unless the necessary information or the original of the document is available at another state or municipal institution. A certified real estate appraiser is entitled, on the assignment of the bailiff, to familiarise himself with information available to state or municipal institutions for the valuation of building rights.

(8) If the debtor has paid in full the debt and the costs of execution of the judgment to the bailiff no later than seven days before the auction closing date indicated in the auction announcement, the sale of building rights shall be cancelled, but the auction already commenced shall be terminated. The aforementioned shall not apply when executing such decisions that provide for the sale of building rights at forced auction.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018 with amendments made by the laws of 25.10.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 618.3 Debtor's obligations

(1) From the day of receipt of the bailiff's notice, the debtor is prohibited from:

1) alienating the building rights or pledging them;

2) alienating or damaging the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on the basis of the building rights or its accessories;

3) concluding lease and other contracts that reduce or may reduce the value of the building rights or the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on its basis.

(2) Contracts which, contrary to the prohibitions established in paragraph one of this Article, the debtor has concluded after an enforcement note has been made in the land register, shall not be valid in relation to the creditor and the purchaser of the building rights at auction.

(3) The debtor has an obligation to notify, within the time limit set by the bailiff, who is the actual possessor or manager of the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on the basis of the building rights, if such exists, as well as about all concluded lease and other contracts relating to the building rights or the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on its basis, to submit copies of these contracts and to present their originals.

(4) The debtor has an obligation to notify the bailiff whether he is registered as a value added tax payer and whether, when selling his building rights at auction, the auction price is subject to value added tax. If the auction price is subject to value added tax in accordance with the regulatory enactments regulating value added tax, in the said information the debtor indicates the taxable value of this price.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Article 618.4 Description and management of the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on the basis of building rights

The bailiff describes the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on the basis of building rights at the request of the creditor in the procedure established in Article 603 of this Law. The management of the described non-residential building (engineering structure) shall be ensured in accordance with Article 605 of this Law.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Article 618.5 Valuation of building rights

The building rights shall be valued at the debtor's expense at the request of the bailiff by a certified real estate appraiser, determining the forced sale value of the building rights. The valuation shall be notified, as well as the right to request a re-valuation and the procedure by which a re-valuation is carried out, shall be determined according to the provisions of Article 604 of this Law.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Article 618.6 Sale of building rights

(1) The auction of building rights, confirmation of the auction act and registration of building rights in the name of the acquirer shall take place according to the rules provided for the auction of real estate. The bailiff also sends the notice of auction to the owner of the land plot.

(2) In the event of an auction not taking place, in addition to the persons referred to in Article 615 of this Law, if they are not debtors, the owner of the land plot also has the right to retain the building rights.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 74
Forced transfer of property awarded by the court and execution of actions imposed by court decision
(Chapter title in the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 619.pants. Delivery of items specified in court judgment to the creditor

(1)	If specific items specified in the court judgment have been awarded to the creditor, the bailiff shall notify the debtor of the obligation to execute the judgment in the procedure laid down in Section 555 of this Law. In the notification, the bailiff shall also indicate the date on which the forced execution of the court judgment will be carried out if it has not been executed. If the court judgment is to be executed immediately, the bailiff shall not give the debtor a time limit for execution of the court judgment in the notification, but shall indicate the date and time when the forced execution of the court judgment will be carried out.

(2)	At the time of forced execution of the judgment set by the bailiff, upon the bailiff's request, the debtor has an obligation to present the items specified in the writ of execution to be delivered to the creditor. Upon delivery of the items, the debtor and the creditor have the right to invite no more than two witnesses. The non-appearance of witnesses shall not suspend the execution of the judgment.

(3)	If, at the time of forced execution of the court judgment, the debtor does not present the items specified in the judgment to be delivered to the creditor, refuses to disclose their location, and the items are not found after inspection of the premises, the bailiff shall draw up a report, which shall be signed by the bailiff, the creditor and the witnesses, if any have participated. After a report has been drawn up on the absence of property to be delivered to the creditor, the bailiff shall carry out forced execution actions in accordance with the provisions of this Law for the recovery of the sum specified in the court judgment (Section 196).

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 08.09.2011. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

### 620. pants

Consequences arising from failure to execute a decision imposing on the debtor an obligation to perform specific actions

(1)	If a decision imposing on the debtor an obligation to perform specific actions not related to the delivery of property or a sum of money is not executed, the bailiff shall draw up a report on the non-execution of the decision.

(2)	If the decision specifies the consequences of non-execution of the decision provided for in the second paragraph of Section 197 of this Law, the report drawn up shall be sent to the district (city) court according to the place of execution so that it may adopt a decision on the application of the consequences specified in the decision in connection with the debtor's failure to perform specific actions.

(3)	If the decision does not specify the consequences of its non-execution, the report drawn up shall be sent to the court that made the decision in the case, and that court shall decide the question of the procedure for execution of the decision in accordance with the provisions of Sections 206 and 438 of this Law.

(4)	If, within the time limit set by the court, a decision imposing on the debtor an obligation to perform actions that can only be performed by the debtor personally (first paragraph of Section 197) is not executed, the bailiff shall send the report drawn up to the court according to the bailiff's place of office. The question of non-execution of the decision shall be decided at a court hearing. The creditor and the debtor shall be notified of the time and place of the hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to considering the question of non-execution of the decision. If the debtor does not execute within the time limit set by the court a decision imposing on the debtor an obligation to perform actions that can only be performed by the debtor personally, the court may impose a fine of up to 3000 euros on the debtor, setting a new time limit for execution of the decision. The fine shall be recovered from the debtor to state revenues. Payment of the fine shall not release the debtor from

the obligation to perform the actions provided for in the court decision.

(5)	If the debtor continues to fail to execute the decision after imposition of the fine, the sworn bailiff shall send a submission to the prosecutor for initiation of criminal proceedings.

(6)	If an employer does not execute a court decision on reinstatement of an unlawfully dismissed or transferred employee, the court, at the employee's request, shall adopt a decision on remuneration for the entire period from the date of making the decision until the date of its execution.

(7)	An appeal may be lodged against the court decision.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 12.09.2013., 09.06.2016., 31.05.2018. un 25.03.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 20.04.2021.)

74.1	nodaļa
Eviction of persons and property from premises

## (Nodaļa 31

10.2002. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2003.)

620.1 pants. Notification of obligation to execute decision

(1)	The notification of the obligation to execute the court decision and, together with family members and other accommodated persons, to vacate the premises shall be delivered by the bailiff to the debtor in the procedure laid down in Section 555 of this Law.

(2)	In the notification, the bailiff shall also indicate the date on which forced execution of the decision will take place if the debtor does not execute it.

(25.03.2021. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 20.04.2021.)

620.1A pants. Protection of third party rights in forced eviction

Forced eviction shall not affect the rights of other persons to use the premises if the right to use the premises arises from an entry in the Land Register.

(25.03.2021. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 20.04.2021.)

620.2 pants. Eviction in the presence of the debtor

(1)	In forced eviction, the creditor and the debtor have the right to invite no more than two witnesses each. The bailiff shall verify the identity of the witnesses and indicate these persons in the report. The non-appearance of witnesses shall not suspend the forced execution.

(2)	The bailiff shall invite the debtor to remove property from the premises specified in the court decision and, together with family members and other accommodated persons, to vacate these premises.

(3)	If the debtor does not comply with the bailiff's invitation, all persons present in the premises shall be evicted, and the bailiff shall describe and value the property in accordance with the provisions of Sections 577 and 578 of this Law, and shall appoint a custodian of the property.

(4)	The bailiff shall issue one copy of the report to the debtor.

(5)	After execution of the decision, the premises shall be delivered to the creditor.

(6)	If items that perish quickly have been described, the bailiff shall sell them in accordance with the provisions of the second paragraph of Section 581 of this Law. The money received shall be credited to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but any surplus money shall be paid to the debtor.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 31.05.2018. un 25.03.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 20.04.2021.)

620.3 pants. Eviction in the absence of the debtor

(1)	If the debtor does not appear at the time set for eviction and there is no information about the reason for non-appearance, or if the debtor has not appeared for an excusable reason, the bailiff shall postpone the eviction.

(2)	If the debtor has not appeared at the time set for the repeated eviction and has not notified the reason for non-appearance, or has not appeared for a reason that the bailiff does not recognise as excusable, the premises shall be opened by force in the presence of a police representative. The bailiff shall make a note in the report about the forced opening of the premises.

(3)	The eviction shall be carried out in the procedure laid down in Section 620.2 of this Law.

(4)	The debtor has the right to receive one copy of the report describing the property.

620.4 pants. Handling of the debtor's property

(1)	The debtor has the right to receive the property placed in custody within one month by paying the costs of execution of the judgment.

(2)	If the debtor refuses to pay the costs of execution of the judgment, the bailiff shall seize the debtor's property to the value necessary to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but shall deliver the remaining property to the debtor.

(3)	The bailiff shall sell the seized property in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this Law.

(4)	The money received from the sale of the property shall be credited to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but any surplus money shall be paid to the debtor. The bailiff shall notify the debtor of the sale of the property if the bailiff has information about the debtor's official electronic address, e-mail address or place of residence.

(5)	If the debtor does not appear within one month to receive the property placed in custody, the bailiff shall sell it in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this Law.

(6)	Property that has no market value or cannot be sold and which the debtor has not appeared to receive within the time limit and in the procedure specified in the first paragraph of this Section shall be destroyed by the bailiff in the presence of witnesses, drawing up a report thereof.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 05.02.2009. un 25.03.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 20.04.2021.)

74.2	nodaļa
Introduction into possession of immovable property

## (Chapter 31

Edition of law 10.2002, which enters into force 01.01.2003.)

Article 620.5 Notice of obligation to execute decision

(1) The notice of obligation to execute a court decision, together with family members and other persons to vacate the immovable property and transfer it to the acquirer, shall be sent by the bailiff to the debtor in the procedure specified in Article 555 of this law.

(2) In the notice, the bailiff shall also indicate the date on which the introduction of the acquirer into possession of the immovable property will take place if the debtor fails to fulfil the obligation.

(3) Introduction into possession shall also take place if the acquirer has not yet registered the property rights in the Land Register.

(4) If introduction into possession of such immovable property is to be carried out which the bailiff has alienated as heirless property, the bailiff shall prepare a notice of the date and time of the introduction of the acquirer into possession of the immovable property and issue it to the person encountered on the immovable property. If no adult person is encountered on the immovable property, the bailiff shall leave the notice at the respective immovable property.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 620.6 Introduction into possession of immovable property in the presence of the debtor

(1) The introduction into possession of immovable property shall be carried out by the bailiff in the presence of the acquirer of the immovable property and the debtor or another adult person living together with him or her on the immovable property. These persons have the right to each invite no more than two witnesses. The bailiff shall verify the identity of the witnesses and indicate these persons in the record. Non-appearance of witnesses shall not suspend enforcement.

(2) The bailiff shall invite the debtor to vacate the immovable property of property belonging to him or her and to leave the immovable property together with family members and other persons.

(3) If the bailiff's invitation is not complied with, all persons in the premises shall be removed, but the property shall be described and valued by the bailiff in accordance with the provisions of Articles 577 and 578 of this law, and a custodian of the property shall be appointed, the property shall be removed and transferred to the custody of the custodian of the property according to the description record. Movable things belonging to the immovable property shall not be included in this description record and shall not be removed. Introduction into possession shall not affect the rights of other persons to use the premises if the rights to use the premises arise from registration in the Land Register.

(4) The bailiff shall issue one copy of the record to the debtor or the person in whose presence the introduction of the acquirer into possession of the immovable property was carried out.

(5) At the request of the debtor or the acquirer, the bailiff shall draw up a separate record of the immovable property to be transferred to the acquirer, which shall indicate the condition of the immovable property and the movable things belonging to it which are transferred to the acquirer.

(6) If things that spoil quickly have been described and removed, the bailiff shall sell them in accordance with the provisions of the second part of Article 581 of this law. The money received shall be credited to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but any surplus of money shall be paid to the debtor.
(Edition of law 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 620.7 Introduction into possession of immovable property in the absence of the debtor

(1) If at the time appointed for introduction into possession of the immovable property neither the debtor nor any of the other adult persons living together with the debtor on the immovable property appears and there is no information about the reason for their non-appearance or they have not appeared for a justifiable reason, the bailiff shall postpone the introduction into possession.

(2) If neither the debtor nor any of the other adult persons living together with the debtor on the immovable property appears at the time repeatedly appointed for introduction into possession of the immovable property and there is no information about the reason for their non-appearance or they have not appeared for a reason which the bailiff does not recognise as justifiable, the premises shall be opened by force in the presence of a police representative. The bailiff shall make a note in the record of the forced opening of the premises.

(3) Introduction into possession of the immovable property shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Article 620.6 of this law.

(4) The debtor is entitled to receive one copy of the property description record.

(5) Introduction into possession of such immovable property which the bailiff has alienated as heirless property shall be carried out in the presence of a police representative and the acquirer of the immovable property. If persons are encountered on the immovable property, the bailiff shall act in the procedure specified in Article 620.6 of this law.
(Edition of law 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 620.8 Disputes and complaints in connection with introduction into possession of immovable property
(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 620.9 Handling of property transferred to custody

(1) The debtor has the right within one month to receive the property transferred to custody by paying the costs of execution of the judgment.

(2) If the debtor refuses to pay the costs of execution of the judgment, the bailiff shall seize the debtor's property in such value as is necessary to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but shall transfer the remaining property to the debtor.

(3) The seized property shall be sold by the bailiff in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this law.

(4) The money received from the sale of the property shall be credited to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but any surplus of money shall be paid to the debtor. The bailiff shall notify the debtor of the sale of the property if he or she has information about the debtor's official electronic address, e-mail address or place of residence.

(5) If the debtor does not appear within one month to receive the property transferred to custody, the bailiff shall sell it in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this law.

(6) Property which has no market value or which cannot be sold and which the debtor has not appeared to receive within the time limit and procedure specified in the first paragraph of this Article shall be destroyed by the bailiff in the presence of witnesses, drawing up a record thereof.

(7) Property which has been described on immovable property alienated as heirless property and which has no market value shall be destroyed by the bailiff in the presence of witnesses, drawing up a record thereof, but the property description record in the part concerning property which has market value shall be sent by the bailiff to the notary who made the notarial deed on termination of the inheritance matter for amendments to be made therein.
(Edition of law 08.09.2011 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 74.3
Return of a child to the country of his or her place of residence

## (Chapter 04

Edition of 08.2011 law, which enters into force on 01.10.2011.)

620.10 Article. Costs of enforcement of a decision and the procedure for their payment

(1) The creditor, when submitting an enforcement document for enforcement, shall pay the state fee and cover the costs of enforcement of the decision in accordance with the first part of Article 567 of this law.

(2) The creditor who does not participate in the enforcement of the decision shall, at the request of the bailiff, in addition to the costs of enforcement of the decision referred to in the first part of this Article, pay a sum of money to cover the costs associated with the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence (including costs associated with the child's stay in a crisis centre or other safe conditions, travel costs, costs for interpreter and psychologist services and other costs). The amount of these costs and the procedure for payment shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(3) After the child has been handed over to the representative of the orphan's court, the bailiff shall immediately transfer the costs referred to in the second part of this Article to the account specified by the orphan's court.

(4) When issuing an enforcement document to the creditor (points 7 and 8 of the first part of Article 565 and the third part of Article 620.13), the bailiff or the orphan's court shall refund to the creditor the costs referred to in the second part of this Article that have not been used for the enforcement of the decision.

(5) The bailiff shall recover the costs of enforcement of the decision from the debtor.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

620.10A Article. Time limit within which an enforcement document must be submitted for enforcement

An enforcement document for the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence, including a relevant European Union enforcement document, may be submitted for compulsory enforcement within one year from the date of entry into force of the court or foreign court decision.
(Edition of 16.06.2022 law, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

620.11 Article. Notice of the obligation to enforce the decision

(1) The bailiff, when commencing enforcement in the procedure established in Article 555 of this law, shall notify the debtor of the obligation to enforce the decision within 10 days. If the creditor submits the enforcement document for enforcement repeatedly after the bailiff has issued it to him or her in accordance with the third part of Article 620.13 of this law, the notice shall not be sent.

(2) Upon receiving for enforcement a European Union enforcement document which does not specify a time limit for voluntary enforcement of the decision, the bailiff shall, in the procedure established in Article 555 of this law, send to the debtor a notice of the obligation to enforce

the decision within 30 days. In the notice, the bailiff shall warn the debtor of the consequences provided for in this chapter that will occur if the decision is not enforced.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

620.12 Article. Consequences arising if the debtor does not enforce the decision voluntarily

(1) The bailiff shall send information that the debtor has not voluntarily enforced the decision to:

1) the district (city) court which adopted the decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence — upon receiving the said decision for enforcement;

2) the district (city) court in whose territory of operation the foreign court decision is to be enforced — after the expiry of the time limit for voluntary enforcement of the decision specified in the enforcement document or in accordance with Article 620.11 of this law.

(2) The court, upon receipt of the information referred to in the first part of this Article, shall impose a fine of 750 euros on the debtor.

(3) The issue of imposing a fine shall be examined in written proceedings.

(4) The court decision on the imposition of a fine shall be sent to the debtor.

(5) An appeal may be lodged against the court decision on the imposition of a fine.

(6) The fine shall be recovered from the debtor to state revenues.

(7) Payment of the fine shall not release the debtor from the obligation to enforce the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.09.2013, 09.06.2016, 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

620.13 Article. Ascertaining the child's daily routine

(1) Simultaneously with the sending of the information referred to in the first part of Article 620.12 of this law, the bailiff, if necessary for the enforcement of the decision, shall give an order to the orphan's court according to the child's location to ascertain the child's daily routine within 15 days from the date of receipt of the order and to inform the bailiff thereof.

(2) The orphan's court shall immediately inform the bailiff of information relating to the child and the child's location which it has obtained in executing the order specified in the first part of this Article. If it is not possible to obtain the said information, the orphan's court shall inform the bailiff thereof. The bailiff, upon receiving information that the child's location is not known, shall, in accordance with Article 569 of this law, request the judge to adopt a decision on the search for the child or the child and the debtor with the assistance of the police and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

(3) The bailiff, having received from the orphan's court or the police information about the child's location which is in the territory of operation of the regional court to which this bailiff does not belong, shall make a note thereof in the enforcement document, indicating information about the child's location, and shall immediately issue the enforcement document to the creditor, explaining to him or her the right to submit the enforcement document for enforcement in accordance with the provisions of Article 549 of this law.

(4) (Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015)
(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

620.14 Article. Handing over of the child to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court

(1) Upon receiving the information referred to in the first part of Article 620.13 of this law, the bailiff shall determine the times and places when and where the child will be handed over to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court if the creditor does not participate in the enforcement, and shall notify thereof:

1) the creditor, informing him or her of the creditor's right to be present at enforcement actions;

2) the orphan's court and the police according to the child's location, giving an order to their representatives to participate in compulsory enforcement. The orphan's court shall, at its discretion, invite a psychologist to participate in the compulsory enforcement of the decision.

(2) The bailiff shall not inform the debtor of the times and places when and where the child will be handed over to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court if the creditor does not participate in the enforcement.

(3) The handing over of the child to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court shall be carried out as soon as possible.

(4) The handing over of the child shall be attended by the bailiff, representatives of the orphan's court and the police, as well as a psychologist if the orphan's court has invited one. At the time and place specified in the bailiff's order, the representative of the orphan's court, in cooperation with the psychologist if one has been invited, shall conduct conversations with the debtor or other persons with whom the child is located in order to persuade them to hand over the child to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court if the creditor does not participate in the enforcement, as well as to prepare the child for return to the country of his or her habitual residence. Police representatives shall ensure public order and compliance with the bailiff's order.

(5) If the bailiff is not allowed into premises about which there is information that the child is located therein, they shall be opened by force in the presence of a police representative. If no person older than seven years is found in the premises, the bailiff, after the forced opening of the premises, without describing the property in the premises, shall ensure the secure closing and sealing of these premises. The bailiff shall leave at the relevant immovable property or premises a notice with an invitation to come to the bailiff's office to receive the keys to the premises. The bailiff shall make a note in the record of actions related to the forced opening of premises.

(6) If the child is handed over to the creditor, the bailiff shall make a note in the record of the handing over of the child, indicating that the decision has been enforced.

(7) If the child is handed over to the representative of the orphan's court for further actions to be taken to return the child to the country of his or her habitual residence, the bailiff shall make a note in the record of the handing over of the child. A copy of the record shall be issued to the representative of the orphan's court. After receiving a notice from the orphan's court that the child has been returned to the country of his or her habitual residence, the bailiff shall draw up a record that the decision has been enforced.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

620.15 Article. Actions of the bailiff if it is not possible to hand over the child to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court

If it is not possible for the orphan's court to obtain the information referred to in Article 620.13 of this law or the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence is not possible because the child has not been found at the times and places determined by the bailiff, the bailiff shall draw up a record thereof and send this record to the prosecutor's office so that it may decide on the initiation of criminal proceedings against the debtor in connection with his or her malicious evasion of enforcement of the decision, and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

620.16 Article. Refusal or postponement of enforcement of the decision

(1) The debtor may submit to the district (city) court which adopted the decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence a proposal for postponement of enforcement of the decision or refusal of enforcement of the decision if a substantial change of circumstances has occurred.

(2) A substantial change of circumstances within the meaning of this Article shall include:

1) the fact that the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence is not possible due to the child's health or psychological condition, as evidenced by a hospital or psychiatrist's certificate;

2) the child's objections to his or her return to the country of his or her habitual residence, as evidenced by the opinion of a psychologist appointed by the orphan's court;

3) the fact that the creditor shows no interest in restoring contact with the child.

(3) The proposal referred to in the first part of this Article may be submitted if more than one year has passed since the decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence (Article 644.20), except in the case referred to in point 1 of the second part of this Article.

(4) The application shall be examined at a court hearing, having previously notified the parties and the orphan's court thereof. The failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(5) In the decision on postponement of enforcement of the decision, the court shall indicate the obligations of the debtor and the creditor during the time while enforcement of the decision is postponed and, if necessary, also the procedure for restoring contact between the child and the creditor.

(6) The decision shall be enforceable immediately. An appeal may be lodged against the court decision. The lodging of an appeal shall not suspend the enforcement of the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

74.4 Chapter
Enforcement of decisions in matters arising from custody rights


This excerpt sits under: Publisher: Saeima Type: law Adopted: 14.10.1998.

## (Chapter 29

Edition of law 10.2015, which enters into force 03.12.2015.)

620.17 Article. Notice of obligation to execute decision

The bailiff shall send or issue to the debtor a notice of the obligation to hand over the child to the creditor within 15 days in the procedure specified in Article 555 of this law. In the notice, the bailiff warns the debtor of the consequences provided for in this chapter that will arise if the decision is not executed.

620.18 Article. Civil procedural consequences arising if the debtor does not execute the decision

(1) If the debtor has not executed the decision within the time limit specified in the bailiff's notice, the bailiff shall send information about it to the district (city) court which adopted the decision in a case arising from custody rights, or in whose territory of operation a foreign decision is to be executed.

(2) The judge, upon receipt of the information referred to in paragraph one of this Article, shall impose a fine on the debtor of up to 1500 euros.

(3) The question of imposing a fine shall be examined in written proceedings.

(4) The judge's decision on imposing a fine shall be sent to the debtor.

(5) An appeal may be submitted against the court's decision on imposing a fine.

(6) The fine shall be recovered from the debtor to state revenues.

(7) Payment of the fine does not release the debtor from the obligation to execute the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 09.06.2016 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

620.19 Article. Ascertainment of child's daily routine

(1) If it is necessary for the execution of the decision, the bailiff shall issue an order to the orphan's court according to the child's location to ascertain the child's daily routine within 15 days from the date of receipt of the order and to inform the bailiff thereof.

(2) The orphan's court shall immediately inform the bailiff of information relating to the child and his or her location which it has obtained in executing the order specified in paragraph one of this Article. If it is not possible to obtain the said information, the orphan's court shall inform the bailiff thereof.

(3) The bailiff, having received information that the child's location is not known, in accordance with Article 569 of this law shall request the judge to adopt a decision on the search for the child or the child and the debtor with the assistance of the police and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

(4) The bailiff, having received from the orphan's court or the police information about the child's location, which is in the territory of operation of the regional court to which this bailiff does not belong, shall make a note thereof in the enforcement document, indicating information about the child's location, and shall immediately issue the enforcement document to the creditor, explaining to him or her the right to submit the enforcement document for execution in accordance with the provisions of Article 549 of this law.

620.20 Article. Handing over of child to creditor

(1) Having received the information referred to in paragraph one of Article 620.19 of this law, the bailiff shall determine the place and time where and when the child will be handed over to the creditor, and shall notify the creditor, the orphan's court and the police according to the child's location thereof, issuing an order to their representatives to participate in the forced execution. The orphan's court at its discretion shall invite a psychologist to participate in the forced execution of the decision.

(2) The bailiff shall not inform the debtor of the place and time where and when the child will be handed over to the creditor.

(3) The child shall be handed over to the creditor as soon as possible.

(4) If the creditor does not appear at the time and place determined by the bailiff, the bailiff shall postpone the handing over of the child. If the creditor also does not appear repeatedly at the determined time and has not notified the reason for non-appearance or has not appeared for a reason which the bailiff does not recognise as justifiable, the enforcement document shall be issued back to the creditor without execution.

(5) The bailiff, representatives of the orphan's court and the police, as well as a psychologist, if the orphan's court has invited one, shall participate in the handing over of the child. At the place and time determined in the bailiff's order, the representative of the orphan's court in cooperation with the psychologist, if one has been invited, shall conduct conversations with the debtor or other persons with whom the child is located, in order to persuade them to hand over the child to the creditor, as well as to prepare the child for handing over to the creditor. Police representatives shall ensure public order and compliance with the bailiff's orders.

(6) If the bailiff is not allowed into premises about which there is information that the child is located therein, they shall be opened by force in the presence of a police representative. If no person older than seven years is found in the premises, the bailiff, after the forced opening of the premises, without describing the property in the premises, shall ensure the secure closing and sealing of these premises. The bailiff shall leave a notice at the relevant immovable property or premises with an invitation to come to the bailiff's office to receive the keys to the premises. The bailiff shall make a note in the record of actions related to the forced opening of premises.

(7) The bailiff shall make a note in the record of the handing over of the child to the creditor, indicating that the decision has been executed.

620.21 Article. Bailiff's action if it is not possible to hand over the child to the creditor

If it is not possible for the orphan's court to obtain the information referred to in Article 620.19 of this law or the handing over of the child to the creditor does not take place because the child is not found at the place and time determined by the bailiff, the bailiff shall draw up a record thereof and send it to the prosecutor's office so that it may decide the question of initiating criminal proceedings against the debtor in connection with his or her malicious evasion of execution of the decision, and shall also send the record to the orphan's court for evaluation of the debtor's conduct and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

620.22 Article. Refusal or postponement of execution of foreign decision
(Deleted from 01.08.2022 by the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force 07.07.2022. See transitional provision point 177)

74.5 Chapter
Execution of decisions in cases arising from contact rights

## (Chapter 29

Edition of law 10.2015, which enters into force 03.12.2015.)

620.23 Article. Notice of obligation to execute decision

(1) If the decision (including a foreign court decision and a court decision on the review of the time and place of exercise of contact rights adopted in the procedure specified in Article 244.13 of this law, if the court has not ordered the forced opening of premises) specifies the procedure, time and place for the creditor's exercise of contact rights, the bailiff shall send to the debtor, in the procedure specified in Article 555 of this law, a notice of the obligation to execute the decision in the procedure, time and place specified therein. If the time and place are not specified in the decision, the bailiff shall determine the place of execution and the time of execution within a reasonable period, but not later than two weeks, unless otherwise follows from the decision. In the notice, the bailiff warns the debtor of the consequences provided for in this chapter that arise in the event of non-execution of the decision.

(2) If the decision specifies that contact rights are to be exercised at a specified place or in the presence of a contact person or a representative of the orphan's court, or a person authorised by the orphan's court, or at a specified place and in the presence of a contact person or a representative of the orphan's court, or a person authorised by the orphan's court, the bailiff shall also notify the contact person, the orphan's court and the user of the premises of the specified place of the time and place of execution of the decision, giving an order to the contact person or the representative of the orphan's court, or the person authorised by the orphan's court to participate in the execution and an order to the user of the premises of the specified place to ensure access to the specified place.
(With amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force 07.07.2022.)

620.24 Article. Act on execution or non-execution of decision

(1) If, at the time and place determined by the bailiff, the debtor ensures the creditor's contact with the child in accordance with the procedure for exercising contact rights specified in the decision, the bailiff shall draw up an act that the decision is being executed. If, at the time and place indicated by the bailiff, the child is not found and the debtor has not notified the reason why the child is not found, or has notified a reason which the bailiff does not recognise as justifiable, or the debtor refuses to execute the decision for a reason which the bailiff does not recognise as justifiable, the bailiff shall draw up an act on non-execution of the decision.

(2) If, at the time and place indicated by the bailiff, the child is not found, but the debtor has notified the reason why the child is not found, and the bailiff recognises this reason as justifiable, or the debtor refuses to execute the decision for a reason which the bailiff recognises as justifiable, the bailiff shall draw up an act on non-execution of the decision for justifiable reasons and shall determine a new time and place for execution of the decision.

620.25 Article. Civil procedural consequences arising if debtor does not execute decision

(1) The bailiff shall send the act on non-execution of the decision to the district (city) court which adopted the decision in the case arising from contact rights, or in whose territory of operation the foreign court decision is to be executed.

(2) The judge, upon receipt of the act referred to in paragraph one of this Article, shall impose a fine on the debtor of up to 1500 euros.

(3) The question of imposing a fine shall be examined in written proceedings.

(4) The judge's decision on imposing a fine shall be sent to the debtor.

(5) An appeal may be lodged against the court decision on imposing a fine.

(6) The fine shall be recovered from the debtor to state revenues.

(7) Payment of the fine shall not release the debtor from the obligation to execute the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 09.06.2016 and 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force 07.07.2022.)

620.26 Article. Bailiff's action if it is not possible to hand over child to creditor

If, after the question of imposing a fine has been examined (Article 620.25), the debtor does not execute the order repeatedly given by the bailiff in accordance with the procedure specified in Article 620.23 of this law regarding the obligation to execute the decision and an act on non-execution of the decision has been repeatedly drawn up in accordance with paragraph one of Article 620.24 of this law, the bailiff shall send the said act to the prosecutor's office so that it may decide the question of initiating criminal proceedings against the debtor in connection with his or her malicious evasion of execution of the decision, and shall also send the act to the orphan's court for evaluation of the debtor's conduct and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

620.27 Article. Issuance of enforcement document to creditor

If, after resumption of enforcement proceedings, the debtor continues not to execute the decision or there are other circumstances that make execution of the decision difficult or impossible, the bailiff shall return the enforcement document to the creditor, informing him or her of his or her rights under Article 244.13 of this law to request the court to review the procedure for exercising contact rights.

620.28 Article. Procedure for executing decision on review of time and place of exercise of contact rights if court has ordered forced opening of premises

(1) The bailiff, upon commencing execution of the court decision on the review of the time and place of exercise of contact rights adopted in the procedure specified in Article 244.13 of this law, taking into account the address indicated in the decision and the time period during which the premises may be opened by force, shall determine the time and place when and where the child will be handed over to the creditor for the exercise of contact, and shall notify:

1) the creditor, informing him or her of the creditor's obligation to be present at the enforcement actions;

2) the contact person in whose presence, in accordance with what is specified in the decision, contact rights are to be exercised, giving an order to this person to participate in the execution;

3) the orphan's court at the child's place of location, giving an order to its representative to participate in the forced execution. The orphan's court, at its discretion, shall involve a psychologist in the forced execution of the decision;

4) the police at the child's place of location, giving an order to its representative to participate in the forced execution.

(2) The bailiff shall not inform the debtor of the place and time where and when the child will be handed over to the creditor for the exercise of contact.

(3) At the place and time specified in the bailiff's order, the representative of the orphan's court, in cooperation with a psychologist, if one has been involved, shall conduct discussions with the debtor or other persons with whom the child is located, in order to persuade them to hand over the child to the creditor for the exercise of contact. Police representatives shall ensure public order and compliance with the bailiff's orders.

(4) If the bailiff is not admitted to the premises indicated in the court decision, they shall be opened by force. If no person older than seven years is found in the premises, the bailiff, after forced opening of the premises, without describing the property in the premises, shall ensure the secure closing and sealing of these premises. The bailiff shall leave a notice at the relevant immovable property or premises with an invitation to come to the bailiff's office to receive the keys to the premises. The bailiff shall make a note in the act of actions related to the forced opening of premises.

(5) If the child is handed over to the creditor, the bailiff shall draw up an act on execution of the decision.

(6) If contact rights are to be exercised at a specified place or in the presence of a contact person at another place that is not the place of execution, the child shall be handed over to the representative of the orphan's court or the contact person so that he or she, together with the creditor, may take the child to the specified place for the exercise of contact. The bailiff shall draw up an act on execution of the decision, indicating the person to whom the child has been handed over.

(7) If, when performing the actions specified in this Article, it was not possible to hand over the child to the creditor, the bailiff shall close the enforcement case without execution and shall inform the creditor of his or her rights under Article 244.13 of this law to request the court to review the procedure for exercising contact rights.
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

620.29 Article. Postponement or refusal of execution of foreign decision
