(In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

166. Complaints about the actions of an administrator, sworn bailiff or sworn notary, for which a state fee has been paid and which were submitted until the date when amendments to the first part of Article 34 of this law enter into force, which delete point 14 and delete the words "for complaints in connection with the decision or action of the insolvency proceedings administrator (hereinafter — administrator)" in point 13, shall be examined in accordance with the procedure set out in this law as it was in force until the date of entry into force of the amendments mentioned in this point. (In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

167. Until the date when document circulation in civil proceedings has completely transitioned to electronic form, documents prepared in paper form shall be converted to electronic form by certifying them with an electronic signature within the meaning of point 10 of Article 3 of Regulation No. 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council and observing the following provisions:

1) the representation and compliance of the content of the original document with it during the specified data storage period is ensured; 2) the reading of the content electronically and, if necessary, the creation of a derivative in paper form is ensured; 3) the converted document is protected against additions, changes or unauthorised access or destruction. A document converted to electronic form for storage in electronic media in the procedure specified in this point has the same legal force as the original document. (In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

168. To writ of execution in paper form or writs of execution signed with a secure electronic signature issued until 30 November 2021, the provisions specified for other enforcement documents, as well as the provisions that applied to writs of execution and were in force until 30 November 2021, shall apply. (In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

169. In the event of loss of a writ of execution in paper form or in the case of requesting a writ of execution not issued until 30 November 2021, the court, upon the application of the creditor, shall prepare a writ of execution and ensure its availability in the online system or, if this is not possible for technical reasons or the writ of execution is to be submitted to the court for the establishment of a mortgage, shall issue a writ of execution signed with a secure electronic signature in accordance with the procedure that was in force until 30 November 2021. (In the wording of the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

170. From 1 December 2021, with respect to a document created or attached in the online system, the requirement for a signature specified in this law is fulfilled if the document is signed with an electronic signature within the meaning of point 10 of Article 3 of Regulation No. 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council. (In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

171. From 1 December 2021, a ruling of the court or judge, which is adopted in the form of a separate procedural document, shall be signed with a secure electronic signature, except when this is not possible for technical reasons. (In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

172. Documents to be attached to the case materials that were submitted to the court from 1 December 2021 in paper form shall be converted to electronic form by the court. The court may not convert documents submitted until 31 May 2026 to electronic form if there is a large volume of documents in paper form or if this is not possible for technical reasons. (In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021 with amendments made by the law of 05.10.2023, which enters into force on 02.11.2023.)

173. Until 31 December 2026, Chapter 48.3 of this law, as well as amendments to Article 613 and Chapter 74.2 of this law shall not apply in cases where introduction into possession is to be carried out in such real estate for the use of which a residential premises lease agreement was concluded until 30 April 2021 and it is not registered in the land register. (In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

174. Until the date of entry into force of the Cabinet of Ministers regulations referred to in the second part of Article 39 of this law, Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No. 983 of 1 September 2009 "Procedure for Calculating Expenses Related to the Examination of a Case" shall apply, insofar as they are not in conflict with this law. (In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

175. Until the date of entry into force of the Cabinet of Ministers regulations referred to in the second part of Article 39 of this law, the amount of expenses related to the preparation of derivatives of court documents shall be determined by applying point 2 of Annex 2 of Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No. 96 of
19 February 2013 "Regulations on Fee-Based Services Provided by the Court". (In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

176. With respect to the suspension or refusal of enforcement of a foreign court ruling for which a certificate has been issued in accordance with point 1 of Article
41 or point 1 of Article 42 of Council Regulation No. 2201/2003 in the event of a substantial change of circumstances, the provisions of this law that were in force until 31 July 2022 shall apply. (In the wording of the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

177. Point 20 of Article 540, the eighth part of Article 563, the amendment to the first part of Article 559 regarding the deletion of the numbers "620.22" and "620.29", amendments regarding the deletion of Articles 620.22 and 620.29, as well as amendments to Articles 244.2, 541.1, 543.1,
545.1, 555, 644, 644.1, 644.2, 644.3, 644.12, 644.15, 644.18, 644.19 and 653.1 in connection with the application of Council Regulation (EU)
2019/1111 shall enter into force on 1 August 2022. (In the wording of the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

178. The amendment to point 4 of the first part of Article 400 of this law regarding protested bills of exchange that are not issued in the form of a notarial deed, point 6 of the second part of Article 539 and point 16.1 of Article 540 shall enter into force on 1 October 2022. (In the wording of the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

179. Amendments to points 3 and 19 of the first part of Article 34, point 1.2 of the first part of Article 43, the first and second parts of Article 341.2, Article 341.4, the second, third, fifth and sixth parts of Article 341.5, Article 341.6, the third, fourth and fifth parts of Article 341.7, the first part of Article 341.8, Article 341.11, Article 341.12, amendments to Articles 363.9, 363.23,
363.24, 363.25, 363.26 and 363.27, the first part of Article 363.28, Article 363.29, the first part of Article 363.36, Articles 363.37 and
363.38, amendments to Articles 440.1 and 440.11, the first and third parts of Article 560, the first and fourth parts of Article 562 and the first part of Article 563 of this law, which are related to the implementation of Directive (EU) 2019/1023 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 June 2019 on preventive restructuring frameworks, on discharge of debt and disqualifications, and on measures to increase the efficiency of procedures concerning restructuring, insolvency and discharge of debt, and amending Directive (EU) 2017/1132 (Directive on restructuring and insolvency), shall enter into force simultaneously with amendments to the Insolvency Law and shall apply to legal protection proceedings, insolvency proceedings of legal persons and insolvency proceedings of natural persons that are commenced from 15 September 2023. (In the wording of the law of 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

180. The amendment to Article 223 of this law regarding its supplementation with point 10 in the part on the termination of proceedings in a case if the debtor's insolvency proceedings administrator has submitted a request in a claim for the exclusion of this debtor from another company, which was filed in accordance with Article 136.1 of the Commercial Law, shall enter into force on 1 July 2023. (In the wording of the law of 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

181. Amendments to Articles 374, 375 and 388 of this law in connection with the selection of an administrator in a credit institution insolvency case shall enter into force on 1 September 2023. (In the wording of the law of 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

182. Part 1.2 of Article 77 of this law, which provides for the prohibition for the Maintenance Guarantee Fund debtor to assign claims, shall enter into force on 1 December 2023. (In the wording of the law of 05.10.2023, which enters into force on 02.11.2023.)

Informative reference to European Union directives
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2006 with amendments made by the laws of 20.12.2010, 15.03.2012, 19.12.2013, 04.02.2016,
19.10.2017, 28.02.2019, 16.06.2022 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

The law incorporates legal norms arising from:

1) (deleted by the law of 19.12.2013); 2) Directive 2004/48/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 April 2004 on the enforcement of intellectual property rights; 3) Directive 2008/52/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 May 2008 on certain aspects of mediation in civil and commercial matters; 4) Council Directive 2010/24/EU of 16 March 2010 concerning mutual assistance for the recovery of claims relating to taxes, duties and other measures; 5) Directive 2011/7/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 February 2011 on combating late payment in commercial transactions; 6) Directive 2014/67/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 May 2014 on the enforcement of Directive 96/71/EC concerning the posting of workers in the framework of the provision of services and amending Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012 on administrative cooperation through the Internal Market Information System ('the IMI Regulation'); 7) Directive 2014/104/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2014 on certain rules governing actions for damages under national law for infringements of the competition law provisions of the Member States and of the European Union; 8) Directive (EU) 2016/943 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 June 2016 on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (trade secrets) against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure; 9) Directive (EU) 2019/1 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2018 to empower the competition authorities of the Member States to be more effective enforcers and to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market; 10) Directive (EU) 2019/1023 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 June 2019 on preventive restructuring frameworks, on discharge of debt and disqualifications, and on measures to increase the efficiency of procedures concerning restructuring, insolvency and discharge of debt, and amending Directive (EU) 2017/1132 (Directive on restructuring and insolvency). The law enters into force on 1 March 1999. The law was adopted by the Saeima on 14 October 1998. President of the State G. Ulmanis
